papers.title: VisDrone-ReID: A Unified Multi-Category Object Re-Identification Benchmark
papers.abstract: Object re-identification (Re-ID) benchmarks remain predominantly confined to single-category evaluations, limiting the development of unified systems capable of operating across diverse object types. This paper presents VisDrone-ReID, a unified multi-category Re-ID benchmark derived from the VisDrone2019-MOT dataset through a principled conversion pipeline. The pipeline resolves structural incompatibilities between multi-object tracking annotations and Re-ID evaluation requirements, addressing sequence-scoped identity collision, temporal redundancy, and the absence of a principled identity-level train/test split. The resulting benchmark comprises 9,516 identities and 150,016 images across ten object categories - pedestrian, people, bicycle, car, van, truck, tricycle, awning-tricycle, bus, and motor, sourced from 80 unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) sequences captured across urban environments. A leave-one-out (LOO) evaluation protocol is adopted to provide a comprehensive assessment. Baseline experiments across four representative Re-ID models spanning CNN and transformer architectures establish the first systematic performance reference on this benchmark. Results reveal a consistent Rank-1 to mAP gap across all models, suggesting that VisDrone-ReID presents a genuine retrieval challenge beyond nearest-neighbour matching. Per-category analysis identifies pedestrian as the most challenging category and reveals that vision-language pretraining provides a measurable advantage on semantically distinctive categories. VisDrone-ReID provides a consistent platform for studying multi-category object re-identification under the scale variation, viewpoint challenges, and category diversity characteristic of real-world surveillance scenarios.

papers.title: Is It Still There? Place-Registered Verification Makes VLMs Reliable Scene-Change Detectors
papers.abstract: A robot that returns to a space must tell which objects were added, removed or moved since its last visit, while its trajectory, viewpoints and lighting differ between the two visits. We find that multi-image vision-language models (VLMs) fail at this task mainly because they cannot find the place where an object was. A VLM recognises what each frame shows but cannot check whether an object is still at its place in the other capture. It therefore reports objects that only one capture shows and misses most removed and moved objects. We propose STILL, which reformulates change detection as object verification at a registered place. 3D geometry registers the place of each change hypothesis in the other capture, and one VLM answers, from a scene view and a local place view, whether the object is still at that place, trained with supervision of the same form. Under the official SceneDiff protocol, STILL raises the main metric obj/sc AP from 24.0 to 37.8, and from 11.6 to 20.6 on the egocentric kitchen subset without any kitchen training data. It improves F1 by more than 21 points over a VLM fine-tuned on the same annotations and adds only about 11% to the runtime.

authors.name: Baihua Li
authors.institution: China International Center for Economic and Technical Exchanges

papers.title: A Scalable Decentralized Event-Triggered Topology-Switching Protocol for Verifiable Safety in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: This paper develops a decentralized event-triggered topology-switching protocol that allows agents to disconnect from the communication network while preserving state safety and excluding Zeno behavior. We establish a robust barrier function condition that guarantees safety as long as the estimation error remains within a prescribed threshold. Each agent uses locally computable certificates to determine when to connect and disconnect from the network. The certificate construction improves scalability by reducing the complexity of topology-dependent computations from $O(2^N)$ to $O(N)$, where $N$ is the number of agents. We formally prove that the protocol ensures the estimation error does not exceed the prescribed threshold and is non-Zeno. An alternating method computes an error-weighting matrix and a quadratic barrier function that guarantee safety under the proposed protocol. Finally, we evaluate the protocol on four interconnected microgrids. Compared with maintaining network connectivity at all times, the protocol reduces the time agents remain connected while keeping phase and frequency within their safe operating region.

papers.title: Singular Birth-Death model
papers.abstract: We introduce and study a one-dimensional singular birth-death model constructed from It\^o's Brownian excursion measure. In this model, particles are born at the origin at infinite rate, evolve as Brownian excursions away from the origin, and are killed upon returning to the origin. Although the number of particles alive at any fixed deterministic time is almost surely finite, we prove that the set of exceptional times at which infinitely many particles are alive is almost surely dense and has Hausdorff dimension $1/2$. We further investigate the spatial structure of the particle system at such exceptional times. In particular, we identify the critical near-origin profile of the infinite particle cloud, which is governed by a scale of order $\log\log(1/|x|)^{-1}$ as $x\downarrow0$. Finally, we establish laws of large numbers and central limit theorems for two natural observables of the system: the $\alpha$-power sum of the positions of all alive particles and the top particle position.

papers.title: Scalable composite likelihood inference for directed probit networks
papers.abstract: We develop scalable estimation and inference for directed probit networks with correlated sending and receiving effects and residual reciprocity. An incomplete composite likelihood in two stages combines exact bivariate margins of sampled dyads and triples, avoiding integration in high dimensions and cubic enumeration. For fixed parameter dimension, criterion evaluation is linear in the number of draws. Averaging a fixed number of fits from independent index samples reduces sampling variation and allows parallel computation. We establish consistency and joint asymptotic normality with different directional rates, allowing a singular node projection when draw counts lie between the node and dyad scales. An overlap covariance accounts for network and index variation and is consistent relative to each directional variance. Independent index samples stabilize covariance estimation without refitting. The resulting procedure provides standard errors, mapped joint regions and score tests for zero variance components. Simulations show improved estimation from averaging and substantially lower computation times than default Bayesian fitting. An application to a fly brain network with 21,738 neurons demonstrates estimation and inference at a scale relevant to modern network data.

papers.title: Communication-Efficient Hamiltonian Evaluation for Massively Parallel Tensor-Product Bitstring Selected Configuration Interaction
papers.abstract: Extreme-scale selected configuration interaction (SCI) requires coordinated Hamiltonian evaluation, distributed CI-vector storage, and interprocess communication on massively parallel computers. Our previous work [J. Chem. Phys. 164, 194103 (2026)] introduced the tensor-product bitstring selected configuration interaction (TBSCI) framework, combining on-the-fly Hamiltonian evaluation with fully distributed CI-vector storage and enabling parallel diagonalization of trillion-determinant spaces on up to 54,000 Fugaku nodes. Here, we introduce FLIP, a new Hamiltonian evaluation algorithm within TBSCI that reorganizes the CI-vector layout and excitation-link data to replace remote CI-coefficient transfers for $\alpha$-electron double excitations with local coefficient access and link retrieval from nearby MPI ranks. In communication-intensive full configuration interaction (FCI) benchmarks on Fugaku, no exposed communication waiting time was recorded on the slowest process across all 32 measured Hamiltonian-vector multiplications. For N$_2$/cc-pVTZ with $2.62\times10^{12}$ determinants, the multiplication achieved 91.3% strong-scaling efficiency from 18,000 to 81,000 nodes (more than 3.8 million compute cores). We also obtained an FCI reference potential-energy curve for N$_2$/cc-pVTZ. At all six bond lengths, spin bitstrings selected by their collective weights in reference SCI wavefunctions yielded variational TBSCI energies within 0.1 m$E_h$ of FCI using fewer than 1% of the FCI determinants, demonstrating the compactness of the tensor-product bitstring representation. Finally, we discuss local construction of double-excitation links to substantially reduce communication volume and eliminate persistent storage of precomputed double-link tables for future second-order perturbation theory calculations with large external determinant spaces.

papers.title: Will it bend? Modelling hydrogel box hinges with a gel Lattice Spring Method
papers.abstract: Hydrogels are biocompatible smart materials comprised of a hydrophilic polymer network which can absorb a large volume of water (swelling). The changes in shape the gel undergoes as it swells or de-swells can be utilised in the design of actuators. This is of particular interest for many applications whereby hydrogel actuators would be combined into a complex origami-inspired structure which can fold and unfold according to application needs. In this paper, we therefore focus on one such actuator design, the bilayer hinge, which can induce bending (for potential use in a fold/unfold mechanism). We develop a model using the gel lattice spring method (gLSM) which can be used to simulate composite structures comprised of hydrogel and elastomer and compute the equilibrium bending angle of bilayer hinges for a range of geometries and material properties.

papers.title: A Polynomial-Time Algorithm for Maximum Witness Set
papers.abstract: A witness set in a polygon is a set of points whose visibility regions are pairwise disjoint. Since no point of the polygon can see more than one witness, the cardinality of a witness set provides a lower bound on the minimum number of guards required to cover the polygon. Finding a maximum witness set is therefore a natural packing counterpart to the classical Art Gallery problem. While the latter is $\exists\mathbb{R}$-complete, the computational complexity of finding a maximum witness set in a general simple polygon has remained open. In this paper, we present a polynomial-time algorithm for computing a maximum witness set in a simple polygon with $n$ vertices, of which $\rho$ are reflex, assuming that no three vertices are collinear. Our algorithm runs in $\mathcal{O}(\rho^4n^6\log n)$ time. Our approach exploits a tree structure induced by witness visibility regions and employs geometric dynamic programming over nested regions determined by visibility windows.

papers.title: Explicit geometric integrators for Langevin equations with superquadratic potentials
papers.abstract: We propose a new class of explicit methods for Langevin equations with a superquadratic potential that simultaneously preserve the conformal symplecticity and ergodicity as well as achieving high-order convergence. The construction is based on a mollified potential approach, in which the original potential is truncated to quadratic growth at infinity and globally mollified to control the superquadratic behavior while maintaining the underlying properties of the original dynamics. By appropriately choosing the cut-off radius, the far-field quadratic coefficient, and the step size, we obtain the coercivity of the mollified potential and derive its derivative estimates. These estimates allow us to prove uniform-in-time weak convergence for the proposed (including higher-order) explicit conformal symplectic numerical methods. Since the mollified potential is identical to the original one in a ball whose radius grows as the step size decreases, the computational cost of the new methods is essentially the same as that of the usual schemes (e.g., BAOAB) applied to the original potential. Numerical experiments are provided to illustrate the theoretical results.

papers.title: Density-First Design of Anti-Jamming Sparse Spreading Codes for NB-IoT
papers.abstract: As narrowband Internet of Things (NB-IoT) systems continue to be deployed in increasingly heterogeneous and demanding wireless environments, including those characterized by interference, high mobility, and potentially hostile conditions, enhancing the resilience of the physical-layer waveform has become an important and timely design consideration. Motivated by this need, the present paper introduces a density-first framework for the design of anti-jamming sparse spreading codes in NB-IoT systems. Building on this framework, we propose a generalized method for constructing sparse codes that decouples column density from the conventional Alamouti-paired structure, thereby enabling both disjoint-support and deterministic code designs. In addition, we develop a generative machine-learning approach based on a variational autoencoder for synthesizing jamming-robust sparse spreading codes. To evaluate the performance of sparse spreading under conditions of additive white Gaussian noise, fading, and pulse jamming, we present a bit-error-rate (BER) analysis framework. Extensive Monte Carlo simulations, conducted across a wide range of density, channel, and jamming conditions, show that the performance of sparse spreading codes is determined primarily by column density rather than by optimization of code coefficients. In particular, highly sparse codes with disjoint support offer the greatest robustness to jamming while avoiding the unfavorable intermediate-density regime. Relative to the prior-art Alamouti-paired low-density spreading code, the recommended uniform-density design reduces pulse-jamming BER by roughly 5 times; a deterministic Lempel-Costas construction attains the empirical optimum in closed form, while the variational-autoencoder generator yields a further 45% improvement over the best algebraic design.

papers.title: iEEG Can Help EEG: Improving Clinical Scalp EEG Analysis through Intracranial Priors
papers.abstract: Scalp electroencephalography (EEG) is a cornerstone of clinical brain monitoring, making the quality of its signal fundamental to downstream tasks and models. However, that signal is heavily contaminated by non-neural interference and blurred by volume conduction. Existing methods operate almost exclusively within the scalp modality, so they inherit the contamination they would need to overcome. In practice, intracranial EEG (iEEG) observes the neural activity with far higher fidelity, yet it is invasive and therefore scarce, and the two modalities are rarely recorded as pairs at scale, share no common channel space, and offer no clean ground truth to directly supervise a mapping. Motivated by the neuronal synchronization mechanism shared by the two modalities, we propose a reprogramming approach that fits a signal-to-signal model on iEEG alone and freezes it as a cross-modal prior. We introduce ReBrain, a framework to transfer an iEEG-learned prior to scalp EEG, which re-expresses any scalp signal through that prior and can be inserted upstream of any downstream model with no pairing or fine-tuning. ReBrain consistently improves host models across recordings from multiple hospitals and across architecture families, and our analysis traces this gain to genuine neural structure carried by iEEG rather than to the architecture itself. This work provides evidence that a scarce clean modality can serve as a transferable prior for an abundant noisy one, offering a general recipe for cross-modal transfer among biosignals. Our code is available at https://github.com/Xianglong-Bao/ReBrain.

authors.name: Kewen Wang
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Jetriever: Shifting Agent Memory Retrieval from Similarity to Utility
papers.abstract: A useful memory need not resemble the question it helps answer. Jetriever ranks each stored memory by Jev's decision score for its usefulness to the current question, replacing similarity search with full-pool utility scoring. On InMind's 125 indirect-query tasks, it places the gold exchange first in 84.8% of cases; matched BM25 and MiniLM controls reach 1.6% and 0.0% when indexing user turns. A 20-question comparison separates finding evidence from ranking it: Jev and Qwen3.5 9B each find 90% of gold exchanges by rank 50, while Laya finds 30%; at rank one, Jev reaches 85% and Qwen3.5 9B 40%. On a dimension-proportional random sample of 60 MemoryAgentBench questions, Jetriever's four-dimension score is 55.4%, against 44.3% for ReFind on the same questions. Jev retrieval costs USD 0.00834 per InMind question and USD 0.03103 per MAB question on average. These results show the value of world knowledge, scores that rank decisive memories first, and affordable full-pool scoring.

papers.title: Kinetic and Thermodynamic Limits of Sodium Pore Filling in Hard Carbon
papers.abstract: The low-voltage plateau-like capacity of hard carbon anodes is widely regarded as a key signature of sodium storage in closed pores, often defining the performance of Na-ion batteries. Here, we combine first-principles calculations with a grand canonical Monte Carlo pore-filling model to show that Na storage in closed pores is not governed by a single equilibrium-plateau mechanism but by a distribution of pore-specific thermodynamic and kinetic activation processes. Thermodynamically, the voltage at which Na pore filling becomes favorable decreases with increasing pore size. Kinetically, pore filling involves Na nucleation, coalescence, growth, and bulk diffusion. While small pores fill rapidly, large pores exhibit both a smaller thermodynamic stimulus and significant kinetic limitations. Nucleation can be accelerated by introducing defects at the pore walls, although an excessively high defect concentration slows bulk diffusion. This work shows that not all closed pores contribute equally to Na storage: some may be thermodynamically favorable but kinetically inactive under realistic charge/discharge rates. Because of this, the inverse design of hard carbon electrodes should target a kinetically accessible pore-size and defect-density window that balances high plateau-like capacity with fast-charging performance.

authors.name: Yuxin Tang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: ReScene: Incremental Scene Chronology from Sparse Revisits
papers.abstract: Scene chronology aims to reconstruct a scene across visits separated by hours or days, during which objects may change in position, presence or shape. Such reconstruction must retain every earlier state, yet each revisit often provides only a few images. Storing a complete model for each visit duplicates the unchanged scene, whereas updating a single shared model alters earlier states. We present ReScene, which stores each visit as an immutable compact update, so that any earlier visit can be recovered exactly by applying the stored updates in order, without retaining past images. To localise each update, ReScene attributes the disagreement between the preceding reconstruction and the new images to individual Gaussians through their compositing weights. This attribution guides the suppression of outdated Gaussians and the refinement of persistent ones, while newly visible surfaces are initialised from learned multi-view depth. We also introduce Multi-State, a benchmark of non-rigid deformation and partial material removal, including synthetic scenes with ground-truth geometry. ReScene achieves quality higher than sequential 3DGS checkpointing with 2.5--4.8$\times$ less uncompressed history storage. At comparable PSNR, it also reduces foreground depth error by 3.2$\times$ relative to sequential ChronoGS, showing that accurate rendering does not necessarily imply accurate geometry. Code and benchmark are available at https://waychin-weiqin.github.io/ReScene/.

papers.title: Small Harnesses, Default Checks, Limited Coverage: Bounded Model Checking in Practice
papers.abstract:
The growing use of AI to generate software and verification artifacts has increased the need for automated systems that provide reliable software assurance. Bounded model checking (BMC) offers a practical foundation for such systems by automatically checking correctness and security properties directly on software. However, effective verification requires choices about properties, input assumptions, function models, and execution bounds that influence the guarantees obtained. Little systematic evidence exists on how practitioners make these choices, limiting the empirical foundation for developing automated verification systems.
  We present an empirical study of BMC practices in open-source C and Rust projects using CBMC and Kani. Through LLM-assisted open coding, static analysis, and artifact execution, we characterize verification properties, artifact complexity, and verification outcomes. Our findings reveal diverse verification objectives and generally small harnesses, but also property-specification errors and extensive use of execution bounds and environment models. Most artifacts complete verification quickly and achieve high coverage within their scope, while repository-level coverage decreases with project size. Our findings and annotated dataset provide empirical baselines for verification automation and motivate improved techniques for property validation, harness generation, and scaling verification breadth.

authors.name: Ricardo Calvo
authors.institution: Centro de Investigación Biomédica en Red Diabetes y Enfermedades Metabólicas Asociadas

papers.title: A Scalable Multi Task Learning Framework for Modeling Demographic Disagreements in Annotation Tasks
papers.abstract: Annotators from different demographic backgrounds often disagree in systematic ways due to varying lived experiences, cultural contexts, and their relationship to the content. When such disagreement occurs, one group's perspective may sometimes warrant prioritization because they hold an epistemically advantaged standpoint or bear greater stake in the outcome. For example, when assessing toxicity of posts on social media, it may be important to prioritize a targeted group's viewpoint. We propose a Stakeholder-Aware Joint Multi-Task Learning (SAJ-MTL) framework to jointly model demographic disagreement both across- and within- annotator groups. The model uses conditional gradient routing to handle sparsity induced by group-conditional labeling, and parameterization supports customized weighting of groups in different task settings. SAJ-MTL improves group-level performance in toxicity detection through better context-aware understanding of demographic-sensitive content. Only annotator group-membership information is required, which is more practical than existing methods requiring more privacy-invasive individual-level annotator details. Our scalable architecture is also computationally efficient to support large-scale deployment.

authors.name: Matthew Lease
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

papers.title: Where slide-level foundation-model classifiers fail on atypical breast lesions
papers.abstract: Whether a ductal breast lesion is called atypical hyperplasia or low-grade carcinoma in situ increasingly determines surgery. However, slide-level classifiers built on pathology foundation models (PFMs) perform worst on these lesions. Using four PFMs, cross-validation on BRACS and preregistered hypotheses, we studied where the classification of atypia fails. Because slides are labelled with their most severe lesion, only 39% of the slides with annotated atypical ductal hyperplasia (ADH) were labelled ADH. Attention ranked the lesion high but rarely first, and showing the model only the lesion helped little, whereas classifiers trained per decision with lesion-level labels improved all four atypical boundaries. ADH regions inserted into benign slides raised the probability of malignancy more than that of atypia. In a hospital with pathologist-labelled single-subtype slides and in HISTAI, benign slides were scored closer to lesions and triage specificity fell from 0.48-0.53 to 0.00-0.07 and 0.22.

papers.title: Splitting of separatrices in generalized standard maps
papers.abstract: We consider generalized standard maps, that is, maps $F_h:(x,y) \mapsto (x+y+f(x;h),y+f(x;h))$ under quite general assumptions. These maps are area preserving. In particular, the Chirikov standard map, the area preserving H\'enon map and the case $f(x;h)= \varepsilon(x-x^n)$, $n\ge 2$, where $\varepsilon = 4 \sinh^2(h/2)$ satisfy our hypotheses. For all these cases, the problem of the existence of transverse homoclinic points arises. We prove that, for a wide class of generalized standard maps, the primary homoclinic points are transverse, provided that some constant is different from 0.

papers.title: Percolation under Edge-Reversal: Creation and Destruction of Strong Connectivity in Directed Networks
papers.abstract: We study how the connectivity of a directed network changes when each edge is independently reversed with probability $p$, while the underlying connections remain fixed. Reversal changes the in- and out-degrees, and we derive the exact transformation of the joint in--out-degree distribution and characterize its evolution under repeated reversal. However, the transformation does not rewire the network, and every edge still connects the same pair of vertices. As a result, the transformed degree distribution alone does not determine whether a giant strongly connected component exists, and a reconstruction based only on the transformed degrees can even place the network on the wrong percolation state. For the directed configuration model, we account for the preserved structure by separately tracking edges that retain or reverse their original direction, leading to a two-type branching process. From this formalism, we obtain explicit analytical criteria for the creation or destruction of a giant strongly connected component and illustrate these contrasting outcomes with empirical examples. Consistent with the predicted creation criterion, randomizing edge directions in a \emph{S. cerevisiae} transcriptional regulation network dramatically increases the size of the largest strongly connected component. In the San Diego directed road network, the degree moments satisfy the destruction criterion, and the largest strongly connected component decreases to virtually zero, although its decline occurs well below the predicted configuration-model threshold. These results provide a framework for assessing the sensitivity of mutual reachability to changes or uncertainty in edge directions and show that directional disorder can either enable or suppress global connectivity without changing the underlying connections.

authors.name: M. Angeles Serrano
authors.institution: Institució Catalana de Recerca i Estudis Avançats

papers.title: Early UAV Detection Using 5G NR LEO Downlinks for Passive ISAC
papers.abstract: 5G New Radio (NR) low-Earth-orbit (LEO) downlinks enable passive integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) detection. Weak echoes require motion-compensated accumulation, but exhaustive searches postpone alerts. We propose a receiver that combines selective Doppler-rate search, early UAV alerts and continued delay-Doppler estimation. Classical, statistical and neural configurations select rates of Doppler change to search, while a shared correlation score determines detection. Simulated echo delay, Doppler and power follow the moving satellite-UAV-receiver geometry, propagation loss, assumed scattering and antenna response. In a line-of-sight scene with acquired beams and UAVs at 5-8 km horizontal distance, all three configurations match exhaustive search at 92.9% correct final detections, with 0.10-0.13% observed false alerts on no-UAV recordings. The neural configuration reduces mean time to the first correct alert by 36.5% versus exhaustive search and 21.9% versus the closest literature baseline, averaging over successfully detected UAVs. These results demonstrate earlier UAV alerts while preserving exhaustive search's final detection accuracy, supporting passive sensing over cellular satellites.

authors.name: Hamid Saeedi
authors.institution: University of Doha for Science and Technology

authors.name: Halim Yanikomeroglu
authors.institution: Centre Tecnologic de Telecomunicacions de Catalunya

papers.title: Low-energy states of a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain connected perpendicularly to a metallic lead
papers.abstract: Recently, Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chains (SSHCs) coupled to metallic leads have attracted attention. In particular Mart\'{\i}nez {\it et al.} [Phys. Rev. Res. {\bf 8}, 043118 (2026)] studied a topological SSHC connected at one of its ends perpendicularly to a metallic lead modeled by a tight-binding chain. Here, we extend their results by incorporating the finite-size splitting of the end modes of the isolated SSHC, which are determined analytically with high accuracy. We also derive simple analytical expressions, valid in the low-energy regime, for the zero-temperature conductance through the lead and the relevant spectral densities. We find that, when the chemical potential coincides with that of the half-filled SSHC, the conductance reaches its maximum value, equal to that of the lead in the absence of the SSHC. By contrast, the conductance vanishes when the chemical potential is shifted by an amount equal to half the end-mode splitting.

authors.name: A. A. Aligia
authors.institution: Institut Català de Nanociència i Nanotecnologia

papers.title: Perfect 3-colorings of the generalized Petersen graphs GP(n,2)
papers.abstract: We enumerate the parameter matrices of all perfect 3-colorings of the generalized Petersen graphs GP(n,2), n >= 5. We show that there are only five matrices that can be the parameter matrix of such a coloring. Two of them occur if and only if 5 | n, two occur if and only if 3 | n, and the remaining one occurs if and only if 10 | n.

authors.name: Hamed Karami
authors.institution: Barcelona Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: A Crowd-Audited Atlas of Implicit Bias in LLM-Powered Agents
papers.abstract: Prior work has shown that large language models (LLMs) express implicit biases in high-publicity, one-off decision scenarios such as hiring and intelligence assessment. However, as people increasingly employ autonomous, LLM-powered AI agents that make decisions on their behalf in doing day-to-day tasks, it is of critical importance that we understand how implicit biases, based on sociodemographic assumptions, emerge across a broad milieu of workaday decision scenarios. We used the 17 domains of daily activity in the American Time Use Survey (ATUS) to generate an atlas of 506 decision scenarios in which LLMs --- endowed with personas representing different races, gender identities, and political ideologies --- expressed significant implicit bias. Next, in a crowdsourced audit, 500 participants made 8,010 binary choices about which implicitly biased decision scenarios most deserved further review. We found that participants prioritized decision scenarios that had broad relevance (e.g., about food choices), were high stakes (e.g., about health), and where all members of a simulated sociodemographic group made unanimous decisions (because it was a clear indication of stereotyping). They were less swayed by the magnitude of an observed disparity or the specific ATUS domain the decision scenario represented. When examining the rationale behind their prioritization choices, we found that participants often interpreted disparities as traits of demographic groups and judged whether those traits seemed plausible, often based on their own internalized stereotypes. We discuss implications for building personalized AI agents, digital twins, social simulations, and for using crowdsourced bias audits.

authors.name: Wesley Hanwen Deng
authors.institution: Microsoft Research New York City (United States)

papers.title: From Recursion to Convolution: Parallel Self-Improvement for Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: Multi-agent self-improvement enables agents to improve through interaction and feedback. However, sequential dependencies across agents and refinement rounds can propagate errors, increase computational costs, and limit parallelism. Moreover, refining individual features or agents in isolation can overlook their dependencies and restrict collective coordination. To address these challenges, we propose ConvRSI, a framework for parallelizing multi-agent self-improvement through convolution. ConvRSI couples intra-agent convolution, which jointly refines related agent features, with inter-agent graph convolution, which aggregates messages according to the collaboration topology. Both stages operate in latent space, enabling parallel updates without repeatedly decoding and re-encoding intermediate messages. Experiments on MATH-500 show that ConvRSI achieves 5.04% performance improvement while reducing 17.27% inference cost, and 45.11% latency compared with RecursiveMAS. It also supports diverse collaboration patterns by representing their topologies as adjacency matrices. These results demonstrate the potential of convolutional co-evolution for efficient multi-agent self-improvement. Our code and datasets are provided in https://github.com/LYA2333/ConvRSI.

authors.name: Zheng Wang
authors.institution: State Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: Slow and rapid mixing in $\mathbb{Z}_2$ hyperlattice gauge theory
papers.abstract: The Ising model under Glauber dynamics on the torus is known to exhibit a phase transition in its mixing time. The mixing is exponentially slow when $\beta >\beta_c$ and logarithmically fast when $\beta <\beta_c$. In this paper, we generalize the slow-mixing result to $\mathbb{Z}_2$ hyperlattice gauge theory when $\beta$ is large enough. This is a higher-dimensional analogue of the Ising model, with spins on $k$-cells. Specifically, on the torus of any dimension $m \ge k+2$, we prove explicit exponential lower bounds on the mixing time of Glauber dynamics when $\beta$ is sufficiently large. More precisely, we prove that the result holds for a broader class of dynamics, allowing more than one $k$-cell to change its value at each step of the algorithm. Finally, we show that there are distinct slow and rapid mixing regimes, as for sufficiently small $\beta$ the Dobrushin condition is satisfied for Glauber dynamics under the heat-bath rule, which implies logarithmic mixing.

papers.title: Formalizing Formal Semantics: The Formal Atlas
papers.abstract:
In this paper we present the Formal Atlas, a system for the study of natural language semantics using proof assistants. Our aim is to formalize semantic accounts,
  check their predictions and compare the implemented theories. To this end, we connect source records and formal developments with an interactive application, where
  researchers can inspect proofs and modify supported Rocq files. Montague's PTQ and Gallin provide our main cases, followed by dynamic and type-theoretic
  comparisons, RSA and distributional semantics. We also discuss what it takes to formalize less explicit analyses. Lastly, we consider the use of AI, both for
  assistance in developing these resources and for inference systems that can make use of them. This work extends an earlier programme in proof-assistant semantics,
  with research and teaching as complementary uses.

papers.title: Value and Policy Calibration from Execution Feedback for Socially Compatible Driving
papers.abstract: Autonomous vehicle (AV) decisions at intersections affect the delay, braking, and motion smoothness of surrounding human-driven vehicles (HDVs). Learning socially compatible behavior requires connecting imagined interaction outcomes with feedback from executed actions. We propose a world-model reinforcement learning framework combines imagined policy improvement with direct value and policy calibration from finalized interactions, balancing AV progress with HDV interaction burden. An interaction-aware latent model supports imagination, while off-policy correction and replay updates enable observed rewards and transitions to supervise both the critic and actor. Simulation experiments at an unsignalized intersection achieve a 100% success and reductions in following-HDV acceleration variation of 65.5% and 44.0% relative to PIWM and DreamerV3, respectively. Ablations identify complementary roles for value calibration in reducing HDV burden and policy calibration in improving passage efficiency. Tests under out-of-distribution traffic shifts further show lower ego jerk and HDV acceleration variation than PIWM at comparable passage times.

authors.name: Yingwei Li
authors.institution: Agency for Science, Technology and Research

papers.title: World-Model-Guided Plan Search for Cooperative Mixed-Traffic Control at Bottlenecks
papers.abstract: Cooperative speed control by connected and automated vehicles can reduce congestion at lane drop bottlenecks. However, effective coordination depends on vehicle roles and execution timing, while initial holding costs may be offset by later traffic benefits. This paper proposes an offline plan search framework that combines world model guidance with simulator verification. A traffic world model incorporating physical dynamics guides evolutionary search over vehicle roles, target speeds, holding durations, and start times. Paired SUMO simulations screen candidates for total delay reduction and limits on additional mean delay across vehicle groups. Accepted plans form a reusable library whose actions temporarily override a frozen MAPPO policy. Across 192 paired test scenarios at 60% penetration and a demand of 2,800 vehicles per hour, the searched library reduces mean total delay by 14.3% relative to MAPPO and by 3.8% relative to a handwritten plan library. The largest increase in group mean delay is 6.2 s, below the prescribed 10 s limit. In a separate screening experiment, the guided search achieves a 30.0% pass rate compared with 2.6% for random sampling. These results support the use of predictive search and independent verification for discovering cooperative plans under group delay constraints.

papers.title: Exploration of Reinforcement Learning in Generative Recommendation Models
papers.abstract:
Traditional cascaded recommender systems balance accuracy and efficiency over large item spaces, but misaligned stage-wise objectives hinder end-to-end optimization. Generative recommendation unifies these stages in an autoregressive framework, providing a natural interface for reinforcement learning (RL) to optimize the entire generation process. However, directly applying RL often leads to unstable optimization and degraded recommendation quality.
  We revisit Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) and other ratio-based objectives through a unified logit-gradient view. We identify three issues: (i) clipped surrogates create dead-gradient regions, under-utilizing samples; (ii) negative-advantage updates can become effectively unbounded as importance ratios grow, allowing a small subset of negatives to dominate optimization; and (iii) ratio-based control lacks sensitivity to absolute policy confidence, so updates on high-confidence cases may fail to vanish.
  Motivated by this diagnosis, we propose \emph{Gradient-Bounded Policy Optimization} (GBPO), a simple objective with stop-gradient normalization that is simultaneously (a) fully gradient-active, (b) sign-symmetrically bounded for both positive and negative updates, and (c) explicitly confidence-weighted under current policy probabilities. This ensures that updates gracefully vanish for $\pi\!\to\!1$ positives and $\pi\!\to\!0$ negatives. Across the evaluated settings, GBPO achieves competitive recommendation performance with more stable training than competing RL methods.

authors.name: Han Li
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: Siphon faces in slow-fast mass-action networks
papers.abstract: When the species of a siphon in a mass-action network, however many, are fast and their invariant face loses transverse stability along the slow flow, trajectories follow the face past this loss before leaving it. We study three consequences. (i) If the transverse Metzler linearisation is irreducible, the entry-exit relation with its Perron root gives the exit. Under acyclic feeding between its strongly connected components, a max-plus recursion over the reactions gives it; in general neither the Perron root nor the diagonal blocks do. (ii) With one slow species, acyclic feeding and a transversal exit, a fold of the interior critical manifold followed by a drop onto the face gives a unique, exponentially attracting relaxation oscillation whose turning points tend to the fold and exit point. Exactly $3474$ minimal planar networks of molecularity $\leq 3$, with fast per-capita rate affine and decreasing in the slow species, meet our sufficient conditions for it. (iii) A siphon-breaking reaction of rate $\delta$ and finite min-plus breaking order $w$ unfolds the transcritical point into a fold if a Perron-weighted second-order self-interaction is positive, and not if negative; the fold's critical component lies at distance of order $\delta^{w/2}$ from the face. For $\delta=e^{-\mu/^Karepsilon}$ the broken face is a floor at $-\mu$ in the recursion, and planar cycles leave it between the entry-exit and transcritical points, depending on $\mu$. Simulations confirm predicted exits and cycles, including cyclic feeding, where the prediction is conjectural, and high-precision computations confirm the folds; the errors shrink as $^Karepsilon$ or $\delta$ decreases.

authors.name: Andrei-Dan Halanay
authors.institution: Université de Pau et des Pays de l'Adour

papers.title: When Zero Is Competitive: A Descriptive Pilot of Transformer and Gate-Graph Surrogates on Random-Angle Quantum Circuits
papers.abstract: We examine supervised classical prediction of all one-qubit Z and two-qubit ZZ expectation values on noiseless, layered 4-10-qubit RX/RY/RZ-CNOT circuits. In a 63-cell stratified workload with disjoint circuit-template tests, we evaluate one transformer encoder and gate-dependency graph neural networks against literal-zero and training-derived constant predictors. On the Arm K training labels, 44.89% of scalar targets have absolute magnitude below 0.05. The held-out-template zero predictor has equal-instance mean absolute error 0.193399, and none of the evaluated transformer checkpoints or final graph-network endpoints achieves a lower score. A separate product-state positive control achieves MAE 0.007755 versus 0.514811 for zero, but does not explain the failure on the entangled workload. The difference between zero and a training-fitted mean constant under training MSE is only 0.14%, a descriptive point estimate without uncertainty analysis. The transformer's 815,233-parameter source identity is locally verified; detailed packed-input semantics have not been independently audited. These results constitute a descriptive pilot, not a causal explanation, formal equivalence test, or impossibility claim. Comparable circuits can be regenerated from the workload specification, but exact frozen datasets and model-run evidence remain private.

papers.title: DoF-Query Transformer for Adaptive Fusion of Egocentric Vision and Forearm HD-sEMG in Continuous Hand Kinematics
papers.abstract: Continuous and accurate estimation of human hand kinematics is important not only for intuitive human-machine interaction, but also for capturing fine-grained human manipulation demonstrations that can provide action supervision for embodied-intelligence datasets and dexterous robot learning. However, individual sensing modalities may be insufficient for reliable estimation under varying operating conditions. We present a finger-unencumbered multimodal framework for continuous regression of 20 hand joint angles from egocentric RGB images and 128-channel forearm high-density surface electromyography (HD-sEMG). The framework combines a Vision Transformer-based visual encoder, a Transformer-based EMG encoder, and a degree of freedom (DoF) query Transformer fusion decoder. To account for the varying informativeness of visual and EMG cues across joint DoFs and input conditions, the decoder assigns a separate learnable query to each DoF, enabling DoF-specific and context-adaptive fusion of the two modalities. The framework was evaluated on synchronized multimodal data from 10 participants. Averaged across participants, the proposed fusion model achieved a mean coefficient of determination ($R^2$) of $0.88$ and a mean absolute error (MAE) of $2.80^\circ$, compared with $0.82$ and $3.21^\circ$ for the vision-only model and $0.68$ and $5.13^\circ$ for the EMG-only model. It also outperformed the evaluated representative unimodal baselines and alternative fusion designs. DoF-wise analyses showed larger fusion gains for visually ambiguous joints and viewing conditions, while synthetic visual occlusion demonstrated greater robustness than vision-only estimation. These results highlight the complementary value of egocentric vision and forearm HD-sEMG for capturing fine-grained human hand kinematics, with potential applications in human demonstration acquisition and dexterous robot learning.

authors.institution: Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics

authors.institution: Chongqing College of International Business and Economics

papers.title: Ca II IRT activity indices from $Gaia$ spectroscopy: a baseline method for photospheric contribution estimates
papers.abstract: The $Gaia$ high-resolution spectroscopic observations using Radial Velocity Spectrometer offers a unique opportunity to study stellar Ca II infrared triplet (IRT) activity. A key step in estimating activity indices is subtracting the photospheric contribution. The canonical template-based method often fails because, for many stars, the observed line cores are deeper than the model predictions, which prevents valid activity measurements. In this work, we explore an alternative approach that constructs a baseline from less active stars as a function of effective temperature (and metallicity) to represent the photospheric contribution. Our results show that, for dwarf stars, compared with the canonical method, the baseline method not only yields far more objects with valid activity measurements, but also avoids many extremely low and unreliable values (e.g., log$R'_{\rm IRT} \lesssim -6$). The Ca II IRT activity indices derived from the baseline method correlate well with other activity proxies, confirming their reliability as activity indicators. Furthermore, they show a relation with stellar rotation, not only recovering the typical rotation--activity relation, but also revealing fine structures that may be associated with different regimes in gyrochronology. Our findings suggest that the baseline method can serve as a robust alternative for deriving accurate activity estimates, and will be particularly useful for obtaining activity indices for tens of millions of stars with the upcoming $Gaia$ Data Release 4.

papers.title: GRAZE: Text-Free Grasp Synthesis for Unseen Objects from Human Gaze
papers.abstract: Text-conditioned hand-object interaction (HOI) generation provides intuitive semantic control, but language is an indirect way to specify where an interaction should occur on an object. Naming the part to grasp requires object-specific words, and naming the approach side requires a reference frame that a prompt lacks. We propose GRAZE (GRAsp from gaZE), which generates hand-object grasp motion from recorded gaze instead of object and part names. Its Geometry-Aware Gaze Encoding (GeoGaze) maps gaze rays to cues on object geometry, and cross-attention conditions a diffusion Transformer on these cues. We also introduce HOT3D-Grasp, a grasp-centered benchmark with object-disjoint folds built on HOT3D recordings. On unseen objects, GRAZE grasps the target part more often than the strongest text-conditioned baseline (49.3% vs. 43.6%), achieves the highest grasp success (66.3% vs. 46.6%), and transfers without fine-tuning to GazeHOI (45.3% vs. 33.8%). Gaze conveys the approach side: when gaze is rotated around the object, the approach turns with it in 59.1% of cases, against 20.5% for a text model retrained with clock words. On the same backbone, a text prompt names parts better, but gaze adds the approach side. Given both, GRAZE keeps the prompt's part accuracy and follows gaze.

papers.title: ShiftGuard: Evaluating Confidence and Feature Distance for Risk-Controlled Image Classification
papers.abstract: A classifier that is usually right still makes confident mistakes, and a deployed system needs some way to decide when to answer and when to abstain. Cheap post-hoc scores such as maximum softmax probability (MSP) and predictive entropy are the standard answer. Distances in feature space are a popular alternative, and fusing several signals into one score is a natural next step. We ask whether adding a feature distance signal to MSP and entropy improves error detection, and whether it increases the share of predictions that can be accepted at a certified error rate when only a small labelled calibration set is available. We train a CIFAR-adapted ResNet-18 from scratch on CIFAR-10 (92.92% test accuracy, one seed) and compare five reliability scores: MSP, entropy, distance to the predicted-class centroid, a logistic fusion of MSP and entropy, and a logistic fusion of all three signals. Acceptance thresholds are chosen on a held out calibration set with Clopper Pearson upper bounds, Bonferroni corrected over a prespecified family of 315 rules at 95% simultaneous confidence. Confidence based scores were best. Error AUROC was 0.9230 for MSP, 0.9233 for entropy and 0.9235 for MSP plus entropy, against 0.8814 for the three signal fusion and 0.8224 for distance alone. At a 5% risk target with 1,000 calibration images, entropy accepted 84.82% of test images with 2.05% observed error, while three signal fusion accepted 80.61% with 2.21%. With 250 calibration images, neither distance nor the three-signal fusion could certify the 5% target at all. The results come from one seed, one dataset and one architecture, with no corruption experiments, so they say nothing about distribution shift detection. Within these limits, the distance signal did not earn its added complexity.

papers.title: Ensemble Bounds for Pairwise Dissimilar Decomposition of Deterministic Datasets
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study reduced similarity decompositions of \emph{deterministic} datasets using redundancy graphs and obtain \emph{ensemble} bounds for the minimum size of such constrained decomposition. We consider batch decompositions that reduce similarity \emph{across} batches and use the Lov\'asz local lemma to obtain bounds for the minimum size of a decomposition with a given pairwise dissimilarity. We then consider unique batch decomposition with a given relaxation parameter and obtain upper and lower ensemble bounds for the minimum size. Throughout, we use Binomial random graphs to obtain the desired ensemble bounds, by conditioning on the number of similar \emph{pairs} of data points.

papers.title: MARLIN: Multiscale And Directional Sparse Representation Learning for Imbalanced SAR Ship Classification
papers.abstract: Despite recent progress in SAR maritime monitoring, ship classification remains challenging due to limited labeled data, class imbalance, large intra-class variability, fine-grained inter-class similarity, and variations in target scale, orientation, and backscattering structure. To address these challenges, this paper proposes MARLIN, a class-frequency-aware framework with directional sparse and hierarchical multi-scale feature extraction for ship type classification in SAR images. The proposed architecture first constructs two complementary representations of each input image, where each views are processed by parallel encoder branches. Each branch begins with a directional sparse convolutional stem designed to capture elongated and orientation-dependent ship scattering patterns, followed by customized hierarchical multiscale feature extraction blocks. To improve learning under imbalanced class distributions, we introduce a class-frequency aware objective. The proposed objective combines margin-based classification with class-frequency-weighted prototype compactness and class-pair frequency weighted margin separation. This formulation shapes the embedding space by encouraging samples from the same class to form compact clusters while enforcing stronger separation for class pairs involving underrepresented ship categories. Extensive experiments on three complementary datasets demonstrate that in addition to being lightweight and parameter efficient, MARLIN improves both overall accuracy and class-balanced metrics, confirming its effectiveness for robust SAR ship-type classification under limited and imbalanced training conditions. The codes are available at github.com/benyaminhosseiny/marlin.

papers.title: Microfitting: Continual Learning via Cached Test-Time Training
papers.abstract: Continual learning is a promising approach to specialize language models to an organization's private data. However, current methods exhibit a number of drawbacks including catastrophic forgetting, where new training updates overwrite prior knowledge. We present microfitting, which trains and caches a small adapter for each document. Each adapter is trained once, offline, on synthetic questions targeted at demonstrated base-model shortcomings and reused whenever that document is queried. This method borrows from test-time learning literature and sidesteps the problem of continual learning through parameter isolation, allowing the system to specialize on new data without overwriting prior knowledge. The process that generates adapter training data also improves over time, revising its recipe from previous outcomes and fresh examples of the target workload. On DeepSeek V4 Flash, microfitting substantially improves accuracy over the base model. In Enterprise Document Operations (EDO), an open-book Q&A environment over real-world enterprise documents, our method achieves a 38.2% relative improvement over base-model performance. Microfitting makes continual specialization practical and cost-efficient: a frozen model can adapt to an evolving private corpus overnight on local hardware, without modifying the base model or previously cached adapters.

papers.title: TacBridge: Learning Unified Tactile Representations through Cross-Sensor Correspondence
papers.abstract: Optical tactile sensors record tactile videos that capture local deformation and its temporal evolution during contact, supporting robot manipulation, force estimation, and tactile representation learning. Differences in imaging geometry, background appearance, illumination, resolution, and deformation response lead to sensor-dependent observations of the same contact across GelSight, DIGIT, GelSlim, TacTip, and other optical tactile sensors. This variability limits representation transfer and the joint use of multi-sensor data. We introduce TacBridge, a framework for learning unified representations from multi-sensor tactile videos through cross-sensor correspondence. Specifically, multi-sensor masked tactile-video pre-training learns spatiotemporal representations across sensors. We then train the same masked model jointly on same-sensor and cross-sensor reconstruction, using paired source and target videos of matched contact events. Experiments on cross-sensor translation and downstream perception demonstrate the cross-sensor generalization and task transferability of the learned tactile representations.

papers.title: Incentive Alignment for Electricity Data Assets in China: A Blockchain-Enabled Contribution-Credit Framework
papers.abstract: Modern electricity markets increasingly rely on reported operational contributions to allocate incentives, recognise cooperation, and coordinate activities across multiple organisations. However, supporting evidence for many reported contributions becomes available only after subsequent metering, dispatch, settlement, or auditing processes, making it difficult to reward genuine contributions while discouraging strategic over-reporting. Existing approaches largely address data sharing, performance verification, blockchain record management, or incentive allocation in isolation, providing limited support for integrating delayed evidence into a unified incentive mechanism. This paper proposes a blockchain-enabled contribution-credit framework for truthful reporting under delayed evidence. The framework links authenticated evidence to contribution recognition through dynamic credit updating, escrow, report-linked penalties, and automated incentive execution. Developed using the Chinese electricity market as the primary setting, it is demonstrated through two representative coordination scenarios, with adaptations illustrating its applicability to UK and US electricity-market structures. A controlled heterogeneous-agent simulation evaluates the behavioural effects of the proposed mechanism, while security analysis, public-data workflow analysis, and blockchain implementation experiments assess its practical feasibility. The results show that integrating delayed evidence with dynamic credit, escrow, and report-linked penalties promotes truthful reporting while providing a transparent and auditable process for translating verified operational contributions into incentive allocation. The proposed framework offers a practical mechanism for improving accountability, coordination, and incentive compatibility in collaborative electricity markets.

authors.name: Jiazheng Zhang
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Beijing

papers.title: Complex Moments of the Derivative of the Riemann Zeta Function
papers.abstract: We investigate the complex moments of the derivative of the Riemann zeta function through a random Euler product model. For each fixed $\sigma>1/2$ and every $s\in\mathbb{C}$ with $\operatorname{Re}(s)>0$, we show, under the Lindel\"of hypothesis, that the $2s$-th moment of $|\zeta'(\sigma+\mathrm{i}t)|$ over $t\in[1,T]$ converges, as $T\to\infty$, to the corresponding moment of the derivative of the random Euler product. We then establish, unconditionally, an asymptotic formula for the latter moment as $\sigma\downarrow 1/2$ throughout the half-plane $\operatorname{Re}(s)>0$. For positive real moments, our approach is based on a change-of-measure argument and a Gaussian limit theorem for the logarithmic derivative under a tilted probability measure. For general complex moments, we combine Fourier analysis of weighted complex measures with regularized Riesz distributions. As an application, under the Lindel\"of hypothesis, we resolve the conjecture of Simm and Wei [J. Lond. Math. Soc. 113 (2026)] on the complex moments of the derivative of the Riemann zeta function for every $s\in\mathbb C$ with $\operatorname{Re}(s)>0$. We establish the predicted asymptotic formula as $\sigma\downarrow1/2$, with the leading order $s^2+2s$ and an explicit leading coefficient involving an arithmetic factor and the confluent hypergeometric function of the first kind. The conjecture also holds unconditionally when $\operatorname{Re}(s)\in (0,2)$.

papers.title: Harish-Chandra Modules for the Lie algebra of Divergence-Free Vector Fields on a Two-Dimensional Torus
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal S_2$ be the Lie algebra of divergence-free Laurent polynomial vector fields on a two-dimensional torus. We determine its simple weight modules with uniformly bounded weight multiplicities. As a consequence, we obtain a classification of its simple Harish-Chandra modules, i.e., weight modules with finite-dimensional weight spaces, which are either simple generalized highest weight modules or simple quotients of tensor fields modules.

authors.name: Yufeng Yao
authors.institution: University of the West of England

papers.title: On p-adic modularity of abelian threefolds with imaginary multiplication and rational p-isogeny
papers.abstract: We prove $p$-adic modularity of a certain class of abelian threefolds over $\mathbf{Q}$ (with imaginary multiplication and rational $p$-isogeny), including the Jacobians of some genus 3 curves known as Picard curves. More precisely, we study a deformation problem for residual 3-dimensional totally reducible Galois pseudorepresentations over an imaginary quadratic field which are ordinary at primes over $p$ and conjugate self-dual. We show that under certain conditions the universal pseudodeformation ring in any weight (including the non-classical low weight corresponding to an abelian threefold) is isomorphic to a specialization of the ordinary Hida Hecke algebra on $U(2,1)$. The conditions that we assume are essentially class group conditions as well as weak regularity of the Hecke algebras in sufficiently high classical weights.

papers.title: Corporate Stances on Societal Issues in the US
papers.abstract: When do firms take public positions on divisive societal issues and why? We assemble a comprehensive dataset on corporate stance-taking in the United States, using large language models to read 52,000 news articles and press releases about 836 companies that belonged to the S&P 500 at any point between 2008 and 2025. We identify 9,917 stances on nine partisan issues such as climate change, abortion, and racial discrimination. We show that stance-taking increased fourfold after 2008 and peaked in 2021. It is overwhelmingly liberal and concentrated among the largest firms. A quarter of stances give no explicit business justification. Stance-taking is only weakly related to lobbying and campaign contributions and, unlike them, does not follow the electoral cycle. Instead, firms tend to speak when media coverage and public interest in an issue peak. Together, these findings suggest that stance-taking can be understood as a contribution to broad policy debates rather than a strategy to shape policies that affect firms' core business. Finally, we investigate whose views corporate stances represent. Consumer-facing firms take more stances, and firms whose consumers lean Democratic take more liberal stances on issues other than climate. Companies with larger shares of Democratic employees, executives, and board members also take more liberal stances. Exploiting within-firm variation, we find that having more Democrats among a company's leadership increases liberal stance-taking, while having more women increases stance-taking on gender-related issues and abortion.

authors.name: Andrew Hall
authors.institution: Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation

papers.title: Budgeted Decision-Model-Guided Joint-Action Search for Satellite Edge Computing
papers.abstract: Efficient task offloading in satellite edge computing requires coordinated allocation of communication and computing resources. Search methods based on large language models (LLMs) have been shown to generate high-quality resource allocations, but the latency of individual model requests and repeated model interactions can lead to substantial solver overhead. We propose budgeted joint-action search (BJAS), an integrated decision-model-guided solver that jointly optimizes satellite offloading and power allocation to minimize average task-completion latency under explicit search budgets. Its bounded candidate pools combine single-terminal updates with power-inheriting offload replacements for batched selection, retaining two-terminal coordination without enumerating additional power vectors. Across 60 completed runs per method under the workflows' respective configurations, BJAS reduces mean total solver time by 97.16% relative to LLM-generated offloading while achieving a mean task-completion latency close to that of the LLM baseline. BJAS also achieves lower mean task-completion latency than the tested genetic algorithm and deep deterministic policy gradient baselines.

papers.title: EdgeNet City: Context-Aware AI-RAN Planning toward Autonomous Urban Connectivity
papers.abstract: The evolution from 5G toward 6G calls for more anticipatory and context-aware Cell-on-Wheels (COW) planning in wireless networks. We present EdgeNet City, an online framework that grounds free-form natural-language inputs in geographic activity representations and path-gain data. A catalog-referenced representation links activity roles, geographic features and predefined demand profiles, separating semantic selection from deterministic spatial computation. The algorithm combines prescribed demand with relative propagation support to screen service areas for subsequent COW assessment. We publicly release a London dataset with 22,678 transmitters, approximately 449.4 billion path-gain records and retained receiver geometry. Within prepared propagation domains, the online prototype reuses these records without new ray tracing or live operator measurements. In a matched 20-event study across six London environments, the expanded representation increases mean spatial overlap with the reused full technical-review reference from 0.4929 for the single-feature Venue-only baseline to 0.7203. Rule-based and language-model planners select identical activities in this panel. With need-aware ranking and a three-cell diagnostic budget fixed, the expanded representation increases mean Reference-need Capture by 25.44 percentage points over Venue-only.

authors.name: Qixing Deng
authors.institution: Guangxi Vocational College of Water Resources and Electric Power

papers.title: Feasibility certificates for DeePC: A set invariance approach
papers.abstract: DeePC is posed on a window of past inputs and outputs, so its feasible set is a set of histories and is not available in closed form. We write the DeePC solution as an implicit ReLU network whose weights are built from Hankel matrices and whose activation patterns are the critical regions of the underlying quadratic program. This gives, directly from the Hankel matrices, the feasible set of DeePC as a polyhedral projection, its explicit piecewise-affine control law, and an exact linear model of the history window. We compute three invariant sets of histories: the maximal positively invariant set of the unsaturated linear branch, the region of recursive feasibility of DeePC without terminal ingredients, and the maximal control invariant set of admissible histories. We show these sets are nested and provide numerical examples.

papers.title: The Bipartible Architecture Pattern: Transparently Directing HTTP Requests over InfiniBand
papers.abstract:
Large-scale compute (HPC) systems with coherent-memory workloads often deploy InfiniBand (IB) networks for high-bandwidth and low-latency inter-node and storage communication. A separate TCP network is typically used for control-plane and general-purpose communication. The last decade has seen the rise of cloud-native software patterns. These patterns are characterized by container-based software distribution and inter-node and storage communication over TCP/IP. In an unoptimized HPC environment, a cloud-native workload will typically use HTTP for some or all communication.
  This paper introduces the Bipartible architecture pattern to optimize cloud-native workload traffic in HPC environments. This paper focuses on optimizing HTTP storage service requests. These requests are transparently transformed onto IB traffic without modifying workload implementation or network configuration. This is achieved by 'cloning' a global HTTP service (BPService) onto the HPC cluster compute host(s) where the workload executes at scale. Provided the global persistent storage is on the IB network the HTTP service requests are returned to the workload via IB and not TCP/IP.
  The feasibility of this pattern is demonstrated by implementing a prototype BPService for S3 and a Hybrid-BPService (service metadata is accessed over TCP, bulk data over IB) for a software repository service. We offer this pattern in addition to many alternative approaches to address the performance challenges of executing workloads written to cloud-native design patterns in HPC environments. Finally, while the initial results are encuraging signficant validation of any service must be performed under both read and write scenarios before deployment into production is planned.

papers.title: Ultra-CAN: A Lightweight Blind ISAC Receiver for Chaos-Based Telemetry and Local-Seed Ranging in the Internet of Drones
papers.abstract: The Internet of Drones (IoD) needs secure telemetry and proximity sensing within the SWaP-C constraints. We show that a single blind neural receiver driven by one chaos-based waveform performs both functions without a separate radar transceiver. In telemetry mode it decodes a peer's burst blindly; in radar mode it regenerates the per-burst chaotic reference locally and ranges the echoes of its own transmission. Ultra-CAN pairs a shared $64$-dimensional representation with two ultra-light backbones, an attention-pooled Conv1D network and a multi-head QKV network ($27.6$k--$44.2$k parameters), feeding communication and sensing heads. Both ship as int8 TensorFlow Lite Micro firmware; the Conv1D receiver decides a burst in $16.9$ ms on a $240$ MHz microcontroller with $24.2$ KiB of activations, a measured energy of $2.2$-$3.4$ mJ per burst, and float-equivalent decisions, sustaining up to $59$ bit/s of telemetry or a $7.4$ Hz range track. The two variants rank first and second among learned demodulators in four aerial swarm scenarios, with a pooled BER down to $4.6 \times 10^{-4}$ on the single-echo link ($2.4 \times 10^{-3}$ with three echoes). Its sensing head identifies true obstacles in $66.8\%$ of peer-laden bursts (vs $42\%$ matched filtering, $44\%$ OFDM-ISAC, $48\%$ peak-picker ceiling). A peer-exclusion gate cuts peer reports from $4.4\%$ to $0.02\%$ of answered bursts, answering $23.5\%$ of total bursts ($75\%$ on the exact tap) with $0.70$ m/s velocity tracking. In-domain refitting recovers telemetry BER by up to three orders of magnitude under 3GPP channels, jamming-aware training restores the link, and frequency agility adds a $6$--$9$ dB margin against partial-band jamming.

papers.title: A new approach to Tur\'{a}n inequalities for classical orthogonal polynomials
papers.abstract: Let $f,g\in C^{2}\left( a,b\right) .$ In this paper we investigate properties of the function% \[ v_{g}\left( f\right) \left( x\right) =-\frac{f^{2}\left( x\right) }{g\left( x\right) }\frac{d}{dx}\frac{g\left( x\right) f^{\prime}\left( x\right) }{f\left( x\right) }% \] where $f:\left( a,b\right) \rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ is a solution of the second order differential equation $f^{\prime\prime}+pf^{\prime}+qf=0.$ Criteria for the monotonicity of $v_{g}\left( f\right) $ are given which depend on the coefficients $p$ and $q$. It is shown that for classical orthogonal polynomials $p_{n}\left( x\right) $ the Tur\'{a}n inequalities are equivalent to the non-negativity of the functions $v_{g}\left( p_{n}\right) $ for a suitable function $g.$ This allows new and simple proofs of classical and recent Tur\'{a}n inequalities.

papers.title: Linearization and local controllability of nonautonomous differential inclusions
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the linearization of nonautonomous differential inclusions, whose right-hand side is integrably Lipschitz in the state variable and measurable in time. We establish measurability results for time-dependent graphs and identify the Clarke tangent cone to the set of their measurable selections in $L^\infty\times L^1$. Combining this characterization with a subtransversality argument, we obtain a lower estimate for the Clarke tangent cone to the set of all admissible trajectories starting from a fixed set. As an application, we give sufficient conditions for local controllability around a closed terminal set.

papers.title: A compact non-K\"ahler shrinking Ricci soliton
papers.abstract: We construct a gradient shrinking Ricci soliton on the simply-connected eight-manifold $\mathsf{SU}(3)\times_{\mathsf T^2}\mathbb{CP}^1$. This Riemannian manifold is not Einstein, is nowhere locally K\"ahler, is locally irreducible, and is invariant under the effective cohomogeneity one action of $\mathsf{PSU}(3)\times S^1$. This new gradient Ricci soliton is found by first constructing an approximate solution, certifying the residual, and applying a fixed-point theorem.

papers.title: InvarOrd: Self-Supervised Ordinal Knowledge Distillation with Rank-Invariant Alignment for Label-Efficient Cross-Species Hyperspectral Fish Freshness Assessment
papers.abstract: Hyperspectral models of fish freshness rarely transfer between species, and labelling a new species is slow and destructive. Freshness is also ordinal, and standard domain alignment can erase that order. We present InvarOrd, which adapts to a new species from 30 labelled cubes (5 per rank) in three stages: self-supervised spectral pretraining on unlabelled source cubes, cross-species alignment by a shrinkage covariance discrepancy computed only within matched ranks, and ordinal distillation into a compact student. The alignment term is provably invariant to the rank means, so it gives no incentive to collapse the ordinal axis. On paired salmon and cod data (800 cubes each, 16 days), a source-trained teacher reaches 1.6 to 1.9 days mean absolute error (MAE) on the other species, with quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) below zero. The 423K-parameter student, 2.54 times smaller than its teacher, attains the lowest MAE (1.476 days) and highest within 1-day accuracy (56.1%) among 14 configurations, matching the best of six ImageNet-pretrained backbones (ConvNeXt-T, 1.503 days) at 66 times fewer parameters, 1.44ms per cube on a GPU and 5s re-adaptation. InvarOrd beats target-only training by 0.29 days (p = 0.031). Among alignment objectives, rank-invariant alignment retains the most ordinal structure (embedding rank correlation 0.183, QWK 0.112), whereas global discrepancy lowers the rank correlation to 0.049 and QWK to zero at only 0.014 days higher MAE.

papers.title: Simplify, Agree, Distill: Label-Free Self-Distillation with Stepping Stones
papers.abstract: Can a language model teach itself to reason without labels? On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) uses the model as its own teacher, but strengthens that teacher with a ground-truth solution. The natural label-free substitute, voting over the model's attempts, fails precisely on hard problems: attempts disagree, and their most common answer is often wrong. We propose STONE, a label-free alternative that moves agreement to easier related problems. The model writes these stepping stones, keeps those it solves consistently, and shows the teacher their worked solutions, with final answers removed; the student sees only the original problem. No step reads a label, and inference needs no extra context or model calls. Across five math benchmarks, the proposed method achieves the highest average accuracy for Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B in thinking mode. Without thinking mode, it gains 13.2 and 22.7 points, 2.5 and 2.7 times the gains of OPSD with ground-truth solutions.

authors.name: Xinyang Shen
authors.institution: Hunan University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: PRISM: Primitive-Integrated Separable Modulation with Priority Visual Memory Queue for Compositional Zero-Shot Learning
papers.abstract: Compositional Zero-Shot Learning (CZSL) recognizes unseen attribute--object pairs by recombining primitives from seen compositions. Existing methods stop sharing evidence at deployment: fixed prototypes cannot exploit unlabeled test streams, while composition-wise refinement cannot propagate corrections across pairs sharing a primitive. We introduce PRISM, an online CZSL framework that extends primitive sharing to test-time adaptation. Its Hierarchical Knowledge Accumulation Module (HiKAM) factorizes prototype migration into composition-, attribute-, and object-level residual banks. A Priority Visual Memory Queue (PVMQ), initialized by Prototype Queue Initialization (PQI), grounds text updates with bounded visual evidence. The same adaptive core supports exhaustive Full PRISM and recall-calibrated Adaptive PRISM-Lite, which selects candidate budgets from held-out ranks. Comprehensive closed- and open-world experiments on UT-Zappos, MIT-States, and C-GQA demonstrate the state of the art, with Full PRISM achieving the best open-world AUC and harmonic mean on all three benchmarks and the best closed-world results on UT-Zappos and C-GQA. Fine-grained long-tail and non-stationary primitive-block evaluations reveal gains on under-supported concepts and stable adaptation under prolonged skew. Adaptive PRISM-Lite further delivers substantial efficiency gains in the full open-world space with only a small accuracy cost. PRISM thus combines primitive-shared online adaptation, multimodal grounding, and candidate-aware inference.

papers.title: Scintillator-Based Event-Mode Neutron Imaging with Timepix4 Readout
papers.abstract: Scintillator-based event-mode neutron imaging is emerging as a powerful approach to neutron radiography. Unlike conventional integrating-mode neutron imaging, which accumulates scintillation light during an exposure, event reconstruction estimates neutron-event positions and arrival times from time-stamped optical responses. We investigated this approach using a self-developed Timepix4-based optical readout system, image-formation analysis, and beam experiments at the China Spallation Neutron Source under different scintillator and optical configurations. The analysis explains how event localization can reduce image blur associated with the spatial extent of individual scintillation responses. Under the same 0.35$\times$ optical configuration, event reconstruction improved the spatial resolution from 164.2 to 91.9 $\mu$m at 10% modulation transfer function (MTF), while a 2.1$\times$ configuration with a $\mathrm{Gd_2O_2S:Tb}$ scintillator achieved 26.1 $\mu$m at the same MTF threshold. Following event reconstruction and rejection of single-photon reconstructed events, the mean peak-normalized spectral response in the 6-8 angstrom out-of-band interval decreased by 85.4% relative to the raw-pixel wavelength-count spectrum, indicating reduced afterglow-related spectral background. Under the tested pulsed-beam conditions, the maximum instantaneous pixel-hit rate per pixel was approximately four times its time-averaged value, providing an experimental basis for assessing readout requirements at higher neutron flux. Conventional radiography resolved structural details, while energy-selective imaging enhanced the contrast between materials with similar broadband transmission and Bragg-edge imaging revealed crystallographic features in steel. These results demonstrate the imaging-quality benefits and capabilities of scintillator-based event-mode neutron imaging.
