papers.title: Synapse: Optimizing Natural-Language Agent Skills through Program Repair
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can improve task performance by optimizing reusable natural-language skills without updating model parameters. Execution feedback reveals failures but does not directly identify which instructions to edit, which related instructions matter, or which tasks an edit may break. We propose Synapse, which casts skill optimization as generate-and-validate repair over a partial program view. A deterministic compiler translates recognized skill constructs into SkIR, a source-linked intermediate representation, while retaining other requirements in the text. Synapse combines execution traces with control-flow and dependence relations to localize faults, propose typed mutations, and select related repair tests, including previously passing ones. Each mutation is written back to its mapped source span and recompiled; validation determines acceptance. Every accepted patch yields a well-formed skill and preserves untargeted instruction spans. Under a one-hop-local execution assumption, selected tests include every test an edit can affect. On DocVQA and LiveMath with three execution models, Synapse improves task success rates over SkillOpt by 3.74-4.54 and 2.40-4.00 percentage points, respectively, and outperforms Trace2Skill and SkillBoost in all six settings. Replacing SkIR-based repair and its test screening with constrained text editing screened only on failing tests lowers DocVQA success rates by 2.40 and 2.67 percentage points for two models. In two recorded repair runs, structural relations add tests for 23 of 37 patches; in one repair, a test added through a control-flow relation exposes a regression missed by coverage of the edited instruction.

authors.name: Chenxi Zhang
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: TopSDF: Topological Signed Distance Field for High-Quality Triangle Mesh Extraction from 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.abstract: Recent advances in 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) have demonstrated its effectiveness for photorealistic novel view synthesis. However, extracting clean, watertight, explicit surface meshes from 3DGS remains a critical challenge. Previous methods approximate geometry via discrete Marching Tetrahedra, where each grid vertex is assigned a single scalar signed distance value. At complex geometric boundaries and thin structures, this suboptimal parameterization forces severe compromises across shared vertices, causing gradient collisions and geometric frustration. Furthermore, existing optimization objectives neglect element shape conditioning, producing degenerate triangles. We introduce TopSDF, a framework that models the signed distance state as a multivariate Gaussian random field. By learning latent topological covariances across tetrahedral vertices, our formulation expands local degrees of freedom for SDF estimates, allowing the candidate mesh vertices to be placed flexibly along the bipolar edges in the tetrahedra as driven by such topological correlation. Concurrently, we directly integrate variational meshing energies into the joint optimization, coupled with an energy-driven Gaussian densification strategy to improve triangle mesh quality. Our experiments across Mip-NeRF 360, Tanks & Temples, and ScanNet++ show that TopSDF achieves state-of-the-art mesh-based novel view rendering (+0.86 dB PSNR on Mip-NeRF 360) and triangle-mesh quality (from 0.37 to 0.49 aspect ratio).

papers.title: Skill Transfer: Adapting Agent Skills from Strong to Weak Agents
papers.abstract: Agent skills are modular bundles of instructions, code, and resources that an agent loads on demand, increasingly authored and validated on frontier models and shared as an open standard. The same skill behaves differently across models: a strong model turns it into a large performance gain, while a weak model realizes little of that gain and sometimes does worse than with no skill at all. Cost and resource constraints, however, often restrict real deployments to exactly these weaker agents. We hypothesize that the strong model silently supplies procedural steps the skill leaves implicit, which the weak model omits, and formalize closing this gap as \emph{Skill Transfer}: holding the skill's capability ceiling and the model's parameters fixed, we adapt the skill so a specific weak agent can execute it well. Our method abstracts strong and weak trajectories into typed execution structures, localizes their structural divergence with a graph edit distance (GED), and repairs the skill through an iterative diagnoser-patcher loop. Across three benchmarks and two model families, Skill Transfer raises pass rate over the unmodified skill significantly and well over other skill-evolution baselines. The adapted skill also improves the strong agent it was never adapted for, and transfers out of distribution to a structurally related, unseen task. Code is available at https://github.com/Yifan-Lan/Skill-Transfer

authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: On the numerical representation of atmospheric Lamb waves in dynamical cores
papers.abstract: Atmospheric Lamb waves are horizontally propagating acoustic waves that are supported by hydrostatic and nonhydrostatic compressible equation sets. They are classically defined in an isothermal atmosphere and generate no vertical velocity. In a dynamical core, the numerical representation of the Lamb wave is sensitive to modelling choices, such as the upper boundary condition and spatial discretisation. To evaluate the numerical Lamb wave in dynamical cores, we present a new idealised test case that contains a localised pressure perturbation to primarily excite the Lamb wave mode, in a nonrotating, isothermal atmosphere at rest. Lamb waves are identified through their phase speed and the vertical structure of their zonal velocity in three dynamical cores: Spectral Element (SE), Finite-Volume Cubed-Sphere (FV3), and Model for Prediction Across Scales (MPAS), which are available in the Community Atmosphere Model (CAM). Consistent with vertical structure equation theory, the pressure-based coordinate models with an isobaric lid (SE, FV3) generate reduced Lamb wave speeds with low model tops; we show speed reductions of around 25% for a 10 km model top and an isothermal initial temperature of 275 K. For a rigid lid upper boundary condition, such as for the height coordinate MPAS model, the Lamb wave speed is virtually independent of the model top height. Wave amplitudes differ substantially among the tested configurations, with SE producing the largest amplitudes. MPAS' time-adjusted acoustic filter strongly attenuates and broadens the Lamb wave signal, whilst the amplitude and propagation speed are sensitive to the dynamics time step in FV3. Zonal wavenumber-frequency spectra reveal how well the numerical dispersion relations of Lamb and gravity waves follow the theoretical relations, and show element-order-dependent behaviour in SE consistent with linear dispersion theory.

papers.title: Exact mobility edges in high-dimensional quasiperiodic networks
papers.abstract: Inspired by the one-dimensional hidden self-duality [Phys. Rev. Lett. 134, 246301 (2025)], we establish a generalized theoretical framework for a specific class of high-dimensional quasiperiodic network models. Specifically, as long as the periodic network acts as bond-decorating links and the quasiperiodic potentials are spatially separable, the system can be mapped onto an effective high-dimensional generalized Aubry-Andr\'e equation by integrating out the periodic sites. This mapping restores the hidden self-duality symmetry in these complex models, thereby yielding exact mobility edges. Taking two-dimensional and three-dimensional models as examples, we demonstrate the consistency between the theoretical prediction and the numerical results. This paper establishes a clear paradigm for mapping high-dimensional quasiperiodic networks to high-dimensional Aubry-Andr\'e models, providing a systematic pathway for the construction and exploration of the exact mobility edge in high-dimensional systems.

papers.title: Critical corner angles and defect exchange in confined nematics with splay-bend anisotropy
papers.abstract: In confined nematics, the director turning imposed by the walls is absorbed by defects, and we show that the corners exchange these defects with the liquid. A tangentially anchored corner of opening angle $\omega$ takes one of several types, labelled by the number $m$ of half-turns of the director relative to the radius; neighbouring types differ by a bound defect of index $\pm\frac12$, and logarithmic energies decide when the corner sheds or absorbs it. For equal elastic constants the critical angles are $72^\circ$, $120^\circ$, $216^\circ$ and $360^\circ$, with windows of bistability between them, explaining the hidden defect near $72^\circ$ vertices and selecting the equilibria of polygons and discs. We introduce unequal splay and bend constants through the cubic invariant $Q_{lk}\,\partial_lQ_{ij}\,\partial_kQ_{ij}$ in reduced Landau--de Gennes theory; bounding the order by its bulk value makes the problem well posed, without further elastic terms, whenever both Frank constants are positive. At first order only the splay corner feels the anisotropy; other corner and defect energies are even in it and follow exactly by quadrature. The anisotropy moves the angle above which a splay corner sheds a $+\frac12$ defect from $104^\circ$ to $136^\circ$ as $K_3/K_1$ rises from $0.54$ to $1.86$, and so predicts which polygons prefer splay corners and which interior defects. Finite-element computations for polygons of three to eight sides and the disc confirm this: the exchange occurs within the predicted range by migration of $+\frac12$ defects into the corners, near which states with zero, one and two splay corners are nearly degenerate.

papers.title: Conditional Optimal Transport and Triangular Maps for Imitation Learning
papers.abstract: We introduce a unified formulation of imitation learning from demonstrations as a conditional sampling problem solved by triangular transport: a policy is the second block of a triangular map that transports a reference distribution to the conditional distribution of the action chunk given the observation history. Unlike in Diffusion Policy, where it is a fixed Gaussian, the reference becomes a design variable; we take it to be the empirical distribution of the demonstrated action chunks and introduce three instances of the formulation: an optimal transport policy (OTP), a flow matching policy (FMP), and a stochastic interpolant policy (SIP). On the Push-T and robomimic Square tasks, the three policies are competitive in task performance with Diffusion Policy and Consistency Policy while using considerably smaller networks and shorter training, and the informative reference accounts for a substantial part of their performance when few network evaluations are used. The three instances offer different trade-offs rather than a single best method: OTP generates an action chunk with a single evaluation of the smallest network (0.23 million parameters on Push-T) and is suitable for settings in which inference time and model size matter, whereas SIP attains the highest scores among the proposed policies at a higher cost.

papers.title: Foundation Pareto Flow Policy for Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: The overarching goal of reinforcement learning (RL) is to efficiently optimize the agent's policy for various environments, tasks, dynamics, and even user preferences, which often consist of multiple and potentially conflicting rewards/objectives. This necessitates the learning of Pareto-optimal policies that can navigate different trade-offs among objectives. However, existing multi-objective RL (MORL) methods, whether trained online or offline, are typically limited to task- or objective-specific policy learning and do not address generalization of learned trade-offs to unseen tasks/objectives. In this work, we propose the Foundation Pareto Flow Policy (FP2) for offline MORL in continuous robotic control, inspired by the pre-mid-post-training paradigm underlying recent foundation models. Specifically, we instantiate FP2 as a multi-modal diffusion transformer equipped with a likelihood-free flow matching loss, enabling unified, scalable, and instructable learning of diverse trade-off trajectories. We further develop a three-stage training pipeline to gradually optimize the policy: (1) pre-training on a large-scale MORL dataset, (2) mid-training on a carefully curated high-quality dataset, and (3) post-training on few collected trajectory data from new tasks and trade-offs. Empirical results demonstrate that FP2 outperforms previous state-of-the-art methods on most tasks of the D4MORL benchmark, achieving superior zero-shot interpolation and extrapolation on complex Pareto manifolds as well as efficient few-shot adaptation of the learned trade-off prior to new continuous-control tasks. Code is available at https://github.com/FibonacciRabbit/FP2.

papers.title: Morphology-Decoupled Segmentation for Multiple Tunnel Defects Under Complex Environments
papers.abstract: Automated tunnel-lining inspection must segment different defect geometries: cracks are thin, elongated, and connectivity-sensitive, whereas leakage, lining falling off, and segment damage are spatially extensive and context-dependent. Existing approaches generally apply a common decoder across defect classes or introduce boundary, topology, and directional mechanisms as isolated enhancements. This paper introduces Morphology-Decoupled Segmentation (MDS), in which defect morphology becomes the organising principle for feature routing, decoding, and interaction. A supervised routing module partitions multiscale encoder features into complementary linear and areal streams. The linear stream employs Deformable Strip Attention with image-conditioned direction hypotheses to preserve crack continuity without assuming fixed horizontal or vertical orientations, while the areal stream combines Pyramid Pooling with feature-pyramid fusion to capture diffuse boundaries and regional context. The representations are coupled through gated cross-morphology attention, allowing complementary information exchange while retaining morphology-specific features. A resolution-adaptive tiling and probability-blending pipeline preserves fine defects across variable-resolution imagery. MDS achieves 81.17% mIoU on the internal validation set and improves foreground image-level recognition over a backbone-matched SegDINO model, primarily for areal defects. Controlled ablations demonstrate the complementary contributions of routing supervision and cross-stream interaction while revealing a trade-off between areal-class performance and crack specialisation. The submitted model achieved 67.55% mIoU on an organiser-controlled hidden test, and the team placed second. Selective dynamic INT8 quantisation reduced model storage by 2.83 times with negligible accuracy loss.

papers.title: Two approaches of estimation for a tempered fractional Brownian motion with drift
papers.abstract: We investigate the problem of estimation for a tempered fractional Brownian motion with drift of the form: $X_t=\mu t + \sigma B_{H,\lambda}(t)$, for all $t\geq 0$. Based on discrete observations of $X$ and by using the method of moments with the ergodic theorem, we construct estimators of the drift parameter $\mu\in\R$ and noise parameters $ \sigma^2,H,\lambda \in(0,\infty)$. We establish the asymptotic properties of the proposed estimators, including convergence in probability, almost sure convergence, and asymptotic normality. Finally, by using Gladyshev's results \cite{gladyshev1961new} we provide some consistent alternative estimators of $\sigma^2$, $H$ and $\lambda$, when $\mu=0$ and $H\in (0,1)$.

papers.title: The Frontier Must Grow - Self-proposed, interpreter-labelled training roughly doubles a 4B model's accuracy on a fresh exam as its verified frontier grows
papers.abstract: A model can learn from problems it poses itself when an executable oracle supplies the answers. Qwen3-4B proposed Lua 5.1 programs; those it predicted wrong at least once in four samples joined a pool labelled by the interpreter, each round adding twice as many programs as the last (300, 900, 2100 in total), and each round trained a fresh adapter from the base on the pool. On the original exam the procedure met its registered criterion, an item-level test of each adapter against its predecessor. On a 2340-item exam drawn afterwards, accuracy rose from 8.3% to 16.7%; that follow-up's registered criteria were not met because round 1 gained nothing, while rounds 2 and 3 added 5.0 and 2.9 points on average, both intervals above zero. One fit on the same amount of base-proposed frontier data reached 14.6%, so the rounds' 2.1-point advantage is inconclusive. Three earlier registered series met no per-lineage criterion, and the same loop showed no gain on repository tasks or for a 27B agent in those configurations.

papers.title: Wideband Terahertz Pinching-Antenna Systems (PASS): Bandwidth Limits, Ergodic Rate, and Placement Optimization
papers.abstract: Terahertz (THz) bands offer the vast bandwidth that sixth-generation (6G) networks demand, but their severe path loss makes bringing the radiator close to the user decisive. Pinching-antenna systems (PASS) do exactly this, turning path loss into a programmable parameter by sliding radiating points along a dielectric waveguide, which makes THz their native regime. That regime, however, is inherently wideband and the waveguide is dispersive, whereas every existing PASS analysis is single-frequency and assumes a non-dispersive guide. This paper develops the first wideband, dispersion-aware theory of PASS and uncovers a limitation intrinsic to the pinching mechanism. Because co-phasing by physical position equalizes path length only modulo a wavelength, a pinching array is inherently beam-squint limited, and we show its frequency response is a Dirichlet kernel with a closed-form coherence bandwidth and an irreducible dispersion floor that even true-time-delay (TTD) correction cannot remove. A single unifying law governs the behavior, in which array gain trades against both coherence bandwidth and spatial robustness through one invariant that TTD correction breaks, reaching the floor with far fewer delay elements than a conventional array. We further characterize the wideband ergodic rate under random user locations, show that molecular absorption acts as a deterministic taper that multiplies the squint, and derive a simple rule for the rate-optimal number of pinches. Finally, by exploiting the integer structure of co-phasing, we recast the non-convex placement problem as a mixed-integer program that can be solved exactly in polynomial time. Together, these results move PASS from the narrowband, dispersion-blind setting to the wideband, dispersive regime that THz operation actually requires.

papers.title: Rigidity and classification of complete translating solitons and self-expanders with constant curvature in $\mathbb{R}^{4}$
papers.abstract: For complete immersed surfaces in Euclidean four-space whose mean curvature vector has constant length, translators are affine planes parallel to their fixed nonzero velocity, and self-expanders are planes through their centre. This rigidity requires no Lagrangian assumption, properness, volume growth control, or bound on the second fundamental form. Complete Lagrangian translators and self-expanders in $\mathbb{C}^{2}$ with constant Gaussian curvature are flat and, up to unitary equivalence, are properly embedded products of two complete planar curves. Translating factors are lines or grim reapers. Expanding factors are lines through the origin or nonstraight self-expanders. The proofs use moving frames, a transnormal function, a cubic tensor identity, and analytic continuation.

papers.title: ForeSay: Tell the Future in Words, Branch the Details in Noise for Precipitation Nowcasting
papers.abstract: Precipitation nowcasting involves two distinct scales of uncertainty: macroscopic storm evolution and fine-scale local convective variations. Current generative ensemble methods entangle both scales within independent random noise draws. This coupling causes two practical limitations: every ensemble member must execute the full sampling trajectory from scratch, so an N-member ensemble costs N times a single forecast; moreover, divergent trajectories spatially misalign heavy-rain echoes across members, causing standard pixel-wise averaging to blur critical high-intensity extremes. We present ForeSay, a generative nowcasting framework that decouples macroscopic evolution prediction from local stochastic detail generation. Given historical radar frames, a vision-language model first predicts a textual scenario of future storm dynamics to condition a Rectified Flow generator. Guided by this shared macroscopic prior, ensemble members share early trunk sampling steps to establish the storm trajectory and branch with fresh noise only in later steps to explore local convective details. Because members then differ mainly in local details, self-anchored support-consensus decoding replaces pixel averaging with discrete support voting to preserve sharp heavy-rain cores. Across six datasets, ForeSay achieves the best CSI at the highest precipitation thresholds, with relative improvements over the strongest baseline on each dataset ranging from over 10% to 84%. Our 8-member ensemble retains the forecasting skill and diversity of eight independently sampled runs while reducing computational cost from 8x to 5.2x that of a single forecast.

authors.name: Guiduo Duan
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: "I Am Not a Kiddo!": Quantifying Epistemic Infantilization in Large Language Models via Multi-Metric Bias Analysis
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for tutoring and professional knowledge retrieval, yet safety evaluations still focus mainly on overt harms such as toxicity while overlooking benevolent failure modes. We study epistemic infantilization, defined as an identity-conditioned reduction in technical depth that appears when disability disclosure precedes an expert-level query. To measure this effect, we construct a counterfactual dataset of matched question-answer pairs and compare model responses across three settings: no identity context, disability disclosed in prior conversational context, and disability disclosed via a short query prefix. We introduce two composite metrics, the Infantilization Bias Index (IBI) and the Epistemic Accessibility Response Score (EARS), which capture retention of mathematical and formal content, domain terminology, reasoning coverage, and tone signals such as simplification markers and unsolicited offers to adjust the level. Across five open-weight model families, we find consistent evidence that disability disclosure reduces epistemic access by replacing formal explanations with higher-level summaries, with Physics and Mathematics most affected. Using question-clustered inference that respects the repeated-measures structure of the data, the effect remains reliable after accounting for correlated observations. These findings suggest an inclusion tax, where disabled users must request rigor more explicitly than non-disabled users. We conclude by arguing that accessibility should mean format adaptation rather than content simplification.

authors.name: Dev Utkarsh
authors.institution: SRM Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Structure of gaps and generalized Wilf's conjecture
papers.abstract: In this article, we study the gaps, the maximal gaps, and the pseudo-Frobenius elements of generalized numerical semigroups of minimum embedding dimension. For these semigroups, we give an explicit description of the set of gaps, explicit formulas for the genus and the number of maximal gaps, and an explicit description of the set of pseudo-Frobenius elements in terms of the blocks of consecutive gaps of an associated numerical semigroup. In particular, we obtain an explicit formula for the type. As a consequence, we show that the type is unbounded even in minimum embedding dimension. Further, we prove that every generalized numerical semigroup with minimum embedding dimension has at least as many non-gaps below its gaps as gaps, and therefore satisfies the generalized Wilf's conjecture. We also prove the conjecture for generalized numerical semigroups in $\mathbb{N}^2$ graded by two-generated numerical semigroups, and asymptotically in higher dimension. For an arbitrary generalized numerical semigroup we bound the number of non-gaps below the gaps in terms of the genus and the type. Finally, we introduce nearly-symmetric generalized numerical semigroups and classify them in minimum embedding dimension. Although the type is unbounded in minimum embedding dimension generalized numerical semigroups, nearly-symmetric ones have type at most two.

papers.title: From Hosted Service to Field-Owned Infrastructure: Open, Self-Hosted Real-Time Camera-Trap Alerting with Regional Open-Weight Models
papers.abstract: Cellular camera traps can alert field teams within minutes, supporting anti-poaching, threatened-species protection and human-wildlife conflict mitigation. Most systems use central servers, sending images of people and sensitive species locations outside the collecting organisation and often across national borders. We ask whether this capability can run on infrastructure owned by field organisations. Trap Tracker RT is an open-source, self-hosted application that receives images by email or locally via FTP/SFTP, classifies them with a project-specific model and sends alerts through a mail server chosen by the organisation. We evaluated DeepFaune-SSA v1.2, pairing MegaDetector v6 with a DINOv3-based classifier for 33 sub-Saharan taxa, against three open alternatives on 31,131 out-of-distribution images from Kenya, Namibia and Malawi, independent of its training data. DeepFaune-SSA achieved image-level species accuracy of 0.901 (95% CI 0.894-0.908), versus 0.530 for the global SpeciesNet classifier and 0.556 and 0.547 for YOLOv10x and YOLO26x detectors trained on the same regional data. DeepFaune-SSA had the highest recall for all 26 species evaluated. The single-stage detectors missed animals in about a quarter of images; SpeciesNet assigned species labels in only 57%, usually falling back to coarser labels otherwise. In bench tests of the fully local path, alerts were issued about 6 s after upload completion, including with slowed and interrupted uploads. The two-stage pipeline processed 19 images per minute on eight CPU threads without a graphics processor. Trap Tracker RT is used by five organisations in the United Kingdom and Kenya, including for human-elephant conflict mitigation. We discuss how data paths, rather than inference location, determine data sovereignty, the responsibilities of self-hosting and the ethics of real-time monitoring.

papers.title: Local limit theorems and counting for transverse subgroups
papers.abstract: Transverse subgroups form a special class of discrete subgroups of connected semisimple real algebraic groups that includes all discrete subgroups of rank-one Lie groups, as well as Anosov and relatively Anosov subgroups. We study the joint distribution of partial Cartan projections and the two associated Cartan flags for Zariski dense $\theta$-transverse subgroups. Assuming local mixing of the associated Bowen-Margulis-Sullivan measure, we prove two local limit theorems and deduce counting asymptotics in Euclidean balls and tubes, together with equidistribution of the Cartan flags. These qualitative conclusions hold for $\theta$-Anosov subgroups, for which the local mixing hypothesis is satisfied. If the group is linearly $\theta$-regular near the direction of maximal growth, a polynomial error in local mixing gives polynomial errors in these results. Applying the quantitative local mixing theorem of Kim-Oh-Pan, we obtain local limit and counting theorems with polynomial error estimates for several classes of relatively Anosov representations of Fuchsian groups.

papers.title: Haar local mixing for transverse subgroups
papers.abstract: Transverse subgroups form a special class of discrete subgroups of connected semisimple real algebraic groups that includes all discrete subgroups of rank-one Lie groups, as well as Anosov and relatively Anosov subgroups. For torsion-free Zariski dense $\theta$-transverse subgroups, we establish Haar local mixing for the partial Weyl chamber action under a Bowen-Margulis-Sullivan (BMS) local mixing hypothesis. The proof is based on a transfer principle using the domains of discontinuity introduced by Delarue-Monclair-Sanders and extended to transverse subgroups by Guedes Bonthonneau-Lefeuvre-Weich. For $\theta$-Anosov subgroups, we verify the BMS hypothesis by adapting existing arguments and hence obtain Haar local mixing. As a consequence, we obtain asymptotics for the volume and distribution of long returns and recover the growth indicator from return volumes. Under linear $\theta$-regularity, the transfer also holds with polynomial error estimates. This condition is satisfied by subgroups of $\theta$-Anosov or relatively $\theta$-Anosov groups.

papers.title: On Mean Field Games with Focusing Logarithmic Local Couplings
papers.abstract: In this note we study the existence theory of classical solutions to a second order stationary discounted Mean Field Games (MFG) system with focusing logarithmic local coupling in one space dimension. We then show the convergence of classical solutions to the discounted stationary MFG system in the large discount/cheap control limit in the spirit of the work of Bardi--Cardaliaguet.

affiliations.raw: Department of Mathematical Sciences, Durham University, Durham, DH1 3LE, UK

papers.intro:
We consider second order stationary discounted MFG systems with focusing logarithmic local couplings in one space dimension. In particular, the focusing nature of the coupling corresponds to the negative sign on the logarithm, which means that players are incentivised to concentrate, the opposite of the classical Lasry–Lions monotone regime. The strength of this incentive to aggregate is in competition with the strength of the diffusion, which we will see to play a key role in the form of an inequality that roughly imposes that the diffusion coefficient has to be bigger than the coefficient of the logarithmic local coupling.

In particular, the focusing nature of the coupling corresponds to the negative sign on the logarithm, which means that players are incentivised to concentrate, the opposite of the classical Lasry–Lions monotone regime. The strength of this incentive to aggregate is in competition with the strength of the diffusion, which we will see to play a key role in the form of an inequality that roughly imposes that the diffusion coefficient has to be bigger than the coefficient of the logarithmic local coupling.

The theory of MFGs were initiated by Lasry–Lions [19] and by Huang–Caines–Malhame [17]. In particular, since the seminal works of Lasry and Lions, there has been great amount of literature studying MFGs which are of “defocusing” type, more commonly known in the literature as Lasry–Lions monotone. Focusing MFGs (also called aggregating MFGs) have been studied in the series of papers [12, 5, 11, 7], where existence and nonexistence of classical solutions have been established in the framework of power-like couplings using PDE methods. We also would like to note that the first two papers cited above study stationary problems of ergodic type, instead of the discounted problems we consider here.

In particular, since the seminal works of Lasry and Lions, there has been great amount of literature studying MFGs which are of “defocusing” type, more commonly known in the literature as Lasry–Lions monotone. Focusing MFGs (also called aggregating MFGs) have been studied in the series of papers [12, 5, 11, 7], where existence and nonexistence of classical solutions have been established in the framework of power-like couplings using PDE methods. We also would like to note that the first two papers cited above study stationary problems of ergodic type, instead of the discounted problems we consider here.

Classical solutions for MFG systems with singular local couplings have previously been studied in the works [8, 15], both papers studied time dependent problems that are in the defocusing framework where agents prefer low density regions and the Hamiltonians have subquadratic growth. The former studied local coupling with power like growth, while the latter studied logarithmic local couplings as in the current paper but with the opposite sign (hence are defocusing), moreover these papers require subquadratic growth of the Hamiltonian. In the paper [16], a model similar to ours had been studied, where it was observed that in the case of quadratic Hamiltonians, MFGs with logarithmic local couplings essentially fall into the class of so-called linear–quadratic–Gaussian problems and can be solved by using quadratic-Gaussian ansatzes. We depart from this regime as we consider general Hamiltonians with quadratic growth and a spatially dependent running cost that is not necessarily a quadratic polynomial. As a consequence ansatzes can no longer be used and the method we propose is completely different from those used in the all the aforementioned references.

We depart from this regime as we consider general Hamiltonians with quadratic growth and a spatially dependent running cost that is not necessarily a quadratic polynomial. As a consequence ansatzes can no longer be used and the method we propose is completely different from those used in the all the aforementioned references.

The core idea of our method is inspired by the existence proof of the paper [21], where control theory based estimates on value functions to fully convex optimal control problems were used to derive classical solutions to MFG systems with nonlocal couplings. In our logarithmic coupling setting, a key observation is that supposing we have a fully convex control problem, the stationary profile to the Fokker–Planck equation with drift associated to the optimal control is log-concave, which in turn means that the control problem with (minus) logarithmic local coupling is again a fully convex control problem. Therefore we will be able to “close the loop” and build a Schauder type fixed point scheme.

Let us also mentioned that this convergence is quantified in the recent works [6, 13].

In the second half of this note we show the convergence of classical solutions to the discounted stationary MFG system in the large discount/cheap control limit in the spirit of [1], where it was shown that in the limit players “lose rationality” and the measure flow converges to the solution of an aggregation equation. Let us also mentioned that this convergence is quantified in the recent works [6, 13].

papers.title: Beveridge: Open Weight System One Decision Models with Calibrated Probabilities
papers.abstract: Many production systems need a model to make a narrow decision about a document (route a ticket, check a limit, refuse a request, pick the next step of a browser agent) rather than to write text about it. We present Beveridge, a family of open weight System One decision models that take a document and up to 15 typed questions (yes/no, choice among described options, or a level on an ordered scale) and return, in one forward pass without generating text, an answer with a calibrated probability for every option. Beveridge-Large-C (398M parameters) adds a 3.5M parameter decision network to ModernBERT-large: typed number and date features in the input, exact facts from a rule engine, question-to-document evidence attention, a three-step recursive core with learned halting and an exact yes/no path. Beveridge-Pro-C adapts Gemma 4 26B-A4B with LoRA to score option letters, and Beveridge-Pro-C-Web extends it to the next step of a browser agent. On held-out tests the 0.4B model reaches 93.0% on our operations-document benchmark against 91.1% for the best of five general LLMs (31B-675B) and 87.9% for a commercial System One API, and, because its confidences are calibrated (ECE 0.029 on that benchmark), it can hand over 76% of decisions automatically at 95% accuracy, where no general LLM we tested can hand over any. It answers in 4.9 ms per decision on one NVIDIA H200 GPU and 60 ms on the 14 core CPU of an Apple M4 Pro laptop. Beveridge-Pro-C-Web raises next-step accuracy on web pages from unseen site types from 49.4% to 98.2% and completes live browsing tasks without losing document accuracy. We describe the models, the training recipes and an evaluation on 19 held-out test sets against a commercial System One API and five general LLMs, including where the models are weak. Weights and inference code are released under Apache 2.0.

papers.title: Ontology-Compiled Control Barrier Functions for Heterogeneous Robot Teams
papers.abstract: Safety filters for heterogeneous robot teams fail because of missing constraints, overestimated braking capabilities and conflicts between individually satisfiable constraints. We present OntoCBF, which compiles a domain ontology with a class taxonomy, typed relations, safety axioms and a dynamics profile per robot class into a control barrier function filter with one quadratic program per agent. Description-logic entailment supplies the constraints of any team online, including those that follow from chains of relations and from classes defined by what a robot carries, so the existing safety axioms cover new robot classes, payload classes and combinations. We prove that a subclass may reuse the braking capability of its parent whenever it can produce every velocity of the parent, a property separate from subsumption. For box-bounded double integrators this property is also necessary, and every loss of safety then begins with a conflict. Once three robots interact, the safe set of pairwise barriers contains states from which a collision is unavoidable, and such states persist in larger teams under any fixed capability reduction. In a simulated warehouse where humans ignore the robots, a filter written for the design classes violates safety in 89-100 % of the episodes with unseen classes. In all scenarios, including one with 32 robots, OntoCBF violates safety in 20-70 % of the episodes, each time after a conflict, with a median deepest intrusion of 10-17 % of the keep-out distance. A multi-agent PPO policy trained with the filter in the loop lowers the rate of infeasible quadratic programs, nearly all of them conflicts, by 18-41 %.

papers.title: FDAM: A Frequency-Direction-Aware Multi-Task Framework for Pavement Crack Grid Localization
papers.abstract: Pavement crack grid localization remains challenging for thin and tiny cracks due to weak visual cues and background interference. Box detection often misses these cracks, while supervised semantic segmentation faces limited pixel-wise annotations and high labeling costs. In this paper, we propose a Frequency-Direction-Aware Multi-Task framework (FDAM) with box detection and grid classification branches. The core grid classification branch comprises Frequency-Domain Enhancement (FDE) and Directional Feature Refinement (DFR). FDE adaptively weights spectral bands and fuses reconstructed features with spatial features. DFR captures thin crack patterns through multi-scale strip convolutions, direction-sensitive modulation, and feature recalibration. Sparse positive cells and ambiguous local predictions motivate adaptive grid supervision. Adaptive Importance Reweighting emphasizes uncertain predictions and local label transitions, with focal supervision for all cells. Our contribution is to couple the box detection and grid classification branches through shared feature learning for pavement crack grid localization. We validate FDAM on our RoadDistress2026 dataset of thin and tiny cracks and further evaluate it on public datasets Crack500 and DeepCrack. The code is available at https://github.com/Lab-PANbin/FDAM

authors.name: Mengze Wang
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Pros4D: Modeling Evolving 4D Worlds in Latent Space for Dynamic Spatial Reasoning
papers.abstract: Dynamic spatial reasoning from monocular video enables vision-language models (VLMs) to understand how 3D environments evolve over time, supporting physical world understanding and embodied intelligence. Existing efforts primarily address observed-dynamics understanding, whereas agents in dynamic environments also require future-dynamics prediction beyond the observation boundary. Moreover, external geometric processing and textual descriptions can increase inference complexity or lose information when representing continuous dynamics. These limitations motivate a shared internal state that preserves observed dynamics and remains predictive beyond the input video. Accordingly, we present Pros4D, a framework for modeling evolving 4D worlds in latent space that unifies retrospective understanding of observed-dynamics with prospective reasoning for future-dynamics prediction. Specifically, Pros4D-Engine derives geometry-grounded supervision and constructs paired examples for both tasks, while Pros4D-Bench evaluates them across eight spatial task categories spanning dynamic cameras, objects, and scenes. At the model level, Pros4D compresses observed dynamics into latent observed states and autoregressively rolls them forward into latent future states. 4D Latent Alignment (4DLA) grounds these states through complementary visual-semantic and geometric supervision, while joint language supervision connects them to task reasoning. Experiments across benchmarks show consistent improvements over strong baselines in both capabilities.

papers.title: Paying Creators for Training Data Can Increase AI Displacement
papers.abstract: Generative AI increasingly competes with creators while using their content as training data. In response, policymakers have called for platforms to compensate creators for training data use and allow opting out. We study how such policies affect creator displacement in a model of a platform where creators choose whether to contribute training data and consumers choose between purchasing from creators and prompting generative AI trained on their content. When compensation is required, the low-quality creator chooses to remain solely as a training data supplier while AI fully displaces her demand, despite AI quality and the price the platform charges for AI-generated content being identical with and without compensation. Without compensation, the risk of losing creators and their training data constrains the platform to set the price of creators' content to preserve their demand. This constraint also prevents further AI displacement as AI improves, with the platform raising AI prices while keeping creators' prices and demand unchanged to prevent exit. Compensation increases creators' payoffs and total surplus but reduces consumer surplus. Our findings highlight how compensation policies for training data can shape creators' economic roles in a future with more capable generative AI.

papers.title: Language-model agents' beliefs can be manipulated via truthful evidence in open channel
papers.abstract: Language-model agents' beliefs can be manipulated through open channels such as social media, even when the information they receive is truthful. When agents fill gaps between fragments with self-induced relationships, they may accept those relationships as established facts and pass the resulting rumours to others. Drawing on cognitive theory of narrative understanding and film theory of montage, we introduce Generative Montage to operationalize this failure, termed narrative overfitting, by coordinating agents to arrange truthful fragments into misleading narratives. Across 1,090 rumour targets from six Twitter events, agents often accepted rumours overconfidently, with overall acceptance exceeding 65 percent in twelve of fourteen models. Acceptance remained above 50 percent after majority voting or review of the same evidence, showing how errors can reach downstream decisions. To explain this susceptibility, fragment interventions identify posts that influence belief within complete narratives. Synthetic controls then show that similar response patterns arise from valid evidence, separating belief influence from evidential support. This distinction motivates Grounded Monitor, a proof-of-concept neuro-symbolic runtime monitor that checks direct evidential support to guide agents' judgements, improving decision accuracy by 5.6 to 29.0 percentage points across original and anonymized settings. These findings expose a cognitive route to rumour amplification and support monitoring inferred relationships before agent-generated conclusions guide public decisions.

authors.name: Youcheng Sun

papers.title: QuantileGS: Quantile-Based Conformal Bounds on RGB Rendering Errors for Novel View Synthesis with 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.abstract: Uncertainty quantification for novel view synthesis with 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) assesses rendering reliability at unseen viewpoints. This reliability depends on the discrepancy between rendered and true colors, which cannot be measured without ground-truth images. We therefore quantify uncertainty in this unknown discrepancy through upper bounds on per-pixel RGB mean absolute error. However, learned bounds may underestimate these errors and overstate rendering reliability, motivating calibration to a prescribed coverage level. In this paper, we propose QuantileGS, a post-hoc framework that combines learned rendering-error quantiles with scale-normalized conformal calibration to produce spatially adaptive error bounds. The framework comprises three phases. Phase 1, Rendering-Error Computation, measures RGB mean absolute error between observed images and predictions from a frozen 3DGS model. Phase 2, Ordered Gaussian Quantile Fields, learns two scalar attributes per Gaussian to predict lower and upper rendering-error quantiles. Phase 3, Scale-Normalized Conformal Calibration, calibrates the upper prediction on held-out images, using the quantile gap to scale the correction. Under the stated assumptions, the resulting bounds provide finite-sample marginal coverage. At a nominal coverage level of 90%, calibration raises mean empirical test coverage from 69.6% to 89.6% on LLFF and from 80.1% to 92.1% on Mip-NeRF 360. On LF, coverage remains conservative at 96.3% before and 96.4% after calibration. Applications to active view selection, Gaussian pruning, and RGB-D simultaneous localization and mapping illustrate how these bounds inform downstream decisions.

authors.name: Xia Xu
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: The microscopic origin of the hysteretic hydrogen adsorption in Double Wall Carbon Nanotubes bundles
papers.abstract: In a recent study we reported large hysteretic hydrogen adsorption in samples made out of Double Wall Carbon Nanotubes (DWCNT) at supercritical temperatures (50 K, 77 K and 150 K), a physical behavior of practical interest. Here, we center our efforts in elucidate its physical origin by means of neutron diffraction (ND) and computer simulations. After a detailed theoretical modeling of the ND signal we were able to quantitatively study how the nanostructure of the material reacts to the hydrogen loads. An expansion of the bundle structure with increasing hydrogen load was found. Taking advantage of the translational symmetry of a DWCNT bundle along the nanotube axis, a two dimensional numerical analogue of the system helped us to clarify the microscopic origin of the hysteresis. Two microscopic mechanisms are identified as responsible for the metastable hydrogen adsorption, one structurally static in character, namely, H$_{2}$-load dependent effective energy barriers between interstitials, the other related to the structural deformation, namely, the opening/closing of the channels between interstitials with increasing/decreasing H$_{2}$ loads owing to the concomitant bundle expansion/contraction.

papers.title: Strain-Engineering Giant Pseudo-Electric Fields in Multilayer Graphene
papers.abstract: Electromagnetic scalar and vector potentials can be engineered in solids through lattice distortions, providing a versatile means of tuning electronic band structures. The pseudovector component, which generates pseudo-magnetic fields, has received much attention for its ability to realize a zero-field quantum Hall effect. However, the pseudoscalar component, giving rise to pseudo-electric fields to which many electronic systems are intrinsically susceptible, has not yet been experimentally explored. Here, we demonstrate the emergence and profound consequences of the pseudoscalar potential in a multilayer graphene system. Atomic relaxation reconstructs the system into large Bernalstacked domains separated by one-dimensional rhombohedral channels. Within this inter-dimensional system, we achieve the first direct atomic-scale imaging of distinct lattice deformations in graphene under strain. In rhombohedral channels, we observe that the tensile lattice deformation induces giant pseudo-electric fields, producing ultra-flat dispersion with divergent density of states and a large energy gap. This results in enhanced electronic correlations, leading to flat-band instabilities and striped modulation in the density of states that would otherwise require strong external displacement fields. Moreover, the gap opened by the pseudoscalar potential protects topological boundary states that persist in the absence of applied fields. Our results provide a comprehensive atomic-scale characterization of graphene elasticity and direct spectroscopic evidence for the nontrivial pseudo-electric field arising from lattice distortion. More broadly, it provides an intrinsic and tunable pathway to new quantum states

papers.title: Between Rigor and Reality: How AI Safety Benchmark Developers Understand Benchmark Use and Maintenance
papers.abstract: Safety benchmarks are cited as the primary tool to understand the risks posed by generative AI (GenAI) systems, yet growing evidence suggests they often fail to meet the needs of real-world safety evaluation. We present findings from five interviews with AI safety benchmark developers in academia and industry. We find a disconnect between perceptions of the intended usefulness of safety benchmarks and their practical usefulness in safety evaluations of deployed systems. Our participants offered perspectives on two challenges contributing to this disconnect: (1) the difficulty of achieving inter-rater reliability on safety constructs, and (2) a lack of clarity regarding how to address persistent threats to external validity. Based on our analysis, we argue that safety benchmarks must not only be grounded in deployment contexts, but actively integrated with them. To facilitate this, we outline pathways for more transparent communication between academic and industry AI safety stakeholders.

papers.title: MarineSparkLM-4B: A Lightweight Language Model for Marine and Offshore Engineering Built by Parameter-Efficient Adaptation
papers.abstract: Marine and offshore engineering text is spread across preprints, open-access journals, encyclopedias and institutional documents, and the amount of it is small by pretraining standards. We ask how far a lightweight language model for marine and offshore engineering can be taken with parameter-efficient adaptation on a single workstation-class device. Starting from the 4-billion-parameter OceanGPT-basic-4B-Instruct, we train two independent LoRA adapters, each updating 33.0 million of 4.06 billion parameters (0.81%). Training took 4 hours 40 minutes for the first adapter and 10 minutes for the second on one NVIDIA DGX Spark. The first adapter is trained by next-token prediction on a 61.6-million-token corpus covering ten engineering themes. The corpus was built from 13,879 source documents, of which 7,069 were retained after deduplication and a two-tier keyword filter that removes cross-domain lexical collisions. Its validation loss falls from 2.082 to 1.976 over 1,500 steps. Direct testing showed that this adapter could still drift off topic on a retrieval-grounded ballast-water prompt, so we trained a second adapter on 2,295 question-answer pairs (114 hand-written and 2,181 generated by the base model from corpus passages) with the loss restricted to answer tokens. On 20 held-out prompts scored by hand for accuracy, topicality and specificity (maximum 120), the plain base model, the continuation adapter, the instruction adapter and the instruction adapter with retrieval scored 42, 56, 84 and 88. Absolute accuracy stays low (14 of 40 without retrieval and 20 of 40 with it). We report the full pipeline, two negative results (a reverted keyword fix and an instruction run that overfit within 100 steps), and the limits of the evaluation, which uses one small prompt set, no inter-rater agreement measure and model-generated reference answers.

papers.title: Polynomial growth and dynamic asymptotic dimension
papers.abstract: We show that principal ample groupoids with local polynomial growth of degree at most $s$ have dynamic asymptotic dimension at most $\lfloor s\rfloor$. As a consequence, $\sigma$-compact principal ample groupoids with local polynomial growth have slow dynamic asymptotic dimension growth.

papers.title: An all-steps-at-once algorithm for time-domain wave propagation in heterogeneous and unbounded media
papers.abstract:
We propose, analyze, and implement a convolution quadrature (CQ) algorithm for transient acoustic waves in an unbounded medium consisting of a heterogeneous domain embedded in free space, where the wave speed may be spatially variable and discontinuous. Multistep CQ, applied to the time-domain solution operator, reduces the evolution problem to a family of Helmholtz problems with damped complex frequencies, which can be solved independently in parallel, all time steps at once. The frequency problems are discretized by an overlapping coupling of finite elements (FEM) on a polygonal/polyhedral domain containing the inhomogeneity, and boundary elements (BEM) on a smooth curve enclosed by that domain, in the region where the medium is homogeneous, which accounts exactly for the unbounded exterior. Neither discretization needs to conform to the geometry of the heterogeneous domain, nor to each other.
  For the resulting FEM--BEM coupling we prove bounds for the solution operators of the transformed problems that are explicit in the Laplace parameter and the wave speed. These bounds yield convergence of the time discretization for A-stable multistep schemes. We also prove explicit estimates on the exponential decay of the transformed solutions away from the heterogeneity, which show that the correction provided by the BEM part is small but relevant, and cheap to compute: a few GMRES iterations suffice, and the correction is needed only over a fixed range of weakly damped frequencies, beyond which it becomes negligible and can be dropped. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted convergence rates in time and space and explore iterative (multigrid) methods for the interior FEM problems.

papers.title: Factorized Self-Supervised Speech Tokenization
papers.abstract: Speech tokenizers convert audio into discrete units, enabling language models to process and generate speech. The goal is to learn compact, text-like representations while preserving enough detail to reconstruct a speaker's voice and delivery. We propose Facto: a factorized tokenizer that disentangles time-varying information (content and prosody) from static components (speaker identity and recording conditions). We build on a recent linear factorization method for self-supervised features, extending it to handle unseen speakers. Then, we cluster the factorized space and train a lightweight decoder to reconstruct audio from the resulting tokens. By removing the static components before clustering, our tokens are more robust to small noise perturbations. We validate this by testing token stability under various noise conditions. Next, we theoretically analyze Facto's convergence and scaling properties, quantifying how the factorization improves with the number of training speakers. Finally, we evaluate Facto on a range of downstream tasks. We show that greater token stability translates into improved text-to-speech performance and competitive results in voice conversion and spoken language modeling. Code and checkpoints at https://github.com/ubisoft/ubisoft-laforge-facto/ and demo page at https://ubisoft-laforge.github.io/speech/facto/.

authors.name: Herman Kamper
authors.institution: Universitatea Națională de Știință și Tehnologie Politehnica București

papers.title: Generic splitting types and Terao's conjecture for seventeen and eighteen lines
papers.abstract: We prove that the generic splitting type of the logarithmic bundle of an arrangement of at most eighteen lines in the complex projective plane is determined by the intersection lattice. In particular, Terao's freeness conjecture holds for seventeen and eighteen lines. For any number of lines, it holds for free arrangements whose smaller exponent is at most eight. By the theorem for at most sixteen lines, the problem reduces to a uniformity condition for lattices of seventeen lines: if all realizations have minimal Jacobian-syzygy degree at least seven, then all or none have degree seven. The proof has two parts. First, a realization of minimal degree seven has defect at most four, the defect being the length of the zero scheme of a minimal section. This uses the residual inflection quartic of the associated degree-seven foliation, local inflection identities, and fixed-point theory for critically fixed rational maps of degree seven with exact finite certificates. Second, the uniformity condition holds at these defects. For multiplicities at most six, a critical realization contains a twelve-line core of minimal weight, and an exact search through extensions of the cores shows that the lattice has a single Galois orbit of realizations; the only family left at defect four has no critical member. For a point of multiplicity seven we use the zero scheme of the pencil derivation and a classification of transversal structures. Terao's conjecture for seventeen and eighteen lines needs only defects one, two and three and, for seventeen lines, this classification at multiplicity seven. The proof is computer-assisted.

authors.institution: Universitatea Națională de Știință și Tehnologie Politehnica București

authors.institution: IMAR - Institutul de Matematică „Simion Stoilow” al Academiei Române

papers.title: AI Cannot Review What Humans Catch: A First Look at the Reviews of Agent Instruction Files
papers.abstract: Agents increasingly shape software, and instruction files steer them. Files such as AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules, and SKILL.md act as executable policy: prose that a machine reads and acts on. Unlike ordinary documentation, a single edit to one of these files can silently redirect how an agent behaves across an entire repository. Natural-language rules have no per-change oracle, so they slip past the compilers, type-checkers, and test suites that guard code. Review is therefore the only quality gate, but no prior work has studied how that review happens. We analyzed 2,870 instruction-file pull requests across 2,246 repositories. The gate is largely broken: over 70% of instruction-file changes receive no substantive review. When an AI reviewer substitutes for a human, it is structurally blind to the concerns that most need human judgment. It catches surface structure but misses factual errors, necessity questions, and staleness problems. We contribute the first taxonomy of instruction-file review concerns (16 categories), which exposes this sharp human/AI divergence, and a benchmark of 1,962 human-checked concerns across 468 PRs. We ran three widely-used agents (Codex, OpenCode, and Claude Code) against the benchmark, giving each reviewer the full repository at review time. They recovered only 1.3-3.9% of the concerns humans raise. Even the strongest current agents cannot substitute for human attention on these files.

papers.title: Mapping the Afterlife of Future Work Statements in NLP Research
papers.abstract: Future work statements are one of the few places in scientific papers where authors explicitly describe what they think should happen next. We study what happens to such statements after publication. We construct a dataset of 72,070 future work items extracted from 23,113 ACL Anthology papers published between 1979 and 2025, categorize them by type, retrieve candidate follow-up papers through citation-based and content-based search, and use LLM-based judgments to assess whether later papers pursue the proposed directions. Using this resource, we analyze patterns across time, venues, categories, themes, and authors. We find that many items are later addressed, often within a few years, with clear differences across types and themes and a largely community-driven pattern. Our results suggest that future work statements provide useful evidence for studying how research directions develop in NLP. To support further research, we release our dataset at: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20385239.

papers.title: ReCALM: A Residual-enhanced Crowdsourced Analytic Learning Mechanism for Distributed Continual Service Construction
papers.abstract: Crowdsourcing has emerged as a promising paradigm for constructing AI services by harnessing the collective capabilities of distributed workers. As consumers' demands continually evolve, service models must acquire new knowledge while retaining previously learned information. However, due to the inherited reliance on gradients for backpropagation, existing approaches typically suffer from catastrophic forgetting during continual model updates on heterogeneous data. Recent studies have introduced analytic learning, a gradient-free paradigm that achieves invariance through recursive closed-form solutions. Nevertheless, existing analytic methods are typically constrained by single-layer linear networks, which tend to suffer from underfitting due to their inability to perform deep representation learning. To address this issue, we propose ReCALM, a Residual-enhanced Crowdsourced Analytic Learning Mechanism that achieves deep nonlinear invariance for distributed continual service construction. Inspired by the success of ResNet, we develop gradient-free residual blocks for ReCALM with closed-form solutions. To implement distributed continual training for ReCALM, we further devise a cross-recursive strategy via least squares. Both theoretical and experimental analyses verify ReCALM's dual superiority in heterogeneity invariance and deep representation. With 20 residual layers, ReCALM improves accuracy by 8.85%-9.83% over the single-layer analytic baseline, while reducing computational costs by over 94% compared with gradient-based baselines.

papers.title: UbiHearo: Bringing Scenario-Aware Sound Guidance to DHH Users with Mobile Agents
papers.abstract: For Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing (DHH) users, effective sound awareness goes beyond detecting \emph{what} sound occurs; it requires understanding \emph{what it means}, \emph{how urgent it is}, and \emph{what to do}. However, existing mobile assistants largely reduce acoustic scenes to isolated labels or generic alerts, failing to provide contextual guidance when the same sound implies different risks across scenarios. We present \sysname, a mobile hearing assistant agent that closes the sensing--reasoning--action loop for \textit{scenario-aware} and \textit{personalized} DHH assistance. \sysname adopts a \textit{neuro-symbolic} design that transforms continuous acoustic and physical context streams into structured intermediate representations (IRs) for controllable reasoning and guidance. It introduces three key mechanisms. \textit{First}, a perception-thresholded sensing mechanism enables energy-efficient always-on awareness by activating processing only for perceptually meaningful events while preserving safety-critical cues through deterministic overrides. \textit{Second}, a staged neuro-symbolic reasoning framework performs promptless scenario understanding by conditioning an on-device audio-language model on structured IRs instead of user-authored context descriptions. \textit{Third}, a bounded human-in-the-loop personalization mechanism adapts user-specific guidance through lightweight on-device decision-boundary updates while preserving population-aligned reasoning. We evaluate \sysname on smartphones and in-vehicle systems across diverse scenarios. It achieves favorable accuracy--latency--energy tradeoffs and personalized guidance.
