papers.title: Rovibrational state-specific quasi-classical trajectory calculation and master equation analysis of the CNO system in high-energy collisions
papers.abstract: The CNO system governs the formation and depletion of the CN, CO and NO radiative species relevant to combustion, astrophysical and hypersonic applications. The NO($X^2\Pi$) + C($^3P$), CN($X^2\Sigma^+$) + O($^3P$) and CO($X^1\Sigma^+$) + N($^4S$, $^2D$) collisional systems are investigated using rovibrational state-specific quasi-classical trajectory calculations and master equation analysis under hypersonic thermal conditions. Inelastic processes proceed primarily through rotational excitation of low-lying states and rovibrational excitation of high-lying states. For most systems, rotational and vibrational relaxation times exhibit comparable scales and unconventional temperature dependences, invalidating the assumption of decoupled energy modes. Dissociation is governed by high-lying rovibrational states and correlates strongly with the state-specific energy deficit rather than vibrational-specific dynamics. At $T$ = 10,000 K, 72 to 93% of the depletion of the diatomic species occurs within a quasi-steady-state (QSS) regime for all systems. At lower temperatures, a large portion of the depletion occurs outside the QSS regime, indicating that the QSS assumption holds only for moderate to high temperatures. No such regime is established for exchange reactions, demonstrating that the QSS assumption is invalid for modelling them. The NO + C system proceeds predominantly towards CN + O at low temperatures and towards the CO + N channels at high temperatures, preferentially forming N($^4S$). The fraction proceeding towards the CO + N channels remains lower than in available shock-tube measurements, while the thermal exchange rate coefficients reproduce shock-tube measurements and high-fidelity calculations. Finally, consistent similarities across inelastic, exchange and dissociation processes offer promising physical foundations for reduced-order model development.

papers.title: Multi-seed information diffusion with varying reproduction
papers.abstract: We define the $S_hR_k$-process that generalizes the notion of Hamiltonicity through the lense of information diffusion. We say that a graph is $S_hR_k$-infectable if it can be fully infected by transmission trees seeded by at most $h$ initial infections in which each infection leads to at most $k$ others; or, equivalently, if it can be exactly vertex-covered by at most $h$ trees of degree at most $k$. While determining $S_hR_k$ infectability is NP-hard in general, we argue fixed-parameter tractability when parameterised by treewidth. Additionally, we give computational experimental results comparing the performance of several natural heuristics for minimising the number of initial infections required to an optimal LP-based approach on several standard complex network models. We find that a uniformly random approach outperforms greedy heuristics based on degree or clustering.

papers.title: Learning a Task-Adaptive Low-Dimensional Semantic Space for Improved Visual Classification
papers.abstract: Semantic visual classification commonly aligns visual embeddings with semantic spaces induced by pretrained text encoders. However, such spaces are typically high-dimensional, weakly aligned with visual feature geometry, and insufficiently discriminative for downstream classification tasks. We propose TaSS, a framework for learning a task-adaptive low-dimensional semantic space that preserves semantic structure while explicitly optimizing class separability. TaSS is constructed through a parameterized geometry transformation of pretrained text embeddings that enlarges inter-class margins via distance reshaping and improves intra-class compactness through prototype-preserving semantic constraints. The resulting semantic space maintains meaningful semantic relationships while producing a discriminative geometry tailored for classification. Frozen visual encoder features are subsequently aligned to TaSS using a lightweight MLP, enabling improved discriminative learning without fine-tuning pretrained backbones. We further provide theoretical analysis showing that TaSS preserves semantic consistency while enforcing enhanced inter-class separation and controlled intra-class variance. Extensive experiments on skeleton-based human action recognition, video classification, and image classification benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over existing semantic alignment approaches, with gains exceeding 3 percentage points on average and up to 8.5 points on challenging datasets.

papers.title: Network-Native DNN Architecture Synthesis for Distributed Inference
papers.abstract: Distributed deep neural network (DNN) inference typically follows a model-first paradigm, in which a predefined DNN is partitioned and deployed over a physical network. On irregular communication-computation topologies, however, this approach can create transmission bottlenecks and leave distributed resources underutilized. This paper reverses this perspective and asks: given a physical network, what kind of DNN can it naturally support? To answer this question, we propose a network-native DNN architecture synthesis paradigm in which the physical network topology directly defines inter-node neural dependencies. Neural computation is allocated across nodes under communication, computation, storage, synchronization, and latency constraints. We establish structural properties of the synthesis problem and develop linear programming (LP)-based Architecture Synthesis (LPAS), an efficient topology-guided algorithm that produces a feasible architecture with a computable bound on suboptimality. Experiments on physical networks of different sizes show that LPAS achieves relative gaps below 0.6% to the LP-derived upper bound, with substantially lower runtime than direct mixed-integer LP optimization on larger networks. Under matched network deadlines, the network-native architectures activate more compute nodes and utilize a larger proportion of available model-storage capacity than the model-first baseline. After training, the network-native models achieve higher classification accuracy across all evaluated dataset-precision settings, with the average gain of up to 10.69%. This network-native design paradigm thus turns the physical network from a deployment constraint into an architecture design primitive.

papers.title: A Density Functional Tight Binding Model for Rapid Screening of Spin-Orbit-Coupling-Driven Topological Properties in Bismuth
papers.abstract: We present a transferable Density Functional Tight Binding (DFTB) model for bismuth with explicit spin-orbit coupling that enables exploration of the structural degrees of freedom governing topological properties with minimal computational resources. We have used our DFTB model to run high-throughput calculations at a scale that would be significantly more expensive with standard Kohn-Sham Density Functional Theory (DFT) to determine a strain-buckling map of electronic and topological properties for bismuthene, where we identify regions of band gap closure and band inversion as a function of structural parameters. We show that our approach yields an accurate band structure for the rhombohedral phase, where small band gaps exist at or near time-reversal-invariant momentum (TRIM) points. We then demonstrate the transferability of our model to bismuth properties not included in our training data through determination of the rhombohedral phase phonon density of states and energetic ordering of additional bismuth solid phases. Finally, we have validated our topological predictions through comparison to DFT results for the optimized bilayer geometries, a band inversion order parameter, and the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant as a function of monolayer unit cell length. Our efforts establish DFTB as a rigorous approach for topological characterization while yielding approximately three orders of magnitude increase in computational efficiency relative to DFT. Our model can thus serve as a computational tool for topological materials discovery by enabling large-scale computational screening to address the potentially complex relationship between physical-chemical properties and the resulting topological classification.

papers.title: Second-Order Cone Valid Inequalities for Set-Point Tracking with Energy Storage
papers.abstract: Convex relaxations of energy storage models drop the complementarity constraints that forbid simultaneous charging and discharging. In the set-point tracking problem, the relaxation can then charge and discharge simultaneously at no cost, as the tracking error depends only on the net power of the storage. We show that the convex hull of the single-period epigraph of the tracking error, under complementarity, is the epigraph of a parabolic cylinder. The resulting second-order cone inequality adds to the tracking error a penalty on the product of the charging and discharging powers and is the tightest convex member of the pencil of quadrics through the two branches of the epigraph. With power limits and the mode variable, the hull is given by the perspective reformulation of the two modes, which dominates the cylinder. In 20000 instances, the cylinder reduces the hours with simultaneous charging and discharging by more than 99% and yields an optimal schedule in 98.8% of them.

papers.title: Distance-$2$ isolation of connected graphs
papers.abstract:
If $\mathcal{F}$ is a set of graphs and $F$ is a copy of a graph in $\mathcal{F}$, then we call $F$ an $\mathcal{F}$-graph. Let $G$ be a connected $n$-vertex graph. For a subset $D$ of the vertex set $V(G)$, let $N^2[D]$ denote the second closed neighbourhood of $D$. Let $\iota_2(G, \mathcal{F})$ denote the size of a smallest subset $D$ of $V(G)$ such that $N^2[D]$ intersects the $\mathcal{F}$-graphs contained by $G$ (equivalently, $G - N^2[G]$ contains no $\mathcal{F}$-graph). For $k \geq 0$, let $\mathcal{E}_k$ denote the set of connected graphs that have at least $k$ edges (and at least one vertex if $k = 0$). By a well-known result of Meir and Moon, $\iota_2(G, \mathcal{E}_0) \leq n/3$ if $n \geq 3$. We show that $\iota_2(G, \mathcal{E}_1) \leq n/4$ if $n 
eq 2$, $n 
eq 3$ and $G$ is not a $7$-cycle. Hua and Liu recently showed that if $G$ is not a $4$-vertex path or a $4$-cycle or a $9$-cycle, then there exists a subset $D$ of $V(G)$ such that $|D| \leq n/5$ and each component of $G-N^2[D]$ has a universal vertex. We strengthen this result by showing that $\iota_2(G, \mathcal{E}_2) \leq n/5$ if $n 
eq 3$, $n 
eq 4$ and $G$ is not an $8$-cycle or one of five $9$-vertex graphs. It follows that $\iota_2(G, \mathcal{E}_3) \leq n/5$ if $G$ is not a $3$-cycle or a $4$-vertex graph or a $9$-cycle. This also implies the result of Hua and Liu, and that if $\mathcal{C}$ is the set of cycles, then $\iota_2(G, \mathcal{C}) \leq n/5$ unless $G$ is a $3$-cycle or a $4$-vertex graph containing a cycle. All these bounds are sharp.

authors.name: Pawaton Kaemawichanurat
authors.institution: King Mongkut's University of Technology Thonburi

papers.title: Implicit-Reasoning-Enabled Elastic Semantic Communications for AI-Agent Networks
papers.abstract: AI-agent networks introduce new communication demands driven by proactive interactions and autonomous task execution. Existing adaptive semantic communication schemes primarily adjust semantic representations and resource configurations within predefined processing scales and capability sets, which may be insufficient for evolving task requirements. To address this gap, we introduce elastic semantic communications (ESC), a task-driven framework that extends semantic adaptation to the runtime execution and participation of task-supporting capabilities. ESC comprises two complementary dimensions: vertical elasticity adjusts the execution intensity of existing capabilities, while horizontal elasticity reconfigures the participating capability set. The framework connects these dimensions through the expected marginal value of additional information and computation. To realize ESC, we propose an implicit-reasoning-enabled device--edge mechanism that supports variable-depth local inference through shared-parameter state updates and edge-side continuation through wireless transfer of intermediate reasoning states. Experiments on Sudoku-Extreme demonstrate that the benefits of additional inference depend on wireless conditions, while task-aware edge invocation can preserve task accuracy with substantially lower state-transfer overhead.

papers.title: Tunable Multi-Frequency-Band Generator and Detector of AC Signals Based on a Spin Hall Device with Two Antiferromagnetic Layers
papers.abstract: Antiferromagnetic (AFM) spin Hall oscillators offer an electrical route to compact terahertz sources, while AFM spin Hall diodes can be used as a promising detectors of terahertz signals, however, their attainable frequency and the redout efficiency are constrained by the dynamics of a single AFM layer. We theoretically and numerically investigate a spin Hall multilayer junction Pt/AFM/Pt/AFM/Pt comprising two canted AFM layers, driven by independent drive DC currents flowing in the outer platinum (Pt) layers. Using a model based on the coupled Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert-Slonczewski equations for four AFM sublattices and a phase-dependent two-interface spin Hall magnetoresistance model, we show that the device manifests itself as a DC current-driven oscillating spin Hall magnetoresistance. When an additional DC (AC) signal current is applied to the junction, the device generates an output AC (DC) voltage. Our model predicts current-driven, locked, co- and counter-rotational states of the net magnetization at Neel-vector frequencies in the top and bottom AFM layers, respectively. These states result in a multi-frequency response of the spin Hall magnetoresistance at the sum and difference frequencies. The counter-rotation regime additionally activates the phase-sensitive mixing contribution, producing a fourth harmonic. In contrast, the co-rotation regime provides a difference-frequency channel on the order of 100 GHz, although mutual locking prevents this output from being tuned continuously toward zero. Our estimations show that the device matched to an external load can generate output AC power of 1.2 nW at the second harmonic and 0.8 pW at the fourth harmonic, and can produce a DC voltage of about 1 mV for a 6 mA input signal current.

authors.name: Oleh Shtanko
authors.institution: Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv

authors.name: Oleksandr Prokopenko
authors.institution: G.V. Kurdyumov Institute for Metal Physics

papers.title: Group classification and equivalence of two classes of evolution equations of arbitrary order
papers.abstract: We revisit the group classification of the $(1{+}1)$-dimensional evolution equations $u_t=F(u_n)$ and $u_t+uu_x=F(u_n)$ of arbitrary order $n\geq2$, where $u_n=\partial_x^n u$, and describe the usual point equivalence groups of the two classes. We recover the known contact equivalences between the three second-order equations with seven-dimensional maximal Lie invariance algebras and extend the hodograph construction to points where $u_x=0$. For $n>2$, the dimensions of the contact symmetry algebras distinguish the two classes. We give reciprocal transformations linking the two classes at order three and formulate a nonlocal classification problem. We also classify the extensions of the Lie invariance algebra of the Burgers equation in a wider class of Galilei-invariant equations.

papers.title: Relational Semantics and Completeness for Onto-Epistemic Logic
papers.abstract: This paper investigates a relational semantics for onto-epistemic logic with two semi-negations. The frames carry two pairs of quasi-orders and two commuting involutions. Some frames have nondistributive lattices of stable sets. The four- and nine-valued entailments are recovered as joint entailment on two particular finite frames. Sound and complete binary consequence calculi are given for both component entailments and for joint entailment. The joint Lindenbaum algebra embeds subdirectly into the product of its two component quotients. This embedding shows that joint derivability is the intersection of the two component derivability relations. The finite model property is proved using Dedekind-MacNeille completion and a filter-ideal representation of the resulting lattice. All three entailments are decidable by interleaving the search for a derivation with the search for a finite countermodel.

authors.name: Oleg Grigoriev
authors.institution: National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine

papers.title: SEAT: Sign-Type Evidence-Audited Transport for Multi-Label Tongue Diagnosis
papers.abstract: Automated tongue-sign recognition can improve the consistency of non-invasive examinations that otherwise rely on subjective visual judgment. A single tongue image often exhibits multiple coexisting signs characterized by heterogeneous evidence, including localized morphology, global chromaticity, and inter-label dependence. However, existing methods typically rely on shared representations and uniform multi-label heads, making it difficult to verify whether predictions stem from clinically relevant evidence rather than spurious visual correlations. We propose SEAT, an evidence-audited framework that matches distinct evidence types with dedicated prediction and evaluation mechanisms. Built on frozen DINOv2 patch features, SEAT couples mask-guided sign-specific attention for localized morphology, a semi-relaxed optimal transport pathway over LAB/HSV color prototypes to enhance pale-tongue recognition, and a co-occurrence-aware transport regularizer to shape the batch-level predicted label marginal. These components are evaluated through audits matched to their evidence types. On the TongueDx benchmark, SEAT achieves a mean macro-F1 of 72.59 with a standard deviation of 1.04 across six random seeds, with a six-model ensemble reaching 74.15. The ensemble outperforms a backbone-matched baseline and a larger, domain-specialized vision-language model by 8.06 and 2.99 percentage points, respectively. Our results demonstrate that aligning dedicated prediction pathways and audits with sign-specific characteristics improves multi-label accuracy while offering more targeted evidential grounding than uniform post-hoc spatial explanations. Code is available at https://github.com/NEU-TCM-Lab/Sign-type-Evidence-Audited-Transport.

authors.name: Liuyi Xu
authors.institution: National University of Life and Environmental Sciences of Ukraine

authors.name: Zikai Liang
authors.institution: Shanxi University of Finance and Economics

papers.title: Unreasonable Confidence from Simulator Misspecification: Directional Robustness on the SPEED+ Sim-to-Real Benchmark
papers.abstract: Vision-based navigation systems for orbit must be trained almost entirely on synthetic imagery, because real labelled images of a given spacecraft in flight rarely exist. Benchmarks like SPEED+ are built for that situation: the training set comes from a simulator, and the test sets are real images of a satellite mockup under two kinds of lighting. That simulator approximates how light reflects off mylar and aluminium, and like every scientific simulator it is misspecified. Its error is radiometric, since it misses the specular highlights, hard shadows and sensor saturation common in real images. We probe the resulting synthetic-to-real gap, the central risk for such systems, with a deliberately simple monocular pose estimator. In a 2x2 study of backbone adaptation and photometric augmentation, trained on synthetic images and tested on both real hardware-in-the-loop domains, we find three things. (1) The model does not know it is failing: regions conformally calibrated to 90% on synthetic data cover only 9-15% of rotation errors on sunlamp and 21-38% on lightbox, so a wrong pose carries the confidence of a correct one. (2) Transfer is asymmetric: scaling data and features improved synthetic rotation error from 1.65 to 1.03 rad but moved the harshly lit sunlamp domain by only 0.05 rad, under twice its seed s.d., whereas adapting the backbone's last stage carried 63-83% of its extra synthetic gain to both real domains. (3) Once the backbone adapts, augmentation helps only in the direction it models: our photometric stack improved the diffusely lit lightbox domain from 1.17 to 0.99 rad on every seed but moved sunlamp no more than seed-to-seed variation, while with the backbone frozen it helped sunlamp more. Every post-review experiment was pre-registered, and the code, per-image predictions and pre-registration record are at https://github.com/lokindoo/spacecraft-pose-estimation.

authors.name: Nikolay Dolgov
authors.institution: National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine

papers.title: Weak error of approximation of a L\'evy-type process using dynamic cutting
papers.abstract: In this note we consider, on one hand, the implementation of the parametrix method for estimation of the distance between functionals $\Ee^x f(X_t)$ and $\Ee^x f(\widetilde X_t)$ of two L\'evy-type processes $X$ and $\tilde X$. On the other hand, we estimate the weak error appearing by substituting small jumps by a (time-inhomogeneous) diffusion. Both methods rely on the time-dependent cutting procedure, designed to remove small jumps in a time-dependent way.

authors.name: Victoria Knopova
authors.institution: National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine

papers.title: TEMPO: Regime-Aware Operator Learning with Locally Adapted POD Bases
papers.abstract:
Operator learning approximates the solution map of a parametric partial differential equation from data, enabling fast prediction at new parameter values without repeated simulation. The dominant approach fits a single global low-rank basis, typically a proper orthogonal decomposition (POD), to all solution snapshots. This fails when the snapshots span qualitatively different solution shapes, from smooth diffusive profiles to near-discontinuous shocks.
  We propose TEMPO (Trajectory Expectation-Maximization Mixture of POD Operators), a two-phase framework for regime-aware operator learning. In the offline phase, TEMPO recovers latent regimes via expectation-maximization, fitting a dedicated linear or nonlinear basis to each discovered regime. In the online phase, a gating network and per-regime branch networks are trained jointly, routing new inputs to the regimes at inference.
  We test TEMPO on Burgers' flow, Sod shock tubes, Coanda flow, Darcy flow, Navier-Stokes flow and the heterogeneous Helmholtz equation. With 64 total POD modes, TEMPO gives 18.61% test error on Burgers', compared with 19.61% for global POD. It also gives lower errors on Coanda and Helmholtz.

authors.name: Alexander Terentyev
authors.institution: Kyiv National University of Construction and Architecture

papers.title: Concircular Sections Along Submanifolds
papers.abstract: We introduce an equation which generalises that of a concircular vector field to sections of the ambient tangent bundle along submanifolds. Totally umbilic hypersurfaces and various overdetermined systems (such as Obata's and Tashiro's equations) are obtained as specific cases. Given an ambient manifold $M$ and a connected submanifold $P$ of dimension at least $2$, the solution space $W(P;M)$ is shown to have dimension at most $\mathrm{dim } M+1$ with all solutions being of `special type' whenever it exceeds $\mathrm{codim } P+1$. This bound is shown to be sharp. When the submanifold $P$ is simply connected we show the maximum dimension is attained exactly when $P$ has constant sectional curvature $\kappa$ relative to the ambient manifold $M$. In the case of maximum dimension we introduce a bilinear form $\mathbb{I}$ on $W(P;M)$ which is Riemannian, degenerate or Lorentzian, depending on the sign of $\kappa$ and show $P$ immerses into $(W(P;M),\mathbb{I})$'s unit quadric. Hence our main result shows that whenever $P$ is simply connected, has dimension of at least $2$, and has constant curvature $\kappa\neq0$ relative to its ambient manifold $M$, there is an isometric immersion (which we construct explicitly) of $P$ with its metric induced from $M$, into the $\mathrm{dim } M$-dimensional space form of curvature $\kappa$.

papers.title: The length of the longest path in random acyclic orientations of a complete multipartite graph
papers.abstract: We study the distribution of the length of the longest path in a uniformly random acyclic orientation of a complete multipartite graph. We derive an explicit analytic expression for the probability generating function of the longest path length, and, for an arbitrary fixed number of parts of equal size, we apply analytic combinatorics in several variables to obtain asymptotics (as the part size tends toward infinity) for its mean longest path length.

papers.title: Matroid Parity Meets Vertex Splitting
papers.abstract:
A vertex split replaces a vertex by two non-adjacent descendants and partitions its incident edges between them. We study exclusive $\ell$-shallow splitting, where each original vertex has at most $\ell+1$ descendants, with the aim of obtaining a forest, a pseudoforest, or a cluster graph. We consider two natural objectives: minimizing the total number of split operations and minimizing the number of original vertices that are split.
  Our main conceptual contribution is a connection between vertex splitting and matroid parity. For both forests and pseudoforests, we give a characterization of feasible splitting sequences that leads, via weighted linear matroid parity, to polynomial-time algorithms for minimizing the number of split vertices when $\ell=2$. These algorithms are complemented by NP-hardness for every fixed $\ell\ge3$; for pseudoforests, hardness holds even on graphs of maximum degree four.
  The total number of split operations behaves differently: for both sparse target classes, this objective is polynomial-time solvable for every $\ell$, using matroid intersection. For cluster graphs, both objectives admit linear-time algorithms when $\ell=1$ and are NP-hard for every fixed $\ell\ge2$. Together, these results identify how the target class, the local splitting bound, and the choice of objective determine the complexity of vertex splitting.

papers.title: Multivariable $(\varphi, N)$-modules and $(\varphi, N_\nabla)$-modules
papers.abstract: The goal of this article is to introduce the category of effective filtered multivariable $(\varphi, N)$-modules and the category of multivariable $(\varphi, N_\nabla)$-modules of finite $E_{\Delta}$-height over the rigid-analytic open polydisk $\mathcal{O}_{\Delta}$, and to establish an exact tensor equivalence between them. This generalizes Kisin's analytic classification of filtered $(\varphi, N)$-modules and provides the rigid-analytic foundation for multivariable $p$-adic Hodge theory.

papers.title: Evaluating Near-Perfect Accuracy Claims in Machine-Learning-Based Leak Detection for Two-Phase Pipelines: A Condition-Blocked Audit
papers.abstract: Reliable leak detection in gas-liquid two-phase pipelines is important for process safety, yet machine-learning studies frequently report near-perfect performance using evaluation protocols that may not represent deployment to unseen operating conditions. This study audits a pressure-based leak-detection model using condition-blocked leave-one-condition-out validation, in which the classifier is tested on a flow condition excluded from training. Accuracy decreased from 93.3% under within-condition evaluation to 59.1% across fifteen unseen-condition tests. Ablation analysis showed that most of this difference arose from the data-splitting protocol, with a smaller contribution from encoding operating conditions as model inputs. Under condition-blocked evaluation, the false-alarm and missed-detection rates increased to 34.1% and 10.2%, respectively, demonstrating that near-perfect reported accuracy did not translate into reliable operation at unseen flow conditions. The reduction persisted across all evaluated classifiers, indicating that it was caused by the evaluation design rather than a particular model architecture. Grouped evaluation of an independent acoustic pipeline dataset produced a comparable reduction toward chance-level performance. These findings show that validation units must represent the conditions encountered during deployment. Condition-blocked evaluation and explicit reporting of operational error rates are therefore necessary before machine-learning leak detectors can support process-safety decisions.

papers.title: Second-Order Threshold and Value Asymptotics in Multiple-Stopping Secretary Problems
papers.abstract: We study the classical secretary problem with a fixed number of selection opportunities. We derive explicit corrections to the limiting thresholds and to the optimal success probability. A cancellation identity removes the influence of later threshold rounding from the first correction, while a Poisson representation explains its probabilistic meaning. Every bounded rounding of the limiting thresholds shares the first value correction. We obtain integer rounding laws, eventual threshold identities along continued-fraction convergents, and joint rounding frequencies. Rigorous rational bounds show that the first eleven corrections are positive and the twelfth is negative, producing the first shifted convergent identity.

authors.name: Raul Sanchez Galan
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology

papers.title: A conic optimization framework for shape-constrained functional regression analysis
papers.abstract: Standard regression methods do not always guarantee that the estimated model reflects prior knowledge about how predictors relate to the response, which motivates constrained regression. When the effects to be estimated are smooth nonlinear functions, a natural family of constraints is that of shape constraints, such as sign, monotonicity, or curvature, which encode qualitative properties that these functions are often expected to satisfy. While shape-constrained estimation of smooth functions is well established in classical regression with scalar covariates and response, its extension to functional regression, where the coefficients are themselves functions, remains largely unexplored. In this paper, we propose the functional shape-constrained conic P-spline estimator (FunSCOPE), a unified framework for shape-constrained functional linear regression that covers scalar-on-function, function-on-scalar, and function-on-function models, and in which any combination of the shapes above can be imposed on the functional regression coefficient. Building on a P-spline approach, the desired shapes are expressed as conditions on the scalar regression coefficients, which leads to an estimation problem formulated as a conic optimization problem. For univariate coefficients, as in scalar-on-function, function-on-scalar, and a particular case of the function-on-function regression, the concurrent case, these conditions are both necessary and sufficient, in contrast to existing approaches, which provide only sufficient conditions; for bivariate coefficients, as in general function-on-function models, they are neither necessary nor sufficient. Numerical experiments show that FunSCOPE outperforms competing methods in terms of estimation error and computational time.

papers.title: Far-field prediction of algebraic curves via generalized asymptotes
papers.abstract: The asymptotic behavior of algebraic curves is classically described by means of linear asymptotes. However, many infinite branches exhibit a non-linear behavior that cannot be represented accurately by straight lines. In this paper we propose a computational framework for far-field prediction of algebraic curves based on generalized asymptotes. Starting from the asymptotic expansion of a real branch at infinity, we retain its non-decaying terms in order to construct an algebraic surrogate, which is then used as an adaptive far-field model outside a sufficiently large compact region. We introduce explicit discrepancy indicators and a switching radius that determine when the exact branch may be replaced by its generalized asymptotic predictor. The framework recovers the classical linear asymptote whenever the latter exists, while remaining effective for branches with polynomial or Puiseux-type dominant behavior. In the implicit setting, we prove algebraicity and compatibility properties of the predictor and derive asymptotic error estimates from the first neglected term of the expansion. A residual certificate distinguishes guaranteed finite-tail replacement from asymptotic radius estimates. Tangential tails, slow decay, and a smooth transition rule clarify the limitations of truncation. Reproducible finite-window tests compare the predictors with fitted polynomial baselines; these tests are not a benchmark of a complete plotting system.

papers.title: Unstable Periodic Orbit Localization in a Nonlinear System-Environment Model
papers.abstract:
The role of unstable periodic orbits (UPOs) is investigated in the chaotic dynamics of a nonlinear system-environment model composed of a central two-level system coupled to an environment of two-level systems. Families of UPOs embedded in chaotic regions are identified and their local instability is characterized. Their behavior is examined under variations of the environment size, energy, and system symmetry, allowing the model to serve as a controlled testbed in which the dimensionality and dynamical conditions can be systematically modified.
  Characteristic UPO-based dynamical quantities are used to assess the influence of these periodic orbits on nearby chaotic trajectories, including occupation of the UPO tube, its persistence at late times, return fidelity enhancement, and recurrence timing. Across the different model variations considered, trajectories initialized close to the UPOs retain statistically detectable spatial and temporal signatures associated with the periodic orbits. These results indicate that unstable periodic orbits can retain a measurable organizing influence on surrounding chaotic trajectories across changes in dimensionality, energy, and system symmetry, giving rise to scar-like dynamical signatures in a simple nonlinear system--environment model.

papers.title: Dataset Distillation for Handwritten Text Recognition: An Empirical Study
papers.abstract: Dataset distillation (DD) replaces large training datasets with smaller synthetic ones to reduce computational costs. While traditionally used for classification, we present, to our knowledge, the first DD study for line-level handwritten text recognition (HTR). Unlike classification tasks, which use discrete labels, HTR employs unaligned sequences from a virtually infinite output space as labels. To adapt classification-based DD methods to this scenario, we define text pseudo-classes by clustering transcriptions based on character n-grams. We adapt gradient matching (GM), distribution matching (DM) and trajectory matching (MTT) to a Convolutional Recurrent Neural Network (CRNN) trained with Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC). In this process, synthetic line images are generated by optimising only the pixels of real starting lines (either randomly chosen or selected as text medoids), while keeping their original transcriptions fixed. Across four datasets (IAM, George Washington, READ\,2016, LAM) and three budgets (1--10\,\% of the training lines), no distilled set outperforms its real initialisation lines. Random lines prove better than medoids, and further optimisation only degrades recognition. Methodologically, DM lowers its objective without benefit, while GM and MTT barely move theirs. We turn these findings into guidelines for evaluating data compression in HTR.

papers.title: The ordered sum-rank metric and linearized multiplicity codes: NRT meets sum-rank
papers.abstract: In this work, we introduce linearized multiplicity codes, which are a common generalization of linearized Reed--Solomon codes and univariate multiplicity codes. We also introduce the ordered sum-rank metric, which is a common generalization of the sum-rank metric and the Niederreiter-Rosenbloom-Tsfasman (NRT) metric (or ordered Hamming metric). We provide a Singleton bound for the ordered sum-rank metric and show that linearized multiplicity codes attain it. That is, they are maximum ordered sum-rank distance (MOSRD) codes. We introduce the support lattice for the ordered sum-rank metric and study duality, support distributions and weight distributions of MOSRD codes. We also show that MOSRD codes are ordered MDS, dually quasi MSRD and, under some divisibility conditions, MSRD (and thus MDS). For linear MOSRD codes, we give lower bounds on the field extension degree by the number of matrix columns, and upper bounds on the block length by the base field size. We conclude by showing that linearized multiplicity codes attain such bounds exactly in almost all cases, and the same growth order in all cases.

papers.title: A Bleichenbacher bit-by-bit oracle attack from partial message knowledge
papers.abstract: Oracle attacks show the importance of a correct implementation of cryptographic standards when translated into code. A notable example is the Bleichenbacher attack on RSA with PKCS#1 v1.5 padding and all the improvements that have been suggested over the decades. This paper shows how an attacker knowing a few least significant bytes of an RSA message can take advantage of a server with an oracle side-channel to decrypt the full message bit by bit. We will consider two oracles that can be tested with chosen ciphertexts: one revealing whether the decrypted message starts with the 00 02 bytes and a second one revealing if the decrypted message is fully PKCS compliant. For an attacker knowing the three least significant bytes of the message, the first oracle provides an attack where one oracle call gives the next least significant bit of the message and the second an attack which requires, with high probability, a small constant number of oracle calls to the oracle, with a constant which depends on the length of the message and the desired probability of success. The attack divides the message bits into two sections, one with the known part and one with the unknown part, and then chooses transformations that will keep the unknown part, except for the last unknown bit, orders of magnitude below the integer coming from the known part. The resulting string either gives a valid padding or not depending on the value of the unknown bit. The attacker can minimize the number of oracle calls at the cost of some local computation. Finally, the same method is adapted to show how it can also be used to extract the few least significant bytes of the message with an increased cost where the main complexity is finding a second valid message with a correct padding starting from the original captured ciphertext.

papers.title: Schur multipliers, vanishing minors and Gaussian conditional independence
papers.abstract: Conditional independence in a Gaussian vector is the vanishing of almost-principal minors of its covariance matrix $\Sigma$. A sensitivity analysis replaces $\Sigma$ by the Schur product $\Delta\circ\Sigma$, where the symmetric multiplier $\Delta$ differs from one exactly at the changed positions. Such a change generally destroys some conditional independences, and we determine which minors stay zero. A vanishing minor is preserved for every matrix exactly when the corresponding block of $\Delta$ has rank one. When variances or covariances change, each almost-principal minor of $\Delta\circ\Sigma$ is a polynomial in the amounts added, with minors of $\Sigma$ as coefficients, and a conditional independence survives every such change exactly when they vanish. In an undirected graphical model, changing variances joins the neighbours of the perturbed vertices, while changing covariances leaves a structure read from the graph by a separation rule, possibly not graphical. Both extend to ancestral graphs, directed acyclic graphs included, and identify the entries that can vary freely. For the other entries, blocks of rank one along a junction tree characterize the multipliers that preserve a decomposable model. A sensitivity analysis can therefore rest on the conditional independence structure after the change, as illustrated on examination marks of 88 students.

papers.title: GHySSeg: Real-Time Geometric Ground and Road Segmentation for Hybrid Solid-State LiDAR
papers.abstract: Hybrid solid-state LiDAR sensors are making their way into production vehicles, yet the data they produce differs structurally from that of the established spinning mechanical sensors behind today's autonomous-driving datasets: it is ring-free, dense, cluttered, and concentrated in a frontal field of view. The classical geometric methods that autonomous vehicles rely on for drivable space computation and navigation assume the ordered ring-and-column structure of a 360-degree spinning LiDAR and degrade or fail on this data, while learned alternatives are computationally heavy, hard to certify, and trained almost exclusively on spinning-LiDAR data. We demonstrate that the same dense, per-curve geometry is instead an opportunity to close the divide between the industry's preferred sensors and autonomous-driving research. We present GHySSeg, a purely geometric method that segments ground and drivable road from a single hybrid solid-state LiDAR frame by tracing each scan curve and reading two geometric signatures, a step in height and a fold-back in range, with no training and no graphics processing unit. To evaluate it, we release HySoLiD-Drive, the first public benchmark dedicated to ground and road segmentation on an automotive hybrid solid-state LiDAR, comprising 100 manually labeled and 7000 unlabeled frames recorded by two vehicles in real driving. On this benchmark, GHySSeg surpasses both geometric and learned state-of-the-art baselines across ground and road segmentation, reaching an intersection-over-union of 0.907 for road and 0.896 for ground at over 0.96 precision, while running in real time at about 22 milliseconds per frame on a single core.

papers.title: On $z_{2M}(21,4)$: the Hole Extensions of the Chen--Chen Configuration Are Reducible, and the Extremal Configurations of $z_2(21,4)$ Are Not Unique
papers.abstract: The second order extended Zarankiewicz number $z_{2M}(m,n)$ of Qi and Yu allows a secondary half of a $2$-edge to be shared, while the $1$-edge graph stays $C_4$-free and extremal and $1$-edges and main halves stay exclusive. Whether $z_{2M}(21,4)=55$ is open. Since deleting a $2$-edge removes exactly one displayed square, $z_{2M}(21,4)=55$ if and only if there is no irreducible admissible configuration with exactly $56$ displayed squares, and by the cell count of Qi and Yu and the heredity of irreducibility such a configuration without empty cells is an extremal $55$-square configuration of $z_2(21,4)$ plus one $2$-edge at its hole. For the extremal configuration of Chen and Chen we show, by certificates verified in exact rational arithmetic, that all $56$ such extensions have SOS rank at most $55$: $32$ by product relations and $24$ by contraction certificates of Xu--Yan type. We also show, with computer-assisted certificates and an exhaustive isomorphism search, that the extremal configurations of $z_2(21,4)$ fall into at least six isomorphism classes; Chen and Chen leave the structural classification of extremal augmented graphs open. Finally we prove a six-to-four reduction. For irreducible configurations whose $1$-edge graph is $C_4$-free with $m+\binom n2$ edges it bounds the multiplicity of a shared half by $n(n-1)$ ($12$ at $21\times4$), and it applies directly to an explicit number of the extensions of any extremal configuration of $z_2(21,4)$, eight for that of Chen and Chen, bringing each to at most $54$ squares, in agreement with the certificates. The cell count, the heredity lemma, the rows lemma, the six-to-four identity and a $2\times2$ example are checked in Isabelle/HOL; the remaining arguments are written proofs.

authors.name: Gaohang Yu
authors.institution: Zhejiang University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Simulations of turbulent heat and particle transport in stellarator plasmas
papers.abstract:
Achieving sustained energy production in magnetic confinement fusion reactors requires a deep understanding of turbulent transport of heat and particles. This thesis investigates turbulent transport with a particular emphasis on stellarators, using simulations with the $\delta f$ gyrokinetic code stella for the W7-X, LHD, TJ-II and NCSX stellarators, the ASDEX Upgrade (AUG) tokamak and the Cyclone Base Case (CBC). It addresses two questions: how do density gradients affect turbulent heat transport, and can turbulence help retain particles in the plasma core?
  In the first part, an inter-machine study shows a strong reduction of the ion heat flux in NCSX and W7-X with increasing density gradients, attributed to the stabilization of ion-temperature-gradient-driven modes without significantly destabilizing trapped-electron modes or universal instabilities. This beneficial effect is absent in tokamaks, where the heat flux increases with the density gradient, highlighting the role of magnetic geometry. The ion heat flux in stellarators does not follow the growth rate of the fastest-growing linear mode, underscoring the importance of nonlinear effects. Trapped-electron modes dominate in CBC, AUG, TJ-II, LHD and NCSX, while passing-particle-driven universal instabilities contribute significantly in W7-X.
  The second part addresses the long-standing discrepancy between the strongly hollow density profiles predicted by neoclassical theory in large stellarators and the flat or weakly peaked profiles measured in W7-X. Nonlinear simulations and a particle balance analysis show that turbulence provides a robust inward particle flux, driven by finite ion and electron temperature gradients, that can account for the observed profiles: the sign of the turbulent particle flux matches the sign of the discrepancy between the experimental and neoclassical fluxes across the entire plasma radius of W7-X.

authors.name: Hanne Thienpondt
authors.institution: Centro de Investigaciones Energéticas, Medioambientales y Tecnológicas

papers.title: Steering Bayesian Inference and Decisions through Data Poisoning
papers.abstract: Adversarial machine learning has revealed that statistical models can be manipulated through poisoned data, and Bayesian inference is no exception. Earlier work has shown that subtle poisoning attacks can drive the posterior toward a distribution of the attacker's choosing. Such posterior attraction attacks require a fully specified target posterior; however, attackers typically care about only a few posterior quantities or, more consequentially, about a downstream decision. Herein, we study how an attacker can alter Bayesian inference and decisions by deleting or replicating a few observations, chosen to minimize the maximum mean discrepancy between the resulting posterior and a target distribution. A suitable kernel lets the attacker steer selected posterior moments without specifying the rest of the target. Because Bayes actions depend on the posterior only through expected utilities, which are themselves posterior moments, the same approach can target a decision directly. We construct the attacks with a gradient-based heuristic that requires only posterior samples, and analyze its convergence. Experiments with regression and hierarchical models compare moment-based and full-posterior attacks, and illustrate how deleting a handful of observations can flip a Bayesian decision.

papers.title: EasyNav: A Modular Architecture for Real-Time Navigation Across Heterogeneous Robot Environments
papers.abstract: Most robot navigation stacks implicitly bind mapping, localization, planning, and control to specific representations and data flows, yielding architectures hard to extend, compare experimentally, or reason about end-to-end timing. This is critical in heterogeneous scenarios, where multiple spatial representations, sensing modalities, and coordinate frames coexist and evolve at different rates. This paper presents a navigation architecture centered on an explicit, shared navigation state that serves as the sole interaction interface between modular components. Constraining mapping, localization, planning, and control to operate over this shared state enables interchangeable, representation-agnostic pipelines under explicit compatibility and timing contracts. We realize this architecture as EasyNav, an open source ROS 2 framework, and validate it through real-robot experiments, including indoor navigation with laser sensing and large-scale indoor-outdoor navigation with GPS and 3D LiDAR across multi-level routes. Compared with Nav2 under matched conditions, EasyNav reduces reaction latency from 377 to 33 ms indoors and from 71 to 8 ms outdoors, while also using less CPU and memory.

papers.title: Connectivity from activity in spiking neural networks
papers.abstract: We show that a wide range of recurrent neural network models obey a simple set of equations tying synaptic connectivity and single-cell response properties to neural correlations. Our modeling framework considers networks in a stationary, asynchronous state and contains a broad class of synaptic filters, spiking nonlinearities, and random-plus-structured connectivity. The resulting equations naturally decompose into contributions from monosynaptic, disynaptic, and higher order paths through the network. We leverage this decomposition to express the effective monosynaptic connection between two neurons in terms of experimentally measurable statistics of the activity, and in particular, their high-frequency correlations. In this way, we show that it is possible to recover network connectivity from neural activity.

papers.title: Multicollinearity diagnosis in generalized linear models: A systematic review and empirical reassessment
papers.abstract: Ridge-type estimators are widely used to address multicollinearity in generalized linear models (GLMs), yet their empirical justification depends heavily on how multicollinearity is diagnosed. Following systematic review guidelines, we conduct a citation-based review of 120 real-data applications to examine current diagnostic practices. The findings reveal a lack of consensus across studies: approaches vary regarding data transformation prior to diagnosis, applying transformations to either the design matrix or the weighted information matrix, while others omit transformation entirely. Nevertheless, the condition number emerges as the most widely used diagnostic. We review existing methodologies for computing the condition number in GLMs and recommend the optimal approach, as it uniquely attains its minimum value under orthogonality while retaining the intercept. Finally, these formulations are implemented in R and used to replicate five real-data applications from the literature.

papers.title: Zero-Shot Weight-Space Programming for Prediction and Classification of Target Variables in Structured Datasets
papers.abstract: Weight-space programming fixes every parameter of a feed-forward network by hand, with no gradient descent anywhere in the construction. Every demonstration so far starts from a target function handed to the model as a rule system, making it a compilation problem. A supervised dataset withholds that specification, so the procedure must do the statistical inference itself and then express the result in the parameterisation it was given. We ask whether a large language model can do both. It is shown a small dataset in full, with the architecture of a feed-forward network, and writes out every weight and bias as a literal number, with no optimizer, no gradient, no code execution, and no chance to evaluate it first. Each construction is sealed and pre-registers its expected score. The graded suite runs from two toy problems, through nine synthetic problems disguised by a hidden rotation, to the classical benchmarks and one real engineering regression. The frozen network matches the closed-form optimum wherever that optimum is linear, reaches the irreducible error of the generating process on three rungs where it is not, and beats every fitted baseline on two of those, including the same architecture trained by gradient descent. It fails on two rungs, both times because the structure to be found is oblique to the coordinates it analysed. Three further constructors separate two failure modes a single score conflates: one returns no parameter vector at all on the hardest rungs, another delivers everywhere while writing networks worse than predicting the mean. One of those failures proves avoidable: another constructor solves the oblique-hinge rung by a margin that survives multiple-comparison correction. What predicts whether the hidden layer earns its keep is the training error of a linear separator, which the composite complexity index misses.

papers.title: AC Assessment of DC Power Flow Screening for Data Center Hosting Capacity and Siting
papers.abstract: A screening procedure based on direct current (DC) power flow estimates the data center hosting capacity of a candidate bus, termed the DC-screened capacity, and selects the generator commitment that supports it. This paper assesses that estimate under the alternating current (AC) network model. With the selected commitment fixed, an AC optimal power flow reoptimizes dispatch and voltages to find the largest data center load the bus can carry, termed the AC-assessed capacity. On a synthetic Texas system with 123 buses, the DC-screened capacity exceeds the AC-assessed capacity at 113 buses. Across all 123, the ratio of DC-screened to AC-assessed capacity has a median of 143% (a 43% overestimate) and a maximum of 1,070%. At these 113 buses, the DC-screened capacity violates a branch apparent power limit or a generator reactive power limit in the AC model, two limits the DC model omits. The overestimate changes decisions: a 1-GW project passes DC screening at every bus but exceeds the AC-assessed capacity at 37, and the bus ranked first by DC screening has 205.5 MW less AC-assessed capacity than the bus ranked second. Reporting the AC-assessed capacity beside each DC-screened capacity lets planners reject oversized projects or choose better sites.

authors.name: Xingpeng Li
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: DiffWAM: Learning World Action Model from Consecutive Visual Difference
papers.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) have emerged as an important paradigm in robot learning, jointly predicting future scene states and robot actions from current observations and instructions. However, future states entangle task-related changes with large amounts of task-irrelevant content, such as static backgrounds, which weakens the model's ability to capture changes relevant to task execution. To address this, we propose Difference World Action Model (DiffWAM), a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) framework that enhances world representations by jointly learning future-state prediction and consecutive visual difference prediction. We define consecutive visual differences as differences between the latent representations of consecutive observations, providing an explicit learning signal for temporal variation. The framework comprises a World Expert for future frame prediction, an Action Expert for action generation, and a Diff Expert for predicting these latent differences along the trajectory. A structured unidirectional attention mask conditions the Diff, World, and Action Experts solely on the current-frame representation while blocking attention between experts. This design allows both the World and Diff Experts to be removed during inference, introducing no additional inference overhead. DiffWAM achieves state-of-the-art performance on the LIBERO and RoboTwin 2.0 benchmarks and substantially improves over FastWAM on real-world manipulation tasks. Specifically, it attains average success rates of 98.8%, 92.65%, and 88.3%, outperforming the state-of-the-art baseline (i.e., FastWAM) by 1.75, 1.55, and 15.0 percentage points, respectively.

authors.name: Haoyu Xiong
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Large pseudo-orbital magnetic moment of magnons in CrI$_3$ nanotubes
papers.abstract: Recently discovered CrI$_3$ nanotubes are expected to host unusual radial magnetic order states, on account of the strong out-of-plane magnetic anisotropy of the two-dimensional parent material. The detection of these peculiar magnetic states is challenging, and motivates the quest for unique features that can be probed experimentally. Using linear spin-wave theory, we show that an axial magnetic field tilts the radial phase into a conical one that threads the tube with an Aharonov-Bohm flux for magnons. This flux endows magnons with a pseudo-orbital magnetic moment, reaching approximately six Bohr magnetons, three times conventional magnon spin moment, and therefore detectable through magnon spectroscopy, providing a smoking gun for the radial and conical magnetic order in CrI$_3$ nanotubes.

papers.title: On the planar four-junction solution to a vector-valued Allen-Cahn system
papers.abstract: This paper concerns entire minimizing four-junction solutions to a two-dimensional Allen-Cahn system with a four-well potential. In a suitable regime of unequal surface tensions, the construction yields a family of solutions with varying opening angles of phase sectors. The proof employs two-direction slicing arguments for tight energy bounds and localization of the diffuse interface, together with a new iteration scheme that controls change of approximating sharp interfaces at successively smaller scales.

authors.name: Nicholas D. Alikakos
authors.institution: National and Kapodistrian University of Athens

papers.title: A feedback-driven central limit theorem with $q$-Gaussian limits
papers.abstract: We establish a central limit theorem, the feedback-driven central limit theorem, for sums whose summands are independent noise variables multiplied by an amplitude that depends on the preceding normalized sum $y$. The summands are martingale differences whose conditional variance, $c+b\,y^{2}$, depends quadratically on $y$, with feedback strength $b$; unlike in the martingale central limit theorem, this conditional variance does not settle to a constant. The noise has finite variance; for positive feedback we assume, as in Lyapunov's theorem, a finite third moment, and for negative feedback bounded noise, so that the conditional variance stays nonnegative. For positive feedback, the normalized sum converges to a Student law, equivalently a $q$-Gaussian with $1<q<2$, independently of the noise distribution. For negative feedback, it converges to a compactly supported density, which is a $q$-Gaussian with $q<1$ when $-\tfrac12<b<0$. The Gaussian law, $q=1$, is recovered at zero feedback, while the Cauchy law, $q=2$, is obtained only as a limiting case, in a triangular array in which the feedback grows slowly with the number of terms. Thus every $q<2$ is obtained for a fixed feedback strength, and $q=2$ as a limit. We further show that the balance identity behind the theorem singles out quadratic feedback: a $q$-Gaussian with $q<2$ satisfies it only for a quadratic conditional variance, and no $q$-Gaussian with $2\le q<3$ satisfies it for any conditional variance. The proofs use the method of moments for negative feedback and a Wasserstein coupling argument for positive feedback, including cases in which the limiting variance is infinite.

papers.title: A description of the space with no separable quotient presented by OpenAI
papers.abstract: OpenAI recently presented a remarkable solution to the longstanding separable quotient problem in Banach space theory. The result establishes its independence from ZFC, relative to the consistency of ZFC with a measurable cardinal. Under the continuum hypothesis, the paper constructs a nonseparable Banach space $X$ with no separable infinite-dimensional quotient. The present paper offers an alternative exposition of the mechanism leading to $X$ and its properties. Our aim is to make the methods and results more accessible and to offer a clearer understanding of this exotic space.

papers.title: LiNO: Lightweight Network for Occupancy Estimation
papers.abstract: Occupancy estimation for automated vehicles is a crucial task that builds a 3D map using vehicle sensors. This map allows the vehicle to identify drivable areas and various obstacle classes. The task involves complex subtasks such as depth estimation, object classification, and segmentation to align semantic information with the 3D grid. Moreover, producing these estimations from multiple sensors demands significant computational power and memory, as high-dimensional data fusion requires complex feature extraction and processing. Consequently, most existing methods rely on large and computationally intensive architectures that are not suitable for real-time or real-world applications. We present a real-time, lightweight architecture that leverages camera and radar sensors through a residual multi-stage head. Unlike prior methods that rely on heavy camera-only blocks, our architecture employs camera-radar fusion and lightweight components. Additionally, we introduce a task-specific data augmentation strategy that enhances data diversity and improves generalisation. Our method achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance, attaining 45.7 mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) on Occ3D and 41.9 Ray-level Intersection over Union (RayIoU) (41.9) on OpenOcc datasets, running at 17.2 frames per second (FPS) and using only 5.3 GB of memory, compared with 4.1 FPS and 7.7 GB for STCOcc.

papers.title: ReactBench-AD: Do Driving VLAs and World-Action Models React to Imminent Hazards in Their Path?
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) and World-Action Models (WAMs) have emerged in autonomous driving with the promise of strong generalization to long-tail scenarios. Although these models achieve state-of-the-art results on autonomous driving benchmarks, most existing benchmarks are dominated by nominal scenarios and therefore cannot test this promise. To test one such long-tail capability that is critical for safety, we introduce ReactBench-AD, a benchmark that measures how driving models react to objects that appear in the ego vehicle's path. Built on real NAVSIM and PhysicalAI-Autonomous-Vehicles scenes, ReactBench-AD composites a crossing pedestrian, a standing pedestrian, or a stationary car consistently across all camera views and history frames. Each edited scene thus forms an exact, pixel-level counterfactual pair with its original, which allows us to isolate the causal effect of the inserted object on the predicted trajectory. Evaluating four VLAs and two WAMs, we find that they react weakly, often barely at all. Finally, we test how easily one of the evaluated VLAs, ReCogDrive, can be taught to brake hard for imminent hazards: a short fine-tuning stage on edited scenes substantially improves its reactions, with the learned behavior generalizing to unseen objects and fully real scenes, at minimal cost to nominal driving. These results call into question the out-of-the-box long-tail capabilities of these models, but suggest that they can be a strong foundation for acquiring them with little additional training, highlighting the value of real or synthetic data that demonstrates the long-tail behaviors nominal datasets rarely contain. Code and data will be made publicly available.

papers.title: Optimal Operating-Point Selection for Single-Linearization Trajectory Planning of Nonlinear Robot Manipulators
papers.abstract: Single-point linearization provides a computationally efficient basis for optimization-based trajectory planning of nonlinear robot manipulators. However, planning performance depends on the selected linearization point. This paper presents an offline performance-driven approach that treats the location of a single linearization as an optimization variable. Candidate operating points are sampled from a common cubic seed trajectory, and each corresponding affine model is used to solve an identical constrained finite-horizon quadratic program (QP). The resulting control sequences are executed on the original nonlinear dynamics, and the operating point minimizing the nonlinear trajectory objective is selected through grid search and bounded refinement. Evaluation on four point-to-point motions of a three-degree-of-freedom UR5 manipulator yields optimal normalized operating-point locations between 0.325 and 0.935, demonstrating trajectory-dependent selection. Compared with the best-performing conventional initial, midpoint, or terminal linearization, the proposed approach reduces the nonlinear trajectory objective by 17-18%, 21-22%, 37-38%, and 7-8% across the four tasks, respectively. Additional nonlinear execution with identical PID feedback correction confirms that the performance advantage persists for a representative task. These results demonstrate that systematic operating-point selection can substantially improve single-linearization trajectory planning while preserving a fixed affine planning model.

papers.title: Null flag curvature of anisotropically conformal pseudo-Finsler metrics
papers.abstract: We consider the Zermelo navigation problem for a time-dependent Finsler metric, which can be recast as the study of lightlike geodesics of a Lorentz--Finsler metric on a non-relativistic spacetime. To control how such geodesics separate, we introduce a null flag curvature, defined for any pseudo-Finsler metric with a lightlike cone, and show that it governs the Taylor expansion of the norm of a Jacobi field. We then prove a formula relating the null flag curvatures of two anisotropically conformal pseudo-Finsler metrics. Applying it to the spacetime associated with a time-independent Randers metric, which is anisotropically conformal to a stationary spacetime, we obtain compact expressions for the flag curvature of Randers metrics, both in terms of their $(\alpha,\beta)$ data and of their Zermelo data $(h,W)$. These expressions allow us to compute explicitly the flag curvature when $W$ is conformal, affine or projective, and when $\alpha$ is a K\"ahler metric. We also introduce a Weyl-type curvature, invariant under anisotropic conformal changes, whose vanishing characterizes Finsler manifolds of scalar flag curvature, and we obtain the flag curvature of $F + \mathrm{d}f$, showing in particular that $F$ has scalar flag curvature if and only if $F + \mathrm{d}f$ does.

papers.title: VAHBench: A Harness Benchmark for Agentic Long-Video Generation
papers.abstract: AI agents are commonly used for everyday information retrieval and coding. We ask whether they can also interpret human requests and turn them into complete videos. We introduce VAHBench, a benchmark that tests this ability through five short-drama briefs specifying story, characters, dialogue and duration. Agents plan and carry out production using shared generation tools. Evaluation combines video completeness and basic quality with checks of production reliability and reporting accuracy. Across 240 runs covering 48 configurations of general-purpose and video-specific agents, higher quality scores do not necessarily mean more complete delivery. Missing episodes, repeated footage and static filler reveal gaps between producing a video file and fulfilling the brief. Added composition tools help some agents but do not consistently improve performance. VAHBench measures how well agents translate user intent into finished video content and helps identify where that process breaks down.

papers.title: A note on distributive lattices with a commutative generalized implication
papers.abstract: We study distributive lattices with an ideal-valued generalized implication satisfying a commutativity identity. This class extends commutative weak Heyting algebras by allowing implication values to be non-principal ideals. We characterize its intersection with several known classes of gi-lattices, study gi-deductive systems and their relationship with gi-filters and gi-congruences, and extend the relational characterization of commutativity to this setting. The resulting correspondence yields a Priestley-style duality by restricting the established duality for gi-lattices.

authors.name: Sergio Celani
authors.institution: Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas

papers.title: Asymptotics for a continuous-time risk model with multivariate strongly regularly varying claims and stochastic investment returns
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the finite-time asymptotic behavior of the entrance probability of the discounted aggregate claims into an extreme region in a multidimensional risk model. Our non-standard risk model is not restricted to the Levy-Renewal framework, that represents a usual assumption for the stochastic returns and the counting process of the claim vectors, respectively. For the modeling of the distribution of claim vectors, we introduce the notion of set-based multivariate (strongly) regularly varying distributions. For the new set-based classes we provide certain closure properties and some examples to show the difference from the usual definitions of multivariate regularly varying distributions. This set-based framework provides a broad and flexible framework to the actuarial applications, and facilitates the modeling of dependence among the claim vectors that arrive at different time epochs. The two main results of the paper establish a unified asymptotic expression, that demonstrates the presence of multivariate linear single big jump principle. Despite of the assumptions the asymptotic expression remains explicit. In the first main result we suppose that the common distribution of the claim vectors belongs to the class of set-based multivariate regularly varying distributions, and the stochastic returns satisfy a general moment condition. In the second main result, we restrict the claim vectors in the class of setbased multivariate strongly regularly varying distributions, relaxing the moment condition on the stochastic returns. Finally, we conduct a numerical study to illustrate the accuracy of the proposed asymptotic approximation and investigate its sensitivity to the main model parameters.

papers.title: SpecRelay: Amortize or Avoid the Round Trip in Edge-Cloud Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract: Edge-cloud speculative decoding moves autoregressive drafting to an edge device while a larger cloud model verifies draft tokens in parallel, so that edge drafting and cloud verification overlap under a synchronous draft-verify schedule. Beyond low-latency local networks, however, the next verification request of that schedule can be sent only after the previous reply arrives, so every round still waits out a full round trip, and throughput falls as the network RTT grows. To recover this loss, we present SpecRelay, an edge-cloud LLM inference system that addresses this cost at two levels: it amortizes round trips when cloud verification is necessary and avoids them when local reasoning suffices. For cloud-bound queries, an asynchronous verification pipeline keeps fixed-budget draft trees in flight while earlier replies are still outstanding, and the cloud rejects stale requests before the target-model forward pass (the asynchronous schedule). At the query level, an RTT-conditioned router (the Latency-Aware Router) estimates quality and completion latency for three on-device modes (direct generation, Chain-of-Draft, and full reasoning) and cloud speculative decoding, selecting among them under a configurable accuracy-latency objective without adding latency during inference, since the router runs concurrently with the draft-model prefill. The asynchronous schedule alone improves decoding throughput by up to 50% over a reproduced synchronous baseline across multiple benchmarks. At matched target-model accuracy and 250 ms of added round-trip latency, the full system with the router delivers 1.95x and 1.55x the throughput of the same baseline on SPROUT and OlympiadBench, respectively, while sending only 47% and 39% of the queries to the cloud.

authors.name: Duc N. M Hoang
authors.institution: Institut National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Smoothing of the Coupled KdV System on \mathbb{T}
papers.abstract:
We study the nonlinear smoothing properties of the Coupled KdV system posed on the torus. This system arises as a particular case of the four-parameter family of Boussinesq systems studied by Bona, Chen and Saut, corresponding to the choice $\eta^{2}=\frac{2}{3}$, $b=d=0$ and $a=c=\frac{1}{6}$. Although the similarities with the periodic KdV equation and the favorable resonance structure of the Majda-Biello system for the coupling parameter $\alpha =-1$ might suggest that smoothing can be established by a relatively straightforward adaptation of existing techniques, the nonlinear interactions in the Coupled KdV system introduce additional difficulties. In particular, certain mixed interactions lead to degeneracies in the associated resonance functions, resulting in a loss of frequency decay that restricts the attainable smoothing gain. By combining normal-form reductions, duality arguments and Bourgain-space estimates, we establish a smoothing gain of any order $
a< \min \{1,\frac{2}{3}(2s+1)\} $
for $s>-\frac{1}{2}$. Our result demonstrates that the interplay between nonlinear interactions and resonance structures plays a decisive role in determining the smoothing properties of coupled dispersive systems.
