We now turn to the smoothing properties of periodic dispersive equations. In this context, smoothing refers to the gain of spatial regularity exhibited by the nonlinear correction to the corresponding linear evolution. For the periodic KdV equation, Erdoğan and Tzirakis [11] established a fundamental smoothing result. In particular, their analysis yields a smoothing gain of order a<min⁡{1,2​s+1}.a<\min\{1,2s+1\}. Their approach combines the Fourier restriction norm method with normal-form reductions obtained through differentiation by parts. Compaan [10] subsequently investigated the smoothing properties of the Majda–Biello system on the torus. More recently, Başakoğlu and Gürel [2] studied the smoothing properties of the Hirota–Satsuma system on the torus, contributing further results to the study of nonlinear smoothing for coupled KdV-type systems. An observation by Oh [20] concerning the resonance structure of the Majda–Biello system provides further motivation for the present study. Oh observed that, when the coupling parameter α\alpha is negative, the relevant resonance denominator has a favorable nonvanishing structure away from the trivial resonances and yields additional frequency decay. In particular, when α=−1\alpha=-1, the smoothing estimate can be established by a comparatively direct application of KdV-type arguments, leading to the expected range a<min⁡{1,2​s+1}.a<\min\{1,2s+1\}.

papers.title: Motion of a cylinder between parallel plates: complete Stokes resistance and pressure response
papers.abstract: A circular cylinder moving between two parallel plates is the canonical confined problem of two-dimensional Stokes flow. Rotation and translation of the cylinder along the channel become coupled and generate a pressure difference along the channel under zero-net-flux conditions. Existing results use different methods. We develop a completed double-layer boundary integral formulation based on the channel Green function to resolve narrow gaps at arbitrary transverse positions. The channel Green kernels are derived from a Fourier-transformed biharmonic problem, permitting explicit treatment of the free-space singularity, the slowly decaying nearest-wall contribution, and the small-wavenumber limit for accurate kernel evaluation under strong confinement. The boundary integral equation is discretised by a spectrally accurate Nystr\"om scheme on a graded parametrisation, and the pressure jump follows from the zero-wavenumber limit of the streamwise momentum balance. A single linear system yields the full resistance matrix and pressure-jump coefficients for an eccentric cylinder; an additional right-hand side treats imposed net flux. For nonzero coefficients, comparisons with independent COMSOL finite-element simulations show relative differences below \(0.1\%\) for the resistance coefficients and at most \(0.0122\%\) for the pressure-response coefficients and excess hydraulic resistance. Reciprocity, symmetry constraints, and lubrication asymptotics provide additional checks on the numerical results. We track the coupling between rotation and translation and the pressure generated by the cylinder from the channel scale into the lubrication regime, and determine the pressure--flow relation, driving torque and efficiency of the rotating-cylinder pump for asymmetric clearances.

papers.title: Iso-Multiplication Modules over Noncommutative Rings: Triangular Classification and Rational Rigidity
papers.abstract: A right A-module M is called iso-multiplication if for every submodule N of M there is a two-sided ideal B of A such that N ?A MB. We construct noncommutative examples of isomultiplication modules which are not multiplication modules, including triangular algebras of arbitrary dimension. We classify all iso-multiplication modules over T_2(k) without a finitegeneration assumption. For a semiprime right Goldie ring we prove that the classical localization of an iso-multiplication module is multiplicity-free. Further consequences address composition length and local rings; we distinguish these from standard Morita, Ore-localization, and chaincondition results.

papers.title: A multi-fidelity dataset of two-dimensional steady laminar channel flow around obstacles
papers.abstract: Surrogates that correct inexpensive flow simulations need the same flows solved at several fidelities and an estimate of the numerical error of the reference solutions. This dataset contains 4,500 two-dimensional, steady, laminar channel flows past a single obstacle. Each is solved in five numerical configurations: second-order convection on meshes with cell sizes of 2, 1, 0.5 and 0.25 mm, and first-order convection on the 1 mm mesh. A seeded generator draws the obstacles from five shape families in three size classes. All 22,500 OpenFOAM runs were iterated to initial residuals of $10^{-6}$, and each run's residuals, iterations and provenance are recorded. Every run provides the velocity and pressure on a regular grid with geometry channels, and the pressure and wall shear along the obstacle. Its 20 flow attributes, computed on the simulation mesh, include drag and lift split into pressure and friction parts. The four second-order levels give an estimate of the discretisation uncertainty of 19 attributes of every case. Fixed splits include three out-of-distribution test sets.

papers.title: Nonlinear long extensional waves in an elastic layer with irregular free surfaces
papers.abstract: The propagation of nonlinear long extensional waves in a compressible hyperelastic layer with irregular free surfaces is studied within the framework of finite elasticity. The free surfaces are traction-free and symmetric with respect to the middle plane, and their irregularity changes the local thickness of the layer by a finite amount over distances long compared with the wavelength. In a distinguished limit in which weak nonlinearity, dispersion and the irregularity of the free surfaces appear at the same order, a multiple-scales analysis of the two-dimensional boundary-value problem leads to a Korteweg--de Vries equation with variable coefficients for the longitudinal strain. The irregularity acts on the wave only through the traction-free boundary conditions and changes the balance between nonlinearity and dispersion along the layer. After normalisation, the combined effect of the material and of the geometry is carried by a single variable nonlinear coefficient, whose sign decides whether compressive or tensile solitary waves exist. For special choices of the surface irregularity, the evolution equation reduces to forms known to be integrable, namely the Korteweg--de Vries and cylindrical Korteweg--de Vries equations. For periodically irregular layers of iron and copper and for model materials, numerical solutions show that a localized pulse propagates as a solitary wave, splits into a train of solitary waves or disperses into an oscillatory wave train, depending on the material, while the irregularity of the free surfaces redistributes the amplitudes of the emerging solitary waves.

papers.title: Stochastic Modelling of High-frequency (HF) Crypto Limit Order Book (LOB) with General Compound Marked Hawkes Process
papers.abstract: The paper is devoted to the stochastic modelling of high-frequency crypto Limit Order Book (LOB) with general compound marked Hawkes process (GCMHP). We consider marked Hawkes process in a general form. LLN and FCLTs with stochastic and constant centralization are stated. Numerical example for high-frequency LOB dataset for BTC (bitcoin) based on sources from HF crypto LOB data is presented as well. The novelty of the paper lies in the new LLN and FCLTs for the GCMHP, and in the new application associated with high-frequency (HF) crypto LOB.

papers.title: IA-MoE: An Intensity-Aware Mixture of Experts for DNN Inference
papers.abstract: With the ever-increasing parameter scale and structural complexity of deep neural network (DNN) models, traditional cloud-based inference encounters bottlenecks in performance, privacy protection, and energy efficiency. While edge computing and edge intelligence facilitate the migration of inference tasks to edge servers closer to the data source, existing end-edge-cloud collaborative inference still encounters critical challenges, such as sensitivity to heterogeneous resources, complexity in multi-objective optimization, and adaptability to dynamic workloads. To achieve the joint optimization of end-to-end latency and energy consumption under dynamic inference requests with multi-resource constraints, we propose IA-MoE, an intensity-aware Mixture of Experts (MoE) framework. By modeling the model partitioning problem as a bilateral matching problem between layer tasks and virtual machine resources for each inference request, IA-MoE dynamically partitions DNN models in an edge-cloud hybrid computing environment. We evaluate IA-MoE using three representative DNNs (i.e., AlexNet, VGG16, ResNet50) on two public inference datasets in an enhanced CloudSimSDN simulation environment. Experimental results demonstrate that IA-MoE outperforms baseline methods regarding weighted normalized metrics for end-to-end latency and energy consumption. To our knowledge, this is the first study to introduce the MoE paradigm for DNN partitioning and collaborative inference in hybrid computing environments, providing a practical solution for efficient inference in artificial intelligence applications.

authors.name: Meiyan Zeng
authors.institution: Hunan University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: Turing Agent: Agentic Formal Verification for Mathematical Research
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are rapidly advancing mathematical discovery, moving beyond benchmark-level problem solving to tackle frontier research problems. This progress is ushering mathematics into an era of proof abundance, raising a fundamental challenge: how can we ensure the correctness of the ever-growing volume of AI-generated proofs and transform them into trustworthy, machine-verified mathematical knowledge? We introduce Turing Agent, an agent harness designed to orchestrate end-to-end formal verification of research-level mathematics. Its wo-scale architecture integrates theorem formalization and proof formalization agents, empowered by structured proof decomposition, parallel verification, accumulated proof experience, and selective semantic review. Leveraging our collaborations with theoretical computer science (TCS) researchers, we focus our evaluation on TCS, a particularly demanding domain characterized by intricate quantification, complex dependencies, and stringent semantic requirements. Against direct generation and general-purpose coding harnesses, including Codex CLI and Claude Code, Turing Agent achieves approximately 57-62% faithful formalization success on Formal TCS Bench and 83% overall pass@1 on a TCS-focused subset of RLMEval, using GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro. Notably, Turing Agent, built on DeepSeek, successfully completes the formal verification of three previously unresolved TCS tasks from OpenAI's October 2026 collection. One particularly challenging TCS problem required about a hundred formally verified auxiliary claims. Moreover, by actively exploring and refining the formalization process, Turing Agent can uncover simpler alternative proofs, expose unnecessary dependencies in original proofs, and generate reusable mathematical knowledge as a byproduct of verification.

papers.title: Quality and Similarity Indicators for Video-Based Heart Rate and Respiratory Rate Fusion: A Controlled Evaluation
papers.abstract: Camera-based heart rate (HR) and respiratory rate (RR) estimates vary in reliability from window to window, and a common remedy is to fuse several extraction methods with weights from reference-free signal quality indicators. However, few studies test whether these indicators identify the most accurate method in each window or outperform simpler fusion. We evaluate 11 quality indicators and 8 inter-method similarity measures for fusing 7 HR and 10 RR extractors on four public datasets (75 test subjects). Filters, indicator directions, weighting parameters and a learned ridge baseline are selected on a separate five-subject set before testing. Fusion is compared with equal averaging, a constant typical-rate predictor, the best single method selected in advance and in hindsight, and a per-window oracle with a permutation-based null, using subject-level bootstrap confidence intervals. For HR, quality-weighted fusion reduced mean absolute error by 10.9% [5.2, 18.4] relative to averaging and by 15.6% [8.1, 23.1] relative to the method selected in advance, and was statistically indistinguishable from the best method selected in hindsight. Weighting methods by their agreement did not improve on averaging. For RR, the indicators could not identify the more accurate estimates: sharpened quality weighting increased error (-2.6% [-4.8, -0.8]), fused estimates were uncorrelated with the reference (r <= 0.22), and averaging was less accurate than the typical-rate predictor (-3.1% [-6.1, -0.4]). With a second respiratory reference, apparent RR gains reflected estimates moving toward its typical rate. Quality-guided fusion is worthwhile for video HR; for RR, 30-s windows improved estimates but not fusion.

papers.title: Terahertz and infrared links in controlled non-Kolmogorov turbulence
papers.abstract: Hybrid terahertz/infrared (THz/IR) links are usually modeled with Kolmogorov turbulence, but whether the turbulence spectral type matters equally for both bands has not been investigated. We transmit co-propagating 625 GHz and 1550 nm links through laboratory-controlled turbulence while a Mach-Zehnder interferometer and thermistors independently measure its spectral exponent and structure parameter on the shared path. Inlet-air temperature, not airflow speed, drives the exponent from Kolmogorov-like to non-Kolmogorov. At comparable structure parameters, this change reverses which model better reproduces the IR attenuation at the nominal inner scale, whereas the THz attenuation is insensitive to it. With type-matched models, predicted and measured bit-error-rate trends agree within 0.14 (IR) and 0.06 (THz) decades. IR predictions therefore require the spectral shape and inner scale, not turbulence strength alone.

papers.title: Type-Confusion Security
papers.abstract: Type systems are a lightweight way to obtain formal assurance that code upholds security properties. However, decentralized systems, such as smart contracts and Model Context Protocol ecosystems, have limited ability to constrain the behavior of untrusted code. In such systems, attackers may attempt to confuse trusted code by supplying values that do not behave according to their advertised types, an attack that we call type confusion. Well-known attacks such as confused deputy attacks, reentrancy attacks, and control-flow hijacking can be understood as instances of type confusion. We define type confusion security as the property that unrestricted attackers who need not follow the type system have no more power than limited attackers who fully obey it. We formally define type confusion security as a real--ideal emulation, and in the context of an information-flow-typed core calculus that statically enforces security against well-typed attackers, prove that its run-time checks also enforce security against ill-typed attackers. In this system, programmers can write code while reasoning about security only against well-typed attackers; the security guarantees enforced by the type system still hold. We mechanize a proof of type confusion security in Lean.

papers.title: Do Rule-Based Tools Help LLMs Translate Endangered Uralic Languages in the Prompt or over MCP?
papers.abstract: Komi-Zyrian, Moksha, Erzya and Udmurt have mature rule-based resources, among them finite-state analysers, constraint grammars and bilingual dictionaries, which language models do not use. We ask whether giving a model access to these resources improves machine translation from the four languages into English, and whether it matters how the access is provided: as analyses computed in advance and written into the prompt, or as tools that the model calls itself through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). We evaluate manually: an expert linguist read every English output of the strongest model under three conditions, 816 sentences in all, accepted or rejected each one, and named the main error in every rejected translation. With the analyses in the prompt, the number of accepted translations rises from 13 to 43 out of 272; with the tools attached it rises to 55. The gain comes from the bilingual dictionary. For Udmurt, whose dictionary has no English side, the prompt-based condition brings no gain at all, while for the other three languages an English gloss reaches the prompt for 74 to 80% of the source words. Tool calling is also much harder to get working than prompt injection. Of 31 open-weight models, 14 never call a tool, 11 of them because they cannot produce a usable call, and half of the calls that are made name a language the toolkit does not support. We release the data set, every model output and all tool-call logs.

papers.title: Coupling-Response Thermodynamic Density of States for Bosonic Working Media
papers.abstract: We introduce an operational thermodynamic density of states (TDOS), $\mathcal{G}_\lambda=(\partial S/\partial\lambda)_{T,\mu}$, to characterize bosonic working media under microscopic spectral control. At fixed chemical potential, the response is strictly driven by the structural density of states, yielding the exact scaling law $\mathcal{G}_\lambda=-(d/\alpha)S/\lambda$ for homogeneous spectra $\epsilon(k)=\Delta+\lambda k^\alpha$, while coupling-dependent gaps generate edge terms only for finite boundary weight. Under a fixed-particle constraint, a secondary chemical-potential redistribution channel emerges. Exact solutions for quadratic bands and harmonic traps demonstrate that spatial dimensionality dictates whether this constrained TDOS exhibits a jump discontinuity or remains continuous across the Bose--Einstein condensation threshold. For pure scale control, the response maps exactly to the heat capacity, $\lambda \mathcal{G}_\lambda^{(N)}=-C_N$. This framework is applied to evaluate reversible work in Stirling cycles and to identify observables in magnonic platforms, contrasting global spectral edges with topological Dirac gaps in honeycomb ferromagnets.

papers.title: On the Matlis duals of $\mathcal D$-modules in characteristic zero
papers.abstract: Let $R=k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ be a formal power series ring over a field $k$ of characteristic zero, and let $\mathcal D=\mathcal D(R,k)$ be the ring of $k$-linear differential operators. We prove that if $\mathcal M$ is a nonzero left $\mathcal D$-module with $(0)\notin\operatorname{Ass}_R(\mathcal M)$, then $(0)\in\operatorname{Ass}_R D(\mathcal M)$, where $D(-)$ denotes Matlis duality, without assuming holonomicity or finite generation over $\mathcal D$. As a significant consequence of this result, we establish the Lyubeznik--Y{\i}ld{\i}r{\i}m conjecture in equicharacteristic zero. We also obtain a criterion for the Matlis dual of a $\mathcal D$-module to be non-holonomic.
