papers.title: Tight Sequential Confidence Intervals for Online Kernel Regression
papers.abstract: We characterize, in the worst case over kernels, the sharp minimax width of online confidence intervals for elements of a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS). This resolves the open problem posed by Vakili et al. (2021) in its original discrete-time form. A learner observes $y_i=f(x_i)+\epsilon_i$ at adaptively chosen points, with $\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}\le B$ and i.i.d. $R$-sub-Gaussian noise, and reports the interval $|f(x)-\mu_n(x)|\le\rho_n(\delta)\sigma_n(x)$, where $\mu_n$ and $\sigma_n$ are the posterior mean and standard deviation of a surrogate Gaussian process model with regularization parameter $\lambda$. Writing $\rho_n^*(\delta)$ for the minimax confidence width for a fixed kernel, we show that, for the sum of a linear kernel and a periodic Sobolev kernel, all sufficiently large $n$, and all $\delta\in(0,1/4]$, $\rho_n^*(\delta)\asymp B+(R/\lambda)\sqrt{\gamma_n+\log(1/\delta)}$, where $\gamma_n$ is the maximal information gain and grows polynomially in $n$. Building on Lattimore (2023), we construct an adaptive design on a fixed two-dimensional domain for which, under Gaussian noise, the normalized error at a prespecified point is $\Omega(B+(R/\lambda)\sqrt{\gamma_n})$ with constant probability. This rules out the conjectured polylogarithmic width in the worst case over kernels and online designs.

papers.title: AllocFlow: End-to-End Portfolio Trading Action Generation from Raw Market Data
papers.abstract: Real-world portfolio management requires converting noisy market observations into coordinated, simultaneous allocations across multiple assets under shared capital constraints. Advances in forecasting models and alpha discovery help identify opportunities. However, traditional pipelines often decouple signal forecasting from portfolio construction, potentially misaligning learning with allocation and execution objectives. We present AllocFlow, an end-to-end flow-matching framework that directly generates joint portfolio allocations from raw multi-asset market histories. To capture dependencies among portfolio positions, AllocFlow employs a cross-asset flow Transformer conditioned on temporal market representations to generate continuous, signed position weights across all instruments jointly. To address the sample inefficiency and instability of learning continuous allocation policies from scratch, we establish a two-stage training scheme: strategy-supervised imitation shapes a structured distribution of candidate portfolios, followed by group-relative reinforcement learning (RL) that refines joint decisions using portfolio-level financial rewards and a frozen policy reference. On hourly cryptocurrency perpetual futures, RL refinement raises the annualized net return of the imitation policy from $27.79\%$ to $51.38\%$ and its Calmar ratio from $0.955$ to $4.043$, surpassing the teacher strategy on every metric, and AllocFlow reaches a Calmar ratio of $4.90$ on six further months of unseen 2026 data without retraining.

authors.name: Yuchen Xie
authors.institution: Key Laboratory on Development and Application of Rural Renewable Energy

papers.title: Embedding of Barnes-Wall lattices into Cayley-Dickson algebras
papers.abstract: The family of Barnes-Wall lattices includes the balanced Barnes-Wall lattice $M_n$ over $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{2}]$ and two ordinary Barnes-Wall lattices $L_n$ and $L'_n$ over $\mathbb{Z}$, which are geometrically equivalent to each other. Embedding of these lattices into the Cayley-Dickson algebras of an appropriate dimension is considered. It is shown that for all $n \geq 2$ the lattices $M_n$ and $L_n$ are closed under multiplication and are generated by the sets of pairwise products of their elements. The lattices $L_n \cdot L'_n$, $L'_n \cdot L_n$, and $L'_n \cdot L'_n$, generated by pairwise products of elements of the lattices $L_n$ and $L'_n$, also are studied.

papers.title: Hausdorff continuity of logarithmic and Riesz capacities
papers.abstract: Let $E_n$ be $\alpha_n$-uniformly perfect compact sets that converge to a compact set $E$ in the Hausdorff distance $d_n=d_H(E_n,E)$. We prove that the logarithmic capacity of $E_n$ converges to that of $E$ whenever $\log(1/\alpha_n)=O(\log(1/d_n))$ and that no factor tending to infinity can be inserted in this bound. A common energy-transfer theorem also yields Hausdorff continuity of Riesz capacity under local capacity bounds, including bounds obtained from lower Hausdorff content density. Finally, we correct our earlier claims about the uniform convergence of Green functions.

papers.title: Near-Optimal Methods for Generalized Lipschitz Convex Optimization
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider a convex optimization problem, where the upper bound on the subgradient norm depends on the objective function. We establish a lower bound on the number of iterations required by any first-order method to find an approximate solution to the problem. Furthermore, we present two near-optimal algorithms that can match the lower bound up to logarithmic factors. The first algorithm is a projected GD with a carefully designed stepsize schedule which incorporates warm-up and decay phases. The second algorithm is scalar-stepsize clipped AdamW which extends the near-optimal guarantees to the stochastic setting, where only a noisy unbiased estimator of the subgradient is available.

authors.name: Grigory Malinovsky
authors.institution: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Finite generation of the second homology group of the genus three Torelli group
papers.abstract:
We prove that the group $H_2(\mathcal{I}_3;\mathbb{Z})$ is finitely generated, where $\mathcal{I}_3$ is the Torelli subgroup of the mapping class group of a closed genus-three surface $\Sigma_3$. A key role in the proof is played by establishing the following property: for each symplectic transvection $t_x\in\mathrm{Sp}_{6}(\mathbb{Z})$, we have
  $$
  \bigl(t^{120}_x-1\bigr)^{57}\bigl(t_x^{24}-1\bigr)(t_x-1)^6H_2(\mathcal{I}_3;\mathbb{Z})=0.
  $$
  The proof is based on the study of the spectral sequences associated with the action of $\mathcal{I}_3$ on the Bestvina-Bux-Margalit complex of minimizing cycles and with the actions on certain auxiliary complexes of the stabilizers of two- and three-component multicurves on $\Sigma_3$. The remaining ingredients are Tavgen's theorem, which asserts that $\mathrm{Sp}_{6}(\mathbb{Z})$ has bounded elementary generation, and the result of Kassabov and Putman, which asserts that $H_2(\mathcal{I}_3;\mathbb{Z})$ is finitely generated as a $\mathbb{Z}[\mathrm{Sp}_6(\mathbb{Z})]$-module.

papers.title: Settling the Support Complexity of Correlated Equilibria
papers.abstract:
We study the support complexity of approximate correlated equilibria (CE) in two-player games, that is, the minimum number of pure action profiles that must be assigned positive probability to approximate a correlated equilibrium of a two-player matrix game. For $\varepsilon$-approximate coarse correlated equilibria, constant approximation is possible with support $O(\log N/\varepsilon^2)$ in $N\times N$ games. For correlated equilibria, the best known upper bound was $O(\log^2 N/\varepsilon^4)$ [Babichenko et al., 2014, 2017], but whether this bound was tight remained open. We establish a matching lower bound, resolving the open question of Ko and Schvartzman [2017]. Specifically, we show that, already for two-player zero-sum games, for every $1\leq k\leq N^{1/2}$ the worst-case correlated-equilibrium gap achievable by a distribution supported on at most $k$ pure profiles is $$
  \Theta\left(
  \min\left\{1,\frac{\sqrt{\log N}}{k^{1/4}}\right\}
  \right), $$ which implies a $\Theta(\log^2 N/\varepsilon^4)$ worst-case support bound. The proof builds on a probabilistic-method construction based on random sign matrices.

papers.title: Nitrogen Defect Coupling in Epitaxial LaFeO3 From Structural Reconstruction to Water Oxidation
papers.abstract: Earth-abundant ABO3-type perovskite oxides provide a versatile platform for understanding how anion chemistry and defects govern electrocatalytic behavior. Here, we use epitaxial LaFeO3-xNy thin films to reveal how dilute N incorporation (<0.8% N/O) couples to defect formation, structural reconstruction, and water oxidation. Nitrogen-plasma-assisted pulsed laser deposition introduces N and is accompanied by reduced oxygen content, localized Fe-metal exsolution, and pronounced lattice expansion, while preserving predominantly Fe3+ in the bulk of the film. Ab initio calculations identify a plausible charge-balanced extended defect configuration involving coupled oxygen and Fe vacancies with substitutional N incorporation, reproducing the experimentally observed lattice expansion while preserving the bulk-average Fe oxidation state. The resulting electronic-state redistribution is accompanied by substantially modified electrical transport and nearly two orders of magnitude higher initial oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity than undoped LaFeO3. Under OER conditions, however, the highly active as-grown state is metastable: near-surface N depletion and Fe0 oxidation/removal accompany rapid initial activity decay toward a quasi-steady state. pH-dependent kinetics and post-OER anion redistribution are consistent with possible lattice-oxygen participation. These results establish relationships among dilute anion incorporation, coupled defect reconstruction, electronic properties, and electrochemical behavior in perovskite oxides.

papers.title: Rotating Polytropic Twins and the Fragmentation Problem
papers.abstract: Polytropic n=1 stellar configurations with strong differential rotation have been considered. The so-called twin configurations: stars having almost identical integral characteristics, but clearly structurally different have been found. Hydrodynamic 3D modeling has been performed for two such structures and has shown that these configurations also differ in the dynamic aspect: one of them remains practically stationary, while the other turns out to be unstable with respect to the development of the bar mode and fragmentation. The gravitational wave signal accompanying the fragmentation process has been calculated.

authors.name: V. Valiulin
authors.institution: Siberian Branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences

papers.title: Vortex states in submicron titanomagnetite particles
papers.abstract: Numerical simulation is used to study the magnetic properties of spheroidal titanomagnetite particles Fe(3-x)TixO4 (0.4 < x < 0.6) with semi-axes ratio ranging from 0.5 to 1.5 and transverse diameters D = 100 - 480 nm. It is shown that various vortex micromagnetic states can emerge in the titanomagnetite particles depending on the titanium concentration, aspect ratio and particle diameter. The single-domain particle diameters are determined using the energy diagrams for stationary uniform and vortex states. The remanent magnetization of dilute assemblies of titanomagnetite particles with varying titanium content are calculated as a function of the transverse particle diameter D. It is demonstrated that for submicron-sized titanomagnetite particles, D ~ 500 nm, the normalized remanent magnetization of the assembly reaches very low values, M/Ms < 0.01, where Ms is the saturation magnetization of the particles.

authors.name: Olga N. Serebryakova
authors.institution: Ministry of Health of the Russian Federation

papers.title: Modified scattering and asymptotic completeness for a massive Dirac-wave system in dimension three
papers.abstract:
We establish global well-posedness and modified scattering for the three-dimensional Dirac-Klein-Gordon system with a massive spinor and a massless scalar field, for small, sufficiently regular and localized initial data. This answers a question posed by Dong, Li, and Yuan in \cite[Case IV]{DLY23}. We also identify a Majorana-type condition on the initial data that yields linear scattering, showing that both linear and modified scattering solutions coexist in this model.
  Conversely, we establish asymptotic completeness for small asymptotic profiles satisfying suitable regularity and decay assumptions. The forward argument combines the hyperboloidal foliation method with testing by wave packets, whereas the backward construction relies on a contraction argument in suitably chosen norms.

authors.name: Vitor Borges
authors.institution: National Institute of Health Dr. Ricardo Jorge

papers.title: Surrogate-Based Optimization of Tandem Twin-Rotor Wind Turbines Accounting for Wake Interactions
papers.abstract: Wake interaction in a tandem twin-rotor turbine couples power capture with thrust on the shared support. This study develops a time-resolved surrogate for upstream IEA Wind 22 MW and downstream NREL 5 MW rotors. It covers spacing ratios $0.01\leq L/D\leq0.20$ and tip-speed ratios $4\leq\lambda\leq11$. Vortex-method simulations of 160 configurations under turbulent inflow train per-time-node XGBoost models to predict 600 s power, thrust, and torque histories. A CNN-Attention-LSTM network extends these histories, and a genetic algorithm balances the system power and thrust coefficients. Ten-fold cross-validation gives median power-history $R^2$ values of 0.995 upstream and 0.958 downstream for unseen configurations, but the first stage cannot extrapolate in tip-speed ratio. With fixed pitch and prescribed rotor speed, the coefficients apply where both rotors reach the simulated tip-speed ratio below rated wind speed. Increasing spacing raises upstream power by up to 6% and lowers downstream power by up to 62%. System power changes by less than 4% at fixed $\lambda$. The high-power end of the Pareto front lies near $\lambda=10$. At $L/D=0.20$, the system power coefficient is highest. This configuration has the lowest peak thrust among the high-power candidates.

papers.title: Heavy-Light Wall Crossings and Motivic Asymptotics of Moduli Spaces of Curves. Part II: Tameness of Motivic Measures
papers.abstract:
This paper is concerned with the study of the fixed-genus asymptotics of motivic measures of moduli spaces of stable pointed curves and their minimal all-light Hassett compactifications as the number of markings tends to infinity. A motivic wall-crossing argument gives a universal change of variables between the two generating series, depending only on the value of the Lefschetz class. For an arbitrary motivic measure, we use stabilization graphs and support patterns to express the all-light series in terms of universal chain factors and finite residual quotient families. This formal decomposition isolates the rational trivalent contribution without requiring a fixed-locus formula for finite quotients.
  To pass from formal identities to asymptotics, we formulate analytic hypotheses (the $\mathrm{H}_g$-hypotheses) for scalar realizations with positive real Lefschetz value. We introduce vertex tameness and residual-quotient tameness, whose conjunction, graph tameness, provides geometric sufficient conditions for the $\mathrm{H}_g$-hypotheses. In genus at least two, this yields explicit leading asymptotics in both chambers, depending only on the genus and the Lefschetz value; genera zero and one are treated separately. As an application, we prove graph tameness for Hodge-Deligne evaluations and deduce fixed-product universality and asymptotic concentration of Hodge numbers on the diagonal.

papers.title: Benchmark Factory: Agentic Benchmark Creation via Dataset Curation and Label-Free Quality Anchors
papers.abstract: Teams deploying coding agents need benchmarks built from their own code, but curating and validating them by hand is resource intensive, and an unvalidated benchmark can mislead silently. We present Benchmark Factory, an autonomous meta-agent loop with human checkpoints: an LLM agent writes sourcing queries over landed production code changes, runs models of known relative strength on each candidate, diagnoses why a candidate fails, and repairs it by editing its queries, prompts, and configuration until it clears quality anchors that need no per-task human labels. We used Benchmark Factory to build benchmarks for five developer cohorts at our organization. Engineering raters scored a 5% sample 2.3 for task quality and 2.6 for grader verdicts on a 1-to-3 scale. On configurations never used to build them, the benchmarks ranked Claude Opus~4.7 at high reasoning effort above low effort (60.6% vs. 54.4% of tasks passed, $p=0.002$) and GPT-5.5 above GPT-5.4 (65.8% vs. 60.5%, $p=0.004$); 9 of the 10 per-cohort comparisons pointed the same way. A deliberately trivial benchmark failed the anchors; five broken graders failed them, even under a relaxed rule fixed in advance that the real grader passes; and with model labels shuffled so that no true ordering existed, random redraws of a candidate passed in at most 1.4% of simulations. The anchors are necessary, not sufficient, conditions for a valid benchmark, designed to focus human review on what the loop cannot repair.

authors.name: James Poon
authors.institution: Nara Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Angular-Pole Flag Curvature and Conformal Control of Radial Jacobi Fields in Diagonal Conic Finsler Optics
papers.abstract: We study diagonal conic Finsler optical structures with radial coefficients and an arbitrary angular Finsler norm. We obtain the spray curvature block and identify the angular-pole radial-transverse flag curvature at a critical radius with the negative optical-arclength radial Jacobi coefficient. We prove that a compactly supported radial conformal two-jet determines the critical radius and any signed radial coefficient. A navigation Randers sphere yields unequal oriented periods with a common radial coefficient.

papers.title: Wireless Edge-Assisted Adaptive Latent Reasoning for Vision-Language-Action Models in Physical AI
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable embodied artificial intelligence (AI) by translating visual observations and language instructions into robotic actions. Emerging use cases in physical AI are expected to drive the need for efficient inference and communication, as the computational demands of the VLA models pose challenges for real-time control with limited onboard resources. Test-time scaling through latent reasoning allows these models to refine hidden representations without generating explicit chain-of-thought (CoT) tokens, but introduces a trade-off between task success, inference latency, and energy consumption. In this paper, we address the efficient collaborative inference under a realistic communication scenario. We propose a wireless edge-assisted framework for adaptive latent reasoning (WEALR) that augments onboard computation with edge computing. A decision-making agent jointly selects the execution location and latent-reasoning convergence threshold. We formulate this joint adaptation as a constrained Markov decision process (CMDP). A Lagrangian-constrained deep reinforcement learning (CDRL) approach, namely trust region policy optimization Lagrangian (TRPO-Lag), learns to balance task performance and resource consumption under varying wireless conditions and task requirements. We evaluate the framework using LIBERO manipulation tasks, profiled VLA inference costs, and ray-traced wireless channels. Experimental results demonstrate that TRPO-Lag achieves up to 23% higher feasibility-weighted task success rate compared to benchmark CDRL methods.

papers.title: Projection-Based Partitioned MiLAC Architecture for MU-MIMO Precoding
papers.abstract: This work proposes a partitioned Microwave Linear Analog Computer (MiLAC) architecture for user-specific MU-MIMO precoding based on independently configured analog subnetworks. The proposed method reformulates user-level interference suppression as an invertible projection-based transformation, which is computed from the channel and synthesized into the MiLAC admittances. While the resulting offline configuration incurs higher computational complexity than conventional ZFBF and regularized ZFBF, it remains substantially below fully digital Block Diagonalization. Once configured, the Sub-MiLACs perform the precoding operation in the analog domain, yielding significantly lower online processing complexity. Under ideal conditions, the proposed method achieves performance close to fully digital BD.

papers.title: Exhaustive Evaluation of Fixed-Point Reciprocal Architectures for FPGAs
papers.abstract: Fixed-point reciprocals are used in normalization and division on field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs). Designs that share an output format can differ in worst-case error and in their need for memory and multipliers. The effect of table width, internal precision and refinement was evaluated for reciprocal computation in the Q16.16 and Q8.24 formats. Every representable input in the interval from 0.5 to 2.5 was tested against an exact integer reference. Five arithmetic paths were reconstructed from register-transfer-level source. Guarded interpolation, Newton-Raphson refinement and residual correction were then evaluated alongside polynomial and digit-recurrence baselines. Correct rounding was verified for all 131,073 Q16.16 and 33,554,433 Q8.24 inputs by adding one residual check to a guarded interpolated seed and one refinement step. An implementation with product reuse was verified at one input per cycle with a latency of 10 cycles in both formats. The Q8.24 implementation used nine digital signal processing slices in 7 series synthesis. The exact radix-2 control used no such slices and had a latency of 28 cycles. The reconstructed refined paths reduced the maximum relative error by factors of 205 to 223 when eight fractional bits were added. The evaluated designs provide reproducible choices for fixed accuracy budgets. In particular, correct rounding can be obtained on the tested interval by using a compact seed and checking the integer residual before the result is returned.

papers.title: LiDSeg: Linear DehazeFormer Guidance for Efficient Semantic Segmentation in Adverse Weather Conditions
papers.abstract: Robust semantic segmentation in adverse weather is essential for safety-critical autonomous systems. Existing restore-then-segment pipelines introduce latency and prioritize pixel-level restoration over semantic discriminability, while domain adaptation methods often face representation bottlenecks and computational complexity. We introduce LiDSeg, a framework that uses reconstruction-informed guidance to improve segmentation under adverse weather. During training, a lightweight guidance encoder is jointly optimized with the segmentation branch using segmentation and auxiliary reconstruction objectives. At inference, the reconstruction decoder is discarded, while the guidance encoder is retained to extract weather-robust features. A lightweight gated fusion module integrates these features into the segmentation branch, preserving clear-weather accuracy while improving adverse-weather robustness. On Foggy Cityscapes, LiDSeg limits the clear-to-dense-fog mIoU degradation to 2.5-2.8 percentage points, reducing the baseline performance drop by more than fivefold. On the official ACDC test server, LiDSeg-PIDNet achieves 75.07% pooled all-condition mIoU, comparable to supervised HRNet-W48 at 75.0%, while remaining substantially smaller. The gains generalize zero-shot to Foggy Driving and Foggy Zurich without training on real-fog images. LiDSeg adds only 1.9-3.1M parameters across several models, with total model sizes of 5.2-39.5M parameters and no inference-time reconstruction overhead. It delivers real-time inference on the NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin. Code: https://github.com/yobsanb/LiDSeg

authors.name: Yobsan Bayisa Leta
authors.institution: Southern University of Science and Technology

papers.title: PBit1: One Programmable P-Bit per Parameter - A Finite-Control Representation of Pretrained Networks
papers.abstract: We introduce PBit1, a finite-control representation of pretrained neural networks that assigns one programmable p-bit to each learned parameter. A 12-bit command sets its probability, a shared affine range maps that probability to the weight domain, and temporal observations reconstruct the weight for inference. Operator-aware range grouping and sensitivity-based sampling allocation adapt the representation to the network. Across five independent weight draws at 32,768 observations per scalar, selected configurations preserve task quality in GPT-2, DistilBERT, and LFM3-1.7B with every learned scalar converted and no fine-tuning. GPT-2 and LFM3 perplexity increase by approximately 0.66% and 0.26%, respectively, while DistilBERT accuracy changes from 87.51% to 87.49%. A sensitivity-based policy reduces GPT-2 reconstruction observations by 41.7% while retaining the quality criterion. Complete-model evaluations reuse reconstructed weights in BF16 inference, and THRML operator experiments examine native sampling and spatial-temporal tradeoffs. Together, these results establish PBit1 as a concrete construction for studying finite-control weight representation and temporal reconstruction in pretrained networks.

papers.title: Beyond Prompts: Runtime Contracts for Coding Agents
papers.abstract: Coding agents act on repositories through shell commands and file edits, and teams steer them with written engineering rules. Industrial settings expect such rules to be enforced and their application to be evidenced, and a rule given as prompt text provides neither. We test whether executable contracts enforced while the agent works reduce rule violations compared with the same rules in the prompt, retrieved as guidance, or checked only after generation. Violations are scored by an oracle whose methods differ from the in-loop checks, and the oracle is validated by two human reviewers and a model reviewer. Across three studies on two model families (240, 112 and 108 runs), enforcement during execution produced no oracle-detected violation in 104 paired runs, against 21 to 55% of runs without rules, and no loss of functional correctness in the two confirmatory studies. In the confirmatory study on tasks aimed at known failure situations (Study 3, protocol hashed before the first run), enforcement lowered the share of violating runs by 31 percentage points relative to no rules (Holm-adjusted p = 0.014); the 17-point difference from prompted rules was not significant (p = 0.12), and neither was any contrast in Study 2, where only 3 of 14 tasks produced a violation. Prompted rules removed some violation types but not recursive deletes of scratch directories, and checks after generation repaired file edits but not commands that had already run. That enforcement satisfies the rules it enforces is expected by construction; what the data add is where prompting falls short, the absence of a functional cost, and the limits of the rules and of the oracle themselves. The studies use low-cost models and one small fixture.

papers.title: Random compositions of quasiperiodic cocycles
papers.abstract: We consider the multiplicative process given by random compositions of linear cocycles over toral translations. Under appropriate generic assumptions, we establish effective large deviations estimates as well as the H\"older continuity of the associated Lyapunov exponent of the process. These properties in particular show the regularizing effect of randomness on quasiperiodic dynamics. The novelty of our approach allows for the study of such properties notwithstanding the lack of a spectral gap for the corresponding transition operator.

authors.name: Silvius Klein
authors.institution: Pontifícia Universidade Católica do Rio de Janeiro

papers.title: KneeFS-Net: A Lightweight Deep Learning Model for Knee Osteoarthritis Severity Assessment with Cross-Domain External Validation
papers.abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (OA) grading from radiographs using the Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) scale requires expertise that may be scarce. We present KneeFS-Net, a lightweight ordinal grader (0.8 million parameters; 0.33 GFLOPs) combining spatial, Fourier and state-space features with landmark-guided attention. On the Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI) test set, KneeFS-Net achieved a quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) of 0.863, mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.325 and 97.2% within-one-grade accuracy, comparable to models with 9-35-fold more parameters. We evaluated cross-population generalization on two Bangladeshi cohorts, a single-center hospital cohort and a multi-center teleradiology cohort. Without further training or adaptation, the OAI-trained model achieved QWK 0.803, MAE 0.339 and 98.2% within-one-grade accuracy on its hospital cohort, declining to QWK 0.656 and MAE 0.522 on multi-center teleradiology images. Self-supervised pretraining on 6,092 unlabeled radiographs followed by joint fine-tuning achieved QWK 0.823, MAE 0.329 and 99.7% within-one-grade accuracy in cross-validation. These findings demonstrate accurate, efficient KL grading and potential adaptation to new populations with limited annotation.

authors.name: Shafqat Alam
authors.institution: Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology

authors.name: Md. Ibrahim
authors.institution: Egypt-Japan University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Independent set reconfiguration is hard at treewidth four
papers.abstract: Independent Set Reconfiguration asks whether one of two given independent sets of equal size can be transformed into the other by moving one token at a time while keeping the occupied vertices independent. In token sliding, a token moves along an edge. In token jumping, it may move to any unoccupied vertex. For both rules, the problem is solvable in polynomial time on trees and is PSPACE-complete on graphs of treewidth at most $c$ for some fixed constant $c$. For each rule, the smallest treewidth bound that suffices for hardness has long been open. We narrow this gap by proving that both versions are NP-hard on graphs of treewidth four.

authors.name: Hussein Abbas
authors.institution: The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center

papers.title: Constructing high-dimensional representations of twin groups via several techniques
papers.abstract: In this article, we consider the twin group $T_n$ for a positive integer $n$ and present two techniques for constructing high-dimensional and complicated representations of $T_n$. The first technique consists of composing a known representation of $T_n$ with the well-established Cohen map, while the second technique relies on the tensor product of two known representations of $T_n$. To implement these techniques, we consider the two representations $\eta_1$ and $\eta_2$ of $T_n$ introduced recently by Nasser. The first technique is applied to the representation $\eta_1: T_n \longrightarrow \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{F}_n)$, which maps $T_n$ into the automorphism group of the free group $\mathbb{F}_n$ with $n$ generators. The second technique is applied to the representation $\eta_2: T_n \longrightarrow \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{Z}[t^{\pm 1}])$, which maps $T_n$ into the general linear group over the ring of Laurent polynomials in an indeterminate $t$. Using these techniques, we construct new high-degree representations of $T_n$ and examine, for some of them, structural properties such as faithfulness and reducibility. This work provides new avenues for developing representations of $T_n$ and related groups using these techniques.

papers.title: Power Scaling Across Link Utilization with GPAM-4 Signaling and Event-Driven Reception
papers.abstract: This work highlights the potential of combining event-based signaling with event-driven reception to achieve receiver power scaling across link utilization, without requiring wake-up, locking, or data-rate reconfiguration. The approach is demonstrated using the proposed four-level Gaussian pulse-amplitude modulation (GPAM-4) scheme and a corresponding event-driven receiver. By employing a resettable ring voltage-controlled oscillator (RRVCO) as its front end, the receiver achieves inherently event-driven symbol measurement, initiated directly by each received pulse. Symbols are decoded directly from the final RRVCO phase state, eliminating a counter-based back end. Simulated in 28-nm CMOS, the receiver power is evaluated across a $100\times$ range of effective data rates---from 0.15 mW at the peak rate of 8 Gb/s, down to 2.5 $\mu$W under active/idle operation and 1.6 $\mu$W under data rate change at 80 Mb/s. The receiver thus achieves power reductions of $59.5\times$ and $90.0\times$, while its energy per bit increases by only $1.68\times$ and $1.11\times$, respectively.

papers.title: Improving fine-grained expressivity of graph neural networks
papers.abstract:
This thesis investigates the expressive power of neural networks for structured data, focusing on graph neural networks and symmetry-aware architectures.
  We present four main contributions. First, we characterize the generic expressive power of geometric message-passing neural networks on sparse graphs and introduce EGenNet, an architecture achieving the corresponding guarantees. Second, we use representation theory to characterize linear layers equivariant to multiple permutations, including wreath-product symmetries. Third, we study permutation-invariant set representations that preserve containment, establish dimensional bounds and impossibility results, and introduce MASNet. Finally, we propose FSW-GNN, a message-passing architecture combining strong expressivity and bi-Lipschitz stability guarantees with strong empirical performance on long-range graph-learning tasks.
  Together, these results provide a broader understanding of how neural architectures can preserve the geometric, algebraic, order-theoretic, and metric structure of their inputs.

papers.title: CapCover Filter: Semantic Approximate Membership Queries over Embeddings
papers.abstract:
Determining whether an embedding is sufficiently similar to any vector in a vector store without performing a nearest-neighbor search can substantially improve query throughput in vector-store systems. We study Semantic Approximate Membership Queries (SAMQs), which allow queries to be rejected when no indexed vector meets the requested similarity threshold, while guaranteeing no false negatives.
  We introduce CapCover Filter, a geometric data structure that summarizes a set of embeddings using spherical caps. Its representation is independent of the query threshold, allowing a single filter to support arbitrary thresholds without reconstruction. We evaluate alternative construction and quantization methods, compare CapCover Filter with competing filters, and measure its impact on query throughput.
  Across five real-world datasets, at a cosine similarity threshold of 0.95, CapCover Filter eliminates approximately 20--100\% of index accesses while using only 2\% of the raw (FP32) embedding memory. When placed before a FAISS flat index, it improves query throughput by up to 382\% and by approximately 116\% on average across the five datasets, while returning the same range-search result. We also evaluate lower similarity thresholds. Our results show that CapCover Filter can substantially improve vector-store throughput when similarity thresholds are tight, retrieval is expensive, and indexed embeddings are highly clustered. We release an optimized implementation of CapCover Filter and its evaluation framework.

papers.title: EvoMem3D: Adaptive-Depth Temporal Representation Memory for Multi-Camera 3D Detection
papers.abstract: Modern multi-camera 3D detectors increasingly rely on large Vision Transformer (ViT) image encoders, making repeated full-depth encoding a dominant inference cost even though adjacent driving frames are highly redundant. We present EvoMem3D, an adaptive-depth temporal framework that caches the most recent full-depth detector-interface appearance representation as a read-only anchor and combines it with policy-selected partial features from the current frame. A lightweight pre-encoding controller chooses among semantic encoder exits before image processing, allocating shallow computation to stable frames and deeper computation when the visual state changes. To reuse appearance without carrying stale geometry, we decouple temporal appearance from geometric alignment: current-frame calibration defines the decoder geometry at every timestamp, while a motion-conditioned positional adapter accounts for anchor-to-current ego motion. On nuScenes, EvoMem3D achieves 61.50 NDS and 52.76 mAP while reducing end-to-end latency from 364.4 to 168.7 ms (x2.16) relative to standard dense DETR3D. With StreamPETR, it reaches 61.36 NDS and 52.55 mAP at a x1.92 speedup. Controlled studies isolate the effects of current evidence, temporal reuse, memory correction, and adaptive routing, while our audit confirms that the policy learns to distinguish semantic driving regimes.

papers.title: Rounded Potentials Certify Exact Maximum Flow
papers.abstract:
The textbook certificate for maximum flow is lopsided: the cut takes one bit per vertex, while the flow takes one number per edge. Indeed, some graphs have $\Theta(n^2)$ terminal pairs for which every maximum flow uses $\Theta(n^2)$ edges. Yet we show that one short number per vertex suffices for both cut and flow: $n$ vertex potentials, each rounded to $O(\log(nW))$ bits, certify the exact maximum $st$-flow value in any directed graph with integer capacities at most $W$. Exact potentials can have exponentially large representations. Rounding them may violate flow conservation, but the total error across any cut is less than one unit, so integrality of cut capacities absorbs it. Checking conservation is local and linear in the capacities, allowing the same certificate to yield new bounds in four models (capacities are polynomially bounded unless stated otherwise):
  - Online annotated streaming. $\widetilde{O}(n)$ total cost (help plus space) for the maximum $st$-flow value, optimal up to logarithmic factors, answering a question of Thaler (ICALP 2016) on whether $o(n^2)$ is possible.
  - Broadcast proof-labeling. $O(\log(n+p))$-bit labels certifying a maximum $st$-flow value of $p$ in directed and undirected graphs with arbitrary capacities, optimal for $p\ge n^{\Omega(1)}$, settling that regime of a question of Korman, Kutten, and Peleg (Distributed Computing 2010).
  - Merlin-Arthur verification. $\widetilde{O}(n^3)$ time and $O(n^3\log n)$ proof length for directed All-Pairs Max-Flow, improving on previous verification times of $n^{4+o(1)}$ for general capacities and $n^{3.5+o(1)}$ for unit capacities, and answering a question of Akmal (TheoretiCS 2024).
  - Nondeterministic algorithms. $O(n^{3.614})$ time for directed All-Pairs Max-Flow, or $n^{3.5+o(1)}$ if $\omega=2$: the first subquartic bound for general edge capacities, answering a question of Trabelsi (SODA 2025).

papers.title: Lazy-MOSAIC: Accelerating Skill-Centric Manipulation Planning with Learned Skill-Effect World Models
papers.abstract: Long-horizon manipulation tasks require a robot to perform a sequence of physical interactions with its environment, typically combining several different skills. Planning such behaviors efficiently is challenging: given a library of parameterized skills, solutions lie in a vast hybrid space of skill sequences and their parameters, and evaluating each candidate skill's feasibility and effect with a high-fidelity world model such as a physics simulator is computationally expensive. MOSAIC, a recent skill-centric approach, lets the skills guide a non-sequential search toward the regions of this space where they are likely to succeed; however, it pays the full cost of simulation for every parameterized skill it considers. In this work, we introduce Lazy-MOSAIC, a lazy planning framework that instead searches over hypothesized skill outcomes. A cheap learned skill-effect world model predicts, in a fraction of a millisecond, a skill's feasibility and the world state it produces. Lazy-MOSAIC then uses these predictions to focus expensive simulation on promising candidate skills and, when a hypothesis is invalidated, repairs only the affected part of the search, while ensuring that every skill in a returned plan is validated in simulation. We evaluate Lazy-MOSAIC on cluttered-shelf retrieval tasks of increasing difficulty and demonstrate it on a physical robot, showing that it plans substantially faster than baselines with fewer simulator queries, while matching or exceeding their success rate in every setting. Visit skill-mosaic.github.io.

papers.title: The Stability Frontier of Interacting Binary Stars
papers.abstract: We derive a conservation based dynamical stability frontier for interacting binary stars that distinguishes stationary mass transfer from the restoration of a perturbed contact state. We apply the formalism to conservative white dwarf binaries with direct impact accretion, coupling Roche overflow, stream angular momentum, gravitational radiation, and both stellar spin reservoirs. From the contact equations, we obtain the required orbital return torque, and an exact Jacobian identity yields the restoring gradient and an oscillatory stability boundary in the computed white dwarf domain. A dimensionally normalized quadrupolar tide reveals separate equilibrium fold and oscillatory thresholds, including coexisting stable and unstable stationary branches. Finite donor synchronization introduces an additional oscillatory stability frontier. The model recovers the classical Roche and gravitational radiation limits, while the calculated orbital period derivatives are consistent with published binary timing measurements within their combined observational and model uncertainties. These results specify the torque amplitude, restoring stiffness, and synchronization rate needed for local stability, providing quantitative targets for stellar tidal calculations and the interpretation of interacting binaries in the millihertz gravitational wave band.

authors.name: Hisham Anwer
authors.institution: Zewail City of Science and Technology

papers.title: Representing Differential Inclusions as Monads: A Framework for Compositional Controller Synthesis
papers.abstract:
Sequential composition of safety-certified controllers for hybrid and non-smooth robotic systems is well studied piecewise. Yet no existing framework reduces this question to a single algebraic condition. We construct a \emph{trajectory monad} for Filippov-regular differential inclusions. Its Kleisli category treats controllers as morphisms and sequential execution as trajectory concatenation. Control Barrier Function (CBF) certification, a guarantee of forward invariance, corresponds to a sub-monad of this category. Joint safety of composed controllers then follows from one algebraic condition. All controllers must land in a common sub-monad, which is closed under the monad multiplication.
  The sub-monad condition recasts recasts existing CBF composition practice categorically. It explains why a smooth intersection of multiple barriers supports safe composition, while enforcing barriers phase by phase does not. For the phase-by-phase case, we derive a closed-form Bernoulli model of the failure rate. We validate it over a randomized sweep of 3{,}000 instances. The same sweep shows that the standard baseline degrades under constraint conflict as the barrier count grows. This baseline enforces all barriers simultaneously as constraints in a single quadratic program (QP). We instantiate the framework on a four-mode piecewise-affine system and on a unicycle reduced-order model over heterogeneous terrain.

papers.title: Scaling Fourier Inequalities for Locally Compact Quantum Groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study Fourier and convolution inequalities on locally compact quantum groups in the presence of the scaling group. For $1\le p\le 2$, we investigate a family of scaling Fourier transforms and the associated norms $H_{p,\theta}(\mathbb G)$, and we show that $H_{p,\theta}(\mathbb G)<1$ for the real quantum $az+b$ group and $0<\theta<1$, $1<p<2$. We also investigate scaling convolution for locally compact quantum groups and, by extending the ordinary convolution, obtain the corresponding scaling Young inequality in four different regions. In Young Region~II, under $1<p,s<2$ and $2\leq r<\infty$, we construct sequences proving norm one at every effective vertex and prove strict inequality at every other effective point.

authors.name: Fulin Yang
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: M\"obius-Pseudorandomness for Algebraic Circuits
papers.abstract:
We define a notion of M\"obius-pseudorandomness for integer sequences generated by multivariate polynomials computed by small and simple algebraic circuits. This mirrors a related definition of Kalai that concerns boolean functions computed by small boolean circuits.
  We then prove M\"obius-pseudorandomness results for polynomials computed by algebraic circuits with few multiplication gates (of any depth), for polynomials with small-dimensional partial derivative space, and for the determinant and permanent. We conjecture that these results hold in general for polynomial-size algebraic circuits.

papers.title: Online and Fully-Dynamic Sorting
papers.abstract: Online sorting asks how to place $n$ sequentially arriving elements in an array to minimize the sum of absolute differences between consecutive elements. Fully-dynamic sorting further extends the problem to allow both element insertions and deletions. Without recourse, these problems face strong lower bounds on the competitive ratio: $\Omega(\sqrt{n})$ for online sorting and $\Omega(n)$ for fully-dynamic sorting. In sharp contrast, we show that allowing only poly-logarithmic recourse yields at least exponential improvements in the competitive ratio for both problems:(1) Our main algorithmic result is a deterministic fully-dynamic sorting algorithm that is $O(\log^2 n)$-competitive and has $O(\log^4 n)$ amortized recourse per update. We complement this with a lower bound showing that any deterministic algorithm with any $O(\mathrm{polylog}(n))$ competitive ratio has amortized recourse at least $\Omega(\sqrt{\log n})$.(2) For the insertion-only setting, we establish a family of approximation--recourse tradeoffs, including $O(\log\log n)$ competitive ratio with $O(\log\log n)$ amortized recourse. Given the lower bound in the fully-dynamic case, this result shows that the insertion-only problem yields exponentially better bounds than the fully-dynamic one.(3) Finally, we show that the stronger approximation-recourse tradeoff for the insertion-only case extends to the fully-dynamic setting when the array has $(1+\varepsilon)n$ space.

papers.title: Broadband Absorption Bounds for Coated PEC Spheres: Curvature, Angular Momentum, and Localized Sources
papers.abstract: We investigate fundamental limits on broadband electromagnetic absorption by a material-coated perfectly electrically conducting (PEC) sphere. Exact reflection coefficients are derived for the transverse-electric (TE) and transverse-magnetic (TM) spherical modes. Their long-wavelength asymptotics, combined with causality and contour integration in the complex wavelength plane, yield sum rules relating the wavelength-integrated modal reflection to the static material parameters, coating thickness, curvature, and complex reflection zeros. For the dipolar modes ($n=1$), known passive spherical-wave sum rules establish analytically a material-dependent lower bound on the weighted logarithmic reflection integral. Extension to higher-order modes requires a nonnegativity condition on higher odd moments of the reflection zeros; we formulate this condition as a conjecture and provide extensive Monte-Carlo evidence for passive dispersive coatings. The resulting bounds establish a per-channel absorption--bandwidth tradeoff and reveal the spherical-harmonic order as a discrete transverse-wavenumber variable, recovering the familiar planar attenuation factor in the locally planar limit. Finally, we show how the modal bounds can be combined for a localized external source. For a radial electric dipole outside the sphere, the near-field excitation is decomposed into TM spherical channels, leading to a source-weighted broadband absorption bound. As the source approaches the surface, progressively higher angular momenta contribute, directly linking near-field spatial localization to the hierarchy of modal absorption constraints.

papers.title: Expansion in powers of simple groups of Lie type
papers.abstract: We prove an expansion theorem for direct powers of all nonabelian finite simple groups $G$ other than the alternating groups and the Suzuki groups ${}^2B_2(q)$. If $G^m$ is generated by $d\ge2$ elements, then $G^m$ has a symmetric generating multiset of at most $Cd$ elements and normalized spectral gap at least $C^{-1}d^{-\log_2 3}$, for an absolute constant $C>0$. In particular, this answers a question of Sabatini on $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{F}_p)^p$. For $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$, we use the expander graphs constructed by Lubotzky--Samuels--Vishne, and an amplification trick for direct powers; in high rank, we use the Ershov--Jaikin-Zapirain property (T) theorem.

papers.title: Criterion for Glasner property and IC-Rigidity for actions on homogeneous space
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a semi-group acting continuously on a compact metric space $X$. The action $G\curvearrowright X$ is called Glasner if for every infinite set $A\subseteq X$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists $g\in G$ such that $gA$ is $\varepsilon$-dense in $X$. Let $\mathcal{K}(X)$ denote the space of nonempty compact subsets of $X$. A $G$-invariant Borel probability measure on $\mathcal{K}(X)$ is called an invariant random compact (IRC), and the action is IC-rigid if $\delta_X$ is the only IRC supported on infinite compact subsets of $X$. In this paper we give a pair-correlation criterion implying both IC-rigidity and the Glasner property. As an application, we prove both these properties for finitely generated $\operatorname{Ad}$-Zariski-dense semi-groups acting on compact homogeneous spaces $G/\Lambda$, where $G$ is connected and noncompact with simple Lie algebra and $\Lambda<G$ is a cocompact lattice; in particular, this applies to finitely generated Zariski-dense semi-groups of $\mathrm{SL}_d(\mathbb{R})$ and $\mathrm{PSL}_d(\mathbb{R})$. We also derive a Fourier-analytic criterion for semi-group actions on $\mathbb{T}^d$ and use it to prove IC-rigidity for actions arising from suitable matrix-valued polynomials.

papers.title: Wideband Hybrid Beamforming via Programmable Unitary Mixer--TTD RF Networks
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a wideband hybrid beamforming architecture whose analog front-end consists of fixed unitary mixers interlaced with programmable diagonal phase-shift/true-time-delay (TTD) layers. Under ideal passive-component assumptions, the analog beamformer is semi-unitary on every OFDM subcarrier, so the injected RF-chain power reaches the antenna ports without analog-network loss. We design the phase shifts and delays of the programmable diagonal phase-shift/TTD layers for OFDM sum-rate maximization. Numerical results show that increasing mixer--TTD depth improves the sum rate under ideal component assumptions and a common injected RF-power budget. With component losses included, a shallow design retains an advantage over the evaluated hybrid baselines at low-to-moderate powers, motivating deeper implementations with low accumulated loss.

papers.title: Torsion phenomena in symplectic capacities via Clarke duality
papers.abstract: We study Gutt--Hutchings capacities with finite cyclic coefficients and show that torsion in positive $S^1$-equivariant symplectic homology detects new obstructions to symplectic embeddings between convex toric domains. Prime-field coefficients give no additional obstructions in this class, while the torsion responsible for the new obstructions already appears over $\mathbb Z/p^{p+2}$ for every prime $p$. We prove a stabilization theorem for these capacities on convex bodies with arbitrary commutative coefficients, yielding a sharp stabilized embedding obstruction in an explicit example. Clarke duality makes these phenomena accessible to computation. We extend the filtered equivariant Clarke--Floer comparison to arbitrary commutative coefficient rings and compute the capacities using models of dual action sublevels built from representation spheres. The circle-action weights encode orbit covering multiplicities, whose products govern the new obstructions.

papers.title: Whose Side Are You On? Measuring Stance at Scale for Reddit Discourse Analysis During the Israel-Gaza War
papers.abstract: Large-scale discourse analysis often requires stance labels, yet for many high-salience political events such labels are unavailable at the comment level. We introduce and validate a comment-level stance measurement instrument that assigns Pro-Israel, Pro-Palestinian, or Undefined stance using Reddit comment text. The instrument is calibrated from a small, manually annotated gold-standard dataset and scaled through large language model-assisted labeling, achieving weighted-$F_{1}=0.88$ against held-out human annotations. To enable corpus-scale measurement, we operationalize the instrument as a lightweight classifier based on DistilBERT embeddings and an RBF SVM, which achieves weighted-$F_{1}=0.7935$ on the original gold-standard set. Applying this instrument, we measure the stance of approximately 2.7 million Reddit comments posted between 2023 and 2025 during the Israel-Gaza war. We demonstrate what this measurement enables by analyzing stance-conditioned asymmetries in sentiment, toxicity, and emotional framing across political affiliations. This work shows how validated, low-cost stance measurement can support large-scale descriptive analysis of polarized discourse, without relying on network structure or prior labeled corpora.

papers.title: Explicit Regularization for Flow Matching
papers.abstract: Learning the underlying probability distribution from samples is a core problem in statistics and applied mathematics. Generative models based on diffusion and flow matching learn a velocity field whose flow transports a known distribution to the data distribution. They produce novel, realistic samples, although the empirical learning problem is ill posed near the data distribution. Its minimizer transports the samples onto the training data, and small perturbations of the data change the velocity field strongly near the end of the flow. The observed generalization is often attributed to implicit regularization by the network parameterization, early stopping of the training, and the time integration during sampling. Explicit regularization has advanced the theory and computation of many inverse problems and has recently been proposed to prevent memorization in generative models. With a regularizer on the magnitude of the velocity, however, the field approaches the memorizing velocity unless the regularization parameter grows to infinity fast enough, and it then stays bounded by a constant that is small only for large parameters. We show that penalizing the derivatives of order $k$ of the velocity renders the $D$-dimensional empirical problem well posed uniformly in time if $2k > D$ and the training points are in general position. Our experiments in one and two dimensions discretize the velocity with splines and use direct solvers for the regularized least-squares problems to exclude optimization error. Refining the discretization in space and time changes the error of the Hessian-regularized flows only marginally, whereas without the regularizer the error tends to that of memorization. These flows generalize, with errors comparable to or lower than those of well-tuned kernel density estimates.

papers.title: Minimal Models for Free Quasi-Invariant and Stationary Actions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we generalize the fact that essentially free p.m.p. actions of a countably infinite group admit a minimal model, proved by Weiss and Zucker. We prove that minimal models exist for every essentially free non singular action. Furthermore, as in the p.m.p. case, we prove that all essentially free $\mu$-stationary actions (with respect to a fixed generating probability measure $\mu$) admit a common minimal model.

papers.title: FIDEL: Abugida-Aware Pre-tokenization for Ethiopic Languages
papers.abstract: Subword tokenizers assume that meaningful linguistic units can be recovered by splitting text at learned boundaries, an assumption better suited to concatenative morphology than to Semitic root-and-pattern systems. The challenge is acute for the Ethiopic languages, whose abugida script encodes consonant-vowel units as single characters and hides consonantal structure. We introduce FIDEL (FId\"al DEcomposition and Linearization), a family of reversible abugida-aware pre-tokenization schemes that expose consonant and vowel-order structure, extend SPLINTER reductions from abjad scripts to the Ethiopic abugida, and evaluate them on three Ethiopic languages under controlled conditions, holding corpus, architecture, budget and protocol fixed so that tokenization is the only variable. We report intrinsic tokenizer statistics for BPE and UnigramLM across vocabulary sizes alongside downstream NLP tasks, including transfer scenarios. We find that FIDEL reduction improves news classification consistently and named-entity recognition at larger capacity, while sentiment analysis performance declines under the more aggressive schemes, and extractive question answering performance is preserved.

papers.title: Tracing the Luminosity Evolution of Globular Cluster Systems with JWST: MACS J1149.5+2223 at z=0.544
papers.abstract: We present a study of the compact-source population associated with the massive galaxy cluster MACS J1149.5+2223 at z=0.544 using deep JWST/NIRCam imaging in F115W, F150W, and F200W. After photometric and morphological selection, we identify 1,202 unresolved compact-source candidates. The observed luminosity distribution samples only the bright side of the expected globular-cluster luminosity function (GCLF), remaining several magnitudes above the turnover. Based on published GCLF turnovers for Abell 2744 and MACS 0417, we adopt an expected turnover magnitude of m_0=33.66 mag for MACS 1149. A forward-modeled fit then yields sigma=1.71 mag, which characterizes the observed bright-side slope under the adopted turnover rather than the intrinsic width of the full GCLF. Comparison with PARSEC simple stellar population models shows that the elevated luminosities of the compact sources are consistent with the expected fading of younger stellar populations as they evolve toward the present epoch. The brightest sources reach luminosities comparable to those of ultra-compact dwarfs. However, stellar-population degeneracies and possible foreground contamination make it difficult to distinguish. Together with recent JWST studies of globular cluster systems across a range of redshifts, MACS 1149 extends the emerging observational sequence of compact stellar systems and supports stellar population fading as an important contributor to their luminosity evolution across cosmic time.

papers.title: Rest-frame annihilation lines of $\sim70$ GeV WIMPs in 23,000 stacked galaxy clusters
papers.abstract: Weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) annihilation features were reported as a 43 GeV line in three Fermi-LAT galaxy clusters ($\mathtt{S}_3$), as triad $\{\gamma\gamma, \gamma Z,\gamma h\}$ lines from $\sim70$ GeV WIMPs in LAT data cross-correlated ($\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$) with western eROSITA X-rays, and as a nonad (combining three triads) of two cross-annihilating WIMPs in $\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$. A blind scan of LAT 16.3-year data around 23,343 high-latitude clusters in their rest frames finds three triads, at 70 GeV ($2.8\sigma$ trial-corrected, henceforth), $72$ GeV ($1.3\sigma$; strengthening to $2.7\sigma$ if mass-fixed by $\mathtt{S}_3$, $4.0\sigma$ combined with $\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$ masked around the clusters, $5.7\sigma$ if also combined with $\mathtt{S}_3$), and 74-75 GeV: a triplet not only rare ($3.5\sigma$) but also forming a $\{70,74\}$ GeV nonad ($3.4\sigma$; strengthening to $4.0\sigma$, $4.6\sigma$, and $6.1\sigma$, respectively). The spectral features, robust in and out of the $\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$ region and $\mathtt{S}_3$ clusters, appear in all Galactic quadrants and only in the cluster rest frame (vanishing upon redshift rescaling or permutation), fade away from cluster centers, are absent from their surrounding stacked fields, and like $\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$ indicate intrinsic few $10^{-19}$ cm$^3$ s$^{-1}$ cross sections (uncorrected) across samples. All features are largely explained by cross-annihilating $69.7^{+0.4}_{-1.0}$ and $74.5^{+1.1}_{-0.6}$ GeV WIMPs.

papers.title: Fix, Don't Retake: Physics-Simulated Training for Correcting Patient Positioning Errors in Dental Panoramic Radiographs
papers.abstract: Patient-positioning errors can distort panoramic radiographs and lead to repeat examinations. This study investigated artificial intelligence for correcting these errors in existing images. A physics-based simulator generated paired correctly positioned and mispositioned panoramics from cone-beam computed tomography volumes, with controlled individual and combined positioning errors. Five approaches were compared: U-Net, pix2pix, conditional diffusion, an error-conditioned model, and a mixture of error-specific specialists. Evaluation used image similarity and geometric metrics across three test sets. All approaches improved mean image similarity and reduced geometric errors, with U-Net and the two error-aware approaches outperforming pix2pix and conditional diffusion.

papers.title: IZM-DSR: A New Zone-Disjoint Multi-path Routing Algorithm for Mobile Ad-Hoc Network
papers.abstract: Some of multi-path routing algorithms in MANETs use multiple paths simultaneously. These algorithms can attempt to find node-disjoint to achieve higher fault tolerance. By using node-disjoint paths, it is expected that the end-to-end delay in each case should be independent of each other. However, because of natural properties and medium access mechanisms in ad hoc networks, such as CSMA/CA, the endto-end delay between any source and destination depends on the pattern of communication in the neighborhood region. In this case some of the intermediate nodes should be silent to reverence their neighbors and this matter increases the end-toend delay. To avoid this problem, multi-path routing algorithms can use zone-disjoint paths instead of node-disjoint paths. In this paper we propose a new multi-path routing algorithm that selects zone-disjoint paths, using omnidirectional antenna. We evaluate our algorithm in several different scenarios. The simulation results show that our approach is very effective in decreasing routing overhead and end-to-end delay.

papers.title: Improving X-Ray Baggage Instance Segmentation with Shared Point-Based Mask Refinement
papers.abstract: Overlapping projections and complex object contours make prohibited items difficult to delineate in X-ray baggage images. This study investigates shared point-based mask refinement to improve instance segmentation within Cascade Mask R-CNN. The framework combines a ResNet-101 backbone with an attention-based feature pyramid and progressively updates uncertain mask locations, increasing mask resolution from $28 \times 28$ to $112 \times 112$. A single refinement module is shared across cascade stages and refinement levels, with transformer and multilayer perceptron (MLP) variants used to examine the role of interactions among selected points. Ten configurations were evaluated on the official PIXray split across three training seeds using the original target-instance annotations for evaluation. The transformer and MLP refiners achieved mean mask average precision (AP) of 71.79 and 72.47, respectively, compared with 70.50 for the unrefined detector, yielding gains of 1.29 and 1.97 AP points. The MLP achieved the highest mean mask AP among the evaluated configurations. Both variants also improved boundary agreement on commonly detected objects, supporting improved mask delineation, while detection diagnostics did not establish a corresponding positive gain. These findings demonstrate that shared point-based refinement can improve segmentation quality in the tested cascade architecture using existing target-mask annotations, without additional occluder supervision. Evaluation on independent X-ray datasets is needed to determine how well these improvements generalize.

authors.name: Qasim Umer
authors.institution: King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals

papers.title: Beyond Seeing: Fine-Grained Preference Validation and Severity-Aware Alignment for Mitigating Visual Hallucinations in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Large vision-language models can produce fluent responses containing objects, attributes, or relations unsupported by the image. We study an implemented alignment pipeline that normalizes released fine-grained hallucination supervision, validates chosen-rejected preference pairs with vision-language judges, repairs rejected chosen responses, and trains LLaVA adapters with standard or severity-aware direct preference optimization. The study uses 16,143 normalized feedback records and 8,386 released preference pairs, comparing direct training with zero-shot and two-shot judged severity-margin variants. The zero-shot variant reduces Object HalBench CHAIRs from 53.00 to 36.00 and CHAIRi from 15.72 to 10.41. Across aligned models, AMBER-Hal decreases from 35.90 to 25.10-26.90, accompanied by reduced visual coverage. In contrast, the base model retains the highest valid POPE adversarial F1, 84.18 versus 83.87-83.91 after alignment. These results support benchmark-dependent reductions in generative hallucination rather than uniform superiority of severity-aware alignment. We distinguish implemented pipeline components from the preference paths used in the reported experiments and discuss the limits of attributing gains to judging, repair, or the training objective individually.

papers.title: Technical Report of Auriga's 1:10 Scale Autonomous Vehicle Robot
papers.abstract: This report presents the design and implementation of Auriga Robotics' 1:10 scale autonomous vehicle, developed at Shahid Beheshti University's Robotics and Intelligent Automation Laboratory. The platform integrates a custom mechanical chassis, a distributed embedded system based on ESP32 microcontrollers, and a Jetson Orin NX module for high-level perception and control. The embedded layer manages sensor interfacing, real-time data acquisition, and actuator control, while the Jetson handles environment perception through deep-learning--based lane, sign, and traffic light detection, as well as decision-making and trajectory control. System communication is achieved via structured UART links, ensuring synchronized operation between perception and control subsystems. The vehicle's software stack incorporates ROS, modular firmware design, and multiple control algorithms---Stanley, PID, and Pure Pursuit---to achieve stable autonomous navigation in structured driving scenarios. The overall system demonstrates robust performance and reliability in urban-like environments, serving as a modular research platform for future autonomous driving studies.

papers.intro:
Autonomous driving represents one of the most advanced integrations of control theory and computer vision, and is of high importance in self-driving cars in the current age. To explore these concepts in a manageable and scalable way, Auriga Robotics at Shahid Beheshti University developed a 1:10 scale autonomous vehicle designed to perform perception, decision-making, and control in real time. The project was carried out as part of the team’s ongoing research in intelligent robotics and autonomous navigation systems, with the goal of building a modular platform suitable for academic experimentation. An image of the robot is attached in Fig. 1.

Autonomous driving represents one of the most advanced integrations of control theory and computer vision, and is of high importance in self-driving cars in the current age. To explore these concepts in a manageable and scalable way, Auriga Robotics at Shahid Beheshti University developed a 1:10 scale autonomous vehicle designed to perform perception, decision-making, and control in real time. The project was carried out as part of the team’s ongoing research in intelligent robotics and autonomous navigation systems, with the goal of building a modular platform suitable for academic experimentation. An image of the robot is attached in Fig. 1.

The primary objective of the project was to design a complete autonomous driving stack, that includes hardware, embedded firmware, and high-level perception algorithms. The vehicle was required to detect and follow lanes, recognize traffic signs and lights, and maintain stable longitudinal and lateral control under various driving scenarios. To achieve this, the system was divided into three processing layers: low-level sensor integration and actuation was handled by two ESP32 microcontrollers (called CONTROL and ZERO), and high-level perception and decision-making executed on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX mini-computer, in which all three units maintained stable communication with each other. On the software side, implemented on the Jetson Orin NX, the architecture was built around ROS (Robot Operating System) [4] to allow modular algorithm development, parallel debugging, and integration of computer vision and control pipelines.
