This study develops a comprehensive Bayesian stochastic calibration framework integrating sequential Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) estimation via a Metropolis-Hastings within Gibbs sampling scheme with a novel Bias-Variance Cone analysis for asymptotic parameter identification. The framework is applied to 17 macroscopic speed-density models using one full year of 5-minute PeMS loop detector data from three California freeway stations. Sequential MCMC progressively increases the number of randomly sampled days from 1 to 365, enabling systematic evaluation of parameter stability and convergence as a function of data availability. Among the 17 models, nine achieved stable posterior convergence with physically interpretable estimates, while four exhibited catastrophic structural failures due to logarithmic singularities, unit incompatibilities, and initialization sensitivity. The Bias-Variance Cone framework, representing the first application of asymptotic bias-variance decomposition to fundamental diagram calibration, establishes that free-flow speed parameters are reliably identified within approximately 30 days, whereas density and shape parameters require 100 to 182 days, providing the first quantitative minimum data requirements in the literature. Collectively, the findings provide an empirical identifiability ranking of 17 fundamental diagram models, a validated minimum data sufficiency framework, and a replicable, automated platform for large-scale stochastic fundamental diagram calibration.

authors.name: Md Asif Raihan
authors.institution: Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology

authors.name: Md. Hadiuzzaman
authors.institution: Bangladesh Army University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Adaptive nonorthogonal atomic orbitals refine charge transfer and bonding descriptors
papers.abstract: First-principles calculations implicitly encode bonding and charge transfer, but converting periodic electronic structure into interpretable and transferable descriptors remains challenging. Recently, we introduced Crystal Orbital Guided Iteration To atomic-Orbitals (COGITO), a tool for mapping plane-wave DFT back to an interpretable, minimal basis of adaptive atomic orbitals. Here, we show how the high-dimensional bonding information from COGITO can be reduced into chemically useful descriptors of covalent bonding, charge transfer, and crystal-dependent atomic chemistry without collapsing the real-space origin of the interactions. Compared to methods that use static or orthogonal orbital bases, COGITO descriptors of short- and long-range bonding show more stability and a better ability to distinguish between ionic, covalent, and metallic bonding regimes. Lastly, COGITO reliably decomposes band dispersion into range-resolved contributions, allowing us to verify and add to the orbital origins of silicon's low-symmetry conduction band minimum. Overall, the adaptive COGITO-based descriptors encode electronic structure, offering a well-structured route to expose the orbital interactions and charge transfer responsible for electronic properties.

papers.title: Aspirational Identities: How VTubing Affords New Modes of Digital Embodiment
papers.abstract: VTubing, short for "Virtual YouTubing", is a modality of streaming where a CGI avatar is used in place of the streamer's analog face and body. As VTubing has become increasingly popular, especially for queer and trans streamers of color, it is worth studying as a way for streamers to express identities that they hope to embody, which we call "aspirational identities". In this workshop submission, we draw on preliminary findings from qualitative research to argue that VTubing is a potent object of study for understanding digital embodiment and the performance of identity online, especially for questions of race, gender, sexuality, and disability.

papers.title: A Systematic Study of Cross-Token Transfer for Data-Efficient Non-Verbal Text-to-Speech
papers.abstract: Non-verbal vocalizations (NVs), such as laughter and breath, carry affective cues that words alone do not convey. Yet NV data remains scarce because speech annotation pipelines often omit or normalize these events. Existing work has improved NV text-to-speech through model design and data curation, but whether one NV token can help a model learn another has received little systematic study. We investigate this cross-token transferability in a controlled CosyVoice 2 setup. We first trace a laughter-only scaling curve, then hold laughter at 200 or 1,600 examples while adding breath, sigh, cough, lip-smack, or neutral speech. With only 200 laughter examples, adding 3,200 cough examples raises end-to-end laughter F1 from 0.170 to 0.529, surpassing the 0.495 obtained from 1,600 laughter examples alone. At the 1,600-example anchor, cough reaches 0.695, nearly matching 6,400 laughter examples (0.697). Waveform-level Whisper-D scoring and a semantic-token transcriber show consistent trends. Cross-token transfer therefore offers a complementary route to low-resource NV generation.

papers.title: Fourier Crosstalk and Leakage Correction for Binary-Encoded Fourier Single-Pixel Imaging
papers.abstract: Digital micromirror devices enable high-speed Fourier single-pixel imaging (Fourier-SPI), but their binary modulation introduces quantization errors that degrade the reconstructed image quality. In particular, each binarized Fourier probe contains non-target Fourier components, thereby distorting the corresponding Fourier-domain measurement. This Letter presents a Fourier domain correction framework that characterizes these errors using the Fourier-domain response matrix of the decoded binary Fourier patterns. Accordingly, a response-matrix-based Fourier-SPI measurement model is established by partitioning the matrix into components associated with the sampled and unsampled frequencies, thereby decomposing the quantization error into sampled-frequency crosstalk and unsampled-frequency leakage. This model established a generalized correction framework, termed Fourier Crosstalk and Leakage Correction (FCLC), alongside two simplified methods: Fourier Sampled-Frequency Crosstalk Correction (FSCC) and Fourier DC Crosstalk Correction (FDCC). FSCC is implemented via an inversion-free Richardson-type iteration, whereas FDCC admits a closed-form solution. Numerical simulations and experiments across multiple binary encoding strategies reveal that the proposed framework improves reconstruction fidelity without modifying the binary patterns or acquisition process.

papers.title: A quantitative measure of predictability for surface gravity waves
papers.abstract: We introduce a Bayesian inference framework to characterize the predictability of a one dimensional ocean surface wave field given surface elevation measurements from a sensor. Unlike the classical theories that only sketch the boundary of a predictable zone based on group velocity, we use the Bayesian posterior uncertainty of surface elevation to quantify the local predictability at every spatiotemporal location. Our approach first constructs a prior distribution to encode existing knowledge of the wave field such as the spectrum and propagation direction. By conditioning on the (possibly noisy) measurement data, we infer the posterior distribution of the wave field, from which a spatiotemporal uncertainty map is extracted. This map agrees well with the group-velocity-based classical predictable zone theory when the frequency spectrum has bounded support. Meanwhile, it also demonstrates predictability even for a spectrum with unbounded frequency support where the classical predictable zone degenerates. A refined analysis of posterior uncertainty using observability Gramian matrix reveals a `data-informed' part and an `un-informed' part of the wave field, with the latter being fundamentally un-predictable. Furthermore, nonlinear effects can be naturally introduced into the Bayesian framework by incorporating the nonlinear ocean surface wave equations. This is the first time that nonlinearity is rigorously treated in the predictable zone problem. We perform numerical tests using both bounded, piecewise constant spectrum and unbounded JONSWAP spectrum. The numerical results confirm the proposed advantages of our method for linear waves and reveal how wave steepness affects the predictability of nonlinear waves. Nonlinear modal interactions redistribute uncertainty between the inside and the outside of the predictable zone with an amount proportional to the wave steepness.

authors.name: Jing Sun
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: With the Right Representation, Classical Machine Learning Rivals Deep Models for Olfactory Mixture Similarity
papers.abstract: Modeling olfactory mixtures remains a critical challenge in machine olfaction because the task requires reasoning over relationships between sets of odorants rather than over individual molecules in isolation. However, prior comparisons between deep and classical approaches also varied how the relationship between the two mixtures was represented, since the classical baselines primarily relied on weak representations that described each mixture independently and provided little direct signal about how the mixtures differed. In this work, we revisit classical learning using explicit symmetric comparison features on unordered pairs of mixtures, evaluating these representations with XGBoost and kernel ridge regression (KRR). We find that XGBoost with explicit comparison features achieves performance competitive with specialized deep mixture models on the main benchmark. Ablation studies show that coordinate-wise absolute differences alone provide strong predictive performance, while combining them with sums and products yields further improvements. KRR also benefits substantially from explicit comparison features, with further gains from appropriate kernel choice and preprocessing. Overall, these results suggest that explicitly encoding how two mixtures differ is an important ingredient for classical machine learning in low-data olfactory mixture prediction.

papers.title: Demographic dynamics of the Japanese astronomy and astrophysics publication community during 1996-2025
papers.abstract: We investigate the demographic evolution of the Japanese astronomy and astrophysics publication community during 1996-2025 using bibliometric data from 23,274 publications in major journals in the field. The number of active Japan-affiliated authors increased from approximately 600 in the late 1990s to more than 2,000 by the early 2020s, while annual publication output reached approximately 1,400 by 2025. Participation was highly heterogeneous, with 46% of authors observed in only one publication year within the study period and a smaller core showing long observed participation periods. We define the Community Renewal Rate (CRR) as a community-level measure of renewal, calculated as the fraction of active authors not observed during a specified preceding interval. The 5-year CRR typically remained near one quarter of the active community, with annual values ranging from approximately 21% to 33%, indicating persistent renewal despite substantial community growth. An order-of-magnitude comparison suggests that newly entering students account for only part of the renewal-author population. The community therefore expanded while sustaining both continuity through authors with long observed participation periods and renewal through recurring changes in active membership.

papers.title: Learning from Distribution: Rethinking One-Hot Supervision for ASR and QA in Speech Language Models
papers.abstract: Speech language models (SLMs) exhibit strong capabilities in automatic speech recognition (ASR) and general-purpose speech understanding, yet ASR-specific training often degrades spoken question answering (QA) performance. We revisit this conflict from the perspective of task-specific input--output mappings and one-hot supervision. Our findings reveal pronounced task-asymmetric effects: ASR-only training severely limits QA capability, whereas QA-only training retains reasonable ASR performance. We hypothesize that the relatively deterministic mapping of ASR, combined with single-reference supervision, biases models toward transcription-specific behavior. Motivated by this perspective, we advocate broadening ASR learning objectives while preserving recognition accuracy. We propose Learning from Distribution (LFD), which aligns speech-conditioned predictions with the conditional output distributions of a pretrained text LLM. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LFD improves both ASR and QA performance, exhibits superior data efficiency, and remains effective under full-parameter fine-tuning. CoT-ASR further supports the broader applicability of our proposed supervision principle.

papers.title: An Efficient Training Paradigm for Image Restoration via Improved Fr\'echet Loss
papers.abstract: Diffusion-based image restoration achieves strong perceptual quality but typically relies on iterative sampling, leading to slow inference. Existing single-step methods often use diffusion distillation or adversarial training, complicating optimization. To simplify training, we propose FDIR, a framework for training single-pass generative restoration models through regression-style supervised optimization using directly computable objectives. To realize this paradigm, FDIR employs the Fr\'echet distance to match the feature distributions of restored and real images in frozen representation spaces, providing explicit distribution-level supervision. To better accommodate image restoration, we incorporate local patch features to capture fine-grained restoration discrepancies. Moreover, we introduce instance-adaptive statistics by combining the feature moments of each SR-HQ pair with synchronized historical statistics, allowing distribution matching to incorporate input-specific correspondence while retaining distribution-level context. FDIR optimizes only the LoRA parameters of the restoration backbone. Experiments demonstrate strong perceptual restoration quality and efficient training, suggesting a simpler paradigm for generative image restoration.

papers.title: Agent-Native by Design: A Programming Language for Agentic Applications
papers.abstract: Building agentic applications requires combining large language model (LLM) operations, workflow structure and application state, and model-guided routing. With SDKs and agent frameworks, developers connect these components through supporting code that prepares model inputs, propagates state, and dispatches model-selected steps. Workflow changes can require coordinated updates to this code, increasing development and testing effort. Splitting execution logic between application code and framework internals also limits compiler visibility into control flow and state dependencies, hindering automatic optimization. We introduce Agent-Native Programming, which unifies these three components with shared execution semantics. We realize this approach in Jac, a Python-superset language, through "by llm()" for typed model operations and tool use, Object-Spatial Programming for workflow structure and state, and "visit ... by llm()" for model-guided routing. The routing construct derives the model's choices from executable workflow steps and schedules the selected steps. This explicit connection between model decisions and program execution gives the compiler and runtime a common basis for dependency analysis and automatic optimization. Across five benchmarks and five baselines, Jac achieves a 1.8-8.7x reduction in AI-integration code relative to the OpenAI SDK, with competitive observed task quality and lower coding-agent development effort. Two case studies demonstrate speculative execution and service partitioning through configuration alone, using program analysis and runtime checks to preserve workflow behavior under stated conditions.

papers.title: Arithmetic Universality and Integer Decomposition in Disjunctions of Three Staircase Simplices
papers.abstract: The staircase simplices $\{x\in[0,1]^d:x_{\sigma(1)}\le\cdots\le x_{\sigma(d)}\}$, $\sigma\in S_d\,$, are the $d!$ unimodular cells of the staircase triangulation of the unit cube. The disjunctive hull (Cayley polytope) of a selection $P_0, \ldots, P_n$ of them has the integer decomposition property (IDP) if, for all integers $\lambda_i\ge0$, every lattice point of $\sum_i\lambda_i P_i$ is a sum of vertices, $\lambda_i$ of them from $P_i$. For two simplices, IDP always holds. For three, every nontrivial finite abelian group $G$ arises, in the optimal dimension $\Theta(\log|G|)$, as the residue group of a simplex facet whose $|G|-1$ nonzero box points are Hilbert basis elements of the whole cone; $k$ times such a point is a sum of vertices exactly when its order in $G$ divides $k$. Isolating this arithmetic is costly: if a simplex face has a single Hilbert basis element $h$ that is not a vertex, then $kh$ is a sum of vertices exactly when some $q$ divides $k$, and $d\ge3q-2$, attained for every $q\ge3$; we also find the least dimension for each $G$ with the fewest such elements. Without isolation, every nonzero submonoid of $\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ omitting $1$ is $\{k\ge0:kh$ is a sum of vertices$\}$ for a Hilbert basis element $h$ of degree three. For every $0/1$ polytope with $N$ vertices in $\mathbb{R}^r$, three staircase simplices in dimension $O(N(r+1))$ have a face that has IDP exactly when the polytope does. Deciding whether a lattice point $h$ is a sum of vertices is strongly NP-complete, even given vertex expressions of $2h$ and $3h$, and recognizing IDP of a designated facet is coNP-complete; for the whole hull, IDP can first fail in degree linear in $d$, and it holds whenever $d\le5$. For a family of triples defined by words over three letters, we determine the entire Hilbert basis and characterize IDP by two forbidden subsequences.

papers.title: Adaptive Sparsity-Aware Projection-Assisted Spectral Embedding for High-Dimensional Noisy Data with Nonlinear Structures
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose SPASE, an adaptive, sparsity-aware, projection-assisted spectral embedding method for feature extraction from high-dimensional noisy data with underlying nonlinear structures and latent sparsity patterns. We first construct a data-driven projection that adapts to the hidden sparsity patterns and the signal-to-noise ratio, reducing noise-induced distortion of pairwise distances. We then apply kernel-based spectral embedding to the projected data to explore the underlying geometric structure. The key methodological contribution is an energy-based projection selection algorithm that is adaptive to the signal-to-noise ratio and sparsity of the signal representation, while mitigating the impact of noise. On the theoretical side, we show that the resulting embeddings converge to the eigenfunctions of an integral operator associated with the latent signal, and the method can remain effective when the signal-to-noise ratio is low. We demonstrate the empirical performance of the proposed method through simulation studies and real-data applications, showing improved accuracy in downstream tasks such as classification and clustering.

papers.title: SearchChord: Prompt Preselection and Field Recomposition for One-Step Image Editing
papers.abstract: Finding effective prompts and seeds for one-step image editors requires balancing edit fidelity, source preservation, and computational cost. To address this challenge, we explore a large collection of candidate edits, where each candidate is defined by a unique prompt-seed pair, and generate corresponding images on demand. We present SearchChord, a training-free framework that leverages a large pool of such candidates, combining text-based preselection, image verification, and latent-field recomposition. Our ablation studies across pool sizes up to 200 candidates show that a pool of 100 offers a cost-effective operating point. Compared with feeding all 100 candidates into recomposition, TextSim preselects a subset of 10 candidates. Rather than uniform averaging, we incorporate image-verifier scores to weight each candidate during recomposition. Experiments on PIE-Bench and the proposed CropWeed-EditBench reveal a trade-off: candidate selection improves target-text alignment, while recomposition better preserves unmodified source content. The oracle verifier achieves the best performance in both preservation and target-text alignment. Practical verification partially recovers semantic alignment, but recomposition still compromises edit fidelity, including in agricultural image edits. These results motivate text-first preselection and stronger verification to balance preservation, fidelity, and cost. Code and data will be made publicly available.

papers.title: Hardening Agentic Web Populations Through Multi-Criterion Competitive Co-Evolution: Lessons from Wargame Strategy Optimization
papers.abstract: Agents on the open web will face adversaries that keep adapting, so a defense that is only tested once will eventually be found and broken. We propose treating jailbreak attacks and safety guardrails as two populations that evolve against each other, rather than as a fixed attacker probing a fixed defense. This idea comes directly from wargame strategy optimization, where two-population competitive co-evolution with alternating evolution cycles and cross-play evaluation has already been shown to produce strategies that are robust to a moving opponent, and where a companion line of work has shown that the same machinery can measure how much competitive pressure a population must absorb. However, real-world applications can never rely on a single criterion as a key performance indicator, rather must use multiple conflicting criteria, such as, cost and efficiency. We describe how this mechanism transfers to language model safety, argue why the resulting multi-criteria, competitive and coevolutionary arms race is a genuinely networked, population-level problem rather than a two-agent toy setting, and lay out the open problems that stand between the wargame version of this idea and an agentic web version of it.

papers.title: Maximum Scores and Treatment Feedback in Regression Discontinuity Designs
papers.abstract: Hospitals use repeated risk scores to decide when to send an alert. Some evaluations summarize these scores by their maximum and use the maximum as the running variable in a regression discontinuity (RD) design. The maximum shows correctly whether a patient was ever alerted. However, it can include scores recorded after an earlier alert has already changed care. In this paper, we study what the maximum-score RD estimates when an earlier intervention changes a later score. We use a two-assessment model and derive a formula that splits the RD contrast into the causal effect and a composition term. When feedback moves scores in one direction, the composition term equals the relative jump in the density of the maximum at the cutoff times a prognostic contrast. Therefore, an exactly continuous density means no bias, and the population density jump bounds the bias. Valid inference on the jump turns this into a confidence bound under a stated sensitivity assumption. Within this model, bias behind a continuous density requires feedback in both directions. For this case, we bound bias by total boundary movement and construct conservative confidence sets for binary outcomes under explicit sensitivity and smoothness assumptions. We give closed forms for independent uniform scores and for correlated Gaussian scores. In one example, a true risk reduction of four percentage points appears as a one-point increase. Simulations confirm the formulas. Narrower bandwidths, robust bias correction, and machine-learning covariate adjustment do not remove the bias. A fuzzy RD on the first score recovers the causal effect when early and late treatment have the same effect. Our results concern how the running variable is built. We do not assess any published clinical study.

papers.title: Large gaps and the ten martini problem for monotone quasiperiodic Schr\"odinger operators
papers.abstract: We prove the ten martini theorem for a large class of monotone potentials. The key strategy is to establish polynomially large gaps for periodic approximations.

papers.title: LEAP-LLM: Preserving lead-time structure for question-conditioned ECG interpretation
papers.abstract: The electrocardiogram (ECG) records cardiac electrical activity across multiple leads and is used for detecting cardiac abnormalities. Recent ECG-language models enable large language models (LLMs) to interpret cardiac signals and answer clinically relevant questions. However, existing ECG-language models typically encode the ECG independently of the clinical question, forcing the ECG representation to retain broad and potentially irrelevant signal information. Moreover, these models often aggregate information across leads which can obscure lead-specific details needed for a particular question. To tackle these limitations, we introduce LEAP-LLM, an ECG-LLM architecture for Lead-aware ECG Alignment with Prompt conditioning. LEAP-LLM uses the clinical question to guide ECG feature extraction while preserving explicit lead and temporal structure. Task-trained instruction representations distill information from the question and guide two complementary branches. The Lead branch captures question-relevant temporal patterns within each ECG lead, while the Temporal branch summarizes relevant information across leads at each temporal position. Together, they provide the LLM with compact, question-relevant ECG information while preserving lead and temporal structure. LEAP-LLM reduces modality-token count by 89.0% and prefill FLOPs by 7.2x on average relative to other ECG-LLMs baselines. Across four ECG benchmarks, LEAP-LLM achieves better performance, including a 3.4-percentage-point improvement in G12EC over the strongest prior ECG-specific method. We further show that the model adaptively emphasizes the clinically relevant anatomical lead groups for different cardiac abnormalities, with lead importance patterns consistent with established diagnostic knowledge, providing interpretable evidence that the predictions are supported by clinically meaningful ECG structure.

papers.title: A Proof of The Twin-Star Hypothesis in Dimension Five
papers.abstract: It was recently shown that the question of whether the determinant-like map \(\det^{S^2}\) is unique up to multiplication by a scalar is equivalent to a combinatorial conjecture regarding cycle-free \(d\)-partitions of the complete graph \(K_{2d}\), known as the twin-star hypothesis. This hypothesis asserts that every cycle-free \(d\)-partition of \(K_{2d}\) is weakly equivalent to one that contains a component isomorphic to the twin-star graph \(TS_d\). This hypothesis was previously established for \(d\le4\). In the present paper, we prove it for \(d=5\). Consequently, the associated determinant-like map \(\det^{S^2}\) is unique up to a scalar in dimension \(5\).

papers.title: Who Can You Hide Behind? Author-Conditioned Style Transfer and the Evasion of a Commercial AI-Text Detector
papers.abstract: AI-text detectors can be sensitive to changes in writing style. We examined this sensitivity by rewriting 991 AI-generated answers with Gemini, using prompts that included a writing sample from one of 55 named authors. We scored each original and its rewrite with the QuillBot AI detector. The median score fell from 100% to 0%, and the mean fell from 67.9% to 11.2%. Of the rewrites, 66% received a score of exactly 0%. Among the 699 originals scored at least 50%, 71% of rewrites scored below 10% (paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p-value below 1e-100). Scores varied across the authors used in the prompts. All rewrites associated with 10 authors scored 0%, whereas the mean score remained above 50% for six authors (Kruskal-Wallis test, p-value below 1e-80). Greater reuse of five-word sequences from the author sample was associated with lower scores, although rewrites with less than 5% reuse still averaged 15.2%. These results describe one detector and one rewriting system, not detectors in general. The study lacks a generic-rewrite baseline, did not measure preservation of meaning, and produced rewrites that were substantially longer than the originals.

papers.title: The Logic Chain Breaking Point: A Controlled-Variable Benchmark for Reasoning Degradation in Open-Weight Language Models
papers.abstract: We introduce The Logic Chain Breaking Point, a controlled-variable benchmark for deductive reasoning in open-weight language models. It spans three phases: (i) pure modus-ponens chain scaling, (ii) distractor resilience with a fixed core chain, and (iii) contradiction detection under primacy versus recency placement. Independent variables follow a powers-of-two sequence $v \in \{1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128\}$, with ground truth known by construction. We evaluate sixteen open-weight models across instruction-tuned and reasoning-tuned panels, including a small-model suite and a larger local-model extension. All models are evaluated with greedy decoding under model-appropriate context and output budgets, while context- and length-limited trials are quarantined from the valid accuracy denominator. Our results reveal a sharply non-monotonic difficulty surface: pure deductive chains up to $L=128$ remain near saturation for most models, and distractor noise causes only model-specific degradation at high $D$, while the inconsistent premise condition has the lowest accuracy. Instruction-tuned models, including larger 24B--27B baselines, score essentially zero on inconsistent premise sets, while reasoning-tuned models recover only partially and remain below reliable accuracy. Within this benchmark, inconsistent premise sets are associated with the strongest degradation under the benchmark's abstention-based scoring rule.

papers.title: How to make a moral agent: sentimentalism and rationalism as lenses on AI
papers.abstract: Can AI systems be moral agents? That is, can they undertake actions that can be correctly assessed as morally right or wrong? There is no settled normative criterion of moral agency that applies neatly outside paradigm human cases. Because of the difficulties with a normative account, we instead propose a research program to explore descriptive moral agency. Most basically, we ask, what are the capabilities we humans possess that underlie our moral agency? To do so, we draw on historical scholarship in philosophy and moral psychology to isolate candidate capabilities. Then we suggest refining candidate capabilities so that they are testable in the context of AI systems. Finally, we offer specific empirical recommendations to test AI systems, especially large language models (LLMs), for those refined capabilities. Our approach offers several benefits. Firstly, it may demonstrate whether the behaviors of AI systems are aligned, or in a broad sense desirable. Secondly, the debate may inform policy questions (e.g., what models should be deployed in which contexts?). Thirdly, our approach may complement engineering and design efforts: when capabilities can be precisely characterized, they can inform the development of models. Fourthly, applying our moral reasoning concepts in the new context of AI systems should improve our understanding of those concepts.

papers.title: Intrinsic Attention as Navigator: A Non-Generative Retrieval Method for Multi-Hop Queries
papers.abstract: For multi-hop queries in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), it is crucial to accurately obtain evidence pieces. In this study, we propose a training-free method for multi-hop query retrieval, named Intrinsic Navigating-based Non-Generative Retrieval (IN-Retriever). Instead of generating intermediate reasoning text, the method extracts the bridging clue from the internal attention of the embedding model based on the current context and retrieved candidate documents. During iterative clue extraction and document retrieval, IN-Retriever strips away revealed clues from the embedded query vector and then reranks candidate documents in a targeted manner, thereby steering retrieval toward hidden next-hop evidence. In the experiments, we confirm the feasibility and effectiveness of using intrinsic attention signals to guide external multi-hop retrieval. Experimental results show that our method precisely collects sufficient documents to support multi-hop queries and significantly outperforms sparse and dense retrieval methods.

papers.title: Calibrating the Uncertainty of Self-Supervised Monocular Depth without Labels
papers.abstract: Self-supervised monocular depth networks can predict a per-pixel uncertainty, which is mainly evaluated by how well it ranks pixels according to their error. Such metrics are insensitive to the magnitude of the uncertainty, so an uncertainty half as large as the actual error obtains the same score. In this paper, we investigate whether the predicted uncertainty is as large as the depth error, both on average (scale) and across confident and uncertain, near and far pixels (shape). On KITTI, the scale is miscalibrated for every uncertainty estimate we evaluate, and the error of MonoProb is nearly twice its predicted uncertainty. We propose MonoCal, which corrects both the scale and the shape without ground-truth depth. Scale calibration multiplies the uncertainty by a single constant measured from stereo pairs, requiring no retraining, and this constant closely matches the one fitted with ground truth. Since a constant cannot change the shape, we further retrain the uncertainty to predict where the depth of the network disagrees with that of a second self-supervised network. Experiments on KITTI show that MonoCal achieves better calibration across uncertainty levels and depth ranges than rescaling with ground truth, while still using a single image at inference. Code will be made publicly available.

papers.title: Hardware-Friendly Plug-and-Play MVDR Beamforming for Microphone Arrays: Algorithm, Prototype, and System-Level Feasibility
papers.abstract: Beamforming has been widely recognized for its spatial filtering capability in speech signal processing, enabling effective interference rejection and signal enhancement. The performance of adaptive beamforming methods, e.g., the conventional minimum variance distortionless response (MVDR) beamforming, often deteriorate significantly in complex and dynamic acoustic environments. Part of the reason is that such conventional beamforming ignores the intrinsic characteristics of speech. To address this issue, this paper proposes Plug-and-Play Minimum Variance Distortionless Response (PnP-MVDR) algorithm, which integrates data-driven speech prior information into the MVDR framework to enhance robustness against non-stationary noise while maintaining its interpretability. The PnP-MVDR framework supports joint interaction of signal processing and deep learning methods and is designed to be compatible with modern DSP-NPU architectures, making it hardware-friendly for potential edge deployment. Beyond the algorithmic innovation, we have developed a complete microphone beamforming system to validate practical feasibility. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms traditional and deep learning-based baselines, establishing PnP-MVDR as an effective and deployable solution for edge audio scenarios.

papers.title: Computing Independent Sets of Size Three in Disk Graphs
papers.abstract:
We study the problem of computing an independent set of size three in disk graphs, where vertices correspond to disks in the plane and two vertices are adjacent if their disks intersect. While computing a maximum independent set in disk graphs is NP-hard, the fixed-size case admits more efficient solutions. Given a set of $n$ disks, we present an algorithm to compute an independent set of size three in the disk graph and our algorithm runs in randomized expected $O^*(n^{5/3})$ time, where $O^*$ hides a factor of $n^{\epsilon}$ for an arbitrarily small $\epsilon > 0$. Our approach introduces a framework based on semi-algebraic range searching and tree-structured biclique partitions, which allows us to group pairs of disjoint disks into canonical subsets and avoid redundant computations.
  When the centers of the disks are in convex position, we solve the problem in $O(n \log^2 n)$ deterministic time. We also consider the case in which the disks themselves are in convex position, i.e., each disk contributes to the boundary of the convex hull of all disks, and obtain an $O(n \log^2 n)$ time algorithm for this setting as well. Our techniques for these cases are based on geometric properties of disk arrangements. In particular, they rely on new structural lemmas that reduce the problem to efficiently testing certain ordered configurations of disks.
  Our results improve upon the straightforward quadratic time approach and demonstrate how geometric structures and range searching techniques can be leveraged to solve fixed-size independent set problems in disk graphs more efficiently. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first systematic study of independent sets of size three in disk graphs. Our results show that even this smallest nontrivial case exhibits rich structural properties, especially under convexity assumptions.

papers.title: Scale-aware composite forcing enhances forward energy transfer in lattice Boltzmann simulations of forced homogeneous isotropic turbulence
papers.abstract: In forced homogeneous isotropic turbulence (FHIT), conventional large-scale forcing sustains statistical stationarity but offers limited control over energy at intermediate scales. We propose a scale-aware composite forcing strategy for the lattice Boltzmann method, combining large-scale random forcing with feedback aligned with an intermediate-scale velocity field extracted by composite filtering. The magnitude of the cross-power spectrum between feedback and filtered velocity is concentrated in the target band, with a time-averaged fraction of 72.26%-74.56%. Feedback increases energy in both target and high-wavenumber bands, with larger relative gains at high wavenumbers. At feedback strengths $\alpha$ = 1%, 3%, 5%, and 7%, the target-band energy fraction increases by 6.29%, 11.65%, 18.99%, and 19.89% relative to the baseline. The mean forward nonlinear energy flux across K = 12 rises to 1.18, 1.54, 2.32, and 3.06 times its baseline value, with larger relative increases than across K = 4. As $\alpha$ increases from 0% to 7%, the mean Taylor-microscale Reynolds number rises from 73.94 to 97.86 and enstrophy increases by 181.98%, while longitudinal velocity-gradient skewness shifts toward zero and standardized velocity and normalized Q'-R' distributions largely retain their shapes. Mean $k_{\max}\eta$ values of 1.01 and 0.90 at 5% and 7% feedback indicate an approaching resolution limit and a risk of under-resolution, respectively. At approximately matched dissipation rates, 5% feedback gives a target-band energy fraction of 32.36%, versus 27.55% under enhanced large-scale forcing, and a post-transient forward flux across K = 12 generally 2.17-2.39 times larger. The strategy thus enables targeted control of energy distribution and nonlinear transfer, with feedback strength constrained by small-scale resolution.

papers.title: Treewidth and Separation Number: An Optimal Linear Bound
papers.abstract: The \emph{separation number} $\sn(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the smallest integer $a$ such that every subgraph $H$ of $G$ admits a separation $(A,B)$ of {\em order} $|A\cap B|\le a$ whose two sides $A\setminus B$ and $B\setminus A$ each contain at most $2|V(H)|/3$ vertices. Dvo\v{r}\'ak and Norin proved that $\tw(G)\le 15\sn(G)$ for every nonempty graph $G$. We improve the constant to its optimal value: every nonempty graph satisfies $\tw(G)\le 4\sn(G)-2$. This is best possible: for every $k\ge 2$, there is a graph $G_k$ with $\tw(G_k)=4k+2$ and $\sn(G_k)=k+1$.

papers.title: \(A_{\alpha}\)-Wronskian Vertices of Paths and Controllability of Path-Rooted Products
papers.abstract: For a graph \(G\) with adjacency and degree matrices \(A(G)\) and \(D(G)\), set \(A_{\alpha}(G)=\alpha D(G)+(1-\alpha)A(G)\) for \(0\leq\alpha<1\). Using Chebyshev polynomials and a theorem of Conway and Jones, we classify the \(A_{\alpha}\)-Wronskian vertices of every path \(P_n\), \(n\geq2\) (equivalently, the standard basis vectors cyclic for \(A_{\alpha}(P_n)\)). The central vertex of an odd-order path is never Wronskian; for every other vertex, we determine an explicit finite set of algebraic exceptional parameters. These sets contain no rational parameters other than \(0\) and \(1/2\), for which the adjacency and signless Laplacian cases are characterized by gcd criteria. For even-order paths rooted at either central vertex, we explicitly evaluate the root resultant and the walk-determinant polynomial in the rooted-product factorization. The resulting controllability criterion combines \(A_{\alpha}\)-controllability of the base graph with at most three explicit spectral exclusions. For each parameter, one of two fixed complementary base graphs yields controllable products for every even-order path and both central roots. For \(1/2\leq\alpha<1\), algebraic conjugates further simplify the spectral test for general rooted products.

papers.title: ReRead: Wrong Predictions, Useful Representations - Correcting Frozen Robot Policies by Re-reading Their Own Representations
papers.abstract: When a pretrained robot policy fails on challenging tasks, common remedies include retraining the backbone, adding an external visual encoder, or introducing a memory module. We argue that wrong predictions do not imply wrong representations: a policy can retain the required information yet fail to read it out as the correct action. To test this view, we propose ReRead: with the backbone frozen, a corrector re-reads the current and two previous caches to predict an action residual. The corrector sees no images, is trained solely on offline demonstrations from all 50 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks, and adds only 4.17% latency. Ablations and interventions show that the correction relies on the backbone's own representations: none of four external visual encoders adds further gain, and swapping in past caches from other trajectories sharply increases action error. On the 11 hardest RoboTwin 2.0 tasks, ReRead improves the success rates of LingBot-VLA, $\pi_{0.5}$, and Fast-WAM by 23.45, 13.09, and 8.00 percentage points, respectively. In paired evaluation on all 50 tasks, it raises Fast-WAM's average success rate from 90.73% to 92.66%. On a Flexiv dual-arm robot, it raises success on a phase-ambiguous task from 0% to 36%.

papers.title: SPIKE-Accelerated Split-Bregman/ADMM Methods for Obstacle Problems and American Option Pricing under Jump-Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: This paper presents a parallel split Bregman/alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) \cite{goldstein,tran} for obstacle problems and for the linear complementarity problems (LCPs) that arise in the pricing of American options under the Black--Scholes and Merton jump-diffusion \cite{merton} models. The auxiliary variable of ADMM decouples the inequality constraint from the differential operator, so that every iteration consists of a linear solve with a fixed banded matrix and a pointwise projection. The matrix is factorized once by the SPIKE algorithm \cite{spike}, as in the parallel direct approach of \cite{singh}, and reused in all iterations and time steps in a Fortran~90 MPI implementation. Convergence is proved by a Lyapunov functional for every positive augmentation parameter, for the symmetric obstacle problem and the non-symmetric option LCP alike, and the iterates do not depend on the number of processes. The method therefore needs a single factorization, no tuned relaxation parameter and only pointwise, perfectly parallel updates. One- and two-dimensional obstacle problems, the Black--Scholes call and American put, and European and American options under Merton's model are computed and compared with exact, closed-form, binomial and published values. In two dimension a speed-up of $3.92$ on four processes is obtained. It is also shown that the augmentation parameter has to be scaled to the diagonal of the time-stepping matrix when only a few inner iterations are used.

papers.title: TrustBound: Mechanized Completeness for Payment Epochs Initiated by AI Agents
papers.abstract: Payment operations requested by an AI agent may remain executable, or their outcomes unresolved, after the agent has stopped. We study when a trusted payment service can account for every payment in an epoch and exclude further payments under earlier authority. We give a Lean model in which operations are recorded before they receive execution authority and both actions are serialized with an admission fence. We prove that fencing fixes a journal that covers every modeled effect and outstanding right; that discharging those rights prevents further effects; and that truthful outcomes for the recorded identities then give exact accounting. A provider-contract model, mapped to the admission model, makes created payment objects inert until registered. Premise-removal mutations confirm that each key premise is needed. We connect the models to an executable service: six service histories are checked against the model in Lean, and bounded schedules, scripted clients and concurrent workers exercise its reconciliation. The concurrent experiments uncovered a conflict caused by reordered provider reads, which serializing retrieval with journal updates removes in all tested cases. The result separates two obligations that are easily conflated in practice - preventing future payments and accounting for past ones - and states precisely which service guarantees establish each.

authors.name: Soovadeep Bakshi

papers.title: Optical spin Edelstein response of d-wave altermagnets
papers.abstract: The momentum-dependent spin splitting and compensated magnetic order in altermagnets offer opportunities for electrical control of spin polarization. We explore the spin Edelstein effect in the frequency domain of a two-dimensional d-wave altermagnet with Rashba spin-orbit coupling. We calculate the spin-velocity susceptibility response function beyond the intraband response regime and find that the interband longitudinal and transverse Edelstein responses are governed by the Zeeman quantum metric and Zeeman Berry curvature, respectively. The density of states presents a logarithmic van Hove singularity at exactly the negative value of the energy below which four disconnected Fermi contours emerge. This defines three distinctive regions for the position of the Fermi level, through which the Edelstein susceptibility tensor displays characteristic spectral features, reflecting the topological change of the Fermi surface. The resulting spin magnetization shows a strong dependence on the driving frequency and on the orientation of the in-plane external electric field. Our results highlight new possibilities for electrical and optical control of the spin Edelstein effect in altermagnets that could find spintronic applications.

papers.title: RF-Based Macronutrient Estimation in Liquid Foods via Composition-Aware Multi-Task Learning
papers.abstract: Current approaches to macronutrient estimation range from high-overhead laboratory analysis to user-dependent methods such as manual nutritional lookup, reading package labels, and vision-based image analysis. These approaches are often time-consuming, input-dependent, or sensitive to imaging and measurement conditions. In this work, we investigate synchronous 2.4 GHz OFDM radio-frequency (RF) measurements for estimating carbohydrate, fat, and protein content in liquid foods. Using a controlled sensing setup, we study how liquid composition shapes frequency-domain RF responses -- a first step toward a sensor integrated into a liquid-contacting vessel that estimates macronutrient content passively and label-free, and toward composition-aware RF food analysis beyond liquids. We propose the Ingredient-Conditioned OFDM Transformer (ICOT), a structure-aware multi-task Transformer that operates on two-dimensional OFDM channel frequency response matrices. ICOT infers canonical ingredient categories representing dielectric-driver composition and uses them to condition macronutrient regression through feature concatenation. On 28,420 captures spanning 55 beverage classes, ICOT achieves an in-distribution MAE of 0.101 g/100 ml and an out-of-distribution MAE of 0.485 g/100 ml -- comparable in magnitude to deviations present in manufacturer-reported labels -- though generalization to novel formulations remains the primary open challenge.

papers.title: Leaning Over to Reach Far-Away Objects
papers.abstract: We study supported reaching to extend a humanoid robot's workspace by bracing against the environment for stabilization using a straightforward yet capable whole-body model predictive control (MPC) approach, exclusively with local sensing and fiducial markers. While typical solutions for whole body humanoid control aim at avoiding or accommodating contact, contact is explicitly required to reach objects placed on surfaces far out of normal reach. We employ sampling-based MPC for whole-body leaning, bracing, reaching, and recovery on a Unitree H1-2 humanoid. The controller runs in real-time at 34 Hz on a laptop, transfers sim-to-real, extends reach by about 50 cm beyond the unbraced standing workspace, and sustains the loaded posture for over four minutes, before pose estimation drifts. The controller reaches the commanded target in 89% of trials and completes the full reach-and-recovery cycle in 81%, across 54 trials spanning six targets and three table heights. We further characterize why such a small real-time sampling budget is sufficient, finding that temporal persistence of sampled actions and exploration scale strongly govern success, while CEM provides the widest operating region over planning rate and model mismatch. These results establish a real-world baseline for online, contact-rich humanoid manipulation. Code, videos, and full hardware details are available at https://h12leaner.github.io/

papers.title: Predicting local electric field in Al$_x$Ga$_{1-x}$N p-i-n photodiodes using exciton Franz-Keldysh photocurrent spectroscopy
papers.abstract: In AlGaN p-i-n photodiodes, reverse bias redshifts and broadens the sub-bandgap photocurrent responsivity through the eXciton Franz-Keldysh (XFK) effect, and this spectral line shape encodes the local electric field inside the device. Fitting the photocurrent spectra of two such photodiodes, with 5% and 40% Al, to an XFK absorption model at each bias yields the local voltage, $V_l$, a single parameter that sets the line shape and uniquely determines the electric-field profile inside the device. In both devices, $V_l$ varies linearly with the applied bias ($R^2 = 0.994$ and $0.998$) but changes far more slowly than the bias itself, revealing a strong local reduction of the electric field that points to non-uniform electrostatics. The slopes show that only 12.4% of the applied bias in the 5% Al device, and 45.8% in the 40% Al device, drops across the junction at the probed location. Extrapolated to zero bias, $V_l$ gives built-in voltages of 3.39 and 4.29 V, within 0.02 V of the 3.41 and 4.28 V obtained from technology computer-aided design (TCAD) simulation, which validates the extracted local voltages at equilibrium. These results extend sub-bandgap photocurrent spectroscopy to AlGaN devices as an optical probe of local electrostatics, relevant to ultraviolet photodetectors and high-voltage electronics.

papers.title: Model-Free Stealthy Attack on Vehicle Systems and Its Implications for ISO/SAE 21434 Risk Assessment
papers.abstract: This paper investigates a model-free stealthy adversary targeting in-vehicle networks and its implications for automotive cybersecurity risk assessment. Conventional stealthy false-data-injection (FDI) attacks often assume privileged knowledge of system dynamics, estimator parameters, or detector statistics, understating the feasibility of adversaries with limited system information. We develop a model-free FDI attack that uses a Vector Autoregressive model with Exogenous inputs (VARX), identified from passively recorded nominal measurements, to characterize a compromised channel and construct attack sequences within a data-calibrated residual envelope. The construction requires no vehicle dynamics model, estimator parameters, assumed noise distribution, or detector knowledge. In a closed-loop lane-keeping benchmark, the attack induces a 1.25 m lateral displacement, exceeding the specified 0.9 m half-lane width, and keeps the vehicle outside the lane corridor for 9.21 s. At a matched 1 % false-alarm operating point, attack-period alarm rates stay below 2.4 % across five learning-based intrusion detection systems (IDSs), a chi-squared residual monitor, and a liveness monitor, versus 66-100 % for conventional baselines. The proposed adversary matches the impact and evasion of a privileged model-based adversary while requiring 13 fewer attack-potential points, raising its assessed feasibility from Low to High under the considered ISO/SAE 21434 Threat Analysis and Risk Assessment (TARA). We further show that conventional impact-and-feasibility risk scoring can assign identical risk to attacks with substantially different detector responses, and introduce a detection-conditioned risk formulation to distinguish them. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for adversarial knowledge requirements and measured detectability when assessing risks in safety-critical vehicle systems.

papers.title: Pointillist Maize: 3D Reconstruction of Field-Grown Maize Using RGB UAV Imagery
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional reconstruction can extend field phenotyping to individual maize organs, but thin, flexible, occluding structures and plant movement complicate reconstruction. We evaluated whether consumer-grade UAV RGB video processed with Structure from Motion and multi-view stereo could recover recognizable field-grown maize structures, and examined the effects of acquisition trajectories and frame sampling. COLMAP reconstructions preserved recognizable leaves, stems, tassel branches, ears, silks, and brace roots. For an equal-frame comparison, we reconstructed one plant from two sets of 295 frames from the same video: a single orbit sampled at 5 frames/second and three orbits at different altitudes (ribbon skirt) sampled at 2 frames/second. After ground removal, the reconstructions contained 520,601 and 375,318 points, respectively. The single orbit yielded greater point concentration within plant structures and fewer visible gaps, while the ribbon skirt yielded fewer scattered points and slightly lower proportions of isolated points. In densely planted nursery rows, visible voids occupied 17.57% of the rendered scene with one orbit at 1 frame/second, decreasing to 5.07% with additional serpentine passes and 2.68% when the original orbit was sampled at 3 frames/second. Additional observations also increased point dispersion associated with plant movement. A curlicue trajectory tested in a different field in 2024 produced distinguishable individual plants without visible duplicated structures, although substantial voids remained, mainly on the soil surface. These results demonstrate the feasibility of recovering recognizable maize organs from consumer UAV imagery and reveal trade-offs between acquisition strategies, reconstruction completeness, and point dispersion. Independent geometric validation is still needed before quantitative phenotyping.

papers.title: Elliptic Gromov-Witten Invariants of Instanton Moduli
papers.abstract:
We calculate the genus $1$ Gromov-Witten invariants with one tautological divisor insertion of the moduli space $\mathcal{M}(r,n)$ of rank-$r$, $c_2=n$ torsion-free sheaves on $\mathbb{P}^2$ framed along the infinity divisor. As rational functions of the framing parameters, we determine the polar parts of these invariants by exploring the equivariant geometry of the Gieseker-Uhlenbeck map $\mathcal{M}(r,n)\to\mathcal{M}_0(r,n)$. We determine the polynomial part of these invariants by relating their large framing limits to the results \cite{ILPT} for the rank $1$ case, namely $\mathrm{Hilb}^n(\mathbb{C}^2)$. The degree-$0$ invariants with one divisor insertion are evaluated by studying the combinatorics of multi-partitions.
  We also prove reconstruction results for invariants with multiple insertions. Under the assumption that the eigenvalues of the divisor operator are linearly independent as functions of the Novikov variable, these results determine the full genus $1$ theory from the one-divisor series and the genus $0$ divisor operator.

papers.title: Representational Change Under Self-Consuming Training: A Sparse Autoencoder Analysis
papers.abstract: Large language models are increasingly exposed to model-generated text, raising the possibility that future models will be trained recursively on the outputs of their predecessors. Prior work on such self-consuming training loops has largely focused on output quality and downstream performance, leaving their effects on internal representations poorly understood. We study how representations evolve across five generations of self-consumption and whether sparse autoencoders (SAEs) remain reliable under this shift. At each generation, we compare a lineage trained on synthetic data with a matched control trained on real data under the same training settings. We evaluate how well SAEs trained before self-consumption transfer to later generations, measuring reconstruction and sparsity across SAE widths, architectures, and model layers. We then fine-tune the original SAE on each generation and use sparse probing to test whether task-relevant information remains concentrated in a small number of latents or becomes more distributed across the representation. We find that zero-shot SAE performance degrades progressively under self-consumption, with growing reconstruction and sparsity gaps that vary substantially across layers. Fine-tuning largely restores reconstruction, but not feature-level usefulness: task-relevant information remains accessible in the full latent space while becoming less concentrated in individual features. These results show that self-consumption induces representational drift and that reconstruction fidelity alone is insufficient to establish that an adapted SAE remains equally useful for interpretation.

papers.title: Routing Information and Stationary Limits in Many-Server Load Balancing
papers.abstract: We study how routing information determines stationary congestion in many-server systems with Poisson arrivals and homogeneous exponential servers. We consider policies that prioritize idle servers and select a queue stochastically no longer than a uniformly sampled queue. In nondegenerate slowdown, where spare capacity is fixed, we identify population laws from the fraction of queues with waiting jobs at each population level. We establish these laws for one-job priority, join-idle-queue, and idle-first sampling. One-job priority attains the join-the-shortest-queue population law and mean delays; further queue information can improve limiting delays in convex order without changing their means. In the super-Halfin-Whitt and Halfin-Whitt regimes, every such policy has the same stationary limits. Our estimates bound idleness-weighted occupancy tails in terms of ordinary tails, uniformly over queue-length thresholds and policies. They also yield process convergence and limit interchange for initial laws uniformly dominated by stationarity, with convergent scaled initial states.

papers.title: Functional Principal Component Analysis for Ordinal Functional Data with Application in Diabetes Intervention
papers.abstract: Traditional functional principal component analysis (FPCA) is typically designed for continuous functional observations. In this paper, we address the scenario where the outcome consists of repeated categorical data defined over a bounded interval. Our objective is to develop an FPCA methodology tailored specifically for ordinal functional data. Our approach leverages recent advancements in ordinal data modeling to estimate both the mean function and the eigenfunctions, while employing a computationally efficient method for predicting the scores. The performance of the proposed methodology is evaluated numerically in simulation and data application on diabetes intervention.

papers.title: Beyond Leaderboard Ranks: Selecting Software Engineering Agents Under Budget Constraints
papers.abstract:
Teams that adopt LLM agents for issue resolution must decide which agent to pay for, and how much to spend finding out. Leaderboard ranks give weak evidence for this decision. Accuracy differences may be statistically unresolved, reported costs may be inconsistent, and evaluating candidate agents can itself be expensive. We investigate budget-constrained agent selection using 58,197 run--task records extracted from the Holistic Agent Leaderboard (HAL), focusing on SWE-bench and six additional benchmarks.
  Across seven benchmarks, 27 of 35 steps along the accuracy--cost Pareto frontiers are statistically unresolved. On SWE-bench, a run costing $34.16 trails the $170.78 leader by 14.6 percentage points, but the available tasks cannot statistically distinguish their accuracy. Reported costs also differ from standardized token-based estimates by up to 11.7x, while selective task evaluation can bias estimates of full-benchmark execution cost.
  We therefore compare evaluation strategies under explicit evaluation budgets and deployment-cost caps. Under advance knowledge of task costs, successive halving reaches our uncertainty-aware selection target on SWE-bench using 6.6% of exhaustive evaluation spend, achieving the lowest cost on six of seven benchmarks and tying on the seventh. Its advantage narrows when task costs are unknown before execution or exact-best selection is required.
  Our findings motivate decision-oriented agent evaluation that accounts for accuracy uncertainty, validates execution costs, and compares complex selection methods against simple adaptive allocation.

papers.title: The Critic Can Hurt: On the Safety of Critics in LLM-Guided AutoML Search
papers.abstract: LLM critics increasingly steer iterative search in agentic AutoML, prompt optimization, and self-refinement--evaluated for whether they help, but rarely for whether they can hurt. We isolate the critic's marginal effect through a four-arm audit and characterize the loop's tolerance through controlled fault injection. We show a naive 8B critic drives search below the no-critic random-search floor on 7 of 8 tabular datasets, losing up to 0.245 AUC in the worst case; the magnitude varies strongly with dataset, frontier, and budget. When: stronger critics attenuate the loss on the evaluated suite, without establishing a universal capability threshold. Why: controlled fault injection shows that non-directional errors are nearly costless under best-so-far search, whereas directional errors consume finite search opportunities; an idealized effective-sample calculation yields a necessary condition, $q(m-1) > \beta$, not a deployment certificate. How: a simple observable validation gate and a learned detector can reduce realized loss, but neither is guaranteed to preserve the full-budget no-critic baseline. We will release CRITFAULT, to our knowledge the first benchmark for detecting harmful critic feedback in AutoML. A critic is not a free addition: audit before trusting, and gate when capability or verification is insufficient.

papers.title: DT-MATCH: Defect- and Topology-Aware Chiplet Matching for Yield Optimization in Heterogeneous Integration
papers.abstract: Heterogeneous integration (HI) and advanced packaging enable chiplet-based system-on-chip (SoC) designs; however, they also introduce new yield challenges arising from manufacturing defects and complex die-to-die (D2D) interconnect constraints. In particular, lane-level defects, limited spares, and strict structural compatibility requirements impede the efficient assembly of functional systems from defective but repairable chiplets. We present DT-MATCH, a defect- and topology-aware chiplet matching framework that maximizes the number of functional SoCs under realistic assembly constraints. DT-MATCH provides two complementary approaches. The integer linear programming (ILP)-based approach is implemented using a batching strategy to approximate the exact formulation. The greedy randomized adaptive search procedure (GRASP)-based approach provides substantial acceleration, but it does not guarantee yield optimality. Both approaches use a preprocessing pipeline to reduce the problem size. Experimental results on industrial designs demonstrate that, as expected, the ILP-based approach achieves superior solution quality. The GRASP-based approach leads to lower runtimes while still achieving solution quality that is comparable to the ILP-based solution. Together, these methods provide a trade-off between solution quality and efficiency for practical chiplet assembly optimization.

papers.title: Cooperative Transport of Unknown Objects by Distributed Effort Regulation in Multi-agent Systems
papers.abstract: A distributed multi-robot object transportation strategy is proposed for objects of unknown shape, size, geometry, mass and mass distribution without any prior knowledge about the object or number of robots involved in the transportation process. Robots follow the boundary of the object and dynamically determine viable pushing points. A novel object-model-free heading-error-driven pushing effort regulation method is proposed to promote goal-directed object motion; robots regulate their pushing effort using individual and collective heading errors. Robots dynamically relocate around the object boundary if a pushing point is lost or the required pushing effort exceeds its capability to correct its heading. The proposed method is validated using simple and complex shapes with convex and non-convex boundary regions and dynamically changing weight distribution of objects. Detailed analysis on the effects of robot distribution and initial object pose on the transportation performance in terms of required time and path efficiency is also presented. Scalability analysis revealed that object transportation time is dependent on the number of pushing surfaces available which in turn depends on the object size, shape, and set inter-robot safety distance. The proposed system yielded highly efficient object paths with consistent elapsed transport times over several trials robust to external disturbances such as non-uniform friction between contacting surfaces and robot wheel slip.

papers.title: Asymptotic Order of the Minimum Number of Graph-Saturating Edges
papers.abstract: Given an $H$-free graph $G$, a non-edge $e$ of $G$ is called $H$-saturating if $G+e$ contains a copy of $H$. The function $f_H(n,m)$ denotes the minimum number of $H$-saturating non-edges over all $n$-vertex $H$-free graphs with exactly $m$ edges. In this paper, we give a complete classification of the asymptotic behavior of $f_H(n,\operatorname{ex}(n,R)+1)$ for any fixed graph $H$ satisfying $\chi(H)>\chi$ and $\chi(H-e)>\chi$ for every $e\in E(H)$, where $\chi\ge 2$ and $R$ is an arbitrary fixed edge-critical graph with $\chi(R)=\chi+1$. We show that this quantity is of quadratic order, asymptotic to $\frac{2n}{\chi}$, or zero, according to the existence and structure of $\chi$-critical two-edge sets of $H$. In particular, we resolve the conjecture proposed by He et al. ({\it J. Combin. Theory Ser. B} 159 (2023), 42-60).

authors.name: Changxiang He
authors.institution: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Simulating access to alcohol screening, brief intervention, referral to and receipt of specialty treatment for alcohol use disorder in California and Texas: A study protocol for an agent-based modeling study (AUDTxSim)
papers.abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) affects millions of US adults. Primary care-based screening, brief intervention, and referral to treatment (SBIRT) is a leading strategy for identifying heavy drinking early, but access to primary care, screening, and specialty treatment differs markedly across subgroups. Whether scaling SBIRT and expanding treatment capacity narrows or widens these differences is unknown and cannot feasibly be tested in a randomized trial. We present AUDTxSim (AUD Treatment Simulation), a stochastic, spatially explicit, individual-based model of alcohol use, AUD, SBIRT, and specialty treatment for the adult populations of California and Texas. Agents represent every adult in synthetic populations of the two states (28.0 and 19.3 million adults), each geo-located to a Census tract and linked to nearby treatment facilities. In daily time steps, the model simulates: (1) annual transitions among eight alcohol use and AUD states; (2) healthcare visits, screening, brief intervention, and referral; (3) treatment seeking, standalone medication for AUD, mutual help, and requests for hospitalization, residential, or outpatient care; (4) a treatment manager that allocates individuals to facilities by preference, geography, and capacity, with telehealth substitution and waitlists; and (5) treatment progression, stepdown between levels of care, and post-treatment mutual help. It is implemented in Python with Repast4Py to run in parallel on a computing cluster. Once calibrated to state, rural-urban, and demographic targets for healthcare visits, heavy drinking and AUD prevalence, and mortality, AUDTxSim will project population-level and subgroup-specific effects of alternative SBIRT reach and treatment capacity scenarios on AUD prevalence, treatment receipt, and mortality. We report the model structure, decision logic, data sources, and calibration plan.

papers.title: multiCAsp: Spatially Informed Canonical Association Analysis of Multi-Omic Data
papers.abstract: Simultaneous profiling of multiple molecular layers at spatially resolved locations creates opportunities to identify shared cross-modal biological variation in its tissue context. We present multiCAsp (multi-omic Canonical Association informed by spatial graph), a probabilistic latent-factor model for integrating $M \geq 2$ spatially resolved omic modalities. It incorporates spatial dependence through a graph-Laplacian prior on shared latent factors and uses an expectation-maximization algorithm to estimate factor scores and modality-specific feature loadings. Because the prior is defined on a neighborhood graph rather than on Euclidean distances, it accommodates irregular tissue geometries and extends naturally to multiple tissue sections. Simulations show that multiCAsp consistently achieves higher mean latent subspace and loading recovery than alternative methods across varying sample sizes, feature dimensions, and noise levels, with the largest gains under high noise. Compared with an existing Gaussian process-based spatial factor model, it is also less sensitive to how the spatial coordinates are represented, produces spatially smoother factors, and has lower computational cost. Applied to metabolomic-proteomic data from macaque cortex and gene-protein data from human renal carcinoma, multiCAsp recovers spatially coherent multi-omic factors with interpretable biological signatures. In the macaque data, transferred factors retain broad spatial patterns across animals and support cross-modal prediction of protein abundances from metabolomic measurements.

papers.title: Comments on "Deep Fr\'echet Regression"
papers.abstract: We discuss the Journal of the American Statistical Association (JASA) discussion paper "Deep Fr\'echet Regression" and explore an alternative perspective based on conditional flow matching. We propose learning covariate-dependent transport directly within the response space, avoiding separate manifold learning and reverse mapping. This perspective offers a potentially more flexible framework for incorporating geometric structure and modeling full conditional distributions.

papers.title: ExRel: Learning Directed Reuse Relevance between Rich-Text K-12 Question Images with Executable Relation Contracts
papers.abstract: In K-12 education, question images combine text, mathematical expressions, diagrams, and diverse layouts. Variations in wording, conditions, answer options, or task scope can substantially alter their reuse utility despite visual similarity. We formulate this problem as directed reuse relevance, grading candidate utility as Strong, Medium, or Weak. However, generic similarity scores overlook task-specific reuse requirements, while natural supervision is dominated by Strong relations and lacks fine-grained coverage. We propose ExRel, an agentic, code-grounded framework for controllable and verifiable visual data synthesis. It reconstructs real questions into editable HTML/CSS seeds and compiles 15 relation subtypes into executable contracts specifying permitted edits, protected invariants, and query-candidate direction. Synthesized pairs undergo deterministic DOM/render validation and target-hidden, evidence-assisted review, with bounded repair before mild photographic degradation. Only rendered images are used for downstream training. Experiments show that ExRel supervision outperforms size-matched natural data and count- and class-matched replay, particularly on Medium relations, while maintaining comparable query-level ranking performance and improving robustness to visual degradation. Construction ablations demonstrate higher valid yield and fewer false admissions than less structured baselines. Human audits confirm 98.0% post-admission validity, while ExRel achieves a lower per-accepted-pair cost than outsourced annotation (0.70 vs. 1.10 RMB). Downstream answer routing further demonstrates the practical utility of the synthesized supervision.

papers.title: Beyond Marginal Risk: ESG and Multidimensional Fragility in Equity Markets
papers.abstract: Do ESG characteristics provide financial resilience beyond conventional risk, and is that inference stable to the financial state and ESG score being measured? We study a point-in-time panel of nonfinancial S&P 500 constituents from January 2019 through November 2025. Once ex ante return, volatility, and liquidity exposures are modeled explicitly, the broad downside-resilience pattern attenuates and none of the three primary marginal ESG $\times$ Down tests survives Holm adjustment under either conventional or wild-cluster-bootstrap inference. A post-primary exact decomposition then shows that the negative Return+RVOL coefficient is almost entirely allocated to observations that also breach the CHL trading-cost tail, while the mutually exclusive Return+RVOL-only component is essentially zero. Finally, a paired standardized comparison on an identical sample shows that MSCI's downstream Industry Adjusted Score and upstream Weighted Average Key Issue Score imply materially different fitted associations in adverse market states: at a 5% market decline, the difference is about one probability percentage point per score standard deviation. Sector-time, leave- one-month-out, and observed-change timing diagnostics preserve most of this contrast, although the result remains exploratory and inference is sensitive to multiplicity and market-state support. The evidence therefore favors a narrower interpretation of ESG resilience: the apparent association weakens once conventional risk is modeled, while the remaining relation depends on both the adverse state and the MSCI score field used to represent ESG.

papers.title: Brunn-Minkowski inequalities for Riesz capacity in all dimensions
papers.abstract: We prove the Brunn--Minkowski inequality for Riesz $p$-capacity on compact subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n$ when $n-1<p<n$, extending the known endpoint $p=n-1$. For sets of positive capacity, equality holds if and only if they are convex and positively homothetic. The inequality remains conjectural for $n-2<p<n-1$, when $n\ge2$. Known isodiametric counterexamples rule out a general extension to negative $p$, even for convex planar sets.
