papers.title: Invariant-Aware Harness Enforcement to Protect LLM Agents from Silent API Failures
papers.abstract: LLM agents answer questions by calling APIs and trusting the results. An API can fail silently. It ignores part of a request, such as a misnamed filter, yet returns HTTP 200 and a plausible but wrong result. Current fixes, such as checklists, reviewer models and LLM judges, ask the model to catch it. But models often see the problem and answer anyway. We present SilentGuard, which moves the decision from the model to the harness running tool calls. It tests each result against invariants that any correct API must satisfy and withholds values that break one. We find silent failures in 11 of 15 public research APIs, with counts inflated up to 691 times. Current fixes leave over 70% of answers wrong, and agents report 77.4% of counts a judge flags. Across 7 open models, SilentGuard cuts wrong answers on its target faults from 74.0% to 1.7%, with no loss on fault-free tasks. On three frontier models they fall from 70.2% to 0.5%. A warning from the same check leaves 70.1% wrong, so enforcement is the key. On new fault types, the harness alone cuts wrong answers from 61.1% to 24.5%. It avoids wrong answers by abstaining rather than recovering.

papers.title: UNIDE: Cross-PDE Learning for Noise-Robust Discovery of Governing Equations
papers.abstract: Governing partial differential equations (PDEs) provide compact and interpretable descriptions of physical systems. Classical methods, such as sparse and symbolic regression, fit a new equation to each observed field: what is learned on one system is not carried to the next, and observation noise corrupts the derivative features they rely on. This paper introduces UNIDE (Unified Identification of Differential Equations), a data-driven approach that learns across PDE families to identify governing equations from new noisy trajectories. It integrates three components: a self-supervised denoiser trained without clean targets, an encoder shared across PDE families that predicts which candidate terms are active, and weak-form least squares with residual-based pruning that estimates their coefficients. We demonstrate UNIDE on synthetic one-dimensional trajectories from six PDE families with known term structures, including the Burgers and Kuramoto--Sivashinsky equations. We train one model per noise level and systematically compare UNIDE with SINDy, WSINDy, and PySR. The results show that UNIDE recovers the exact set of governing terms more often than all three at every noise level from $1\%$ to $80\%$. At $80\%$ noise, where the noise standard deviation is $0.8$ times that of the field, it recovers the exact terms for $92\%$ of held-out trajectories, whereas the best baseline recovers about $1\%$. UNIDE is also efficient: because its neural components are reused rather than refit, it identifies each new trajectory in $0.45$ seconds, $2.7$ times faster than WSINDy and $51$ times faster than PySR. These results demonstrate the potential of learning across PDE families for efficient equation identification under substantial observation noise.

papers.title: TRACE: Topological Representations for Anomaly detection through Contrastive Embeddings
papers.abstract: Intrusion detectors must recognize evolving malicious behavior even when confirmed attack labels are scarce or incomplete. We present TRACE, a topology-aware graph contrastive learning framework for label-efficient intrusion detection. TRACE learns from benign system-activity graphs by combining message-passing and topological representations, then assigns anomaly scores in the same projected embedding space optimized by the contrastive objective. This design captures both local interactions and graph-scale structural deviations without using attack labels during representation learning. A labeled validation set containing benign and malicious graphs is used only to calibrate the anomaly threshold. We evaluate TRACE on StreamSpot, GraSec-IoT, and Unicorn Wget against a supervised graph neural network and the benign-only GraphCL baseline. TRACE obtains F1 scores of 0.923, 0.790, and 0.583, respectively. Compared with GraphCL, this is higher on StreamSpot (0.450) and Unicorn Wget (0.203), but lower on GraSec-IoT (0.975). The supervised model leads on StreamSpot and GraSec-IoT, whereas TRACE has the highest F1 on Unicorn Wget. The mixed results show that topology-aware benign-only learning can improve detection in some graph settings but does not provide a uniform advantage.

papers.title: GraphPass: A Study of Graph Neural Networks for Compiler Pass Selection
papers.abstract: Compiler pass selection is usually governed by fixed pipelines (-O2, -O3) or hand-written heuristics. We study whether a graph neural network (GNN) over a program's control-flow graph (CFG) can select among a fixed menu of five pass sequences in a single forward pass. GraphPass encodes each CFG with a graph attention (GAT) or graph convolutional (GCN) encoder and classifies it into one of the five sequences. On a synthetic benchmark of 5,000 generated CFGs in five program families, both encoders agree with the benchmark's reference label on about 92% of held-out programs, versus 68.4% for a hand-written rule-based heuristic and 85% for a flat MLP. An edge ablation indicates that this gain comes from per-block processing rather than from CFG edges: a GCN given the same basic-block features with all edges removed scores 95.0%, versus 92.2% with the true CFG. In this benchmark the label is determined by the program family, so the task amounts to family recognition. Real-compiler speedup is not measured. Inference costs O(|V| + |E|) per CFG, measured at 1.7 ms for a typical program and about 0.8 s for a 100,000-block graph on one CPU core.

papers.title: ToolGraph as a Q-Function for Test-Time Scaling of Tool-Use Agents
papers.abstract: Tool-use agents must chain interdependent calls, yet which outputs satisfy which later inputs in a deployed catalog is not something a general-purpose language model reliably infers from tool descriptions alone. We compile that structure once into a reusable external representation. ToolGraph is a directed, weighted dependency graph over a tool catalog: parameter matching and interventional probes, which execute a candidate chain with and without its proposed predecessor, propose edges whose evidence is combined into an edge confidence. Prior work uses such graphs to retrieve tools, search for tool paths, or score the next call. We ask instead whether the same structure can supply a \emph{multi-step} value by composing graph paths into a goal-conditioned action value \(Q(s,a,g)\). We study three estimators (dynamic programming over entity sets, a GraphSAGE estimator distilled from it, and an LLM scorer conditioned on graph evidence) plus a verbalizer that returns action--goal feedback to the agent, which keeps final action selection. Across two tool-use benchmarks and three backbones, we compare value ranking against personalized-PageRank retrieval over the identical graph, and against direct and reflective agents. Composition pays off only when the estimator also reads the concrete state: the LLM estimator improves on PageRank in every benchmark--backbone setting, by \(8.3\) points on average, while the two purely structural estimators fall below it, because a value defined over tool types cannot separate a correct tool called with a wrong argument. Graph construction is a one-time cost; we report it separately rather than assume it amortized away (at our scale it is comparable to request-time cost) and sweep four knobs controlling how much graph evidence to expose against success and tokens.

papers.title: Simulated Annealing with Topological Spatial Chunking for De Novo Protein Sequence Design
papers.abstract: The inverse protein folding problem, designing a discrete amino acid sequence that spontaneously folds into a predefined macroscopic structure, remains a phenomenally demanding combinatorial challenge central to synthetic drug discovery. While algorithms like SA offer a baseline approach for navigating dense biomolecular energy landscapes, applying SA heuristics to large sequences is inherently frustrated by exponentially large search spaces and deep local energy minima. This study proposes a scalable sequence design architecture, Topological Spatial Chunking Simulated Annealing, based on a localized, exact-solving heuristic embedded within a global simulated-annealing wrapper. To fundamentally circumvent exponential scaling walls, we deploy a dynamic solver that segments the global molecular target into shallow, k-variable algorithmic windows. Crucially, rather than partitioning natively by sequential 1D chronology, we introduce topological spatial chunking, which dynamically groups discrete variables based on Euclidean spatial proximity to preserve critical non-local thermodynamic correlations. The spatially localized sub-problems are solved deterministically via exact enumeration, while the global traversal is securely regulated by an exterior simulated annealing governor augmented by dynamic reheating and continuous elitism caching. We comprehensively benchmarked this classical architecture on the standard HP biophysical lattice against targeted 20-merA, 25-mer, 50-mer, and 64-mer geometries. Most notably, when evaluating the computationally exhaustive 50-mer and 64-mer topologies, the framework successfully bypassed widely accepted heuristic boundaries. By leveraging deterministic exact solving to vault classical energy traps, the system algorithmically resolved a novel, ultra-dense sequence-packing configuration for the 50-mer, defining a new theoretical global optimum.

papers.title: SAR-TopoGuard: Training-Free, Speckle-Aware Topological Verification for Structure-Preserving SAR-to-Optical Translation
papers.abstract: SAR-to-optical translators often synthesize detail that the radar measurement does not support, and pixel metrics alone cannot reveal it. We propose SAR-TopoGuard, a training-free inference-time layer for frozen generators: a stochastic sampler draws K candidates (Monte Carlo dropout for GANs, seed variance for diffusion), a speckle-aware verifier ranks them by gradient-magnitude correlation with the SAR input and a hallucination-frequency index, and a SAR-guided frequency gate admits high-frequency detail only where SAR edges support it. With all five hyperparameters frozen and three training seeds, we evaluate on 500 scene-disjoint SEN1-2 test patches, 500 patches of a held-out summer scene, and 200 cross-dataset SEN12MS winter pairs. The layer improves Pix2Pix by +0.060, +0.012, and +0.077 dB PSNR and by +0.0034, +0.0057, and +0.0135 SSIM, respectively (Wilcoxon p < 1e-6), and it improves CycleGAN and CUT on all three sets (+0.013 to +0.076 dB). It raises edge precision at the cost of edge recall (edge F1 -1.3% on the test set). On the latent diffusion model COP-GEN, it adds +0.33 dB (base) and +0.16 dB (Beta) on the winter set, the only set with dual-polarization SAR. An ablation shows that the gate produces the gain for MC-dropout GANs, whose candidates are nearly identical, whereas verifier selection contributes up to +0.26 dB for diffusion, whose samples differ. The layer has zero trainable parameters and adds 0.4 ms per patch beyond the K=5 generator passes.

authors.name: Subhranil Biswas
authors.institution: North Eastern Indira Gandhi Regional Institute of Health and Medical Sciences

papers.title: Sparse Stabilization of Continuous-Time Linear Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: Efficient use of communication resources is crucial for stabilizing a networked control system. Employing \emph{sparse inputs} and event-triggered control are efficient ways to utilize communication resources in networked control systems. This work considers the problem of stabilizing a continuous-time linear dynamical system (LDS) using $s$-sparse inputs. For this purpose, we consider \emph{switched} linear feedback control, where we construct a finite number of feedback matrices with at most $s$ nonzero rows. Using switched systems theory, we show that there exists an $s$-sparse input for any sparsity level $s \geq 1$ that ensures stability when the continuous-time LDS is stabilizable. In addition, using our approach, we can compute the required feedback matrices with minimal overhead even if the sparsity budget $s$ varies over time. We also minimize the maximum Frobenius norm of the feedback matrices, yielding sparse inputs with reduced control energy. We show that an upper bound on the control energy required for stabilization using an $s$-sparse input is inversely proportional to $s^2$, while maintaining the same exponential stability rate. Finally, we combine the design of the \emph{sparse inputs} with the event-trigger rule to further reduce communication resource consumption. Our sparse and event-triggered control strategy ensures that any stabilizable continuous-time LDS can be stabilized using $s$-sparse inputs under both state feedback and output feedback, for any $s\geq 1$. We illustrate our theoretical results for the task of stabilizing a mass-spring system.

papers.title: ECPack.wl: A Mathematica Package for Elliptic Curves over the Rationals and Finite Fields
papers.abstract: We present a Mathematica package entitled ECPack.wl, where we implement many important properties and commands relevant to the study of elliptic curves over the rationals and finite fields, namely $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\mathbb{F}_q$, where $q=p^r$ and $p$ is prime. By streamlining the analysis of general elliptic curves and their transformations, ECPack.wl offers foundational computational tools for applications in high-energy physics, including elliptic Feynman integrals. This package significantly extends the functionalities of a package due to McGee in so far as we are able to study all versions of elliptic curves, such as the long Weierstrass, quartic and Legendre forms. We implement suitable transformations that are required for the general case, as well as those associated with fields of characteristic 2 and 3. Furthermore, the package computes many curve properties, such as point arithmetic, minimality checks, rank bounds and analytic rank, group structure, invariants, and the Weil and Tate pairings, over both $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\mathbb{F}_p$, as well as the Kodaira classification of the singular fibres of one-parameter families of elliptic curves, with the associated F-theory data. The package and its accompanying notebooks are available at https://github.com/DhamakedarDarsh/Mathematica-Code-and-worked-out-notebooks-for-Elliptic-Curves

papers.title: Collapsibility of Vietoris--Rips complexes of hypercube graphs in codimension two
papers.abstract: Shukla conjectured that the collapsibility number of the Vietoris-Rips complex $\mathrm{VR}(I_n;r)$ of the $n$-dimensional hypercube graph at scale $r$ equals $2^r$ for all $n\ge r+1$. We prove the conjecture for $n=r+2$ and every $r$, which gives the first known cases with $r\ge 4$ beyond the cross-polytope case $n=r+1$. Writing $\mathrm{VR}(I_n;r)$ as the independence complex of the graph $H_{n,r}$ that joins two points when their Hamming distance exceeds $r$, we construct a cover of $H_{r+2,r}$ by $2^r$ co-chordal subgraphs. The key general tool is the inequality that, for every graph $G$, the $\theta$-number of B{\i}y{\i}ko\u{g}lu and Civan of the independence complex of $G$, and hence the collapsibility number of that complex, is at most the co-chordal cover number of $G$; this strengthens Woodroofe's regularity bound. We also show, using a theorem of Alon, Jin, and Sudakov, that the induced matching number of $H_{n,r}$ equals $2^r$ for every $n>r$, and that $\mathrm{VR}(I_n;r)$ is vertex decomposable if and only if $r=1$ or $n=r+1$. As consequences, we determine the top degree of nonvanishing homology and the coconnectivity of $\mathrm{VR}(I_{r+2};r)$, and we prove split injectivity in top-degree integral homology. Finally, assuming a recent skew Hamming set-pair theorem of Gao and Zhao, we prove that the collapsibility number of $\mathrm{VR}(I_n;r)$ is at most $2^{r+1}-4$ for all $n>r\ge 2$.

papers.title: Linear Electrostatic Instabilities Driven by Relativistic Non-Maxwellian Pair Beams
papers.abstract: We investigate how non-Maxwellian momentum distributions affect the linear growth of electrostatic instabilities driven by relativistic pair beams, motivated by the lack of a universally accepted analytical description of blazar-induced pair beams. Different beam distributions are used to describe relativistic pair beams in analytical studies and particle-in-cell simulations. A systematic comparison is therefore needed to determine how the beam distribution influences the instability growth rates. We formulate the relativistic electrostatic response in the weak-beam limit for an anisotropic $\kappa$-type distribution and compare the resulting growth rates with those obtained for Gaussian and Maxwell--J\"uttner distributions. We require $\kappa>3/2$ for a finite root-mean-square momentum spread. For the parameters considered, the $\kappa$-type distributions yield higher maximum growth rates than the Gaussian distribution, even when their mean momenta and momentum spreads are the same. The fastest-growing modes correspond to parallel propagation for the $\kappa$ and Gaussian distributions, whereas the Maxwell--J\"uttner distribution exhibits its maximum for oblique propagation for a mildly relativistic beam. An additional calculation for a highly relativistic pair beam with $\kappa=2$ finds an oblique maximum of the electrostatic growth rate. The beam momentum distribution influences the linear growth of electrostatic instabilities under the conditions investigated.

papers.title: Vegetation Health Classification for Low-Data and Edge Hardware Deployment
papers.abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) equipped with cameras are popular, viable tools for vegetation and environmental health monitoring. However, existing image classification methods are incompatible with UAV implementation for independent practitioners in remote, resource-constrained environments due to large dataset requirements, GPU hardware, inflexible retraining, and low interpretability. This paper presents a lightweight, interpretable vegetation classification algorithm operating with as few as five reference images per class, without GPUs or heavy machine learning frameworks. It uses a 2D hue-saturation histogram feature representation and Earth Mover's Distance or Quadratic Form Distance, paired with a log-likelihood probability score, to classify images into three vegetation health categories. We evaluated six systems: three custom pipelines and three established models across low-data scenarios ($n = 5, 10, 25$) and a full-data regime of 2,172 drone images from 28 South American locations. Our custom pipelines achieve competitive Top-1 accuracy (81--85\%) under low-data constraints, maintaining sub-1ms inference times that enable real-time classification and subsequently tasks such as seeding and watering. The algorithms also support incremental retraining without full model reconstruction. We validate edge feasibility by deploying the QFD variant on an ESP32 microcontroller, achieving 82.8\% accuracy with 1.01\% heap memory utilization (45kb), demonstrating that effective vegetation classification is achievable on low-cost, low-power embedded hardware without cellular connectivity.

authors.name: Haoyu Li
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: TIVS: Mapping the Sensitivity Landscape of Visual Token Transformations in MLLMs
papers.abstract: Recent efforts to improve the efficiency of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have explored visual token pruning, quantization, and feature compression. However, the properties that determine whether transformed visual tokens remain usable by a frozen decoder are not well characterized. We introduce \textbf{TIVS (Token Identity Versus Statistics)}, a training-free intervention framework that separately studies sequence permutation, token retention, numerical precision, and statistical replacement under controlled conditions. On 192 POPE questions, three token permutations change TinyLLaVA accuracy by only $-0.17$ percentage points on average, while changing 4.69\% of individual predictions. Diagonal and rank-64 Gaussian replacements decrease accuracy by 25.0 and 28.1 points on the same subset. Further experiments with exact moment constraints, quantization error, token retention, and additional visual tasks reveal how strongly the effects depend on the original feature values and the evaluation setting. These findings provide an empirical basis for assessing visual token transformations in frozen MLLMs and designing more reliable multimodal interfaces.

authors.name: Ziying Song
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: Honest confidence sets under experiment-level failure
papers.abstract: An experiment-level failure replaces the joint observation law while preserving the target. We study honest confidence sets when a declared upper bound on failure probability equals the allowed noncoverage probability. For a Uniform support endpoint and a Gaussian mean on fixed compact parameter intervals, every honest deterministic procedure has full-range worst-case expected diameter under arbitrary or absolutely continuous joint failures. Independent randomisation gives sharp minimax risks of $(2+o(1))\log N/N$ for the endpoint in $[1,2]$ and $(2\sigma+o(1))(\log N/N)^{1/2}$ for the mean with known variance $\sigma^2$. A failure distribution shared by many targets forces average clean-state noncoverage to decrease with expected diameter. One-sided local Kullback--Leibler bounds then yield lower bounds with logarithmic factors. The endpoint experiment also has a sharp deterministic frontier as the remaining error budget vanishes. Under exchangeable failures without ties, observation order recovers both randomised benchmark rates deterministically. In a reference-calibrated roster, we derive the randomised minimax reliability rate. A prespecified reference reserve of logarithmic size permits deterministic attainment of the same order on a subclass whose conditionally independent reserved responses have probabilities bounded away from zero and one in every state.

authors.name: Fengshi Jing
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: Logarithmic thermodynamic cost of prediction from rare observations
papers.abstract: A memory predicting changes in its environment from rare observations must spend energy on sampling and recording. We consider autonomous chemical memories driven by a sample-and-hold sensor observing an environment that switches at rate gamma, with sampling frequency f<<gamma. An ideal observer with access to the full observation history can retain predictive information proportional to f. However, retaining a finite fraction of this information in an autonomous physical memory requires work of order kBT ln(gamma/f) per sensor change. This additional thermodynamic cost arises from the competing requirements of suppressing false records during long intervals between observations and responding rapidly to new observations. We establish a universal low-power bound on predictive information, which grows at most as P/ln(P_ref/P) with power budget P, uniformly over any finite number of memory states and independently of network topology and memory relaxation times. We further demonstrate that memory architecture determines the attainable scaling. With bounded transition rates and readout from the memory alone, two-state memories are limited to P^2 scaling, whereas a three-state memory is sufficient to attain the optimal logarithmic scaling. Our results establish a fundamental thermodynamic distinction between acquiring information and maintaining a useful record of a changing environment.

papers.title: Independent interferometric observable confirms black hole shadow in M87*
papers.abstract: A new epoch for direct visualisation of accretion dynamics near a black hole's event horizon began when the Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration (EHTC) synthesised an Earth-sized aperture with millimeter radio interferometry and published the first reconstructed image of a black hole shadow at the core of radio galaxy Messier 87 (M87). The image appeared as a ring-like structure, representing the gravitationally lensed and redshifted emission around the central supermassive black hole, M87*, located at the galactic nucleus. However, application of various data analysis and imaging heuristics resulted in divergent representations of M87* fine-scale features, with some external analyses even challenging the fundamental ring-like morphology of the source. Such difficulties arise as a consequence of the inherent sparsity of the very-long baseline interferometry (VLBI) measurements, rendering interferometric image reconstruction an inadequately constrained problem. Moreover, the solution is sensitive to instrument calibration, post-processing algorithms, and imaging hyperparameters. Here, we apply a newly-developed independent imaging algorithm to the M87* dataset, which is free from prescriptive morphological priors and founded on observables immune to instrument calibration errors. We reconstruct the black hole shadow image, and unequivocally reproduce a ring-like morphology, with angular diameter 42.2 +/- 1.5 microarcseconds corresponding to a black hole mass of 6.5 +/- 0.5 billion solar masses assuming nominal scaling parameters, observed at an inclination angle of ~20 deg from the approaching jet.

authors.name: Samuel Lai
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

authors.name: Nithyanandan Thyagarajan
authors.institution: Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation

papers.title: RAMP: Rethinking Multimodal Evaluation through Answer Readout Protocols
papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are often evaluated by converting model outputs into discrete answers. The conversion protocol determines which scores become predictions and can strongly influence the reported results. We introduce RAMP (Readout Aware Multimodal Protocol), a systematic framework that compares direct yes/no token logits, surface-form scores, and typed or reversed A/B interfaces under fixed model checkpoints and paired visual questions. On 500 POPE adversarial questions, typed versus bare readout changes accuracy by $-20.2$ percentage points for SmolVLM-256M, $-16.4$ for TinyLLaVA-1.1B, and $+1.8$ for Qwen2.5-VL-3B. Paired transitions reveal extensive prediction changes even when the net accuracy difference is small: 79 of 104 binary ChartQA items change correctness for SmolVLM-500M, despite a $+1.0$-point net difference. We further analyze prompt wording, candidate forms, option position, cross-task effects, and calibration. An independent offline replay reproduces 16,140 first-token decisions from saved raw scores with exact agreement. Our findings establish answer readout as a measurable component of multimodal evaluation and provide a reproducible protocol for analyzing model comparisons.

authors.name: Ziying Song
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: IndustrialKnowEval: A Benchmark for Evaluating Multi-Level Industrial Knowledge in LLMs
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly explored for industrial tasks, yet few benchmarks evaluate their mastery of industrial knowledge across different types of cognitive demand. We introduce IndustrialKnowEval (IndKnow), a benchmark for industrial knowledge and engineering question answering. It contains 43,282 samples covering 21 task types across seven industrial sectors, including aerospace, electric power, and metallurgy, organized into four levels of cognitive demand: memory, comprehension, reasoning, and engineering application. Enterprise-based domain specialists and experienced researchers participate in all stages of dataset construction and quality control. We conduct a series of experiments on 18 representative LLMs, with domain experts deeply involved in the evaluation. Building upon IndKnow, we propose the Industrial Cognitive Capability Gap (ICCG) metric to characterize the performance differential between foundational industrial knowledge and higher-order reasoning and application, and we analyze it alongside absolute performance to provide a more complete view of model capabilities. We anticipate that IndustrialKnowEval will support the benchmarking of LLMs in industrial scenarios and promote the development of robust industrial intelligence. Code is available at: https://github.com/J4cksonLee/IndKnow

authors.name: Haoze Li
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

authors.name: Jingbo Zhou
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: ACiT: Proprioceptive-Prior Action Chunking with Inverted Transformers
papers.abstract: Visuomotor policies condition action prediction on visual and proprioceptive observations. While historical proprioceptive sequences carry rich dynamic priors, current methods treat them as equal to high-dimensional vision, causing the proprioceptive signal to be overwhelmed. To identify what is lost in equal-conditioning fusion, we analyze proprioceptive data and find that strong inter-joint coupling is the key action-determining structure. This finding aligns with the neural sensorimotor loop, in which proprioception first forms a body-centered prior and vision is later calibrated via parietal remapping. Inspired by this, we propose ACiT, Proprioceptive-Prior Action Chunking with Inverted Transformers, which reinforces historical joint-coupling as the primary condition with vision as a later calibration. This design is instantiated through three modules: Inverted State Encoding builds a proprioceptive prior via per-joint tokens and inter-joint self-attention. State-Visual Grounding lets joint tokens query visual evidence, making vision goal- and calibration-only. Inverted Action Chunking decodes per-joint trajectories independently. ACiT improves success rates on most LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, and real-world tasks, with the largest gains on those that require dynamics and coordination. The same conditioning design transferred to the VLA backbone pi_0-ACiT yields significant gains with better execution efficiency.

authors.name: Haixiang Wu
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: Motor Imagery Classification Using Hybrid Cross-Subject Class Mixup and Selective Attention
papers.abstract: Motor imagery (MI) enables a brain-computer interface (BCI) to decode movement intentions without overt movement. Hybrid electroencephalography (EEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) classification combines complementary signals, but inter-subject variability and the design of information exchange between modalities affect generalization to new subjects. We propose a framework that combines Cross-Subject Class Mixup (CSCM) with Selective Attention. CSCM aims to construct new training data to make the model robust against inter-subject variability. It independently selects EEG and fNIRS donor trials from other training subjects within the anchor class and mixes each modality while preserving the original label. Selective Attention provides an effective way to simultaneously model the temporal signal characteristics and fuse the two modalities. It retains causal temporal self-attention for EEG and uses a classification token (CLS) to integrate both modalities, without fNIRS attention updates or direct cross-modal temporal-token attention. Leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) evaluation across 28 subjects on a public EEG-fNIRS dataset yields a mean balanced accuracy (BA) of 76.85% and a macro-averaged F1 score (Macro-F1) of 76.58%. The proposed model achieves the highest mean performance among five reimplemented baselines. We also examine the contributions of CSCM and Selective Attention through modality-specific mixing and donor-policy comparisons, temporal-policy comparisons, interventions on direct cross-modal paths, and component ablations.

authors.name: Chae-Won Lee
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: Inside the Brain Tumor: What MRI-Defined Habitats Exist Within Glioblastoma, How Are They Spatially Organized, and What Molecular Processes Are Associated with Them?
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma exhibits substantial spatial heterogeneity, but MRI studies often emphasize tumor extent rather than the organization of imaging phenotypes. We investigated whether multiparametric MRI identifies reproducible habitats and whether habitat abundance and spatial architecture provide distinct information. Preoperative T1, contrast-enhanced T1, T2, and FLAIR scans with manual segmentations from 97 TCGA-GBM patients were analyzed. Unsupervised clustering of normalized voxel intensities identified two habitats. An Interface Ratio quantified the observed H1-H2 boundary relative to abundance-preserving spatial randomization. Molecular associations were assessed using matched Affymetrix U133A expression data and seven prespecified transcriptional programs. H2 showed higher T2 and FLAIR signal, while habitat distributions corresponded poorly to conventional segmentation compartments. Among 66 mixed-habitat tumors, Interface Ratio varied substantially and was independent of H2 abundance (rho = 0.074, p = 0.555). Molecular data were available for 89 patients, including 60 mixed-habitat tumors. Higher H2 abundance was nominally associated with hypoxia-program scores after adjustment for Interface Ratio (beta = 0.337, 95% CI 0.089-0.584; p = 0.0077), but not after multiple-testing correction (FDR = 0.108). No Interface Ratio association survived correction. Habitat composition and spatial organization represent two complementary dimensions of glioblastoma heterogeneity. The H2-hypoxia relationship remains exploratory and requires independent, spatially resolved validation.

papers.title: Variational Estimates for the Bilinear Hilbert Transform
papers.abstract: We prove that for every $q>2$, the $q$-variation operator associated with the bilinear Hilbert transform is bounded from $L^r(\mathbb R)\times L^s(\mathbb R)$ to $L^p(\mathbb R)$ whenever $1<r,s<\infty$, $p>2/3$, and $1/p=1/r+1/s$.

papers.title: Multidimensional mixed Bohr radii for Banach space valued holomorphic functions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce and study a generalized notion of multidimensional mixed Bohr radii for holomorphic functions defined on the unit ball of the finite-dimensional Minkowski sequence space with values in complex Banach spaces. We first prove that the multidimensional mixed Bohr radius is positive for every non-null bounded linear operator whose norm is sufficiently small relative to the scaling parameter. We then determine the exact asymptotic behavior of the multidimensional mixed Bohr radius for infinite-dimensional Banach spaces of finite cotype and we obtain analogous bounds for spaces without finite cotype. Finally, for concave Banach lattices and summing operators, we prove lower bounds that involve a logarithmic factor. These results connect classical scalar Bohr phenomena with operator-valued and Banach space valued settings, and highlight how the geometry of the spaces and the mapping properties of the operator influence coefficient estimates and their dependence on dimension. Several examples illustrate the consistency of our results with the classical Bohr radius and the sharp Defant--Frerick asymptotics.

papers.title: Multi-Library Feature Engineering and Statistically Validated Classification for Power Swing Detection and Stability Assessment
papers.abstract: Faults occurring during power swings, and the evolution of a swing into an unstable condition, cause distance-relay maloperation and cascaded outages. This paper identifies faults, faults during power swings, and power swings, and distinguishes stable from unstable swings in a 9-bus WSCC system modeled in PSCAD/EMTDC. Three time-series feature libraries (tsfresh, TSFEL, and tsfeatures) are applied to the 3-phase relay voltages and currents, giving 3286 statistical, temporal, spectral, and fractal descriptors per event window. A two-step feature selection (Boruta all-relevant filtering followed by RFECV- and SHAP-guided minimal-optimal pruning) reduces the feature set to 18 compact, non-redundant features. 14 classifiers spanning linear, kernel/instance-based, probabilistic, neural, and tree-ensemble/boosting families are then benchmarked under repeated stratified cross-validation, with model differences assessed by a Friedman/Nemenyi omnibus-and-post-hoc test and a Nadeau--Bengio corrected paired t-test. Rotation Forest (ROF) identifies the three event types with 99.98% and SVM-RBF distinguishes stable from unstable swings with 97.97% balanced accuracy. The results show that automated, library-driven feature extraction combined with rigorous statistical model comparison achieves near-perfect discrimination while retaining feature-level interpretability through SHAP importance.

papers.title: Lower Bound of Thermal Conductivity in Graphene
papers.abstract: The intrinsic thermal conductivity ($\kappa$) of graphene remains highly controversial because of physical and metrological complexities. Although the thermal bridge method enables reliable measurements, sample fabrication remains challenging. Here, we develop a highly efficient patterning and transfer technique to systematically fabricate and characterize suspended bilayer graphene (BLG) thermal bridges with lengths of 1-30 $\mu$m. Suspended BLG with unavoidable polymer residues exhibits length-independent thermal conductivity of approximately 570 W/(m K) at room temperature, remaining nearly constant from 250 to 350 K and robust to rigorous surface cleaning and amorphous silicon nitride substrates. Homogeneous non-equilibrium molecular dynamics (HNEMD) simulations show that amorphous carbon coverage of only approximately 0.01 monolayer is sufficient to suppress out-of-plane flexural acoustic (ZA) phonons. These findings challenge the prevailing view that rigid substrates suppress ZA phonons more strongly than surface contamination and identify a robust lower bound of $\kappa$ governed by amorphous surface scattering. This lower bound reflects heat conduction in graphene under realistic device conditions and provides a reference for fundamental phonon transport studies and the integration of graphene into thermal management applications in electronic devices and chips.

authors.name: Yan Gao
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Xiaohang Zhang
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

authors.name: Guimei Zhu
authors.institution: Southern University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Yahui Xue
authors.institution: Southern University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Maximal Independent Sets in Set Systems
papers.abstract: We prove a general theorem on the existence of small maximal independent sets in set systems satisfying natural local density conditions. For an antichain whose degrees are uniform and whose small sets lie in few blocks and whose links overlap little, we show that there is a maximal independent set whose size is asymptotically given by an explicit expression in the degrees, as the degrees grow. The proof comes with a polynomial-time algorithm that finds such a set. This improves on known results for independent sets in uniform hypergraphs; in particular, in a linear uniform hypergraph of large bounded degree, we find an independent set of explicit asymptotic size. Among the applications, we obtain complete arcs in finite projective spaces that come within logarithmic factors of the counting lower bound, improving the known results on Segre's complete arc problem. We also show that, for a wide class of multivariable polynomials, there is a maximal set in a finite field avoiding solutions of the polynomial whose size lies within logarithmic factors of the elementary lower bound.

papers.title: Isolated singularities of solutions to the Yamabe equation with boundary in higher dimensions I
papers.abstract: We study isolated boundary singularities of positive solutions of the scalar-flat boundary Yamabe equation. We prove the critical upper bound for general smooth metrics in dimensions $3\le n\le17$ and for Euclidean domains with smooth boundary in dimensions $3\le n\le22$. For general metrics, this range extends to $n=18$ when the conformal metric is complete near the singularity. In every dimension, the critical upper bound implies removability or a matching lower bound and convergence to a unique flat Fowler solution with a positive power rate. Sharpness of these dimension ranges will be established in a subsequent paper.

papers.title: VideoNexus: Video Perception Beyond the Reasoning Context
papers.abstract: Understanding long videos requires locating evidence, resolving visual details, and integrating observations into an answer. Even when relevant evidence is present, performing these operations within long, dense visual sequences burdens both perception and reasoning. Video agents enable selective inspection, but returning frames to the planner still accumulates visual information in its reasoning context. Delegating perception reduces this burden, yet sparse sampling can miss decisive details, and per-frame descriptions can preserve context growth. We introduce VideoNexus, a training-free framework that separates detailed video perception from evidence-driven planning and reasoning. The planner controls where to inspect, what to resolve, and how densely to sample. Perception sub-agents process native audio-video in independent contexts and return compact, temporally grounded evidence for iterative search and verification. Using Gemini 3.8 Flash for both planning and perception, VideoNexus achieves 88.6% accuracy on full LVBench, exceeding same-backbone static ingestion and built-in agentic processing by 3.6 and 1.1 points, respectively, at 44% of the latter's measured API cost. A paired LVBench subset ablation shows lower planner input and higher accuracy. With Kimi K3 as the shared backbone, VideoNexus improves over the official Video-GAIA ReAct harness by 8.5 points in our evaluation. These results support compact evidence exchange for combining detailed observation with efficient planning and reasoning.

authors.name: Wei Chen
authors.institution: Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: Harmonic-Mean Aggregation of Continuous-Time Markov Chains with Reachability Error Bounds
papers.abstract: Abstracting a continuous-time Markov chain by grouping its states into blocks raises a fundamental question: which rates should the abstract chain use when states within a block have different exit rates and transition probabilities? We study harmonic-mean aggregation, which matches the mean waiting time and next-block distribution of a local experiment that uniformly selects a state within the block and observes its next jump. Equivalently, the abstract transition rates are averages of the concrete rates with inverse-exit-rate weights. Since the aggregation does not preserve reachability probabilities in general, we derive theoretical error bounds for time-bounded reachability. We decompose the error into a blockwise mean and centered-within-block deviations, and show that the rate mismatch has zero weighted mean. Exploiting this cancellation and differences between abstract reachability values, we obtain bounds valid at every time horizon through a linear comparison system with two quantities per block, without computing concrete reachability values. All results are formalized and proven in Lean 4.

papers.title: Emergent Steering Beyond Endpoint Alignment in Chemical Reaction Models
papers.abstract: Machine learning models for chemical reaction prediction are usually evaluated by endpoint accuracy, but endpoint correctness alone does not reveal how a model represents chemical transformation or why it fails. We introduce UniRxnAxis, a unified forward-retrosynthesis framework that models both tasks as direction-conditioned endpoint redistribution in a shared latent space. By aligning source states, transformed states, and encoded target endpoints, UniRxnAxis enables directional auditing of learned latent updates. This shared latent geometry allows the learned displacement (from the encoder source state $S_0$ to the decoder-facing transformed state $S_1$) to be decomposed into an endpoint-parallel component and an endpoint-orthogonal residual, which we call emergent steering. Our evaluation shows that emergent steering is functionally important: in retrosynthesis, it recovers most of the model's utility, remains effective under random, shuffled, and prototype controls, and directly affects which bond edits are promoted or suppressed. The residual-over-parallel ordering persists across alignment strengths, after decoder-interface calibration, against angle-matched random axes, and in a second graph-edit architecture, although its magnitude depends on the reference axis and optimization. The decomposition also supports a proxy taxonomy of model-side failures, showing how reaction models can be audited beyond endpoint accuracy.

papers.title: Same Fix, Different Weights: Replicating Weight-Space Programming with Claude
papers.abstract: Takehi et al. (2026) report that GPT-6 Astra, given the weights of small neural networks as text, can say what they were trained to do, repair them, and write new ones without training. I re-ran the core of that study with Claude Opus 5.5 in ten pre-registered experiments, with untrained-network and permutation controls and hand audits of every sandboxed code cell. Reading was mixed: Claude named 3 of 4 Atari games from policy weights and found the measured copying heads in 15/15 character-LM runs, but its answers about training data often followed priors. Unlike the original, it identified a sycophantic Gemma 3 270M finetune from weights alone in 6/6 runs. One-shot weight edits took a failing MountainCar policy from 0% to 100% success and a hovering LunarLander policy from 0% to 85.6%; zero-shot networks beat PPO at 100k steps on 4 of 5 environments, each implementing a textbook controller. With no training or forward passes, Claude wrote a 1.48M-parameter 9x9 Go network that won 85-94% of games against three PPO opponents. Given Qwen3.5-0.8B's weights and 10, 25 or 50 forward passes of 64 practice problems, Claude raised MATH-500 from 6.7% to 51.4%, 55.2% and 58.1% (+51.4 points at 50 passes, 95% CI [47.9, 55.0]; original 48.1%), GSM8K from 11.6% to 68.2% and IFEval from 22.2% to 54.2%. Unlike the original, which removed an internal loop direction, every edit acted at the output: it scaled the final norm, raising the effective sampling temperature, and lowered the logit of "Wait" while raising that of </think>. The norm scaling alone reaches only 20.9-22.1% on MATH-500. On Gemma 3 270M, which rarely loops, no edit helped (-0.8 points), as in the original.

authors.name: Subham Kundu
authors.institution: Indian Institute of Engineering Science and Technology, Shibpur

papers.title: Can decision models extract clinical data from cancer pathology reports? An evaluation of accuracy, calibration, and failure modes
papers.abstract: Decision models are a new class of language model that, instead of generating text, choose one option per question from a fixed list and return a probability for every option. They have not yet been evaluated on clinical text. We evaluated two open-weights decision models, Nimble 9B and Tev1 4B, for extracting 25 fields from 1,113 oral cavity cancer pathology reports from a single centre, against a prospectively maintained clinical database. We compared them with two generative models: Qwen3.5 9B, run locally, and GLM-5.3-flash, run through a cloud API. Tev1 reached a mean field accuracy of 0.917 (95% CI 0.913 to 0.920), the same as Qwen3.5 9B (0.918; p = 0.26), and was four times faster (15 s against 61 s per report). Nimble reached 0.862 and GLM-5.3-flash 0.986. Both decision models matched GLM-5.3-flash on simple dichotomous categories. They were weak on measurements binned into categories, on fields whose correct answer was not reported, and on some complex decisions (e.g. involved margins). We found that the main cause of the inferior performance of Nimble's came from asking 25 questions in one request: with two questions per request, its accuracy improved. Pooled over fields, the returned probabilities were well calibrated (expected calibration error 0.022 and 0.026), but they did not flag systematic errors within single fields. A simulated strategy of sending answers with a probability below 0.94 to GLM-5.3-flash raised Tev1's accuracy to 0.982, with 38% of answers escalated. Decision models can extract explicitly stated findings from pathology reports quickly on local hardware and return useful probabilities. They should be validated in the configuration in which they will be used, restricted to the fields in which they are reliable, and combined with other methods for numeric values.

papers.title: Current-driven chiral RKKY interaction in altermagnets
papers.abstract: The Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya (DM) interaction between magnetic moments usually requires spin--orbit coupling and broken inversion symmetry. We show that in a spin-split metal without spin--orbit coupling a charge current generates a DM interaction between localized spins. Using Keldysh Green's functions (GFs) with a drifting Fermi sea, we compute the Ruderman--Kittel--Kasuya--Yosida (RKKY) interaction between two magnetic impurities in a two-dimensional $d$-wave altermagnet with an additional exchange splitting. To linear order in the current, the correction is a Fermi-surface term, and all its components are obtained in closed form in terms of Bessel functions, valid for arbitrary values of the two independent spin splittings, $\beta$ and $J_\perp$. The induced DM vector points along the spin-quantization axis, which in the present model is the out-of-plane direction $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$. At long distance it decays as $1/R$, one power more slowly than the equilibrium coupling. In the altermagnet it vanishes for bonds along the nodal directions, where the two spin bands are degenerate, and, for a diagonal current, has opposite signs on bonds along the two crystal axes. This $d$-wave signature reverses with the N\'eel vector and with the current, and distinguishes the altermagnet from a ferromagnet. The current also generates symmetric couplings that are odd in the impurity separation. In low-density two-dimensional conductors, the DM coupling can reach a few percent of the equilibrium exchange.

papers.title: Borel combinatorics of $\mathbb{N}^{\ell}$-shift actions and hypersmooth equivalence relations
papers.abstract: We conjecture that for each integer $\ell\geq 2$, the equivalence relation arising from the shift action of $\mathbb{N}^{\ell}$ on $2^{\omega^{\ell}}$ is hypersmooth. We prove this conjecture for $\ell=2$, reduce the general case to a problem in Borel graph colorings, and establish the general case in measure. We also show that under certain mild hypotheses on a hypersmooth equivalence relation $E$, every finite-index Borel super-equivalence relation of $E$ is hypersmooth.

papers.title: Beyond Binary Audits: Does Guideline Grounding Mitigate Decision-Space Framing in LLM Opioid Prescribing?
papers.abstract: Audits of LLMs for bias in opioid prescribing have largely relied on binary treatment decisions, a signal that current models have saturated. We introduce Q-Pain++, a full-factorial stress test that holds clinical content fixed while independently varying clinical risk factors and the granularity of the available dosage options. Adding an intermediate dosage option to otherwise unchanged vignettes substantially lowers agreement with expert-annotated dosages for most models, while demographic differences in dosage decisions remain small in all but one configuration once clinical risk factors are added. Grounding models in perioperative guidelines through retrieval reduces this framing effect on average but does not eliminate it, and one model's treatment decisions change when the retrieved passages are reordered. These results suggest that audits should vary the answer format, not only patient identity. We will release our codebase as well as Guideline-RAG-associated resources on GitHub (https://github.com/su-boussard-lab/llm-guideline-grounding-opioids).

authors.name: Keyi Yu
authors.institution: Zhejiang Center for Disease Control and Prevention

papers.title: Use of Peer Code Review to Identify Potential Security Vulnerabilities in Open Source Software: A Systematic Literature Review
papers.abstract: Context: Security vulnerabilities in OSS can have severe consequences. OSS project participants widely use peer code review to improve quality and prevent security flaws. However, despite mandatory reviews, OSS projects still contain vulnerabilities, highlighting the need to evaluate code review effectiveness for security. Objectives: This SLR synthesizes evidence on vulnerability types identified or missed, security practices, tool support, reviewer challenges, and factors that improve detection. Method: Searches of five digital libraries yielded 1,067 studies, of which 20 were included. Vulnerabilities were categorized using the Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) framework. Results: Peer code reviews effectively detect localized, well-known vulnerabilities (e.g., buffer overruns, race conditions, crashes, XSS) but often miss subtle, complex, context-dependent issues (e.g., input validation weaknesses, access control weaknesses, resource lifecycle weaknesses). Effective security practices are associated with reviewer expertise, code familiarity, frequent small changes, and organizational support. Security analysis tools, especially Static Application Security Testing (SAST) tools, reduce reviewer effort and improve detection but cannot replace human judgment. Reviewers continue to face limitations in security knowledge, experience, time, and understanding of complex systems. Effectiveness improves through security training, domain expertise, contextual familiarity, formalized review processes, and supportive review environments. Conclusion: Peer code review contributes to OSS security but is insufficient on its own. Improving effectiveness requires structured review processes and checklists, security training, organizational incentives, and lightweight automated tool support to help reviewers detect subtle vulnerabilities while reinforcing secure development practices.

papers.title: Segregated normalized solutions for a nonlinear Schr\"odinger system with two mass constraints
papers.abstract: We study a two-component nonlinear Schr\"odinger system with two prescribed positive $L^2$ masses and a fixed competitive coupling $\beta<0$, for $N=1,2,3$ and $4\le p<2^*$. We first consider families whose peak heights diverge and whose components converge uniformly to zero away from disjoint finite peak sets. For such families, we prove that both Lagrange multipliers tend to $-\infty$ and that the mass of each component concentrates at its own peaks. We also construct positive multi-peak solutions near prescribed nondegenerate critical points of the respective potentials and compute the leading displacement of each peak. The target frequencies may grow at different rates, provided that $\Lambda_*\to\infty$ and $\log(2+\Lambda^*)=o(\sqrt{\Lambda_*})$, where $\Lambda_*$ and $\Lambda^*$ denote their minimum and maximum. In the $L^2$-noncritical case, the first frequency correction is minus the average potential at the prescribed points. In the $L^2$-critical case, the leading mass term is independent of the frequencies. For each component, we compute the mass correction of order \(\lambda_i^{-2}\) in terms of the sum of the Laplacians of its potential at the prescribed points. When both sums are nonzero, these corrections determine the leading-order asymptotics of the two frequencies and the side from which each self-interaction coefficient approaches its critical value.

papers.title: Shared Mobile AR Without Depth Sensors from Monocular Point Maps
papers.abstract: Depth-aware augmented reality on phones needs dense geometry of the surrounding room. iPhones and iPads without LiDAR expose only sparse feature points and detected planes, and ARKit often takes tens of seconds to report the first wall. We describe a scan-free pipeline for these devices. A point-map network (MoGe-2) predicts metric geometry from each camera frame, the remaining depth shift is recovered from the camera intrinsics, and each frame's scale is aligned to views already in the map. A persistent voxel map with visibility-based expiry answers occlusion and collision queries. Co-located devices share one coordinate frame by solving yaw and floor-plane translation from sightings of each other. We evaluate the deployed system on 309 device-sessions from 19 device models without LiDAR, with 179 device-sessions from LiDAR phones in the same deployment as a reference population. A first dense depth map was recorded within 10 s in 80% of sessions, while ARKit had reported a wall plane by then in 25%. The median session scale was 0.98 against ARKit's wall planes and 1.00 against its camera translation. Scale changed by a median of 9% between nearby frames, against 0.4% with LiDAR, and depth points spread three times as widely around walls. In multi-device sessions, 69% of devices without LiDAR reached a converged shared frame, against 84% of LiDAR phones. The main remaining error is scale that changes from frame to frame.

authors.name: Mohammad Rashid
authors.institution: Atish Dipankar University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Probability of Success under Population Shift for Phase III Trial Planning
papers.abstract: Probability of success (PoS) is widely used to inform go/no-go decisions for phase III trials based on phase II evidence. Conventional PoS calculations, however, implicitly assume that baseline covariate distributions are identical across phases. When covariate shift exists between phase II and phase III populations, unadjusted PoS may be biased and lead to miscalibrated decision-making. We propose a Bayesian framework for PoS evaluation that explicitly accounts for covariate shift between phase II and III population prior to phase III initiation. The method adopts a transportability perspective, adjusting phase II evidence to reflect an anticipated phase III target population using available target covariate information. The framework accommodates both individual-level and aggregate-level phase III covariate data. Simulation studies demonstrate that, compared with the conventional approach, the proposed method improves PoS accuracy and decision calibration when covariate shift is present, while maintaining comparable performance when populations are aligned. We illustrate the proposed methodology using clinical trial data from systemic lupus erythematosus.

authors.name: Ying Yuan
authors.institution: The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center

papers.title: Triadic and assortative structure of absorbing states in the Axelrod model
papers.abstract: We study the Axelrod model of cultural dissemination, viewed as a finite-state Markov chain on an arbitrary finite graph, and classify its absorbing states. An absorbing configuration splits the edges into interior edges, whose endpoints share their whole culture, and boundary edges, whose endpoints share nothing. A partition of the vertices into connected blocks is the domain partition of some absorbing configuration exactly when its quotient graph is properly $q$-colourable. The configurations with a given domain partition correspond to homomorphisms from the quotient into the $F$-fold categorical power of $K_q$, so their total number is a sum of chromatic polynomials over connected partitions; this gives closed forms for trees and cycles and the value $2^{n+F-1}$ for $q=2$ on connected graphs. In absorbing configurations no triangle carries exactly one boundary edge, the open-wedge mass of the interior graph is at most that of the host graph, and Newman's assortativity coefficients for domains, cultures and single features are ordered. The feature counts are martingales and their sums of squares submartingales, which yields an absorption-time bound of order $n^2$ that is attained on paths. Exhaustive enumeration and simulations illustrate the results.

papers.title: Betti numbers of powers of Ferrers ideals and edge ideals of threshold graphs
papers.abstract: We provide explicit formulas for the Betti numbers of all powers of Ferrers ideals and edge ideals of threshold graphs.

authors.name: Do Trong Hoang
authors.institution: Trường Đại học Khoa học và Công nghệ Hà Nội

papers.title: Uniqueness of limit cycle{s} in a class of classical trinomial Li\'enard systems
papers.abstract:
This paper studies the number of limit cycles of the polynomial Li\'enard system
  $\dot x=y-F(x)$, $\dot y=-x$, where
  $F(x)=a_1x^{2N}+a_2x^{2m+1}+x^{2n+1}$,
  with integers \(N,m,n\) satisfying $2\le N\le m<n$, $a_1\ne0$ and $a_2\neq 0$.
  It is proved that this system has exactly one limit cycle and that
  every periodic orbit is hyperbolic and attracting
  for $a_2<0$; this system has
  no limit cycles for $a_2>0$. The uniqueness proof compares the widths and relative midpoints of the two scalar
  arcs obtained in potential coordinates.
  This result gives a positive answer to Conjecture 1.4 of
  Cen et al. (Sci. China Math., 2026).

papers.title: A Polynomial-Time Algorithm for Constant-Factor EFX Allocations of Chores
papers.abstract:
We study the fair division of indivisible chores among agents with additive disutilities, focusing on the central fairness notion of envy-freeness up to any chore (EFX), and its multiplicative approximations. Although the existence of constant-factor approximations to EFX are known, computing such an allocation in polynomial time remained open. We resolve this question by giving an algorithm that, for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, computes a $(3+\varepsilon)$-EFX allocation in time polynomial in the input length and $1/\varepsilon$.
  Our result relies on two algorithmic contributions. First, we give a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme (FPTAS) for earning-restricted (ER) equilibria with equal earning requirements and arbitrary feasible chore earning limits. We develop a new nonconvex program with chore payouts and money-flow variables, and prove that every local maximum yields an exact ER equilibrium. We then give a mirror-ascent algorithm for this program and prove that it converges to an approximate ER equilibrium in polynomial time.
  Second, we give a new procedure that converts the approximate equilibrium into a $(3+\varepsilon)$-EFX-friendly allocation, a suitable starting point for the chore-swap framework of Garg and Murhekar (2026). The procedure uses a flexible price threshold to choose swap chores and their recipients together, overcoming a factor-four bottleneck in the earlier approaches while accommodating approximate earnings. We expect these ideas to be useful more broadly in fair division, including for goods and other fairness notions.

papers.title: Frame First, Decode Once: Object-Centric Coordinates and Single-Pass Decoding for System-1 World Models
papers.abstract: Single-pass primitive decoders such as LocateAnything and VFlash predict all quantized coordinate tokens of a geometric primitive in one forward pass, enabling fast, System-1 visual planning. We study what matters when such a decoder serves as a System-1 world model: a fast action-conditioned predictor that ranks candidate pushes by their predicted outcome. On ManiSkill3 PushT-v1 (512 held-out test families, 8,192 rollouts) and on human demonstrations from lerobot/pusht (2,384 test windows), we compare decoders, training losses, rigid-body projections and coordinate frames, using matched checkpoints, hierarchical bootstrap confidence intervals and Holm correction. Two factors of similar size dominate. First, expressing inputs and outputs in the SE(2) frame of the object's initial pose lowers decision regret by 1.9-2.2x for each of five decoders, and the object-frame model trained on 128 families matches the world-frame model trained on 512. Second, single-pass decoding outperforms iterative decoding: in the object frame, single-pass heads reach 0.020-0.021 regret at 1.6-1.8 ms per decision, against 0.046 for 10-step DDIM diffusion and 0.059 for KV-cached autoregression at 10.3 and 12.9 ms. The choice among single-pass heads has no measurable effect on regret, and our registered hypothesis that the frame effect exceeds the decoder spread is not supported. Soft-token expectation with an end-to-end 2D Kabsch projection gives the lowest trajectory error (11.35 px on ManiSkill3, 3.78 px on lerobot/pusht), exact rigid-body consistency, and lower regret than diffusion at every budget from 4 to 50 DDIM steps, at 3-29x lower latency.

papers.title: Replay-Augmented Regularisation for Class-Incremental Network Intrusion Detection: A Three-Dataset Evaluation of EWC and LwF
papers.abstract: As new attack categories emerge, network intrusion detection models need to be updated; however, when fine-tuned sequentially on new classes, previous classes are forgotten, resulting in catastrophic for- getting. The three public datasets we use are UNSW-NB15, ToN-IoT and CIC-IDS2017, and for these datasets, our class-incremental intrusion detection system is built using a CNN with one-dimensional (1D) archi- tecture trained over nine sequential tasks, each of which introduces one attack category. We evaluate sequential fine-tuning without any buffe compared to Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC) and Learning without Forgetting (LwF), both of which include a class-size-adaptive rehearsal buffer of 20% of all previous classes (from 20 to 300 samples). The hyper-parameters were selected using UNSW-NB15 and fixed for the other two datasets. On UNSW-NB15, replay improves the final accuracy of both regularisers to 73.6% (EWC) and 71.1% (LwF) compared to about 32% (no improvement over fine-tuning). LwF with replay achieves 46.1% and 91.6% final accuracy for the two frozen-configuration datasets (ToN-IoT, CIC-IDS2017) while EWC with replay achieves 23.7% and 61.9%. In order to avoid this, EWC was therefore tuned on one dataset and the other two data sets were used as test sets. It is also demonstrated that the common forgetting measure can be misleading for a model which does not learn the old classes. As the fine-tuning baseline was not re- played and all the results were based on a single seed, it is not claimed hat the regularisers provide any extra support over replay alone.

papers.title: VLN-Flash: Parallel Action Decoding with Adaptive Execution for Vision-and-Language Navigation
papers.abstract: When a vision-and-language navigation policy generates an action sequence autoregressively, the robot waits for a chain of dependent predictions. A small discrete action vocabulary makes it possible to score all short-horizon plans in parallel. We introduce VLN-Flash, a training-free decoder that evaluates the complete action-prefix tree in a single forward pass. Branch-specific attention and matched token positions preserve the original policy's conditional action distribution for each prefix in exact arithmetic. We use the score margin between the stepwise-greedy prefix and its strongest alternative at each depth to decide how many actions to execute. The robot then executes the plan with the highest joint score at the chosen depth before observing again. On matched inputs, VLN-Flash achieves a nearly $3\times$ speedup in action decoding over native autoregression on Uni-NaVid and StreamVLN. Compared with the native autoregressive decoders, it improves success rate and success weighted by path length (SPL) on R2R-CE and RxR-CE, with success gains up to 2.7 percentage points. On a Unitree GO2, VLN-Flash improves navigation success and cuts the mean wait between actions by about 160 ms after subtracting network transmission time.

papers.title: Memorization Lives in a Few Attention Heads: Mitigating Memorization in Diffusion Models via Projection-Based Suppression
papers.abstract: Diffusion models can memorize and reproduce training samples during inference, raising serious privacy and copyright concerns. Existing inference-time mitigation methods often suppress conditional information globally, which may reduce memorization but can also harm semantic alignment and image quality. In this paper, we revisit memorization from the perspective of cross-attention heads. Through systematic analysis and targeted ablation, we find that memorization is mainly driven by a small subset of shallow-layer attention heads with abnormally strong semantic control, rather than by the entire cross-attention mechanism. Motivated by this finding, we propose Projection-based Top-k Attention Head Suppression, a targeted inference-time mitigation method. Our method first identifies the top-k attention heads most related to memorization using a semantic-control score, and then removes their condition-specific components through directional projection between conditional and unconditional representations. This design selectively weakens memorization-related features while preserving useful semantic information. Extensive experiments on different diffusion models and datasets show that our method effectively reduces memorization and achieves a better trade-off between memorization mitigation and image quality than existing approaches.

papers.title: Read Before You Fit: Text-Derived Constraints for Discovering Differential Equations from Noisy Biological Data
papers.abstract: Large language models are increasingly used for scientific equation discovery. However, most existing methods are strongly data-driven and assume sufficiently clean and representative observations. This assumption is problematic in biological systems, where individual-level measurements are often sparse, noisy, heterogeneous, and expensive to obtain. While the underlying mechanisms are extensively described in scientific text, they are not explicitly used for the LLM based modeling of such systems. We introduce P2C, an agentic framework that translates textual descriptions of biological systems into a typed set of formal constraints, and use these constraints to restrict candidate ordinary differential equation (ODE) structures before numerical fitting. P2C consists of five stages: Text2Constraint extraction, ODE discovery, symbolic verification, parameter fitting, and model scoring. We evaluate P2C on four published ODE systems of acute inflammation and immune regulation, under clean and noisy observations. By progressively degrading the numerical evidence, we isolate when textual domain knowledge contributes beyond regression alone. Across the four systems, adding Text2Constraint reduces the worst form error from 1.397 to 0.499 on clean data and from 13.096 to 1.095 for data perturbed with Gaussian noise of $\sigma=0.1$; P2C also achieves lower form error and trajectory error than several LLM-based baselines over the tested noise range.

papers.title: DynLimit: A Simulation Benchmark for Dynamics-Critical Planning and Control
papers.abstract: Experiments near vehicle handling limits must keep three questions apart: what a maneuver requests, what the closed-loop system executes, and whether the task is completed. We present DynLimit, a simulation platform that organizes this process end to end. Scenarios are composed from road, friction, obstacle, and reference objects; planners and controllers attach through a shared observation and control interface; a vehicle adapter runs either a license-free four-wheel model or an external dynamics solver; and synchronized records feed task evaluation, replay, and response inspection. The platform carries a task-oriented evaluation method that pairs a prescribed reference demand with a sampled passing set and event-aligned diagnosis. Across eight task families, three friction environments, and three reference-assisted baseline chains we executed 450 runs: 360 nominal, 18 locally refined, and 72 with prescribed initial offsets. Method differences depend on the task family, equal aggregate pass counts arise from different passing cells, and local refinement narrows two sampled transitions without locating a continuous boundary. Two case comparisons show why sideslip or tire-utilization peaks cannot replace task constraints. The three views therefore stay distinct in every reported run: an outcome can be traced from the prescribed demand, through the executed response, to the task rule that decided it. Code is available at https://github.com/Yang2581/dynlimit

authors.name: Yang Xiao
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Yongzhi Liu
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Lao Siji: Adapting openpilot to Closed-Loop End-to-End Driving in Neural Reconstruction
papers.abstract: We present Lao Siji, an end-to-end driving policy that ranks third in the 2026 NVIDIA AlpaSim E2E Driving Challenge, ahead of most entries built on foundation models. Instead of training from scratch on a general-purpose vision backbone, we adapt openpilot, an open-source L2 production model. We freeze its vision encoder and fine-tune the policy layers with an ego-state adapter and a route memory. On closed-loop rollouts in neural-reconstructed scenes, we supervise the policy with a privileged map teacher for lateral self-correction and a body-extent loss for road and obstacle clearance, while distilling the base model's remaining outputs to retain car following. Ablations show that self-correction samples carry the gain, while the clearance loss substitutes for them where no teacher exists. Longitudinal safety instead rests on the base model's lead-vehicle estimate behind a rule-based speed layer. Longer training, imitating human logs, and human-log speed targets yield either no measurable gain or adverse effects. Without further training, Lao Siji also places among the leaders on HUGSIM and Odyssey. The final training takes only one GPU-hour and shifts the weights by 3.9% from the shipped model. Code will be released after review.

authors.name: Yongzhi Liu
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Polarization-Resilient Plasmonic Nanoantenna Arrays for Fiber-Coupled Terahertz Spectroscopy with Record-high Dynamic Range
papers.abstract: Achieving polarization-resilient optoelectronic responses while harnessing the strong light-matter interactions enabled by plasmonic nanostructures remains a fundamental challenge in ultrafast optoelectronics. Here, we demonstrate that the polarization sensitivity of plasmonic optoelectronic devices is governed not simply by optical absorption, but by its interplay with ultrafast photocarrier transport and local electric-field distributions, establishing a design principle for achieving polarization resilience without compromising optoelectronic efficiency. Through theoretical modeling and experimental validation, we demonstrate that this interplay enables plasmonic nanoantenna arrays to maintain highly efficient terahertz generation and detection across different optical polarization states, overcoming a longstanding limitation of plasmonic optoelectronics. Exploiting this principle, we introduce a high-power fiber-coupled terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) architecture that integrates polarization-resilient plasmonic nanoantenna arrays with hollow-core antiresonant fibers. By suppressing optical dispersion and nonlinearities during high-power femtosecond pulse delivery, this architecture unlocks the superior optoelectronic properties of GaAs-based photoconductors without sacrificing the flexibility and robustness of fiber coupling. The resulting system generates a record-high 2.1 mW of terahertz radiation and achieves a 145 dB peak dynamic range over 60 seconds, representing a 300-fold improvement over state-of-the-art fiber-coupled THz-TDS systems. This breakthrough opens new opportunities for probing weak light-matter interactions, characterizing strongly attenuating materials, and realizing high-throughput hyperspectral imaging and spatially distributed terahertz sensing beyond controlled laboratory environments.

authors.name: Ali Jabbari
authors.institution: University of Iowa Hospitals and Clinics

papers.title: Block Generalized Inverses in Skew Corner Pairs
papers.abstract: We view generalized inverses from another perspective, through invertibility in the skew corner bimodules $eRf$ attached to a pair of distinct idempotents $e, f$ of a ring $R$. Many generalized inverses are defined by a system of equations together with conditions on ranges and kernels, which makes them harder to visualize as inverses in the traditional sense. In the language of invertible blocks, however, they become genuine one or two-sided inverses of a suitable compression of the element. We will systematically show how block invertibility in a skew corner $eRf$ can be used to visualize Drazin's $(b,c)$-inverse, which contains the Moore--Penrose, Bott-Duffin $(e,f)$ inverses amongst others. On this foundation we develop a way to produce units of the corner ring from complementary blocks, and transport stable range one across two-sided Peirce decompositions for distinct idempotents.

papers.title: An improved statistical treatment for radioassay-based background projection incorporating part-to-part variation
papers.abstract: For low background experiments, prediction of the background from radioactivity in detector components is of critical importance. Radioassays are often conducted on small samples or individual parts, which may be subject to differences in production or handling resulting in a part-to-part variation. This part-to-part variation can have an impact on the total activity and is not presently captured by the averaging methods used to evaluate radioassays. We propose a new method for the averaging of radioassays to incorporate this part-to-part variation into predictions of the total activity of parts. We also consider how to add component activities based on assays for component groups that are simulated as a single entity.

papers.title: Spectral action in Betti metaplectic Langlands
papers.abstract:
We construct the spectral action in the context of Betti metaplectic Langlands theory. More precisely, we prove that the category of twisted sheaves on $\text{Bun}_G$ with nilpotent singular support admits a canonical action by the symmetric monoidal category of quasicoherent sheaves on the moduli of twisted $H$-local systems, where $H$ is the metaplectic dual group. This confirms the Betti version of the conjecture of Gaitsgory--Lysenko, originally formulated in the de Rham setting under the name ``metaplectic vanishing conjecture".
