On multi-stage MiniGrid and BabyAI benchmarks, including DoorKey and Unlock-to-Unlock, Skill-LR converges faster and more reliably than sparse environmental rewards and strong credit-assignment baselines such as RUDDER and LaRe, demonstrating that subgoal-aligned latent rewards offer a principled path toward stable, interpretable credit assignment in long-horizon tasks.

papers.title: Residual-Tail-Informed Flow Matching for Time Series Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract: Time series anomaly detection (TSAD) models are often trained on nominal data using average-risk objectives, which emphasize dominant normal patterns. However, real time series can contain rare but valid nominal regimes that are underrepresented in the training distribution. We show that data-space flow matching can over-penalize such rare-normal windows and assign them anomaly scores comparable to those of true anomalies. To address this, we propose Residual-Tail-Informed Flow Matching (RT-FM), an unsupervised framework that uses a temporal variational autoencoder to estimate residual latent tailness and converts it into bounded, warmup-annealed weights for training a data-space flow matching model. Experiments on seven TSAD benchmarks show that RT-FM improves rare-normal coverage while preserving strong anomaly discrimination, substantially reducing false alarms on such windows and resulting in improved aggregate detection performance. The code is available at: https://github.com/trustAIoT/RT-FM_time-series-anomaly

authors.name: Shyam Sundar Saravanan
authors.institution: Missouri University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Sanjay Madria
authors.institution: Missouri University of Science and Technology

papers.title: WA-JEPA: Goal-Aware Predictive Feedback Action Refinement for a World-Action Model
papers.abstract: JEPA-based world models predict action consequences in latent space, but representative planning approaches rely on candidate-action search, requiring repeated evaluation of action sequences and incurring substantial online computational cost. Direct action generation avoids this search, yet how to leverage latent predictions to guide action generation given task goals remains a key challenge in translating learned physical dynamics into effective decisions. We introduce WA-JEPA, a world-action model that couples action generation, action-conditioned latent prediction, and goal-aware feedback. The model first generates an action proposal and predicts the resulting future scenes and proprioceptive states, then refines the proposal through two complementary feedback paths, using the task goal as a reference. Goal-discrepancy residual feedback (GDRF) uses differences between the latent representations of predicted scenes and the task goal to guide chunk-wise action refinement. Future-scene context feedback (FSCF) preserves fine-grained predicted scene representations to guide subsequent action refinement. Jointly learned from offline demonstrations, this process iteratively updates the same plan before execution, making future predictions directly participate in action generation without candidate-action search. We evaluate short-horizon goal reaching, long-horizon tasks, and full-task execution. The results show that goal-aware predictive feedback supports competitive task performance while maintaining a compact model and low online computational cost. Code is available at https://github.com/Dovisya/WA-JEPA.

papers.title: Beyond Vehicle-Centric Data: Scaling Autonomous Driving through Roadside-to-Vehicle Generation
papers.abstract: Training autonomous driving models requires large and diverse datasets, collected primarily by vehicles. Scaling them entails investment in fleet operation, data processing and annotation. Road infrastructure records traffic and multi-vehicle interactions, yet the viewpoint gap between roadside and onboard sensors limits its direct use for training. Here we introduce AnyR2V, a framework that transforms multimodal roadside observations into seven-camera surround-view videos for different vehicle perspectives. It aggregates sequential observations into a shared scene representation of geometry and road-user motion, then renders appearance, depth and layout conditions along target-vehicle trajectories. Supervised by spatiotemporally aligned roadside-vehicle pairs, AnyR2V generates surround-view videos guided by scene structure and road-user motion. Existing roadside 3D bounding boxes are transformed into target-vehicle coordinates and paired with generated images, allowing one traffic recording and its annotations to yield training data from multiple vehicle perspectives. We construct R2V360, a dataset of 89 real traffic sequences at an urban intersection, with aligned multimodal roadside data and onboard surround-view videos. AnyR2V outperforms six scene reconstruction methods in image fidelity and in depth and semantic agreement between generated and real onboard images. We further evaluate generated videos along other vehicles' trajectories by adding them to real training data. Adding generated frames equal to 50% of the original real training frame count improves mean average precision (mAP) by 3.3-3.4 AP-points across three 3D object detectors on the real onboard test set, relative to real-data-only baselines. These results demonstrate that roadside traffic records can provide training data from multiple vehicle perspectives, offering a new data source for autonomous driving.

papers.title: Chirality-polarized superradiance induced by quantized orbital-angular-momentum transfer in a ring cavity
papers.abstract: We investigate a spin-$1/2$ Bose-Einstein condensate coupled to two counterpropagating modes of an optical ring cavity and driven by Laguerre-Gaussian Raman beams carrying quantized orbital angular momentum (OAM). We demonstrate that competition between OAM-selective Raman scattering channels controls collective superradiance through self-consistent atom--cavity feedback, linking atomic orbital motion to cavity-chirality selection. For unequal OAM transfer, one cavity mode dominates the superradiant response, with its chirality switchable by the Raman pump strengths. In contrast, equal OAM transfer allows both counterpropagating modes to coexist. The resulting chirality-polarized phases support distinct vortex and vortex--antivortex configurations with reconstructed synthetic gauge-field textures. Remarkably, contact interactions can reshape the vortex topology without changing the dominant cavity chirality, revealing distinct responses of atomic and photonic degrees of freedom. The predicted mode switching and vortex ordering can be probed through cavity output and spin-resolved imaging in a proposed $^{87}$Rb implementation. Our results establish quantized OAM transfer as a mechanism for controlling collective cavity emission beyond conventional atomic SOAMC.

papers.title: EchoSpec: Training Search Agents to Weigh Evidence Above Echoes
papers.abstract: Search agents trained with reinforcement learning decide what to retrieve, when to search again, and when to answer. In real corpora, one claim is copied and paraphrased across many pages while the primary source settling a question appears once. We show that reinforcement-learned search agents grant echoes the credence of independent sources and lose their ability to abstain. Across five base models from 3B to 32B and seven released RL agents on multi-hop Wikipedia questions with primary evidence intact, eight paraphrased false-claim echoes overturn 58-73% of previously correct answers, while exact-match RL drives deleted-evidence abstention below 15%. Conditioning on retrieval localizes the failure to evidence acquisition: once primary evidence enters context, agents overrule eight echoes as reliably as one, whereas echoes fill top ranks and halt search early, so larger budgets, forced search turns, or passive passage filtering alone fail to recover displaced evidence. We introduce EchoSpec, specifying reliability across five corpus transformations with known target answers and training in two stages. Verification warm-start teaches multi-hop bridge-entity recovery past echoes, after which group RL optimizes an evidence-gated $\lambda$-reward with an outcome-independent acquisition bonus and scale-preserving advantages retaining the optimal rule $\lambda/(1+\lambda)$. Across Qwen2.5-3B, Qwen2.5-7B, and Llama-3.1-8B backbones on nine evaluation suites, EchoSpec cuts eight-echo deference by 30-44 points on Qwen2.5-7B down to 29-31%, nearly quadruples eight-echo reach to 26-27% with zero-shot transfer to unseen BGE and BM25 retrievers, and raises standalone QA precision to 47-55%. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/unihsy/EchoSpec.

papers.title: InterRSGaussian: Interactive Multi-view Instance Segmentation for 3D Remote Sensing Scenes
papers.abstract: Remote sensing image segmentation plays a critical role in various applications. Interactive instance segmentation, a specialized task within image segmentation, aims to generate precise segmentation results for target objects based on user input prompts. However, previous studies on interactive instance segmentation primarily focus on single-view images, limiting their ability to comprehensively understand complex 3D remote sensing scenes. In this study, we extend interactive instance segmentation from a single-view to a multi-view framework, which can also be easily converted to a 3D segmentation format, thus achieving more accurate and comprehensive 3D remote sensing scene perception across multiple views. First, we construct a multi-view interactive instance segmentation dataset for remote sensing, comprising five distinct scenes, each captured from about one hundred different views. Second, we propose InterRSGaussian, a novel instance segmentation method based on 3D Gaussians. InterRSGaussian enables users to provide point clicks on target objects from any arbitrary view and generates view-consistent instance segmentation results across all input views without requiring manual annotations. The resulting multi-view segmentation can further be projected onto 3D point clouds for 3D segmentation. To improve training efficiency and segmentation performance, we introduce a prior distillation network for initialization. Overall, this study extends traditional 2D remote sensing scene perception into a 3D multi-view framework, enabling a more comprehensive understanding of target objects in complex environments with user interactivity.

papers.title: Approximation and Error Bounds for Zero-Sum Stopping Games with Probability Criteria
papers.abstract: This paper studies a two-person zero-sum stochastic game, which must terminate when either player quits the game or a state of the game first enters a prescribed target set. The performance criterion is the probability that the total reward reaches a given threshold. First, under a mild condition, we prove the existence of the value and a Nash equilibrium of the game by developing a comparison theorem. Second, for solving the game with infinite states, we develop a finite-state approximation method based on truncation, and derive explicit error bounds between the values of the truncated and original games. Third, using the error bounds, we design an effective algorithm, by which we can not only obtain any approximation of the value and Nash equilibria of the original game, but also provide convergence analysis of the approximation. Finally, a queueing example is used to illustrate the advantage of our condition and the effectiveness of our algorithm.

papers.title: Certified Nash Equilibrium Learning for Nonzero-Sum Jump-Diffusion Games: Policy Iteration and Off-Policy Q-Learning
papers.abstract: This paper establishes two model-free reinforcement learning methods for infinite-horizon N-player linear-quadratic nonzero-sum stochastic differential games whose drift, Brownian diffusion, and Poisson jump amplitudes depend on all players' controls. Control dependence in the diffusion and jump terms couples the players' simultaneous feedback updates. A verifiable certificate ensures that the partially model-free policy iteration map is contractive on an invariant closed ball centered at an admissible initial feedback profile. All feedback iterates are mean-square stabilizing, and the algorithm achieves local geometric convergence of feedback gains and value matrices to those associated with a closed-loop Nash equilibrium. The term certified refers to a verifiable convergence certificate that guarantees mean-square stability of all policy iterates and local geometric convergence to a closed-loop Nash equilibrium. To implement the policy updates from data, the off-policy Q-learning algorithm reuses the same behavior-policy data across iterations without requiring the system coefficients or jump intensity. Under quantitative persistence of excitation and a common initialization, exact population regression reproduces the policy-iteration sequence. The same local convergence guarantee therefore applies to off-policy Q-learning at the population level. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the two proposed algorithms.

authors.name: Na Li
authors.institution: Tianjin University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: Cotorsion pairs in $\eta$-extensions with applications to $\theta$-extension rings and tensor rings
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal B$ be an abelian category with enough projective and injective objects, and let $\mathcal B\ltimes_\eta F$ be an $\eta$-extension of $\mathcal B$ with $\eta$ associative. Given a cotorsion pair $(\mathcal X, \mathcal Y)$ in $\mathcal B$, we show that the cotorsion pair $(\Delta(\mathcal X),\Delta(\mathcal X)^\perp)$ exists for arbitrary associative $\eta$, removing the square-zero assumption $F^2=0$ from Hu's construction. When $(\mathcal X, \mathcal Y)$ is hereditary, the heredity of $(\Delta(\mathcal X),\Delta(\mathcal X)^\perp)$ is characterized by the first left derived functor of a canonical defect functor $\delta$. We also remark that Hu's construction and hereditary result for the cotorsion pair $({}^\perp U^{-1}(\mathcal Y), U^{-1}(\mathcal Y))$ remain valid without the nilpotence assumption on $\eta$. Under nilpotence hypotheses, we establish a completeness criterion for $(\Delta(\mathcal X),\Delta(\mathcal X)^\perp)$ using the Beligiannis radical functor $\mathfrak r$. And we also provide a completeness criterion for $({}^\perp U^{-1}(\mathcal Y), U^{-1}(\mathcal Y))$ if $\mathcal B\ltimes_\eta F$ has enough injective objects. We give sufficient conditions for their coincidence. Dual results are obtained for $\zeta$-coextensions. Finally, we specialize the theory to $\theta$-extension rings and tensor rings, where the abstract conditions admit explicit module-theoretic descriptions.

papers.title: Nonlinear Joint State and Noise Estimation under Packet Dropouts and Additive Measurement Corruption
papers.abstract: This paper investigates joint state and noise covariance estimation for nonlinear systems subject to dual reliability impairments: random packet dropouts and additive measurement corruption. This scenario poses challenging nonconjugate inference, as clean and corrupted measurements share an unknown baseline covariance $\boldsymbol{R}_k$ with fixed known corruption covariance $\boldsymbol{E}_k$. Packet reception is observable, whereas the authenticity of received measurements remains latent and must be inferred. To resolve this intractable estimation problem, we cast joint posterior inference as a variational optimization problem and develop a conjugate variational inference adaptive Kalman filter with dual reliability (CVIAKF-DR). The proposed method retains analytical updates for the prediction covariance and two reliability probabilities, while adopting CVI to estimate the state and baseline measurement covariance. The covariance update combines the analytical contribution from clean measurements with Monte Carlo gradient estimates for corrupted measurements. Numerical results on a re-entry tracking benchmark demonstrate the superior accuracy of the proposed method in both state and noise covariance estimation. Remarkably, even built upon the linear Kalman filtering (KF) framework that is originally designed for linear systems, our method achieves more accurate estimation performance than dedicated nonlinear filtering algorithms based on the cubature Kalman filter (CKF).

authors.name: Peng Sun
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory on Integrated Optoelectronics

papers.title: Formalizing $\mathsf{einsum}$ with Named Tensor Notation
papers.abstract: Einstein notation ($\mathsf{einsum}$) is a widely adopted tensor operation that has proven useful in areas such as machine learning and quantum computing. But it had no formal semantics until recently, and its properties had no mechanized verification. We formalize the denotational semantics of a language of tensors (multi-dimensional arrays) that supports $\mathsf{einsum}$ and repeated tensors ($\mathsf{expand}$). With this semantics, we verify equational rewriting rules about $\mathsf{einsum}$ and $\mathsf{expand}$ that improve the performance of tensor computation. Whereas typical languages use unnamed tensors, whose shape is a sequence of natural numbers, we found it advantageous for mechanization to use named tensors, whose shape is a finite map from names to natural numbers. To our knowledge, this is the first time that the semantics and rewriting rules of $\mathsf{einsum}$ are mechanized in a proof assistant. Our solution is agnostic to proof assistants; we have implemented it in Lean and partially in Agda.

papers.title: Real-Time Air Pollution Monitoring and Tracking via Adaptive Density-Driven Multi-UAV Coordination
papers.abstract: Accurate and timely air pollution monitoring and tracking are critical for protecting public health and supporting effective environmental management. This paper presents an adaptive Density-Driven Control (D$^2$C) framework for coordinating multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to track and map dynamically evolving pollutant distributions. The proposed framework extends the D$^2$C strategy to guide UAV trajectories based on predictive pollutant propagation and dynamically updated reference densities. A sensor-driven surrogate plume update mechanism is employed, in which reference samples are propagated using locally sensed concentration gradients and wind estimates through gradient attraction, wind advection, inter-sample repulsion, and stochastic diffusion, enabling UAVs to maintain an accurate spatio-temporal representation of the pollution field. The framework utilizes a coordinated structure where individual UAVs share their local measurements with a central coordinator to maintain a unified set of reference samples, facilitating systematic target allocation and trajectory planning. Simulation results under both mild and strong wind conditions demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in terms of Sinkhorn distance. Specifically, in scenarios where the plume drifts beyond a fixed monitoring domain under high-velocity, time-varying wind fields, the tested baseline methods fail to maintain tracking, whereas the proposed D$^2$C framework successfully adapts to the evolving distribution. These findings highlight D$^2$C as an efficient and resilient solution for atmospheric monitoring in dynamic environments.

authors.name: Ruchika Singh
authors.institution: Sri Venkateshwaraa Medical College Hospital and Research Centre

authors.name: Mohammad Afrazi
authors.institution: New Mexico Institute of Mining and Technology

authors.name: Kooktae Lee
authors.institution: New Mexico Institute of Mining and Technology

papers.title: A Staggered Discontinuous Galerkin Neural Network Method with a Computable Error Decomposition
papers.abstract: We develop a staggered discontinuous Galerkin neural network (SDGNN) method for scalar elliptic problems with a computable error decomposition. The staggered discontinuous Galerkin (SDG) method requires only local continuity of its trial functions and gives a square, inf-sup stable system without stabilization parameters; we carry this structure over to neural networks. Networks defined on the patches of a staggered mesh satisfy the SDG continuity conditions for all values of the network parameters, and the loss is the squared dual norm of the SDG weak residual. We show that the loss is equivalent, with computable constants, to the square of the training error, the distance between the SDG projection of the network and the SDG finite element approximation, so that the full error is bounded by the discretization error, a multiple of the square root of the loss, and the network projection error. The weak residual requires no derivatives of the networks, the boundary and convection terms carry no penalty or stabilization weights, and the scalar trial functions may jump across the midlines of the primal cells. Numerical experiments show that the square root of the loss tracks the error during the training, that prescribed jumps across a square and a circular interface are captured consistently over the initializations, and that the method is more accurate than physics-informed neural networks at the same parameter counts.

authors.name: Chang-Yeol Jung
authors.institution: Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: Bongsuk Kwon
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Real-world Polarimetric Environment Map Dataset
papers.abstract: Environment maps are a standard representation of illumination, enabling realistic image-based lighting in modern rendering systems. However, existing environment maps typically encode only RGB radiance, omitting polarization, an intrinsic property of light that is imperceptible to the human eye but informative about surface shape and material properties. This omission precludes the physically accurate simulation of polarized light transport under in-the-wild illumination conditions, heavily limiting the development and evaluation of robust polarization-based scene reconstruction and understanding methods. We address this gap by introducing a real-world polarimetric environment map dataset, each providing a full-sphere panorama with per-pixel high-dynamic-range RGB Stokes vectors. To acquire the dataset, we design and calibrate a dedicated imaging system and develop a polarization-aware panorama-stitching pipeline. In particular, we introduce a frame-field representation for perspective cameras, together with singularity-aware blending, to enable smooth polarimetric panorama stitching without singularity artifacts. Using this system, we capture 100 polarimetric environment maps across diverse real-world scenes. We further develop a custom rendering plugin and demonstrate close agreement between real and rendered observations. Finally, we analyze the polarization state of the sky across different times and weather conditions, and demonstrate its practical impact on a downstream shape-from-polarization task.

authors.name: Yunseong Moon
authors.institution: Pohang University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Seung-Hwan Baek
authors.institution: Pohang University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Nonlinear spin generation and spin photocurrent as a symmetry and magnetic domain probe in unconventional magnets
papers.abstract: Unconventional magnets host momentum-dependent spin splitting without spin-orbit coupling. We demonstrate that the combination of nonlinear spin polarisation and spin photocurrent is a powerful diagnostic tool for probing the spin space group symmetry, magnetic domain, and quantum geometry in unconventional magnets, providing information beyond their equilibrium spin texture. We develop a mechanism-resolved joint symmetry analysis of second-order spin photoresponse tensors and analyse their frequency dependence, magnetic parity and relaxation scaling. We show that unconventional magnets are natural platforms to achieve large magnetic-even spin photocurrent induced by unpolarised light, making them promising candidates for polariser-free spin sources. We present numerical illustrations for prototypical hybrid parity and odd parity magnet models. Our work provides optical fingerprints connecting spin-space symmetry to distinct microscopic pathways of spin accumulation and transport.

papers.title: New constructions of optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes for quasi-block monotone Ferrers diagrams
papers.abstract: Constant dimension subspace codes (CDCs) have become an important object in coding theory due to their applications in random network coding. The paper is devoted to constructing optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes for block Ferrers diagrams, which play a crucial role in the multilevel construction of CDCs. Let \(\mathbb{F}_q\) be the finite field with \(q\) elements of characteristic \(p\), \(P\) be a power of \(p\), and \(e\) be a positive integer. Let \(L=\mathbb F_{q^{eP}}\) and \(\sigma\) be the Frobenius \(\mathbb F_q\)-automorphism of \(L\), set \(N=\sigma^e-\mathrm{id}\). Based on the multiplicative property of the kernel filtration of the nilpotent map \(N\), we construct optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes for block monotone diagrams. Specifically, considering \(n \times l\) Ferrers diagrams, we prove that optimal codes always exist for block monotone diagrams when \(n = eP\). Furthermore, by employing puncturing on columns, we prove that optimal codes also always exist for block strictly monotone diagrams, removing the restriction \(n = eP\). Consequently, optimal codes always exist for block upper triangular diagrams, specifically for maximum sum-rank distance (MSRD)-constructible block diagram pairs, which generalizes the corresponding results in \cite{neri2024,calderini2026}, in which the rank distance or the characteristic is restricted. Furthermore, by employing both puncturing and shortening on columns, we prove that optimal codes always exist for quasi-block strictly monotone diagrams, thereby generalizing the corresponding results in \cite{pratihar2023, zhang2019}. The optimal codes constructed in this paper will potentially be beneficial to the further construction of CDCs.

authors.name: Yuhao Ning
authors.institution: Changsha University of Science and Technology

papers.title: DecoEdit: Beyond Flat Control for 3D-Aware Unified Image Editing
papers.abstract: While recent advances in multimodal image editing have achieved impressive results, current frameworks remain largely confined to ``flat" 2D controls (e.g., text prompts, bounding boxes, or masks). Precise 3D-aware geometric manipulation -- such as coordinating an object's location, physical scale, and 3D orientation while strictly preserving its fine-grained identity -- remains an elusive challenge, typically suffering from severe detail degradation or requiring expensive per-instance fine-tuning. In this paper, we present DecoEdit, an all-in-one image editing framework that goes beyond flat control by seamlessly integrating 1D textual, 2D spatial, and 3D volumetric inputs under a unified architecture. First, to power this unified model, we establish a data curation pipeline and curate a large-scale dataset, namely DecoDataset, containing 1.6 million samples, encompassing diverse multi-dimensional (1D/2D/3D) tasks and their complex compositions. Furthermore, we establish a comprehensive image editing benchmark named DecoBench to systematically evaluate multi-task editing performance. Finally, to address the fundamental trade-off between complex spatial transformations and identity preservation, we propose a novel decoupled pipeline: DecoEdit factorizes the editing process by utilizing structural guidance from SAM-3D to anchor the target geometry, scale, and spatial orientation, while concurrently leveraging a detail-preservation path to lock in high-fidelity textures. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DecoEdit achieves state-of-the-art results. Notably, on the challenging 3D spatial pose and orientation control tasks, DecoEdit significantly outperforms leading closed-source models such as Seedream 5.0 in both geometric accuracy and identity consistency.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Causal Reasoning for Nonstationary Robot Dynamics
papers.abstract: Reasoning about what an action will cause requires internalizing how a system behaves. As conditions seldom stay fixed, this must often happen within a few interactions. Yet systems that look identical in a snapshot can respond differently to the same action, depending on physical conditions the snapshot hides. Context-based models capture this separation by summarizing recent transitions into a latent context, but do not specify how that context should change the equations of motion. Physics-informed neural networks build those equations into the model, but describe only a single system and cannot recognize when it has changed. We present Physics-Informed Causal Reasoning (PICR), which bridges the two. Only a context, re-inferred from recent interactions, is updated; it conditions a fixed physics-informed network that determines the robot's inertia and potential energy, so the robot adapts to new physical conditions from its own experience without retraining or a hand-specified robot model. On a Franka Panda arm in NVIDIA Isaac Sim, PICR predicts motion under changing and unseen payloads, reducing error on the latter by 1.6-3.8x over baselines, and extends to counterfactual queries under alternative torques. Our analysis shows that the context, inferred solely from interaction, encodes payload physical properties, tracks their changes, and governs the arm's response. The gravity and inertia terms induced by the context further demonstrate its physical validity, each agreeing with the simulator at the level of individual Lagrangian components.

papers.title: Lindblad and Corotation Resonances as the Common Origin of Moving Groups, Diagonal Ridges, and Velocity Waves in the Milky Way Disc
papers.abstract: The Galactic disc is a complex dynamical system showing various kinematic structures, including moving groups (MGs), diagonal ridges (DRs), and velocity waves. To investigate their possible dynamical connection, we analyzed the phase-space distribution of stars from the extit{Gaia} DR3 catalog. We used angular momentum $L_z$ as a key dynamical tracer and examined stellar densities and velocities as functions of $L_z$. We identified stellar groups at specific $L_z$-values and associated them with extrema in the median radial velocity $\left<V_R ight>$, known as a velocity wave. By cross-matching the extrema of the $\left<V_R ight>$-wave with structures in the $V_R$--$L_z$ and $R$--$L_z$ planes, we established a clear connection between the velocity wave, the main MGs, and the DRs. A similar connection was partially identified for corrugations in the median vertical velocity $\left<V_z ight>$. Both velocity waves are strongest near the Galactic mid-plane and decrease in amplitude with increasing vertical distance. Our results demonstrate that MGs, DRs, and velocity waves in the solar neighborhood are different projections of the same dynamical structures associated with Lindblad and corotation resonances. These resonances arise from coupling between the radial and azimuthal stellar motions and are particularly prominent in the thin Galactic disc. Numerical simulations including perturbations from the Galactic bar and spiral arms confirm these conclusions. Our findings indicate that the local stellar disc is currently evolving in a state of dynamical equilibrium. We also show that in-plane velocity oscillations must be considered when interpreting vertical stellar distributions, as they may produce artifacts in vertical profiles.

papers.title: NF-VLA: A Normalizing-Flow Baseline for Vision-Language-Action Learning
papers.abstract: Autoregressive normalizing flows (NFs) provide a tractable density for learning and sampling continuous robot actions. We show that a single maximum-likelihood objective can train vision--language--action (VLA) policies competitive with leading methods on manipulation benchmarks. We present NF-VLA, which combines conditional autoregressive normalizing flows with score-based action refinement. Its deep--shallow architecture concentrates visual, language, and proprioceptive prefix conditioning in a high-capacity deep block, while unconditioned shallow blocks provide a shared invertible action transformation. The vision--language backbone and flow are jointly trained by exact maximum likelihood on Gaussian-smoothed action chunks. The same learned density supplies a single score-based correction at inference, refining generated actions to account for training-time smoothing without a separately trained denoiser. Trained on LIBERO from a pretrained vision--language backbone without robot pretraining, NF-VLA achieves 98.35\% success across the four standard suites and 72.6\% on LIBERO-Plus using the same checkpoint without further fine-tuning. Ablations show that deep-only prefix conditioning and score-based refinement both improve closed-loop success. Together, these results establish carefully structured autoregressive flows as a competitive approach to VLA control, with one learned density supporting policy training, action generation, and refinement.

authors.name: Mutian Tong
authors.institution: Affiliated Hospital of Guizhou Medical University

papers.title: "Can a Robot Really Care About Me?" How Perceiving a Tutor as Human or AI Affects Computer Science Students' Attitudes and Experiences
papers.abstract: Conversational artificial intelligence can reproduce many instructional and social behaviors of human tutors, but students may interpret those behaviors differently depending on who they believe is providing them. We examined how perceived tutor identity shapes students' evaluations of instructional feedback, satisfaction of psychological needs according to Self-Determination Theory, and their communication strategies with tutors. In a within-subjects Wizard-of-Oz study, 27 introductory computer science students completed two text-based tutoring sessions involving Python code-explanation problems. Participants were told one tutor was human and the other was AI, although the same human provided feedback in both conditions. We found participants evaluated both tutors favorably and reported few consistent differences in the instructional value of the feedback. However, participants frequently questioned whether AI could genuinely care about them, which corresponded with the human tutor having higher scores of relatedness need satisfaction. Human presence offered connection and accountability for some participants but introduced anxiety in others. Participants also reported communicating more casually with the human tutor and more explicitly with the AI tutor. These findings suggest complementary roles for human and AI tutoring and highlight the importance of considering psychological needs alongside instructional quality.

papers.title: FinVerify: A Verification Framework for Financial Agents
papers.abstract: Financial agents produce numerical claims that can be wrong even when their calculations execute correctly, due to mismatched reporting periods, unsupported sources, incompatible units, or incorrect financial definitions. We introduce FinVerify, an evidence-grounded framework for verifying financial agents' numerical claims. Based on an analysis of 190 incorrect trajectories from the Agent Finance Reasoning dataset, we define five error categories--temporal integrity, source fidelity, comparability, accounting integrity, and financial-model fidelity--and operationalize them as verification protocols. An LLM structures claims and supporting evidence, while deterministic validators check financial requirements; when authoritative formulas are available, Z3 checks consistency with grounded inputs. FinVerify accepts only if all applicable checks pass, rejects proven violations, and abstains when evidence is insufficient. We evaluate the framework against a Direct baseline and an LLM judge across five fixed-candidate benchmarks. On Agent Finance Reasoning, accepted-claim precision increases from 56.4% for the LLM judge to 76.7% at 81.2% coverage. On XBRLFiling, FinVerify achieves 99.8% accepted-claim precision and 97.0% decision accuracy; on FinanceBench-67, it reaches 87.9% accepted-claim precision versus 69.7% for the judge. Improvements are smaller on FinQA and TAT-QA, where authoritative evidence is limited. These results suggest that explicit, evidence-backed verification can improve financial-agent reliability while exposing trade-offs between correctness, false rejection, and abstention.

papers.title: Mem2Fair: Online Fairness Control for Text-to-Video Generation via Fair Memory
papers.abstract: Text-to-video (T2V) generation models can produce systematically unfair demographic outcomes when prompts leave protected attributes unspecified. For example, prompts describing nurses without specifying gender may disproportionately generate videos depicting female nurses. Mitigating unfairness in T2V generation is particularly challenging: training-based methods that modify model internals require architecture-specific access and risk disrupting temporal consistency, while sampling-based methods often incur costly pre-deployment video generation. We present the first conditional online approachability formulation of attribute-level fairness for T2V generation. Building on this formulation, we introduce Mem2Fair, a plug-and-play framework that maintains concept-conditioned Fair Memory. Using generated videos at inference time as feedback, Mem2Fair selects prompt-level attribute interventions based on the deviation from each concept's prescribed fairness target, without training or separate pre-deployment sampling. Experiments demonstrate that Mem2Fair consistently improves fairness over the unmodified generator and existing baselines across multiple demographic attributes, prompt settings, and target distributions, while maintaining comparable prompt-video alignment and video quality. We further demonstrate its effectiveness on commercial black-box T2V models.

papers.title: Specificity-Guided Knowledge Diversion for Decomposable Generative Models
papers.abstract: Generative model pre-training typically optimizes a model as a whole without explicitly organizing its parameters for selective reuse. Decomposable pre-training instead learns reusable components for downstream adaptation while retaining strong generative performance. However, existing knowledge diversion methods incur substantial parameter overhead through weight factorization and rely on fixed component assignments to induce specialization, potentially compromising in-distribution generation quality. We therefore propose Specificity-Guided Knowledge Diversion (SGKDiv), which learns how generative knowledge is shared and specialized for effective generation and selective downstream reuse. SGKDiv constructs Knowledge Units from paired feed-forward channels, preserving native computational structure without SVD-based reparameterization. Calibrated condition-wise routing combines a shared usage prior with conditional adjustments, while complementary regularization shapes their allocation, diversity, and magnitude. Together, these designs replace predefined component assignments with adaptively learned and explicitly regulated knowledge specialization. Experiments across diverse model and training settings demonstrate better in-distribution generation than dense and MoE baselines, alongside stronger downstream adaptation than representative PEFT methods across eight datasets.

papers.title: Small Data in Long-Term Environmental Vision: Annotation Noise, Gamification, and Label-Budget Scaling
papers.abstract: Long-running environmental camera networks produce abundant images but few reliable annotations. Using FujiView, a network of webcams around Mount Fuji, we study three linked questions: whether gamification affects annotation participation and agreement, how annotators disagree on ordinal visibility labels, and how label budget affects downstream classification. Across seven nonrandomized sessions with 22 labelers, gamification showed a more promising pattern for sustained participation than for labeling speed or agreement. In the closest remote-session comparison, the session recorded as gamified had longer active labeling time, while throughput and reference agreement remained similar. Annotation disagreement was substantial at fine granularity: crowd votes matched the single-annotator reference on 49.1% of exact visibility classes, versus 90.2% after grouping them into Good/Poor. In five-replicate label-budget experiments, models using 25% of the available label pool achieved held-out exact accuracy only 2.8 percentage points below the full-pool model on average. Together, these findings highlight the importance of designing reliable annotation targets, evaluating engagement mechanisms without assuming causal benefits, and using empirical scaling curves to plan labeling effort.

papers.title: Different Timescales, Different Signals: Multimodal Landmark-Visibility Prediction in a Long-Term Webcam Network
papers.abstract: Scenic visibility is not a single forecasting problem: planning a trip months ahead, deciding whether to go outside today, and judging whether tomorrow will be clear rely on different information. Using a year-scale multimodal archive of Mount Fuji webcams and meteorological observations, we identify a clear hierarchy across timescales. Seasonal climatology provides useful long-range guidance, webcam imagery is the strongest same-day observation (AUC 0.95), and the numerical forecast valid on the target day carries most of the day-specific signal one to three days ahead. Revealing this hierarchy requires evaluation that respects the dependence among cameras observing the same regional weather state: permissive splits substantially overstate multi-day performance, while date-grouped and forward-in-time evaluation reduce the apparent contribution of the current scene and current weather. On 6,575 camera-days, the current visual summary provides no measurable one-day gain once the target-day forecast is available. The remaining opportunity lies at shorter horizons, where the present visual representation discards cloud geometry and motion. These results recast scenic visibility prediction as a multi-timescale sensing problem rather than a single multimodal forecasting task.

papers.title: The structure of variational autoencoder latent spaces and its consequences for representation and optimization
papers.abstract: Variational autoencoders (VAEs) are widely used to build low-dimensional representations of scientific data, with the expectation that regularization yields smooth coordinates for interpolation, generation and optimization. However, applications in microscopy reveal domains, narrow transitions and rare-state islands in VAE latent spaces that smoothness alone does not explain. We show that, for prototype data with squared-error reconstruction and an optimal decoder, the latent-space objective has a direct correspondence with the Flory-Huggins theory of a regular solution, and use it to analyze how the objective, posterior distributions and latent dimensionality organize the representation. Data families occupy domains separated by finite-width walls that broaden with increasing regularization until class separation is lost through posterior collapse. Class centroids behave like particles in a harmonic trap: the prior confines them, and structural dissimilarity sets a soft repulsion that determines which classes become neighbors and how far apart they sit, with separations growing only logarithmically with dissimilarity. Rare states can remain unresolved, form small islands, accumulate within walls or develop intervening domains, depending on their frequency and similarity to common states. The posterior covariance can align domains with the latent axes, but axis alignment does not imply separation of physical factors. Rotations can produce rings and encoder cuts that reflect data symmetry, while insufficient dimensionality can lead to suppression, mixing or folding of additional factors. Comparisons with flow models, deep kernel learning (DKL) and hybrid VAE-DKL models show how these structures change when reconstruction and prediction play different roles. We discuss implications for interpreting data, discovering rare states, generating intermediate states and optimizing properties.

papers.title: An isolated complex Hadamard matrix with nonzero defect
papers.abstract:
We exhibit a complex Hadamard matrix of nonzero defect which is isolated among complex Hadamard matrices, up to Hadamard equivalence. This counterexample is realized by a Butson-type Hadamard matrix of size $13$, with entries roots of order $6$ of unity.
  In the language of commuting squares, this shows that the span condition, previously introduced by the second author as a sufficient condition for isolation, is not a necessary condition for isolation.

papers.title: The exact semisimplicity criterion for Brauer algebras of type $C$
papers.abstract: We determine exactly when the Brauer algebra of type $C$, denoted by $\B_r(C,\delta)$, is semisimple over $\C$, where $\delta\neq0$. We first analyze the two admissible cases for homomorphisms from the top layer to the second layer. We construct an auxiliary operator on the space spanned by symmetric Brauer diagrams with a fixed bottom partial diagram and exactly two horizontal edges in each row. Using this operator, we prove that, in each admissible case, the corresponding quadratic condition is necessary and sufficient for the existence of a nonzero homomorphism. The constant terms of these quadratic expressions depend on sums of contents of horizontal $2$-strips in bipartitions. We then show that a failure of semisimplicity is detected by cell modules in the second layer. Finally, by relating the content sums for admissible bipartition pairs to the known sums for horizontal $2$-strips in ordinary partitions, we obtain an explicit finite set of exceptional nonzero parameters.

authors.name: Dimpi Km
authors.institution: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research Thiruvananthapuram

papers.title: From RuP$_3$SiO$_{11}$ to Ideal Geometry: Parallel-Face Octahedra for Kitaev-Dominated Interactions
papers.abstract: RuP$_3$SiO$_{11}$ has recently been identified as a Kitaev spin liquid candidate via neutron scattering. To assess its proximity to the Kitaev limit, we perform \textit{ab initio} calculations of magnetic interactions, finding good agreement for the Kitaev and off-diagonal exchanges, while the Heisenberg exchange is ferromagnetic rather than the experimentally fitted antiferromagnetic one. We also identify a sizable antiferromagnetic out-of-plane exchange not captured in previous analyses. Extending the study to eight substitutional analogs in the $MT_3Q$O$_{11}$ family ($M$ = Ru, Os; $T$ = P, As; $Q$= Si, Ge), we observe strong variations in magnetic interactions, highlighting the tunability of this materials class. Finally, inspired by RuP$_3$SiO$_{11}$, which exhibits a near parallel-face octahedral arrangement, we compare idealized geometries and show that the parallel-face configuration yields a Kitaev-dominated regime, suggesting a new structural route to the Kitaev limit.

papers.title: A Fast and Accurate Time-Space Decomposition for Unit Commitment With Storage
papers.abstract: Grid-scale batteries couple decisions across time. This makes unit commitment (UC) with thousands of buses, batteries, generators, and alternating current constraints intractable. We introduce a time-space decomposition (TSD) heuristic to solve the problem. We first calculate target net battery charge or discharge rates on a zonal level, relaxing spatial constraints. We then incorporate this target into the Relax-and-Round UC (RRUC) solver from our previous work. RRUC enforces the spatial transmission constraints and transfers power between zones, if that reduces costs. We show that our TSD produces an error of about 0.1% on a simpler economic dispatch problem with batteries. This is larger than the error produced by RRUC in the tests in our previous work. So, we conjecture that the combined error of our two approximations is not much larger than 0.1%. We show that TSD with RRUC can solve systems with 10,000 buses in about 6 minutes, with sub-quadratic scaling, making it suitable for real time operations on an ISO-sized system.

papers.title: Initial Conditions Dictate Gas-Stellar Counter-Rotation in Galaxies
papers.abstract: We present a physical origin of gas-stellar counter-rotation in galaxies. Scale-dependent partitions of tidal torques from cosmic primordial perturbations source angular momentum for distinct baryonic components. This scale dependence maps to radial hierarchy in Lagrangian space clustering: stellar components, assembled at earlier times from the inner protohalo, retain persistent memory of small-scale tidal torques, whereas gas, accreted later from outer Lagrangian regions, is governed by large-scale perturbations and can develop counter-rotation. This mechanism is observationally testable and offers a direct probe of the hierarchical cold dark matter (CDM) paradigm. Unlike conventional late-time scenarios that only explain the existence of counter-rotation, our framework further predicts its component-resolved direction, enabling component-resolved angular momentum to serve as a new probe of primordial density perturbations and improving cosmological initial condition reconstruction.

authors.name: Lin Zhu
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

authors.name: Jian Qin
authors.institution: Southern Marine Science and Engineering Guangdong Laboratory (Guangzhou)

papers.title: A full-wave ICRH solver with full kinetic accuracy using only first order differential equations
papers.abstract: Accurate full-wave computation of ion cyclotron resonance heating (ICRH) typically requires solving the computationally demanding integro-differential dielectric tensor of the hot plasma. Based on the method in [Phys. Plasmas 32, 082110 (2025)], we develop BO-FW1D, a 1D frequency domain finite difference full-wave solver which generates full kinetic, accurate and efficient simulations utilizing a fluid plasma model. To accurately convert the conductivity tensor in phase space into a first-order differential equation, we introduce a mathematically rigorous framework using pseudodifferential operator theory based on Kohn-Nirenberg ordering. Benchmarks with an all-orders 1D full-wave solver show high consistency in critical kinetic effects and electric-field distributions, while substantial computational acceleration is achieved. This work could lay the foundation for developing full-wave solvers that combine full kinetic accuracy with high computational efficiency.

papers.title: SAGE-VQA: A Training-Free, Self-Evolving Agentic Framework with Grounded Evidence for Knowledge-Based Visual Question Answering
papers.abstract: Knowledge-based visual question answering (KB-VQA) aims to combine visual information with external knowledge to answer user questions. Existing methods face two main bottlenecks: visual perception errors can propagate into hallucinations, and generalization across scenarios remains limited. To address these issues, we propose SAGE-VQA (Self-evolving Agent framework with Grounded Evidence), a training-free agentic framework that combines evidence verification with experience evolution. Our key insight is to explore an Evidence-Driven Adaptive Reasoning (EDAR) strategy. It accurately acquires and verifies question-relevant fine-grained visual information. It also extracts and refines reusable experience to support robust reasoning across tasks. Specifically, we design a Co-verified Visual Grounding module that verifies question-relevant visual information and provides grounded evidence for subsequent reasoning. We further introduce a Self-evolving Hierarchical Memory (SHM) mechanism. SHM organizes experiences into declarative and procedural memories based on their nature. These memories can be reused in subsequent reasoning and continually refined through feedback, without updating model parameters. Experimental results show that our method outperforms competing methods based on lightweight open-source vision-language models (VLMs) as well as those based on closed-source VLMs. Moreover, our method can serve as a plug-and-play reasoning framework for existing VLMs without modifying their architectures.

authors.name: Yonggang Zhang
authors.institution: Henan Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: CreaTrace: Video Creative Plagiarism Detection and Evidence Tracing
papers.abstract: Video creative plagiarism refers to the unauthorized reproduction of creative ideas across videos despite substantial differences in visual appearance, posing a new challenge to video copyright protection. However, existing video copy detection methods primarily focus on visual content similarity, struggling to capture abstract creative that are entangled with specific visual realizations. To address this issue, we introduce a novel task, named Video Creative Plagiarism Detection (VCPD), and propose an iterative creative evidence tracing framework, termed CreaTrace, to verify creative similarity and accurately localize the corresponding evidence segments. Specifically, we design a Multimodal Semantic Event Segmentation strategy to divide similar long videos into coherent narrative events, facilitating event-level dataset construction and retrieving similar segments. Based on these events, CreaTrace employs Coarse Creative Matching to identify candidate event pairs through narrative semantics and camera language. Then CreaTrace presents Creative Decoupling to disentangle abstract creative patterns from specific visual realizations. Meanwhile, Creative Swap Contrastive Learning is devised to enhance creative consistency through cross-realization feature swapping. Benefiting from the above designs, our CreaTrace enables accurate creative similarity detection and temporal localization, while providing interpretable evidence report. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of CreaTrace across diverse creative plagiarism scenarios.

papers.title: Reliable Mining of Heterogeneous AI Coding-Agent Data: Context-Aware Prediction and Resource-Aware Ranking
papers.abstract: Operational records from AI coding agents differ across agents, repositories, tasks, and workflows. We study 71,677 pull requests (PRs) from six agents and show that pooling these records can reverse descriptive and predictive conclusions. PRs carrying a co-authorship trailer have a 55.6% merge rate, compared with 77.5% without the trailer, but removing the dominant agent flips this -21.8 percentage-point gap to +23.7 points. We treat this Simpson-type reversal as a data-veracity problem and represent source, environment, and workflow context in a feature cascade. Gradient-boosting merge-prediction AUC increases from 0.774 to 0.832; the advantage persists under temporal evaluation (0.801) and unseen repositories (0.807). The co-authorship coefficient changes from -1.09 to +1.44 after conditioning, whereas repository-clustered AIPW intervals show no stable adjusted trailer association. A strict PR-creation-time model reaches 0.741 AUC in standard evaluation and 0.710 on unseen repositories, although its temporal AUC falls to 0.641. Finally, a separately cross-fitted analysis of an observed-mode functional estimates a +12.3-point doubly robust gain at a 30% allocation budget on the non-Codex population, only 0.5 points above risk ranking. This last result is retrospective decision support over metadata states, not a causal effect of assigning human review.

papers.title: VisualArtifactSpec 1.0: Evaluating Visual Artifacts under Task Specifications
papers.abstract: Visual artifact tasks test agents' ability to translate task specifications and source materials into outputs that meet practical needs. Evaluation across artifact families helps distinguish broadly applicable authoring capabilities from strengths confined to a particular medium. We introduce VisualArtifactSpec 1.0 (VAS), a benchmark of 211 creation and modification tasks spanning presentations, static graphics, animations and videos, and web interfaces. Each task specifies authoring objectives, source materials, constraints, and deliverables. Existing benchmarks provide limited support for systematically evaluating how authoring choices suit different audiences, purposes, and media across artifact families. VAS evaluates two aspects separately: Task Fulfillment verifies explicit requirements and applicable functionality, while Artifact Performance assesses Content, Organization, Visuals, and Delivery. Task-specific rating anchors instantiate shared criteria for the intended audience, purpose, and medium, with judgments grounded in source materials and artifact inspection records. We evaluate nine model-harness configurations on all 211 tasks. Overall scores range from 42.12 to 70.52, with Artifact Performance accounting for 73.4% of the gap between the highest- and lowest-scoring configurations.

authors.name: Mingli Song
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Media Convergence and Communication

papers.title: Numerical Integration Instabilities in Likelihood Fits: Mechanisms and Remedies
papers.abstract: Numerical instabilities in the normalization of probability density functions can produce artificially lower negative log-likelihood (NLL) values than the true minimum of a likelihood fit, even when the resulting fit provides a poorer description of the data. Motivated by anomalously low NLL values found in non-converged fits associated with a recent CMS search for fully charmed tetraquark candidates, we use a pseudo-dataset generated from a likelihood model based on that analysis to investigate how numerical integration can yield unreliable normalization results, how these errors affect likelihood minimization, and how they can be addressed. We find that, even at fixed integration tolerance, the stopping decision of a numerical integrator can change with the fit parameters, introducing discontinuities in the normalization integrals that propagate to the likelihood surface. Such discontinuities can trap the minimizer at a numerical step and yield an artificially lower NLL. Tightening the integration tolerance mitigates these numerical discontinuities, while adaptive integration methods, such as Gauss--Kronrod quadrature, can also improve the numerical stability. A more severe failure occurs when the integration grid cannot adequately resolve a sharply localized contribution. In this case, the integrator may satisfy its estimated-error criterion despite substantially underestimating the normalization, allowing the minimizer to enter a region with an artificially low NLL. Tightening integration tolerances or using alternative adaptive integration methods does not necessarily resolve sharply localized contributions. We demonstrate that a suitable variable transformation can improve their numerical resolution, yielding more accurate normalization integrals and restoring fit convergence.

authors.name: Manqi Zhu
authors.institution: Macau University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Which Mathematical Context Supports Target-Aligned Conjecture Generation? A Paired Ablation Study
papers.abstract: Generating mathematical conjectures from natural-language context is challenging because theorem-relevant information is distributed across multiple forms of mathematical context, including definitions, objects, assumptions, and constructions. We study which of these contextual signals help a model recover the specific claim supported by the surrounding setup, using 61 main theorems from 12 papers across four mathematical domains. For each theorem, we redact the result and represent the remaining setup using six context components. A paired ablation design compares full context, six leave-one-out conditions, and six single-component conditions, yielding 793 generated conjectures. Context components were largely complementary: removing one component usually had little effect, whereas retaining only one substantially reduced expected-theorem alignment. Local Mathematical Objects provided the strongest standalone signal, while Structural Constraints and Conditions produced the largest alignment decrease when removed. These findings suggest that target-aligned conjecture generation depends on combining information that identifies relevant objects with information that constrains admissible claims.

papers.title: CRAFT: A Robot-Agent Harness with Scope-Aware Adaptation
papers.abstract: A robot may know how to move an object yet still need to learn where it belongs. When a person rejects a placement, the robot must decide whether the correction applies only to that situation or expresses a broader rule. We study this problem in CRAFT (Contextual Requirement Adaptation with Frozen Tools), a framework for learning local requirements without retraining robot skills. It records physical success separately from whether an action meets the requirement. Our scope ladder uses memory when an action has already been judged in a nearly identical situation. Elsewhere, it combines memory, explicit rules and a learner for requirements beyond those rules, weighting their predictions by how well they predicted earlier feedback. Controlled studies show gains over correction memory alone in utility, which rewards acceptable actions and charges for mistakes and questions. In camera-grounded robot simulations, the ladder asks fewer questions than language-model agents with persistent memory, but some of those agents take fewer wrong actions and succeed more often after requirements change. All execution failures and timeouts remain in the evaluation. These results support combining specific memories with broader rules, while leaving reliable adaptation to changing requirements unresolved. All evidence comes from simulation with generated requirements and simulated feedback.

authors.name: Jiawen Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Dynamic Shaping: Acquiring Interfaces and Constructing Execution over Frozen Pretrained Components
papers.abstract: We introduce Dynamic Shaping, a method for constructing executable neural arrangements through acquired response and partial-derivative interfaces over frozen pretrained components. The method learns local descriptions of available computation, ranks component rebindings using task-gradient alignment, transports the current interface across a rebinding, and retains changes through behavioral feedback. Continuous interface acquisition uses proximal policy optimization; the source coefficients remain fixed. We derive an exact identity relating transport error in component responses and partials to changes in action logits and their sensitivities. A pixels-only ViZDoom Basic study evaluates first task acquisition without a competent reference controller, demonstrations or intact response targets. Across three initializations and 100 shared held-out game seeds, initial arrangements succeed on 86/300 controller/episode pairs; joint interface-and-binding construction succeeds on 295/300. Fixed-binding interface acquisition also reaches 295/300. Each policy executes four source fragments, with 110 acquired interface values and fixed random visual and action projections. The artifact includes all candidate trials, interventions and costs; all 1,200 recorded initial/retained outcomes replay exactly. The contribution is an explicit profile, rebind, transport and retain procedure and a reproducible reference-free acquisition case over frozen pretrained computation.

papers.title: Low-Latency LLM-Based Streaming Multi-Talker ASR with Verifiable Rewards
papers.abstract: LLM-based architectures offer strong generalization and instruction-following capabilities for streaming automatic speech recognition (ASR), but multi-talker use introduces coupled transcription, attribution, and latency challenges. Our wearable setting requires real-time transcription of a conversation between a near-field device wearer and a far-field partner. Because partial hypotheses are rendered on persistent sides of a dialogue UI, speaker roles cannot be permuted and each speaker tag must precede its turn. These sparse tags are weakly optimized by supervised fine-tuning (SFT), while committing to a leading tag can delay the text that follows. We therefore post-train a streaming LLM-based ASR model with reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), combining a fixed-role Speaker-Attributed WER (SA-WER) grader with a turn-level onset-delay reward. On an eight-direction multi-talker cohort, SA-WER RL reduces SA-WER from $20.51\%$ for SFT to $13.14\%$. Adding the delay objective reduces onset $p50$ by $65\%$ (from $0.918\,\text{s}$ to $0.320\,\text{s}$) and $p90$ by $44\%$ (from $1.389\,\text{s}$ to $0.780\,\text{s}$) relative to SA-WER-only RL, while achieving $12.70\%$ SA-WER. These results demonstrate that fixed-role recognition quality and streaming responsiveness can be improved jointly.

authors.name: Ju Lin
authors.institution: Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development

papers.title: GPRM: Global Perspective Process Reward Model
papers.abstract: Process Reward Models (PRMs) are widely used for step-level evaluation of multi-step reasoning in large language models, but existing methods are often limited by weak historical dependency modeling and insufficient global awareness. They typically fail to leverage prior step evaluations for coherent judgment and lack visibility into subsequent reasoning, leading to suboptimal assessment of intermediate steps. To address this issue, we propose the Global Perspective Process Reward Model (GPRM), which jointly models the problem, previous reasoning steps and their evaluations, the current step, and future steps to enable history-aware and globally informed process evaluation. We further introduce a structured evaluation framework along four dimensions---look back, look ahead, self-check, and goal alignment---to assess prior consistency, future plausibility, step validity, and task alignment. Based on this framework, we construct datasets for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (GRPO). Experiments show that, despite using less training data and smaller model sizes, GPRM outperforms strong baseline models by 7.8 and 5.4 points on PRMBench and ProcessBench, respectively. GPRM also generalizes well across tasks, surpassing the GPT-4.1 baseline on Agent Error Bench, improving strong baselines by around 4 points under test-time scaling (TTS), and achieving competitive performance on PPE.

authors.name: Shaobo Wang
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Jiayi Chen
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: LLMs in DevSecOps: A Systematic Mapping of Models, Evidence, and Research Gaps Across the Software Lifecycle
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being integrated into software security and DevSecOps workflows, yet their adoption, evaluation, and maturity vary substantially across lifecycle stages. This study systematically maps recent LLM-enabled security research published between 2024 and 2026 (until June) across six DevSecOps stages: \textit{Plan}, \textit{Code}, \textit{Test}, \textit{Review}, \textit{Deploy}, and \textit{Monitor}. For each stage, we analyze the security tasks addressed, models and adaptation strategies employed, evaluation settings, reported effectiveness, and key limitations. Our findings reveal an uneven research landscape, with \textit{Test} and \textit{Code} receiving substantially greater attention than \textit{Deploy} and \textit{Review}. Across stages, recent systems increasingly rely on structured context, iterative reasoning, fine-tuning, retrieval augmentation, or agentic workflows rather than direct single-shot prompting. However, reported performance remains difficult to compare because studies use heterogeneous tasks, datasets, metrics, and baselines. Furthermore, most approaches are evaluated using benchmarks or open-source repositories, while industrial-scale evidence remains limited. We also find that existing systems are predominantly stage-specific, with little evidence of LLM-enabled security reasoning spanning multiple DevSecOps stages. Based on these observations, we identify research opportunities in standardized evaluation, production-scale validation, supply-chain and Infrastructure-as-Code security, trustworthy autonomous remediation, and cross-stage LLM integration. This study provides a recent lifecycle-level view of where LLM-enabled DevSecOps research is concentrated, what methodological patterns are emerging, and where significant gaps remain.

papers.title: Matricial stability and central corrections for generalized Jordan derivations on amenable $C^*$-algebras
papers.abstract: We study norm stability of third-type generalized Jordan identities, allowing their auxiliary maps to be arbitrary. A canonical normalization eliminates these witnesses with a factor of four. For a unital $C^*$-algebra and a unital contractive Banach bimodule, the zero-defect maps are precisely sums of a derivation and multiplication by a central module element. We characterize scalar stability by the closed range of the normalized Jordan-defect operator. For operator bimodules, two explicit $2\times2$ tests recover an ordered Leibniz defect and a commutator defect. If the algebra has an approximate diagonal bounded by $M$ and the module is weak$^*$ closed, these tests yield approximation by an inner derivation plus a central multiplier with error at most $8M$ times the normalized matrix defect. The corresponding completely bounded estimate holds at all matrix levels. For full matrix algebras the constant is $8$, independently of their size, and weak$^*$ closedness is unnecessary. When the map vanishes at the identity, the constants improve to $2M$ and $2$, respectively.

papers.title: Existence of alternating Hamiltonian paths on specific bicolored point sets
papers.abstract: Consider a bicolored point set $P$ in general position in the plane consisting of $n$ blue and $n$ red points. We show that if $P$ can be partitioned into bicolored pairs $(a_i,b_i)$ such that, for every $i$, $a_i$ and $b_i$ have different colors and the sets $P\setminus \{a_i\}$ and $P \setminus \{b_i\}$ have the same order type, then there exists a noncrossing alternating Hamiltonian path on $P$. We also investigate the case when $P$ lies on the circle, and every interval along the circle contains at most $c$ more points of one color than of the other. For $c=2$, we show that there exists a noncrossing alternating Hamiltonian path on $P$. For $c=3$, we show that there exist configurations of points for which the longest noncrossing alternating path on $P$ has size at most $(2-1/25)n + O(1)$.

papers.title: Efficient Recursive Evaluation of Gaussian, Gamma, and Inverse Gaussian Tail Probabilities
papers.abstract: Accurate computation of tail probabilities motivates efficient high-order implementations of the $G_n^{(1)}$ extrapolation transformation. We derive finite recurrence relations in the transformation order for Gaussian, gamma, and inverse Gaussian tail approximations. The Gaussian and inverse Gaussian numerator and denominator sequences satisfy four-term recurrences, whereas the gamma sequences satisfy a three-term recurrence. The derivation exploits the structure of the underlying differential operator and shows that the reduced numerator and denominator obey recurrences with identical coefficients. This construction avoids the repeated evaluation of higher-order derivatives and nested sums required by the explicit formulations. As a result, generating the approximation sequence through order $n$ requires $O(n)$ arithmetic operations, compared with $O(n^3)$ for the Gaussian and gamma distributions and $O(n^4)$ for the inverse Gaussian distribution. The recurrence algorithms also require only a fixed number of previously computed quantities at each order. Numerical results for the three distributions are in excellent agreement with values reported in the literature

papers.title: Log-optimal portfolios for market models with regime switching
papers.abstract: This paper considers market models under regime switching mechanism with $D$ states, and analyses the log-optimal portfolio. It is the portfolio, with finite expected utility, that maximizes the logarithmic utility from terminal wealth. We consider a family $\mathbb{X}=(X^{(i)})_{i=1,...,D}$, of $D$-semimartingale models, among which our agent can switch to-and-from following a switching regime modelled by a continuous-time Markov Chain $\alpha=(\alpha_t)_{t\geq 0}$ with $\alpha_0=1$. Then we define a general switching model $\widehat{X}$ that covers the existing cases, and study the impact of the stochasticity of the regime switching and its intrinsic risks on the optimal portfolio in many aspects. On the one hand, we single out the necessary and sufficient conditions on the pair $(\mathbb{X},\alpha)$, which guarantee the existence of the optimal portfolio for $\widehat{X}$. On the other hand, we quantify the factors that fully affect and determine the increment in maximum expected logarithmic utility from terminal wealth for both models $\widehat{X}$ and $X^{(1)}$.

papers.title: Scenario-Based Risk Certificates for Multi-Property Vulnerability Discovery in Parametric MDPs
papers.abstract: Safety-critical systems such as network protocols and distributed algorithms depend on environmental parameters whose exact values are uncertain. Parametric Markov decision processes (pMDPs) model such systems by making transition probabilities symbolic functions of the parameters. For a single quantitative requirement, parametric verification asks which parameter valuations satisfy the requirement. In practice, however, engineers often monitor several safety and performance requirements at once, and one valuation may make several requirements vulnerable simultaneously. In this paper we study multi-property vulnerability discovery under requirement-wise semantics: given a pMDP and M quantitative requirements, we construct candidate regions of the parameter space that may contain violations, and study budgets for random testing under a specified parameter distribution. To solve this, we adopt a two-layered approach in which the scenario-approximation layer provides PAC guarantees on identifying conservative vulnerability regions for each requirement while the testing layer treats random parameter exploration as coverage of overlapping regions and yields a stopping certificate computed from the marginal region masses alone; a composition theorem then bounds the expected non-discovery score by the scenario approximation error plus the testing risk from the two layers. For confirmed discoveries, candidate hits are checked by model checking and budgets use independently certified discovery probabilities. Experiment evaluate these certificates using empirical surrogates and independent confidence bounds.

authors.name: Lijun Zhang
authors.institution: Yunnan University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: A Clifford algebra approach to bosonic strings with fermionic boundaries
papers.abstract: The Brauer-Weyl (1935) theorem states that the algebra of tensor products of spinors is isomorphic to the Clifford (geometric) algebra, in any number of spacetime dimensions. The algebraic relation between fermions and bosons seen in the standard model agrees with the Brauer-Weyl theorem, but not with supersymmetry. It is commonly argued that string theory requires supersymmetry, on the grounds that nonsupersymmetric bosonic string theory (1) does not admit fermions, and (2) has an unstable tachyonic ground state. This paper rebuts those standard objections, pointing out that bosonic string theory admits ferm\-ions lying on a D-brane boundary of open strings, and that the open-string tachyon has all the properties of a Higgs field. The original 1970s formulation of bosonic string theory, re-envisaged as a theory of all the forces, not just the strong force, fits the standard model beautifully.

papers.title: A mesoscale damage model for void nucleation and growth in shock loaded microstructure informed by computer vision
papers.abstract: Spallation in ductile materials under high strain rates occurs through the process of void nucleation, growth, and coalescence. Void nucleation is known to depend on factors ranging from microstructural to stress state. The criteria for void nucleation in damage models are stochastic, and microstructural awareness is often neglected. Recently, it was shown that nucleation propensity can be estimated using computer vision. In the present work, this is integrated with a continuum damage model framework for comprehensive simulation of spallation in tantalum under plate impact. Void nucleation probability is governed by a susceptibility field, predicted from grain orientations and grain boundary (GB) energy, with a mechanical barrier set by the local maximum principal stress. This is coupled to a crystal plasticity model within a Lagrangian shock simulation, with microstructure selectively resolved to reduce computational cost. The model is calibrated at a flyer velocity of 196 m/s, where the simulated free surface velocity (FSV) matches experimental measurements of shock arrival, peak state, release and the pullback signal measured in flyer impact experiments, with some deviations confined to the late time ringing. With no further parameter changes, the model transfers to a 214 m/s case and accurately reproduces the FSV. To demonstrate the microstructure-awareness of the nucleation model, a selection of synthetic microstructures is presented for comparison. In the resolved microstructure, voids nucleate predominantly (though not exclusively) at GBs and triple junctions. It is shown that the FSV differs significantly based on the incorporated microstructure, yielding the correct FSV prediction only in the case of representative microstructures.

papers.title: Same Evidence, Different Verdicts: Delivery of CT Images and DICOM Metadata Changes VLM Quality-Control Decisions
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are being proposed as automated checks on clinical imaging inputs, where a scan and its DICOM metadata can disagree; a truncated CT series wrongly admitted to volumetric follow-up, such as lung-nodule growth assessment in screening, biases the measurement. A natural safeguard is to let the model judge the image before it sees the metadata. We find this backfires. On 60 NLST chest CT pairs with coverage defects whose ground truth is computed from scan geometry, a false header that Claude Haiku 5.5 resisted when shown with the image (2% of its detections overruled) overturned 91% of them when it arrived after the model's answer (Nemotron-3.5-VL 43% to 100%).
