authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Mechanical Transmission

authors.name: Jun Luo
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: ARC-VLN: Adaptive Recursive Computing-based Visual-Language Navigation
papers.abstract: Efficient aerial visual-language navigation (VLN) requires reducing model storage and inference costs while maintaining instruction-conditioned action prediction. We present ARC-VLN, a token-type-aware recursive computation framework built on a language backbone with shared parameters. ARC-VLN retains full-depth computation for text and action tokens while adaptively selecting exit depths for visual tokens. Representations of early-exiting visual tokens are retained, and active-token compaction shortens the sequences processed by subsequent recursive blocks. To mitigate routing collapse to a single exit depth, we design a dedicated learning strategy that encourages the model to distribute visual tokens across multiple exit depths.On OpenFly's Test-Seen and Test-Unseen subsets, ARC-VLN achieves the lowest navigation error and the highest success rate and success weighted by path length among all compared methods. Meanwhile, it reduces the average number of decision steps per trajectory, total floating-point operations, mean model inference time per trajectory, and average GPU memory usage during inference, indicating its great potential as a VLN backbone for lightweight applications.

authors.name: Xiangyu Dong
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Yang Lu
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Recognizing Events Is Not Enough: Why Streaming VLMs Struggle in Compositional Instruction Triggering
papers.abstract: Recognizing individual events does not guarantee correct execution of compositional instructions in streaming video. For example, given the request "Notify me when the pot boils after someone turns on the stove and leaves the kitchen", existing models may recognize the individual events yet notify too early or miss the intended moment, failing to track how their temporal conditions are satisfied over time. To evaluate this gap, we introduce CoTriggerBench, which composes annotated video events into temporally constrained instructions and verifies notification timing and silence through executable event plans and source-event replay. To address this challenge, we propose a real-time VLM agent, TEMPI. TEMPI decomposes instructions into atomic event queries and temporal constraints, and uses Scenario Memory to continuously maintain task progress as event evidence arrives, allowing earlier observations to support subsequent decisions beyond the detector's visual window. Even when no notification is required, relevant events continue to update the scenario state. On CoTriggerBench, TEMPI achieves 44.4% instruction-level success, outperforming the strongest closed-source and fine-tuned open-source VLM baselines by 15.6 (Qwen3.8-Omni-Flash-Realtime) and 18.1 (MOSS-VL-Realtime) percentage points, respectively. To support efficient on-device streaming inference, we further optimize the streaming inference pipeline by overlapping partial visual encoding and LLM prefix prefill with frame arrival. On an 8 GB RTX 5060, our optimized detector implementation achieves a 4.90$\times$ speedup.

authors.name: Yehua Huang
authors.institution: Center for High Pressure Science & Technology Advanced Research

authors.name: Jinhao Zhou
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Xiaowen Chu
authors.institution: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

papers.title: Mid-Infrared Variability as a Probe of Hidden AGN Activity: A Comparison of Seyfert 1 and Seyfert 2 AGNs in the BAT 58-Month Sample
papers.abstract: In accordance with the AGN Unification model, the optical variability of Seyfert 2s is expected to be suppressed because the central engine is obscured by a dusty torus. The absorbed UV/optical radiation is reprocessed and re-emitted in longer wavelengths including the mid-infrared (MIR), making MIR variability a promising probe of obscured AGNs. We investigate the optical ASAS-SN and MIR NEOWISE variability of Seyfert 1 and Seyfert 2 AGNs from the \textit{Swift} 58-month BAT catalog, comparing both populations against non-variable galaxies. One of the first systematic studies of MIR AGN variability, we detected significant variability for Sy1s and the majority of Sy2s. 65% of Sy2s exhibit variability as significant as Sy1s in the MIR, especially in the W2 band, indicating torus dominated MIR variability. Additionally, 22% of Sy2s show higher variability compared to non-variable sources in the W2 band with p-value of $7.1\times 10^{-15}$. Demonstrating MIR variability as an important method to probe the variability of torus and select obscured AGN. Finally, we perform dust reverberation mapping on the Sy1 sample between the optical and W1 or W2 light curves, with measured time delays between 22-786 days (0.02-0.61 pc) for the hot dust in the inner regions of the torus. Our measured torus radius-luminosity slope, $R \propto L^{0.42\pm0.05}$, agrees with literature results. Combining the W1 and W2 band lags with archival NIR measurements, we measured the temperature profile of the torus with $T \propto R^{-\alpha}$, where $\alpha$ values range from 0.3-1.1.

papers.title: Probing Where Surprise Happens: Localized Violation-of-Expectation Evaluation of Video World Models
papers.abstract: Violation-of-expectation (VOE) benchmarks evaluate intuitive physics in video world models by testing whether physically impossible events produce greater prediction errors than matched possible events. However, conventional VOE evaluations aggregate prediction errors across space and time, making it unclear whether successful discrimination reflects model's understanding of physical violations at the locations and time where they occur. To address this limitation, we introduce localized VOE evaluation, a framework that measures prediction error differences between possible and impossible events within spatial regions and temporal intervals associated with physical violations. We compare global, temporally localized, and spatiotemporally localized evaluations of V-JEPA models pretrained on developmental egocentric videos or large-scale natural video datasets. Our results reveal that global and localized judgments can diverge in both directions: global aggregation can either obscure correct localized discrimination or produce apparent discrimination without corresponding localized evidence. During continued pretraining on developmental egocentric videos, agreement between global and localized judgments changes non-monotonically, while confidence in localized judgments increases despite modest improvements in accuracy. Together, these findings establish localized VOE evaluation as a complementary diagnostic for assessing intuitive physics in video world models and demonstrate that global prediction errors do not necessarily reflect the spatiotemporal evidence of physical violations.

papers.title: Model-Free UPS Control Tuning for Improved Low-Voltage Ride-Through in AI Data Centers
papers.abstract: Voltage sags can trigger protection trips in uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems, abruptly reducing the power that AI data centers draw from the grid. This paper improves the low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) capability of AI data centers equipped with double-conversion UPS systems by tuning their existing converter controls. We formulate a bound-constrained optimization problem to maximize the ride-through area, defined as the integral of ride-through time over a range of retained grid voltages. To solve this problem, we develop a batched projected zeroth-order optimization algorithm with adaptive moment estimation (BPZO-Adam). The algorithm evaluates candidate control settings using only simulated ride-through times, making it suitable for vendor-supplied black-box models. Simulations using the TAMU-ERCOT electromagnetic transient (EMT) AI data center model show that tuning converter control parameters increases the ride-through area by 10.6\%. In a separate study, tuning the controls yields a larger ride-through area than increasing the DC-link capacitance tenfold.

authors.name: Haowen Xu
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Decomposing the Associative Chain: Schema-Based Mediation Supports Expression and Understanding in Human-AI Music Co-creation
papers.abstract: Users cannot reliably translate their creative intents into AI-generated music. We contend that the root of this difficulty lies in associative divergence: associations between narratives and musical features are overly remote, and users lack a visible mediation structure to negotiate them. To address this, we introduce five core schema groups as cognitive mediation and propose a bidirectional schema-based framework. Its forward pathway decomposes narrative-to-music associations into staged mappings, while its reverse pathway provides structured interpretations from music back to narrative. Findings from two user studies(N = 188; N = 60) show that the framework led to clearer creative expression and greater perceived control, improved the comprehensibility of generated music, especially for unconventional pieces. Furthermore, it supported cultural and affective thinking while helping users locate associative divergence. Our work points toward better creative intent alignment in human-AI music co-creation.

authors.name: Songruoyao Wu
authors.institution: Zhejiang University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Kejun Zhang
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Learning the Average Dose-Response Function with a Right-Censored Treatment
papers.abstract: This paper considers estimation and inference for the average dose-response function under right-censored treatment duration and missing outcomes for censored units. Using the duration lower bounds provided by censored records, we construct a novel multiply robust estimator through augmented local estimating equations. Under suitable regularity conditions, the estimator remains consistent when any two of the outcome regression, treatment density, and censoring survival function are consistently estimated. We establish its convergence rate and asymptotic distribution within a cross-fitting framework under appropriate conditions on nuisance estimation. To address local smoothing bias that can distort confidence interval coverage, we further develop a debiased estimator that supports asymptotically valid pointwise inference without undersmoothing. Under additional uniform conditions, we construct simultaneous confidence bands using a Gaussian multiplier bootstrap. Simulation studies evaluate estimation accuracy, the validity of pointwise and uniform inference, and robustness to nuisance model misspecification. A semi-synthetic study calibrated to NHANES illustrates the proposed methods in a setting with a known dose-response function.

papers.title: HyperDBDiag: Multi-Root-Cause Identification and Operator-Level Localization for Database Performance Anomalies
papers.abstract: Database performance anomalies in modern production environments are not always triggered by a single cause. Instead, they often arise from the concurrent interaction of multiple causes within the same time window, posing substantial challenges to accurate operator-level root-cause analysis. When multiple root causes interact through shared resources, metric anomalies may be amplified, attenuated, or masked. Consequently, salient local anomalies may no longer correspond directly to the actual root causes, making conventional single-path diagnosis and shallow correlation-based methods prone to misdiagnosis. To address this challenge, we propose HyperDBDiag, a method for multi-root-cause identification and operator-level localization of database performance anomalies. HyperDBDiag connects root causes, performance metrics, SQL templates, and execution operators in a knowledge graph, captures joint anomaly patterns across metrics with a metric hypergraph, and uses a constrained LLM to determine the final root-cause set and provide remediation suggestions. When finer-grained localization is possible, HyperDBDiag also identifies the associated anomalous SQL statements and execution operators. We evaluate HyperDBDiag on a database performance anomaly dataset constructed using DB-MAGS. Experimental results show that HyperDBDiag effectively reduces graph complexity while improving root-cause localization accuracy.

authors.name: Hu Wang
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Qiong Zuo
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Cogirth-Strength Ratios and Matroid Rank Reduction
papers.abstract:
In the rank-$p$ reduction problem, we are given a matroid with nonnegative element weights and seek a minimum-weight set of elements whose deletion lowers the rank by at least $p$. For graphic matroids, this is the minimum $(p+1)$-cut problem. Chekuri, Quanrud, and Xu developed a tree-packing algorithm for minimum $k$-cut, which relies on the fact that the minimum cut of a graph is at most twice its strength, the value of a maximum fractional packing of spanning trees. We generalize this approach from graphs to matroids. The matroid analogue of the minimum cut is the cogirth, the minimum weight of a cocircuit, and the analogue of graph strength is matroid strength, the value of a maximum fractional packing of bases. We show that if every matroid in a deletion-closed class has cogirth at most $d$ times its strength, then for every $p$, the natural linear programming relaxation of rank-$p$ reduction is within a factor of $d$ of the optimum. As a result, repeatedly deleting a minimum-weight cocircuit gives a $d$-approximation, and an optimal solution can be found deterministically in $n^{(2d-1)p+O(1)}$ time on $n$ elements. For graphs, $d=2$ and our framework specializes to the tree-packing approach.
  As applications, we bound the cogirth-strength ratio for two broad classes, and both bounds are tight. For quasi-graphic matroids, which include graphic, bicircular, frame, and lifted-graphic matroids, the ratio is at most $2$ for all weights, giving a $2$-approximation and an exact $n^{3p+O(1)}$-time algorithm. For $(k,\ell)$-count matroids of hypergraphs with $0\le \ell\le k$ and edge size at most $s$, the ratio is at most $ks$ under unit weights. This gives a $ks$-approximation and an exact $n^{(2ks-1)p+O(1)}$-time algorithm for unweighted rank-$p$ reduction.

authors.name: Yajie Zhao
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Semantics First, Pixels Later: Mission-Driven Event Streams for Drone Video over Bandwidth-Starved Links
papers.abstract: A surveillance drone on a bandwidth-starved link cannot send the video its operator would need, yet the operator's questions are often not about pixels: did three people converge, when, and where? We study what should cross a link of 1 Mbps down to 1 kbps instead, and in what order. BPS, a behavior-primitive stream, sends semantics first and pixels later: it runs a detector and a tracker onboard and sends short records (25 bytes on average) of multi-frame events selected by a mission card of 16-125 bytes, ahead of positions and pictures. We measure it by what a ground-side language model answers from it, under a preregistered protocol with a held-out set, against H.265 read by the vision fine-tune of the same model, H.265 on which the ground runs our own perception, a stream of quantized tracks, and onboard captions. On the development set (84% of questions about convergence, mostly one location) the event stream answers 74.3% of questions at 0.13 kbps. A reader that receives nothing answers 57.4%, and the video reader 59.6% at 100 kbps and 64.7% on the source frames. When the ground instead runs our perception on the video, video matches the stream at 100 kbps, about 800 times the stream's rate, and falls behind at 64 kbps and below. A track stream matches it at 96 times the bytes and loses 0.03 at 17 times. On held-out data the result is weaker: with events taken from annotated tracks, an oracle, the stream beats H.265 at 100 kbps (+0.13), but with onboard perception it does not (+0.01 [-0.04, +0.06]) and is no better than receiving nothing. Sent alone through emulated links the event records answer 0.739 at 1 Mbps and still 0.724 at 0.3 kbps; an every-frame track stream holds down to 1 kbps and video with ground-side perception down to about 100 kbps. On a Jetson Orin Nano the unchanged pipeline runs at 4.5 fps and misses most events.

papers.title: Leveraging Dual-Process Theory for Multimodal Multiparty Turn-Taking Prediction
papers.abstract: In multiparty conversations, a pause does not always mean a speaker has finished, and another voice does not necessarily indicate a change in who holds the conversational floor. Reliable turn-taking therefore requires recognising not only whether a speaker is ready to yield the floor, but also when a possible transition deserves attention. We propose a dual-process-inspired framework that separates continuous candidate discovery from selective verification. A fast, recall-oriented stage identifies plausible transition points. In contrast, a deliberative stage combines acoustic, linguistic, speaker-related, and predicted future-activity evidence, together with multimodal cues where available, to reject false candidates and refine transition timing. We evaluate the framework through three distinct tasks: SHIFT/HOLD classification at supplied decision points, verification of automatically generated candidates, and continuous discovery and localisation of floor transfers. On VoxConverse, we derive action-aware turn-taking events from speaker-diarization annotations to examine unconstrained conversations with varying numbers of speakers. Multi-TPC provides complementary evaluation of controlled triadic interactions using speech, gaze, motion, and prosodic information. The findings reveal that identifying plausible transitions is considerably easier than reliably confirming and localising genuine floor transfers, while the contribution of individual evidence sources varies across conversational settings. These results highlight the importance of treating multiparty turn-taking as a continuous discovery-and-verification problem rather than classification at predefined boundaries.

authors.name: Gang Liu
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: DBHiCo: Dual-Branch Hierarchical Contrastive Learning for MRI Image Classification
papers.abstract: Automated Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) image classification provides a crucial non-invasive approach for neurological diagnosis, yet it is fundamentally challenged by inherent acquisition noise and high inter-subject structural similarity, which obscure subtle pathological variations, thereby limiting the performance of deep neural networks. While contrastive learning (CL) offers a promising mitigation strategy, existing paradigms rely on rigid binary partitions that ignore negative sample heterogeneity, and they fail to capture the cross-view structural consistency vital for fine-grained anatomical alignment. To address these barriers, we propose Dual-Branch Hierarchical Contrastive Learning (DBHiCo), a novel framework explicitly designed to collaboratively enforce structural consistency and semantic discrimination. Specifically, DBHiCo leverages a natural anatomical multi-view pair (original and skull-stripped MRI scans), processing them through a dual-branch architecture to seamlessly integrate holistic structural robustness with localized intracranial details. Crucially, we introduce a hierarchical contrastive loss that discards conventional binary constraints in favor of a margin-ranked similarity hierarchy. This mechanism explicitly orders positive and negative pairs based on their structural and semantic difficulty, thereby amplifying the fine-grained semantic discriminability of the learned representations. Extensive experiments across three diverse neurological datasets demonstrate that DBHiCo achieves state-of-the-art performance, consistently outperforming existing MRI multi-view representation learning and advanced contrastive fine-tuning methods.

authors.name: Chenghao Sun
authors.institution: Chengdu University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

authors.name: Xinmei Tian
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Early Readability of Trajectory Quality in Diffusion Driving Planners
papers.abstract: Diffusion-based driving planners can generate multiple trajectories for the same scene, but these candidates vary in quality. Can their internal states reveal which candidate will be better before denoising is complete? We systematically study this question in three pretrained planners: Alpamayo, ReCogDrive-IL, and HDP, using linear probes to predict final trajectory quality from intermediate states and evaluating candidate ranking and selection on held-out scenes. Across all three planners, we observe that states from the first denoiser evaluation already support informative selection, while further denoising does not consistently improve selection quality. Further analyses show that readout depends on the representation and reader, and that selection can coexist with limited overall ranking accuracy. These findings motivate an early-selection method that selects after the first denoiser evaluation and completes only the chosen candidate. This reduces computation relative to fully denoising every candidate and improves open-loop trajectory quality over random selection across all three planners. In particular, it reduces Alpamayo's average displacement error by 17.8% and 13.4% in one- and four-camera configurations, respectively. Closed-loop evaluations also show higher mean driving scores and progress.

authors.name: Yuxin Bao
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Arlington

papers.title: Learning Autoregressive Neural Operators on Solver-Defined Physical Constraint Manifolds
papers.abstract: Autoregressive neural operators approximate time-dependent PDE solvers by repeatedly composing a learned transition, although the resulting states need not remain feasible under the discrete constraints of the numerical problem. We study this issue for incompressible flow, where each velocity state must satisfy solver-level incompressibility together with prescribed boundary values. We formulate autoregressive operator learning as a map between solver-defined affine feasible sets and introduce PCM-NO, a projected-residual realization of this feasible-transition principle. The neural backbone predicts a candidate state increment, a fixed tangent projection extracts its admissible component, and a metric retraction maps the advanced state to the prescribed feasible set. With exact affine constraint solves, the resulting transition is closed on the feasible set, while an affine identity separates admissible-update parameterization from state-level closure. With approximate solves, tangent-only residuals admit a cumulative upper bound, whereas per-step retraction resets feasibility to the residual achieved by the current solve. Experiments on periodic Navier--Stokes flow and lid-driven cavity flow demonstrate the superiority of PCM-NO in preserving solver-level constraints over long autoregressive rollouts and under parameter, boundary-value, and resolution shifts, while achieving lower rollout errors and better flow-specific diagnostics across both in-distribution and stress settings.

papers.title: PISG: Constraint-Aligned Signal Amplification for Diffusion-Based Combinatorial Optimization
papers.abstract: Diffusion-based solvers have become a prominent approach to neural combinatorial optimization. At inference time, they assign each decision variable a prediction score. A greedy decoder ranks candidates by these scores and checks hard constraints to ensure feasibility. Top-ranked candidates should be both promising and jointly feasible, making prediction-constraint alignment critical. When this alignment is weak, greedy decoding skips constraint-violating candidates and falls back to lower-ranked alternatives, degrading solution quality. Existing test-time methods improve search, sampling, or decoding, but do not directly strengthen this alignment before decoding. We observe that trained denoisers already carry constraint-aligned structural signals. Building on this observation, we propose Perturbed Instance-Structure Guidance (PISG), a training-free method that amplifies these signals at test time. At each denoising step, PISG constructs a structure-degraded prediction and extrapolates the unperturbed prediction away from it. The resulting guided prediction improves candidate rankings before constrained decoding. Signal analysis shows that this guidance concentrates on constraint-critical variables rather than uniformly rescaling scores. Under greedy decoding and without downstream refinement, PISG improves all 16 TSP solver-scale pairs across DIFUSCO, T2T, FastT2T, and StruDiCO, and all four MIS-ER solvers, with MIS-ER solved-cost gains up to +4.8%. The gains persist on most large-scale settings after 2-opt, and a preliminary study extends PISG to a Transformer-based solver. These results identify prediction-constraint alignment as an effective test-time enhancement direction for diffusion-based combinatorial optimization. Code is available at https://github.com/Ming-321/PISG.

papers.title: HBF-EventLab: A Discrete-Event Simulator for Studying Host-Device Coordination in High Bandwidth Flash
papers.abstract: High Bandwidth Flash (HBF) combines NAND flash density with high-bandwidth accelerator connectivity, offering additional memory capacity for large language model inference. However, limited hardware availability makes it difficult to evaluate how host behavior and device resource constraints jointly affect HBF request processing. We present HBF-EventLab, an open-source, transaction-level discrete-event simulator based on the Open Compute Project HBF specification. HBF-EventLab connects host request dispatch, command admission, fragmented write assembly, read dispatch, NAND execution, and completion feedback within a shared event loop. It explicitly models distinct resource lifetimes and separates configurable scheduling policies from ordering and resource constraints, enabling controlled exploration of host-device coordination. Experiments show how resource limits, address interleaving, fragment arrival patterns, and scheduling policies affect write completion and request latency. The results highlight the need to consider resource limits and scheduling policies jointly, accounting for their interactions with write assembly and read eligibility. We also integrate HBF-EventLab with real GPU execution of Qwen3-0.6B, combining profiled GPU activity durations with simulated weight-access delays to estimate time to first token and time per output token, with logits and output tokens remaining bitwise identical to those from native GPU execution. HBF-EventLab provides a configurable foundation for studying HBF mechanisms, exploring scheduling policies, and assessing how HBF access delays affect application-level timing. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/sjtu-epcc/HBF-EventLab.

papers.title: Calabi flow in the controlled K\"ahler cone
papers.abstract: We prove that the geometric limit of a global Calabi flow in a real class of the controlled K\"ahler cone is independent of the initial metric. Under cohomological K-polystability, the limit is a smooth cscK metric in the original class and complex structure. We also establish varying-class closedness and an equivariant continuity method. We apply this method to construct a smoothly varying family of cscK metrics throughout an explicit interval of symmetric real K\"ahler classes on the blow-up of the projective plane at four points in general position.

papers.title: Hidden symmetries and echolocation
papers.abstract: We study the echolocation problem: whether local spectral data determine a point up to isometry. We characterize cospectrality by the existence of a spectral symmetry exchanging the two point evaluations and introduce a pointwise analogue of Sunada's method for constructing such symmetries. This yields cospectral, non-similar points on closed hyperbolic surfaces of every genus at least three and on round lens spaces. We also obtain Neumann examples on a scalene triangle and on a planar slit domain, and reinterpret a known Dirichlet example of Dixon, Miah, Safronov, Snyder, Vakaryuk, and Wyman through the same framework.

papers.title: Representability of Intertwining Operators for Weak Modules of Vertex Operator Algebras
papers.abstract: Let $V$ be a vertex operator algebra. For every weak $V$-module $W$, we construct a weak $V \otimes V$-module $\mathcal{R}(W)$ representing the bifunctor $\mathcal{I}\binom{W}{-\;-}$ of intertwining operator spaces, in the sense that there exists a natural isomorphism \[ \mathcal{I}\binom{W}{-\;-} \cong \Hom_{V\otimes V} \ab\big(-\otimes -, \; \mathcal{R}(W)). \] As applications of this natural isomorphism, we first establish a Yoneda-type lemma for spaces of intertwining operators, and then identify the unique largest locally restricted submodule $\mathcal{R}_{\lr}(V^\prime)$ of $\mathcal{R}(V^\prime)$ with the coend of the bifunctor $-\otimes-^\prime$: \[ \mathcal{R}_{\lr}(V^\prime) \cong \int^{M} M \otimes M^\prime, \] where $M$ ranges over restricted $V$-modules. Finally, the connection between $\mathcal{R}(W^\prime)$ and the regular representation $\mathfrak{D}_{\xi}(W)$ constructed in \cite{Li02} is established, where $\xi \in \C^{\times}$. In particular, if $V$ is a $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra and $W$ is a restricted $V$-module, then $\mathcal{R}(W^\prime)$ is also a restricted $V \otimes V$-module and is canonically isomorphic to $\mathfrak{D}_{\xi}(W)$.

papers.title: Augmented Lagrangian methods with Nesterov acceleration for convex optimization with nonlinear inequality constraints
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop Nesterov accelerated augmented Lagrangian methods for composite convex optimization with nonlinear inequality constraints. The methods are derived through a compatible discretization of inertial primal-dual dynamics, yielding a unified framework that couples difference extrapolation of the constraint mapping with a projected multiplier. Under convexity and weighted summability of the primal stationarity errors, we prove boundedness of the primal-dual iterates and simultaneous $\mathcal O(k^{-2})$ last-iterate rates for the objective residual and constraint violation. Under strict parameter conditions, the primal-dual sequence converges to a Karush-Kuhn-Tucker pair, and both residuals improve to $o(k^{-2})$. These results require no strong convexity of the objective or constraints. Numerical experiments examine the performance of the proposed methods.

authors.name: Xin He
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: GlyphAtlas: Disentangling Stroke Detail from Layout for Scene Text Synthesis
papers.abstract: Scene text synthesis requires stroke-accurate characters rendered in a specified layout, as well as visual coherence with the surrounding scene. To achieve this, existing methods commonly pre-render the target text at its intended locations to form a glyph image that jointly specifies layout and glyph structure. However, this representation ties the resolution of each glyph to its target region, limiting fine-grained stroke guidance for small, densely packed, or structurally complex text. To tackle this, we propose GlyphAtlas, a scene text synthesis framework that retains the glyph image as a spatial anchor and supplies fine-grained stroke references through a dedicated glyph atlas. The atlas renders and encodes each character or word in a separate cell, decoupling reference resolution from target-region size. We further introduce atlas-anchored attention, which lets each text region retrieve stroke detail only from its corresponding atlas cells to refine the coarse glyph structure provided by the glyph image. This coarse-to-fine conditioning simplifies stroke rendering while preserving explicit layout correspondence. We optimize GlyphAtlas with a mask-weighted flow matching objective and a timestep-weighted text perceptual loss for writing accuracy and background consistency. Random resolution augmentation of atlas cells supports adjustable atlas budgets at inference. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GlyphAtlas achieves stroke-accurate synthesis of small, dense, and structurally complex text, zero-shot transfer to languages unseen during task-specific training, and leading performance in scenes with many text regions. project page: https://fr0zencrane.github.io/project-glyphatlas/

papers.title: Long time derivation of the Boltzmann equation from dynamics of short-range potentials
papers.abstract: We derive the Boltzmann equation from the Newtonian dynamics of particles interacting through a short-range repulsive potential for arbitrarily long times, in the Boltzmann--Grad limit. This extends the recent hard-sphere result of Deng, Hani and Ma (arXiv:2408.07818) to short-range potentials. Compared with hard spheres, two new difficulties arise: (i) in the absence of a Burago--Ferleger--Kononenko-type bound (Ann. of Math. 147 (1998), 695--708, doi:10.2307/120962), a bounded number of particles may undergo an unbounded number of collisions within a short time; and (ii) since collisions last a positive time, three or more particles may interact simultaneously. To overcome (i), we treat such clusters of recollisions as single objects, called boxes, keeping track only of their entry and exit structure, so that internal collisions do not enter the combinatorial counting. The multi-particle collisions in (ii), together with the boxes, lead to more complicated molecules, which requires adapting the counting estimates and the cutting algorithm.

papers.title: ReconPotBench: Evaluating LLM Honeypots in Multi-Round Linux Reconnaissance
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to build interactive honeypots, yet existing evaluations mainly assess isolated command outputs and cannot determine whether a system remains believable when later commands depend on earlier results. We present ReconPotBench, a multi-round benchmark for Linux reconnaissance honeypots. It contains 1{,}032 three-round reconnaissance interactions across eight reconnaissance categories, with reference outputs collected from a real Linux environment. Under a unified testing protocol, we compare Cowrie, open-source LLMs, and closed-source LLMs along three dimensions: round-level authenticity, cross-round contextual consistency, and hacker-oriented reconnaissance value. Results show that multi-round evaluation exposes failures hidden by single-round testing, as authenticity declines with interaction depth and both open-source and closed-source LLMs struggle to maintain coherent state across rounds. LLM-based honeypots nevertheless outperform Cowrie in authenticity and reconnaissance value, while Cowrie remains more consistent because of its rigid templated behavior. Category-level analysis further shows that tasks requiring systems to preserve network relationships across rounds are harder than tasks centered on explicit entities such as ports. ReconPotBench enables reproducible evaluation of LLM honeypots across authenticity, entity consistency, and hacker-perspective utility in dependent multi-round interactions. The dataset is available at: https://github.com/qianli-wang/ReconPotBench

authors.name: Qianli Wang
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Quantum Computing-Based Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Networks for Airfoil Parameterization
papers.abstract: Airfoil geometry parameterization is essential in aerodynamic design optimization. Optimization search in the large space suffers from low efficiency and modest feasible region, which could further incur failures to convergence. Generative adversarial networks (GAN), aiming to learn the statistical distribution of existing data, pave a new avenue for shape generation and airfoil parameterization. GAN manages to implicitly reduce design space by generating only smooth, realistic airfoils. Meanwhile, quantum computing has been emergingly exhibiting great potential for achieving superior performance in specific types of engineering problems but has not been introduced to airfoil parameterization. To fill this gap, this work develops quantum computing-based Wasserstein GAN (Q-WGAN) and investigates the performance for airfoil parameterization. The Q-WGAN adopts parameterized quantum circuits as the generator to promote the generative performance, while the discriminator remains classical. The developed Q-WGAN is demonstrated on a dataset of optimal airfoils parameterized by free-form deformation (FFD) control points, resulting from 992 airfoil aerodynamic design optimizations. Results show that Q-WGAN achieves 92.1% mean fitting accuracy on the optimal FFD control points and 99.2% accuracy on airfoil coordinates, comparable with the classical WGAN performance of 92.28% on FFD control points and 99.26% on airfoil coordinates. Q-WGAN achieves lower Jensen-Shannon divergence, Fr\'echet distance, and Wasserstein distance than the classical WGAN, indicating an improved agreement with the reference airfoil distribution. Therefore, this work presents a convincing evidence that Q-WGAN makes a viable option for parameterizing airfoils and possesses a great potential for other relevant engineering applications.

authors.name: Xiaosong Du
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: CARE: Contrastive-Anchored Residual Encoding with Listwise Reconstruction for Retrieval-Oriented Semantic IDs
papers.abstract: Generative retrieval replaces nearest-neighbor search with the generation of a document's semantic ID (SID), so the SID tokenizer bounds what the retriever can recall. Common SID constructions (residual k-means, RQ-VAE, finite scalar quantization, capacity balancing) optimize criteria defined on document embeddings alone and do not control whether a query can still find its relevant documents after quantization. We propose two retrieval-oriented SID tokenizers. CARE-SID (Contrastive-Anchored Residual Encoding for Semantic IDs) quantizes in a retrieval-aligned space: a zero-initialized residual alignment network is trained with a query-document contrastive loss before quantization, an anchor loss and a reconstruction target fixed to the original embedding prevent drift and collapse, and reference-vector rating residual quantization assigns the codes. CARE-LR (CARE with Listwise Reconstruction) then distills, for each training query, the similarity distribution that the original embeddings induce over a candidate list into the SID reconstructions, through a function-preserving layer-resolved head. Both keep a document-only encoding interface. We judge SIDs without training a generator, by row-budget recall in a bucketing view (the partition) and a reconstruction view (the SID with its reconstruction). In offline evaluation on industrial video search data, both tokenizers achieve higher reconstruction-view recall than residual k-means, and CARE-LR improves further on CARE-SID, mainly through the listwise distillation. A comparison of two document embeddings shows that contrastive alignment helps most when the embedding has not been trained on search data, and that the embedding affects SID recall far more than the quantizer. CARE-SID is deployed in the generative retrieval stage of an industrial video search system.

papers.title: UniGraph: A Unified Graph-based Index for Dynamic Hybrid Dense-Sparse Vector Retrieval
papers.abstract: Hybrid dense-sparse vector retrieval combines semantic signals from dense representations with lexical signals from sparse representations, typically ranking items by a query-dependent weighted sum of dense and sparse vector distances. Existing systems commonly search separate dense and sparse vector indexes and rerank the union of their candidates, incurring two retrieval passes and potentially discarding items that rank highly only after the semantic and lexical signals are combined. Constructing a graph-based index directly under a hybrid distance can mitigate this premature candidate loss. However, because varying the hybrid weight alters the underlying neighborhood relationships, a single static graph built at a fixed weight cannot accommodate dynamic query-specific weights. Therefore, we propose a Unified Hybrid Graph (UniGraph), which merges neighbor sets computed at multiple hybrid weights into a single bounded-degree graph index, enabling hybrid vector retrieval with different query-specific weights without index reconstruction. We further develop an adaptive weight-guided search framework that chooses between sparse- and dense-guided entry points according to the query weight, together with a dense-first hybrid distance pruning strategy that avoids unnecessary exact sparse distance computations. Extensive experiments show that UniGraph provides a favorable Recall-QPS trade-off across different query weights. In the mixed-weight setting, UniGraph delivers 27.6%~52.3% higher QPS than the fastest baseline on each dataset at Recall@100 greater than or equal to 0.95. UniGraph has been deployed at scale in Ant Group's production environment, where hybrid retrieval with query-dependent weights is in strong demand.

papers.title: FH-Sampling: Frequency-aware Hypergraph-driven Oversampling for Imbalanced Time-Series Classification
papers.abstract: Imbalanced time-series data appears commonly in diverse applications, such as medical diagnosis. When trained on imbalanced data, classifiers tend to exhibit a bias toward the majority class, making it difficult to identify minority-class instances accurately, despite their critical importance. Sampling techniques have proven effective in rebalancing imbalanced data. However, existing interpolation-based oversampling methods typically rely on pairwise interpolation, limiting their ability to capture high-order inter-sample relationships, and their inherent smoothing effects tend to suppress high-frequency components, compromising spectral fidelity. Therefore, we propose a Frequency-aware Hypergraph-driven Oversampling method (FH-Sampling) for imbalanced time-series classification. In FH-Sampling, a hypergraph is first constructed in the original time-series space to capture complex high-order inter-sample relationships, and sampling ratios are adaptively assigned to mitigate the impact of noisy samples. The discrete wavelet transform decomposes each sample into frequency components. Guided by the sample hypergraph, FH-Sampling combines high-frequency components from related samples while retaining the target sample's low-frequency component to help preserve important frequency characteristics. Experiments on 24 imbalanced datasets demonstrate the advantages of FH-Sampling for imbalanced time-series classification. We further apply FH-Sampling to aircraft trajectory generation. Experiments on simulated aircraft trajectories show that FH-Sampling produces trajectories that better match the real distribution, highlighting its potential for practical applications.

authors.name: Qiang Zhang
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: SemiNovo: Learning Beyond Search-Identified Spectra for De Novo Peptide Sequencing
papers.abstract: Sensitive peptide identification is fundamental to protein characterization and novel protein discovery, for which de novo peptide sequencing (DNPS) from tandem mass spectra provides an important database-independent approach. Although deep learning has substantially advanced de novo sequencing, existing models are predominantly trained on high-confidence peptide-spectrum matches obtained through database search. This search-conditioned supervision excludes a large fraction of unidentified spectra, creating a distribution mismatch between the selectively labeled training data and the complete spectrum stream encountered at inference time, thereby limiting peptide identification performance. To address this challenge, we propose SemiNovo, a semi-supervised framework that learns jointly from identified and unlabeled spectra. SemiNovo first constructs DarkSpec, a large-scale quality-controlled corpus of unlabeled spectra collected from diverse public proteomics projects, thereby extending training beyond search-identified spectra and mitigating the resulting shift in DNPS supervision. It then combines stepwise mass-constrained autoregressive decoding with cumulative path confidence to derive reliable supervision from unlabeled spectra. Moreover, SemiNovo introduces head-wise chemical-evidence gating to improve spectral evidence aggregation under noisy and incomplete fragmentation. Experiments show that SemiNovo performs favorably against state-of-the-art methods on multiple benchmarks. Code and dataset are publicly available.

papers.title: VAE Rhythm: Temporal Decoding Traces for AI-Generated Video Detection
papers.abstract: Visible artifacts are an unreliable cue for detecting generated videos, because newer generators learn to remove them. We instead detect a trace left by the generation pipeline itself. Most video generators decode latents with a 3D causal VAE that groups consecutive frames in time, so the fidelity of generated frames rises and falls periodically with their position in a group. We call this periodic trace VAE Rhythm. Real videos are captured frame by frame and do not have it. To reveal it without training, we propose a phase scan. The scan reconstructs a clip with an off-the-shelf VAE from successive start offsets and measures the periodicity of the reconstruction error across these offsets. We find VAE Rhythm in most of the 39 variants of 31 generators we test, including the closed-source Sora, Kling 3.0 and Seedance 2.0. We use the rhythm as a zero-shot score, as a plug-in for existing detectors and as a data engine that pairs real videos with their VAE reconstructions to train our detector CaDet. On DF26, the training-free rhythm score outperforms all 15 retrained baselines, and as a plug-in it improves all 19 tested detectors by 6.7% to 23.7% AUROC. CaDet achieves the best AUROC on AIGVDBench, DF26 and three 2026 closed-source models, and its variant trained without any generated video still exceeds 90% on AIGVDBench.

papers.title: A Polynomial Time Algorithm for Finding a Minimum 5-Partition of a Submodular Function
papers.abstract: Given a real-valued submodular function on a finite ground set, the minimum $k$-partition problem asks for a partition into $k$ nonempty parts minimizing the sum of their function values. We give a polynomial-time algorithm for $k=5$. The idea follows directly from the previous $k=4$ result, where there is precisely one obstruction for generalizing it to $k=5$. We show the special case can be handled by reasoning about a restricted family of $3$-partitions.

papers.title: Attribution-Guided Shared-Private Decoupling for Noise-Reduced Audio-Visual Representation Learning
papers.abstract: Audio-visual representation learning commonly aligns paired audio and visual signals with sample-level contrastive objectives. However, real-world audio-visual pairs usually contain heterogeneous patch tokens: only a subset carries reliable cross-modal shared semantics, while many others mainly encode modality-private residuals. Aggregating all tokens into a single global representation can therefore introduce semantic noise into cross-modal alignment. Motivated by the minimal-sufficiency principle, we propose an attribution-guided shared-private decoupling framework to mitigate this issue. Our key idea is to identify shared-cover subviews that preserve dominant cross-modal information while suppressing modality-private residuals, and use them to supervise decoupled shared and private representations. To identify such subviews efficiently, we draw on transformer attribution method and introduce Layer-Truncated Attribution (LTA), which provides a lightweight estimate of token-level relevance to cross-modal shared information. We further adopt a teacher-student framework, where the teacher provides attribution-induced supervision and the student internalizes shared-private decoupling into its representations, without introducing extra inference cost. Experiments on retrieval, classification, and sound-prompted semantic segmentation show consistent gains over strong baselines. Compared with baseline, our method improves the average zero-shot R@1 by 4.0 across AudioSet and VGGSound retrieval, and improves AS20K classification mAP by 3.1, demonstrating the effectiveness of fine grained attribution guidance for reducing semantic noise.reducing semantic noise. Code will be released at https://github.com/wanglg20/LTA

papers.title: Affordable Analytic Gradients for G0W0-BSE Excited States for Multiple GW Variants via Back-Propagation
papers.abstract: We derive, implement and validate analytic nuclear gradients for three variants of $GW$ self-energies---the contour-deformation (CD), the analytic continuation (AC), and the contour deformation with $W$-analytic-continuation (CD-WAC)---and for the Bethe--Salpeter equation (BSE) built on top of them. All gradients are expressed as contractions of a set of covectors connected to derivatives of primitive quantities in SCF calculations. The derivation of these covectors is a back-propagation procedure through the $GW$ and BSE equations. Central finite differences confirm the correctness of all implemented gradients. With the AC-$GW$-BSE gradient we optimize the excited-state geometries of carbon monoxide, a donor-acceptor dye labelled as DA1, and DMABN, a typical model system for twisted intramolecular charge-transfer phenomena (TICT), and have obtained results that successfully reproduce observations from experiments or high-level calculations. We also performed trajectory surface hopping (TSH) simulations of nonadiabatic molecular dynamics (NAMD) of DMABN using the SHARC NAMD package, showing the capacity of our method to simulate NAMD problems. We performed timing and memory scaling tests, demonstrating that the gradient calculations of both $GW$ and BSE scale asymptotically as $N^4$ for timing and $N^3$ for memory. All source codes used in the present work, including the REST program package and the modified SHARC NAMD package that supports REST as the quantum chemistry backend, are available on Gitee https://gitee.com/restgroup/rest and https://gitee.com/qirui-gao-2025/sharc

papers.title: Interlocking Tiling of 3D Finite Domains
papers.abstract:
A K-hedral tiling of a 3D finite domain is a covering of the domain with tiles without gaps or overlaps, where each tile is congruent to one of the K distinct shapes called prototiles. To use 3D K-hedral tilings in practice, they need to satisfy two requirements. First, K should be small to reduce the fabrication cost (e.g., through reusable molds) and simplify the (dis)assembly process. Second, a K-hedral tiling result should be structurally stable, in particular via interlocking, where all the tiles are immobilized by their geometric arrangement, except the key. Since these two requirements are often in conflict, existing approaches always trade one for the other.
  In this work, we formulate a new tiling problem called interlocking tiling, aiming to generate 3D K-hedral tilings that satisfy the above two requirements simultaneously. Given a 3D finite domain represented as a voxel grid, our goal is to compute a small prototile set whose instances exactly tile the input domain while ensuring that the tiling result forms an interlocking assembly. To solve this challenging problem, we propose a twolevel computational approach that hierarchically decomposes the input domain into interlocking parts (domain-level partitioning) and further partitions each part into interlocking tiles (part-level partitioning). To guide the part-level partitioning, we propose a new graph representation with regular structures to facilitate the generation of tiles with identical shapes while ensuring that they are interlocking. Our approach allows generating interlocking tilings that exactly cover 3D finite domains with diverse shapes while achieving high prototile reuse. We compared our approach with state-of-the-art methods to demonstrate its superiority, and validated the practicality of our interlocking tiling results via fabricating two of them.

papers.title: A bound-preserving hybrid lattice Boltzmann method for scalar hyperbolic conservation laws
papers.abstract: Solutions to scalar hyperbolic conservation laws may develop discontinuities within finite time even from smooth initial data, while higher-order lattice Boltzmann (LB) methods tend to generate non-physical oscillations and out-of-bounds behavior near steep gradients. To address this issue, we first construct a first-order LB method with the upwind-type equilibrium distribution functions under the \(DdQ(2d+1)\) lattice structure, and establish its bound-preserving (BP) conditions. We then develop a second-order multiple-relaxation-time LB (MRT-LB) method by introducing the auxiliary source distribution functions, and analyze its \(L^2\) stability. Building on these, we propose a hybrid LB method that preserves the collision-streaming structure, by conservatively mixing first- and second-order updates through a convex constraint mechanism. We further establish the global BP (GBP), local BP (LBP), and relaxed LBP (RLBP) limiters in the hybrid LB method, together with the associated macroscopic BP constraints. Numerical experiments examine the convergence order, interface capturing performance, and discontinuity resolution capability of the proposed BP hybrid LB method. The results indicate that it effectively suppresses out-of-bounds behavior in the second-order LB method and reduces numerical dissipation in the first-order LB method, while maintaining the prescribed bounds and discrete mass conservation.

authors.name: Zhenhua Chai
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Global existence of an initial boundary value problem for the Einstein equation via a Hamiltonian approach
papers.abstract: The global existence of the initial boundary value problem for the Einstein equation in \((2+1)\)-dimension with totally geodesic timelike boundary is proved by a Hamiltonian approach. The initial boundary value problem is formulated within the framework of the ADM formalism, and the ADM reduction is carried out under the constant mean curvature spatial harmonic gauge. Deriving energy estimates for the flows in the reduced phase space shows the global existence.

papers.title: Rethinking Supervision Scaling in On-Policy Distillation: From Dense Supervision to Stochastic Horizons
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) provides dense token-level supervision along student-generated trajectories, yet the learning benefits of longer trajectories may not scale proportionally with their computational cost. We investigate how supervision utility evolves with trajectory length. Controlled experiments reveal diminishing returns from additional supervised tokens, while showing that later positions remain learnable and exhibit substantial cross-position supervision transfer. Gradient analysis further identifies shared update components across response positions and diverse position-specific residuals whose cross-rollout consistency decreases at greater depths. Motivated by these findings, we propose Stochastic Horizons On-Policy Distillation (SH-OPD), which reduces redundant supervision by randomly varying rollout horizons while preserving access to deeper response states. SH-OPD samples a shared horizon for each training batch, enabling efficient parallel generation without per-sequence horizon scheduling overhead. We characterize the resulting reweighting bias and derive a compute-reweighting trade-off under standard optimization assumptions. Experiments on mathematical reasoning and code generation demonstrate that SH-OPD achieves slightly higher mathematical reasoning accuracy at approximately 45% of the per-update cost of standard OPD, while maintaining competitive code generation performance at around 60% of the baseline cost. These results highlight the benefits of efficient supervision allocation across response depths.

papers.title: PEETS: Preference-aware Embeddings with Explicit Tree Structure for Auxiliary Product Bundling
papers.abstract: Auxiliary products such as flight protection and flexible-change services are recommended alongside primary travel purchases. This setting creates a granularity ambiguity: SKUs within one product type share semantics but differ in price and coverage, while rejecting one offer does not imply disinterest in the entire type. We present \textbf{PEETS} (\textbf{P}reference-aware \textbf{E}mbeddings with \textbf{E}xplicit \textbf{T}ree \textbf{S}tructure), a training-time framework for auxiliary product bundling. PEETS regularizes an existing click--conversion predictor through two conditional comparisons. Hierarchical Contrastive Loss uses the pair's common ancestor as a reference; Negative Contrastive Loss conditions structural sampling and comparison shifts on logged rejection events. Both act on shared SKU representations during training. This separates catalog relatedness from individual preference supervision and leaves the predictive serving path intact. PEETS achieves 78.20\% AUC, exceeding TWIN V2 by 0.90 percentage points and the matched base model by 1.15 points. In a 14-day online evaluation, gross auxiliary GMV per exposed user-day improves by 8.20\% over Policies, 3.06\% over Base, and 0.84\% over TWIN V2, with all three user-bootstrap 95\% intervals above zero. Bundling rate is 0.51 points below Policies. The cancellation interval's upper limit exceeds the prespecified margin. PEETS adds no auxiliary-loss computation to serving and records 42.1~ms p95 latency, compared with 42.0~ms for Base.

authors.name: Jing Tian
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Singular K\"ahler-Ricci solitons and complete gradient shrinking K\"ahler-Ricci solitons on non-compact manifolds
papers.abstract: We construct a class of complete gradient shrinking K\"ahler-Ricci solitons on non-compact toric manifolds by exhausting a family of singular K\"ahler-Ricci solitons associated to multiple divisors. The construction method will be also extended on non-compact $\mathbf G$-manifolds.

authors.name: Feng Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Linear Network Coding for Sum All-Reduce over Ring Networks
papers.abstract: Sum All-Reduce is a fundamental collective communication primitive in which each node holds a local vector and every node must recover the componentwise sum of all vectors. In distributed training, this operation is often implemented over a ring topology using a reduce--multicast scheme. We study sum All-Reduce on directed rings via linear network coding, which includes reduce--multicast as a special case. We give a necessary and sufficient feasibility condition in terms of the coding matrices. For a ring with $N\geq 3$ nodes and unit-capacity links, where each node holds a vector containing $K$ symbols, we prove that the number of time units $T$ required by any feasible linear code satisfies $T\ge\max\bigl\{K+N-2,\ \lceil\frac{2(N-1)}{N}K\rceil\bigr\}$, giving a rate $K/T$ of at most $N/(2(N-1))$. The bound is tight over every field. When $K\ge N$, an interleaved reduce--multicast code achieves the bound; when $K<N$ and $K$ divides $N$, a reduce--partial-multicast code does. When $K<N$ and $K$ does not divide $N$, no coordinate-wise code---in particular, no reduce--multicast code---achieves the bound, while an explicit linear network code does.

papers.title: P\'olya inequalities on thin planar networks
papers.abstract: We construct thin planar domains on which the Dirichlet and the Neumann P\'olya inequalities both hold strictly. For the neighborhoods of a given finite connected embedded polygonal graph (branches and cycles are allowed) there is a single radius threshold below which both inequalities hold for every eigenvalue index. We also show that every nonempty bounded connected open set in the plane can be approximated, in measure and in the Hausdorff distance, by smooth simply connected domains satisfying both inequalities. Along the same sequence, the first Dirichlet eigenvalue tends to infinity, while each Neumann eigenvalue of fixed positive index tends to zero. In the special case of rectangular frames our estimates lead to explicit sufficient conditions, with no restriction on the aspect ratio.

authors.name: Liangdi Zhang
authors.institution: Beijing Institute of Mathematical Sciences and Applications

papers.title: Neural Operator Approximation for Yau--Yau Nonlinear Filtering: Stability, Approximation, and Fast Computation
papers.abstract: Since the introduction of the Kalman filter, nonlinear state estimation has become an important topic in areas such as aerospace engineering, sensor design, and target tracking. Within the optimal filtering framework described by the Duncan-Mortensen-Zakai (DMZ) equation, Yau-Yau filtering (YYF) employs an offline-online decomposition: the Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov (FKE) equations, initialized by a prescribed set of basis functions, are solved offline, and the prior density is projected onto these basis functions during the online stage. However, this approach still faces two computational challenges: solving multiple FKEs offline can be computationally expensive, and the online projection becomes costly when filtering is performed repeatedly or in high-dimensional settings. To address these limitations, we develop a neural operator filter (NOF) that directly learns the mapping from the prior density to the posterior density, thereby eliminating both the expensive offline FKE solves and the online projection. The underlying operator is approximated using a Fourier neural operator (FNO). Numerical experiments on several challenging filtering systems verify both the effectiveness and accuracy of our method, and we further provide a rigorous theoretical analysis of its stability and approximation error.

authors.name: Xiaopei Jiao
authors.institution: Beijing Institute of Mathematical Sciences and Applications

authors.name: Stephen S. -T. Yau
authors.institution: Beijing Institute of Mathematical Sciences and Applications

papers.title: A Negative Answer to a Variant of the Lins-de Melo-Pugh Conjecture
papers.abstract: We study the polynomial Li\'enard system $$\dot x=y-(a_1x^{2m+1}+a_2x^{2n+1}+x^{2N}),\qquad \dot y=-x,$$ where $0\leq m< n<N$ are integers and $a_1a_2<0$. The supremum of the numbers of limit cycles in this family is at least two for every integer $N\geq3$ and at least three for $N=5$. These results disprove Conjectures 1.5 and 1.6 of Cen et al. [Sci. China Math. 69 (2026)].

papers.title: Is This Code Mine? Student Ownership When AI Agents Write the Spec and the Code
papers.abstract: Software engineering courses are starting to ask students to build entire systems with AI coding agents, but little is known about what students actually do with them and whether they still own what they deliver. If the agent writes both the code and the decisions behind it, the artifacts we grade no longer show what students learned. We studied an assignment in which 18 pairs of students built applications with agents under Spec-Driven Development, combining the mined history of their repositories, the prompts they recorded, and a survey of 33 students. The agents wrote 69\% of the specifications meant to keep students in control, sometimes from a prompt of a few words. Students locate their ownership in the ideas, crediting themselves with half of them but a fifth of the code, yet most could not explain that code to a colleague or modify it without the agent, and what they report having written is unrelated to what their own commits declare. The three teams that met the 100,000-line target did so with generated code the application never uses, in one case proposed by the agent itself, and one team rewrote its history to backdate its specifications. Teaching with agents should therefore assess what students specify, review, and can explain, rather than what they ship, and enforce the engineering process with tools rather than trusting it to students or agents.

authors.name: Danilo Monteiro Ribeiro
authors.institution: Centro de Estudos e Sistemas Avançados do Recife

papers.title: Invariant measures with uniform projection on surfaces and billiards
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we study probability measures on the unit tangent bundle which are invariant under the geodesic flow and whose projection to the base manifold is the normalized Riemannian volume. We show that the Liouville measure is the only such measure on a complete oriented surface of finite area with ergodic geodesic flow. In particular, this resolves a conjecture of Katok--Knieper--Weiss in dimension two. The same holds for ergodic planar billiards with piecewise C2 boundary, such as the Bunimovich stadium, the Sinai billiard, and generic polygons. The proof combines the Fourier analysis in the fibers with holomorphic functions on the transport twistor space.
  As a consequence, on these surfaces and on the Bunimovich stadium, a high-energy sequence of normalized Laplacian eigenfunctions tends to be equidistributed in the phase space if and only if it tends to be equidistributed in the physical space. In particular, on every stadium, every failure of equidistribution in the phase space implies scarring in the physical space. Combined with Hassell's theorem, this gives a new proof of scarring in the physical space for almost every stadium.
  In higher dimensions, we obtain an entropy bound for the ergodic components of such measures. We also construct counterexamples for hyperbolic toral automorphisms.

papers.title: Joint Movable Antenna Positioning and Precoding for ISAC via a Two-Timescale Model-Based GNN
papers.abstract: Movable antennas (MAs) allow an integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) base station (BS) to reshape multiuser channels and angular sensitivity. For monostatic multiuser communication and multi-target elevation and azimuth estimation, we minimize the expected target-averaged angular Bayesian Cram\'er-Rao bound (BCRB) subject to per-user block-level and long-term rate requirements. To avoid repeated online optimization, we propose a two-timescale model-based graph neural network (TT-MBGNN) over antennas, users, and targets. The slow policy selects positions from long-term statistics to reduce movement overhead, while the fast policy learns complex corrections to a regularized zero-forcing (RZF) reference using post-movement channels and target-angle priors. We jointly train both policies through a differentiable model of rates and BCRB, without optimization-generated labels. Across tested rate requirements, the network yields lower sensing bounds than variants using a fixed array, RZF, or both, with any-user fast-rate violations in 0.31-2.63% of test blocks. Frozen policies provide competitive sensing bounds for unseen user and target counts, and ten fine-tuning epochs improve communication reliability at higher user counts. Across tested network sizes, our framework achieves up to 3 dB lower BCRB than an idealized alternating-optimization benchmark that uses known target reflection coefficients. The network computes precoders approximately 50-fold faster in matched batch-one tests.

authors.name: Yuchen Zhang
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Architecture and Technology

papers.title: A Unified Control Framework, Mathematical Model, and Five-layer Closed-loop Case Study for Embodied Intelligence Control Systems
papers.abstract: Embodied intelligence holds that an agent develops cognition and behavior through real-time body-environment interaction, so its control system must tightly couple perception, decision making, learning, optimization, constraints, and physical execution. This report asks whether a unified framework exists, how its mathematical models unify, and how the framework is realized computably. Four conclusions emerge. (1) No single framework is accepted, but the field converges on a common skeleton: from operational-space and whole-body control to MPC, reinforcement learning, active inference, and diffusion/flow policies, all reduce to constrained sequential decision making on the configuration manifold. (2) Two languages describe it-deterministic optimal control (Euler-Lagrange plus constrained OCP, reduced in real time to a QP) and probabilistic inference (MDP/POMDP plus free-energy minimization)-rigorously bridged by control as inference and KL/path-integral control. (3) Engineering unification is already achieved by constrained optimization; the new frontier is cross-morphology, cross-task shared representation. (4) The hardest gap is provable stability and safety, the entry point for spectral, geometric, differentiable-optimization, and safe-learning methods. A single-link manipulator then runs through all five layers: L4 parses the instruction into a reference, L3 identifies a Koopman lifted linear world model, L2 solves a receding constrained QP, L1 adds torque saturation and a CBF, and L0 is the true nonlinear plant. Closed-loop tracking RMSE is 0.0218 rad with all constraints satisfied and a world-model error near 5 x 10^-6 rad, reported with curves and a 3D animation.

papers.title: Site-Specific Cell Shaping: An Agentic Framework
papers.abstract: An agentic framework is proposed for cell shaping in future sixth-generation (6G) wireless network planning. Cell shaping controls the coverage and interferences of base stations (BSs) through antenna parameters configuration, providing an important means of improving coverage. In contrast to conventional approaches that reply on costly performance evaluations, the proposed framework achieves intelligent and efficient antenna configuration through a perception-reasoning-reflection loop. Specifically, a Configuration Agent combines scene information, evaluation history, and reflection feedback to generate antenna configuration proposals. Then, a ray tracing(RT)-based evaluator assesses these proposals and returns a structured performance summary. Next, a Reflection Agent interprets these results to diagnose site-specific performance deficiencies, recommend feasible configuration adjustments, and accumulate conditional experience. Through this iterative process, the framework accumulates site-specific experience and progressively refines antenna configurations without human-in-the-loop intervention. Simulations in real-world urban scenarios demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves lower outage probabilities than the considered benchmark methods, highlighting the effectiveness of agentic reasoning and reflection in translating site-specific performance feedback and accumulated experience into adaptive antenna configuration decisions.

papers.title: Agentic On-Policy Distillation Implicitly Reshapes LLMs' ReAct Patterns
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers specialized capabilities to language-model agents, but its cross-domain effects on interaction remain unclear. We investigate how OPD reshapes ReAct interaction patterns across mathematics, ALFWorld, and $\tau^2$-bench, focusing on reasoning, actions, and observation acquisition. General-reasoning supervision reduces mathematical tool attempts from 70.4% to 14.4% while increasing accuracy from 16.7% to 38.0%; code-interpreter supervision improves household actions and retail queries. In contrast, ALFWorld supervision reduces $\tau^2$-bench accuracy from 41.5% to 6.6%, accompanied by frequent tool calls that violate user-information dependencies. To address negative transfer using only source-domain training trajectories, we explore selective OPD guided by teacher preference changes before and after domain-specific RL. Retaining the top 95% of positions raises $\tau^2$ accuracy from 11.5% to 29.9% with a source-learning trade-off.

authors.name: Sijian Ren
authors.institution: Shandong University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Yuan Wei
authors.institution: Shaanxi University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Ying Wei
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Chemical Resource Engineering

papers.title: Auditory-Feedback-Conditioned Flow TTS for Implicit Lombard Adaptation
papers.abstract: Conventional text-to-speech (TTS) systems can lose intelligibility in noise environments because they cannot adapt to environmental changes. However, humans tend to increase their vocal efforts in noisy environments, a phenomenon known as the Lombard effect. Building on an auditory-feedback Lombard TTS, we investigate whether a pretrained Flow-based TTS can learn acoustic adaptation directly from auditory feedback without explicit prosodic control. Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) feedback and automatic speech recognition (ASR) feedback are extracted from the noise-corrupted waveforms and injected into the Flow-matching condition for utterance refinement and causal block-level updates. We assess feedback benefits across prompting and noise conditions using plain/Lombard prompting, prompt-switching controls, and paired-finetuning. Experiments show that while finetuning provides strong robustness under in-domain conditions, auditory feedback yields additional cue-dependent benefits that generalize to unseen noise. Moreover, stronger power/F0 tracking alone does not guarantee better speech intelligibility or quality.

authors.name: Satoshi Nakamura
authors.institution: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

papers.title: Robust Well-Log Reconstruction Across Point Gaps and Whole Wells via Boundary-Gated Soft-Thresholding Kalman Fusion
papers.abstract: Missing wireline logs hinder subsurface characterization. Deep reconstruction networks suffer from gap-boundary steps and cross-basin shifts, while interpolation and Gaussian smoothers struggle with long intervals and outliers. We propose boundary-gated soft-thresholding Kalman fusion (ST-KF), unifying multiresolution wavelet shrinkage, distance-gated residual prior learning, and closed-form robust Kalman smoothing with learning--inference decoupling. Across two public benchmarks totaling 263 wells in the Norwegian North Sea and New Zealand's Taranaki Basin, ST-KF ranks first over 0.15--100-m anchored gaps with 0.09% parameter overhead. Against the strongest of nine baselines, pooled RMSE falls by 5.0%--8.3% for bulk density and 6.4%--15.6% for compressional slowness; against the four strongest baselines, reductions are 0.7%--4.1% for neutron porosity and 1.3%--2.9% for photoelectric factor. Ablations and sensitivity analyses confirm operator synergy and stable performance: removing state-space fusion increases short-gap errors by up to 58.8%, while zero-shot transfer cuts anchored errors by 14%--68%. The results show that local borehole continuity transfers across basins whereas cross-property mappings shift with regional geology, supporting measurement-guided log reconstruction.

authors.name: Zhihan Qiu
authors.institution: Shandong University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Youzhuang Sun
authors.institution: China University of Petroleum, East China

papers.title: A Threshold-Free Visual-Semantic Matching Metric for Evaluating Consistency in Subject-Driven Image Generation
papers.abstract: In subject-driven text-to-image generation, quantitatively evaluating localized visual consistency across varying poses and environments remains a major challenge. Existing metrics either rely on global image embeddings (CLIP, DINO) and Vision-Language Models (VLMs) that pool spatial representations and miss fine-grained textural artifacts, or depend on scalar threshold-gated dense metrics such as Visual-Semantic Matching (VSM) that suffer from point-alignment dropouts, severe threshold sensitivity, and score instability. To overcome these limitations, we propose TF-VSM, a fully continuous, threshold-free visual-consistency metric paired with an extended feature-disentanglement retraining schedule for dual-branch ResNet feature-aggregation networks. Rather than enforcing rigid binary cutoffs $(T_s,T_v)$, TF-VSM weights every object point by a non-linear semantic match confidence $w_j=ReLU(\hat{s}_j)^2$ and continuously integrates visual similarity over all consistency levels $r\in[0,1]$, yielding a closed-form confidence-weighted score without any hand-tuned hyperparameters. On a controlled 100-pair benchmark with ground-truth inpainting oracles, TF-VSM attains Pearson $0.638$ and Spearman $0.674$ oracle correlation, improving over the pretrained VSM baseline ($0.454/0.589$) by $+0.171/+0.116$ after retraining, and drastically outperforming CLIP ($-0.052/-0.004$), DINO ($0.087/0.121$), and VLMs ($0.096/0.003$). Six diagnostic ablations confirm that smooth confidence weighting is the right mechanism, that hard semantic gating is brittle (dropping to $0.533$ Pearson at $T_s{=}0.8$), and that the threshold-free metric is essentially invariant to the training-time loss balance $\alpha$ that the thresholded metric still depends on.

papers.title: Diagonal and Fine Tower Dimensions for Minimal Circle Homeomorphisms and Product Actions
papers.abstract: We study minimal circle homeomorphisms and their products with Cantor systems, and show that these actions have diagonal dimension at most two and fine tower dimension at least two. Consequently, diagonal dimension, fine tower dimension, and tower dimension are all equal to two for minimal circle homeomorphisms. We also obtain a strict separation between tower dimension and fine tower dimension on a one-dimensional space.

authors.name: Kang Li
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Remember, Replay, Adapt: Learning from Past Experience in Online Vision-and-Language Navigation
papers.abstract: Existing feedback-based methods for online vision-and-language navigation (VLN) primarily learn from current episode outcomes, leaving previously acquired feedback underutilized. Inspired by human episodic memory, we propose R2A, an online VLN adaptation framework that continually reuses successful and failed navigation experiences for policy learning. Specifically, Success-Failure Memory (SFM) retains successful and failed navigation episodes with acquired feedback and retrieves task-relevant experiences based on incoming instructions, enabling historical feedback to guide subsequent navigation.
