Prior-Anchored Adaptation (PAA) learns from these experiences by reinforcing successful trajectories and suppressing failed ones relative to a frozen pretrained policy, while regularizing behavioral drift. Together, these modules enable continual feedback reuse and stable policy adaptation without source-domain data or expert supervision. Extensive experiments across three benchmarks, REVERIE, R2R, and R2R-CE, and five navigation backbones demonstrate consistent performance gains. On the REVERIE validation unseen split, R2A improves DUET's SR from 46.98% to 69.84% and SPL from 33.73% to 50.98%.

authors.name: Lixin Xiu
authors.institution: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

authors.name: Songlin Dong
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Latent World Modeling for Point-Cloud Video Pretraining
papers.abstract: Masked modeling is the dominant self-supervised paradigm for point-cloud videos. However, it leaks the information it is meant to predict, whether it reconstructs masked points as in MAE-style methods or predicts their latent features. Because point-cloud tokens are anchored at points sampled from each frame, querying a target at its own position reveals where its geometry has moved, in reconstruction and latent prediction alike. For latent predictors, random spatio-temporal masks introduce a further shortcut, as visible frames on both sides of each target allow interpolation rather than forecasting. The pretext task thus reduces to completion. Once the target positions are withheld, a masked latent predictor performs only slightly better than copying the last frame. To remove this leakage, we propose PointWM, a latent world model that turns completion into forecasting by predicting the features and geometry of future frames from strictly earlier context. Each target is queried only with its last-seen position and timestamp, while a latent action learned without annotations is meant to capture the part of the future that the past leaves undetermined. On HOI4D action segmentation with a P4Transformer backbone, PointWM improves F1@50 over training from scratch by 24.9 offline and 29.1 under strictly causal inference. These results show the promise of latent world models as a leakage-free pretraining paradigm for point-cloud videos.Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/InitalZ/PointWM.

papers.title: Global dynamics of large smooth solutions to the two-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes system with Navier-slip boundary conditions
papers.abstract: We establish global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions containing vacuum to the two-dimensional barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations with bulk viscosity depending on the density, in smooth bounded simply connected domains, subject to the Navier-slip boundary conditions. Without any restriction on the size of initial data, we obtain time-uniform density and velocity bounds and exponentialconvergence to equilibrium in Sobolev spaces for the density and velocity. Moreover an initial vacuum point will persist and force the exponential growth of density gradients.

authors.name: Song Jiang
authors.institution: Institute of Applied Physics and Computational Mathematics

authors.name: Jing Li
authors.institution: Beijing University of Civil Engineering and Architecture

papers.title: Augmenting Pretrained Language Models with N-gram Embeddings through Incremental Training
papers.abstract: As a new scaling technique for large language models, the n-gram embedding improves the base ability of a model while adding almost no inference cost. Mainstream research realizes it through joint training of the n-gram embedding with the backbone, which severely restricts the settings in which an n-gram embedding can be used. We therefore propose training an n-gram embedding onto an existing model through incremental training, to extend where the technique can deliver value. Specifically, we explore several settings of the n-gram embedding under incremental training---the learning rate of the embedding, the vocabulary size, and the injection position---and train an n-gram embedding onto the existing model under the best configuration. Experiments show that the best configuration under incremental training does not fully coincide with that under pretraining; moreover, the incrementally trained knowledge is written predominantly into the n-gram embedding, while the general ability of the backbone is retained throughout this training process.

authors.name: Minghao Shao
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: On the Convergence of Continuous-Time AdamW
papers.abstract: Continuous-time AdamW provides a framework for understanding whether an optimizer widely used to train large-scale neural networks settles to an equilibrium or sustains persistent motion. We study this long-time behavior while retaining bias correction and fixed positive weight decay. Under suitable assumptions, we establish that the dynamics are well defined for all time and remain bounded when the decay is sufficiently small. Our main result connects their limiting behavior to the geometry of the objective: trajectories approach a locally invariant manifold whose dimension equals the Hessian nullity along the associated critical component. When critical points are isolated and have at most one such direction, the trajectory converges to a single equilibrium. With two degenerate directions, however, bounded persistent motion can occur even for a smooth, strictly convex objective with a unique minimum. We also quantify how close the long-time trajectory remains to the critical set as weight decay decreases, without assuming convergence to a point. These results identify objective geometry as a key to understanding when continuous-time AdamW converges and when persistent motion is possible.

papers.title: Compositional Data-Driven Small-Signal Stability Assessment of Power Systems via Output Differential Passivity
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a compositional data-driven small-signal stability assessment framework for interconnected power systems based on output differential passivity (ODP). Without requiring explicit device models, local ODP matrices and scalar indices are estimated directly from measurement trajectories. When internal states are available, trajectory-based linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) are constructed from input-state measurements to estimate the local ODP matrices and scalar indices. When internal states are unavailable, an extended-state representation is constructed from input-output measurements, enabling the same assessment using only external signals. The estimated ODP matrices are combined with the network coupling matrix for compositional assessment of power system stability, while their scalar indices enable decentralized assessment. To address the computational and numerical challenges of trajectory-based LMIs, we introduce right-inverse whitening (RIW) to remove redundant behavioral coordinates and improve computational efficiency, and apply instrumental-variable (IV) preprocessing to alleviate numerical ill-conditioning and mitigate noise effects. Case studies on a modified IEEE 39-bus power system show that ambient measurements satisfy the required informativity conditions and that both formulations yield estimates close to model-based references under the tested noise levels. The reusable local ODP estimates also enable modular stability reassessment after controller updates.

authors.name: Xi Ru
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Power System Operation and Control

papers.title: Global Strong Solutions and Large-Time Behavior for the Two-Dimensional Compressible Flow with General Bulk Viscosity
papers.abstract: The global existence of a unique strong solution to the two-dimensional barotropic compressible Navier--Stokes equations with general density-dependent bulk viscosity is established for large initial data allowing vacuum. Both the periodic problem and the Cauchy problem with far-field vacuum are considered under a common logarithmic derivative bound and growth condition on the viscosity primitive. A time-independent density upper bound and uniform low-order estimates are obtained in both domains. The admissible coefficients include every superlinear power law and near-linear laws with logarithmic gains. Exponential relaxation to the positive equilibrium is proved in the periodic setting. In the whole space, uniform relaxation toward vacuum and algebraic decay of the pressure, velocity gradient, material acceleration, and relative kinetic energy are established.

authors.name: Song Jiang
authors.institution: Institute of Applied Physics and Computational Mathematics

authors.name: Jing Li
authors.institution: Beijing University of Civil Engineering and Architecture

papers.title: When Does Interaction Help? Toward a Reynolds Number for Collective Intelligence
papers.abstract: Multi-agent systems combine distributed information through interaction, which can improve performance but also spread errors or suppress useful differences. Predicting when interaction helps is central to understanding and designing collective intelligence. We investigate whether a few dimensionless parameters can predict gains over explicitly defined non-communicating baselines across group sizes, network structures, and tasks, toward a Reynolds-number-like description of collective intelligence. Using distributed classification tasks, stochastic tracking networks, and neural cellular automata, we combine analytical and empirical evidence to examine information sufficiency, dynamical applicability, and finite-sample prediction. We construct inference systems with bounded random variables and matching specified joint moments up to total degree three, yet opposite interaction gains under a fixed readout. These moments alone cannot generally determine the gain sign. Tracking networks likewise exhibit gain reversals despite matched candidate parameters when task power occupies different spectral modes. Under concentrated task spectra and aligned observation noise, however, we derive a low-dimensional similarity relation with an explicit zero-delay error bound and test it across network sizes and topologies under frozen protocols. The relation does not directly apply to the neural cellular systems, where a separate moment-based predictor underperforms direct gain measurement at matched calibration sample budgets. These results establish conditions and limits for low-dimensional gain prediction, providing a restricted similarity law while leaving a general Reynolds-number-like description of collective intelligence open.

papers.title: QuarkDB: A Hybrid Database System for Quantum Data Management
papers.abstract: Emerging quantum applications like quantum communication generate large volumes of high-dimensional quantum data, requiring efficient data analysis and storage. However, classical database systems often struggle to meet requirements such as quantum processing or version management. This paper presents QuarkDB designed for efficient quantum data management. QuarkDB establishes a unified object model for relational and quantum data and defines the syntax of Quantum Structured Query Language. To support efficient quantum data management, QuarkDB integrates three key components: (1) a Hybrid Query Engine with cost-based hybrid plan selection over classical and quantum operators, (2) an Execution Engine with a three-level instructions intermediate representation, QuarkDB-IR, to support quantum execution and reduce quantum processing costs, and (3) a Storage Engine supporting quantum data version management, state reconstruction and data reuse. Compared with classical databases such as SQLite and PostgreSQL or quantum databases like Qute, our QuarkDB achieves query-latency speedups ranging from 2.14x to 25.86x speedup under extensive real-world workloads.

papers.title: RAGE: Residual-Adaptive Gating for Flow-Based Image Editing
papers.abstract: Recent inversion-free, flow-based image editing methods evolve the source image toward the target via a differential velocity field. We observe that this velocity field does not explicitly account for which regions should be preserved, leading to unintended drift in non-editing regions. To address this, we formulate source fidelity control as a stochastic optimal control problem in which a selective fidelity term on the editing residual is enforced along the editing trajectory. Solving this problem and approximating its solution yields the Residual Gating Principle: each latent component is pulled back toward the source with a gain that decays exponentially with the local residual magnitude, so that small deviations are suppressed while large, semantically meaningful edits pass through unimpeded. The proposed method, RAGE, requires only one lightweight gated interpolation per sampling step, involves no mask estimation, attention maps, retraining, or architecture-specific modifications, and is applied on top of FlowEdit-based editors. On PIE-Bench, RAGE achieves the best overall rank among 17 methods and substantially improves background preservation on both Stable Diffusion 3 and FLUX backbones while maintaining competitive editing quality.

authors.name: Xiangyu Xu
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: LogicEye: Agent Driven Multimodal Dataset for Interpretable Ophthalmic Diagnosis
papers.abstract: Clinical adoption of ophthalmic Artificial Intelligence remains limited by low interpretability and a lack of finely annotated multimodal data. Most existing datasets provide only coarse disease labels without the granular pathological findings required for differential diagnosis. We present LogicEye$^{Agent}$, a dual-pool inference and verification agent that emulates clinical reasoning by jointly verifying positive inclusion signs and negative exclusion criteria. Using LogicEye$^{Agent}$, we curate LogicEye$^{Data}$, a large-scale multimodal dataset of 804,461 fundus and OCT images paired with structured pathological reports spanning 38 diseases and 29 subtypes, with quality assured through joint verification by multimodal large language models and clinical experts. Building on this dataset, we further develop LogicEye$^{Bench}$, which incorporates a category-constrained loss for hierarchical disease recognition and report generation. Grounding coarse labels into verified visual findings effectively curtails diagnostic hallucinations and establishes a solid foundation for interpretable vision-language modeling in ophthalmology. The code is available at:https://github.com/Eden35/LogicEye-Agent-Driven-Multimodal-Dataset-for-Interpretable-Ophthalmic-Diagnosis.

papers.title: RouteDiff: Low-Dose CT Denoising via Fidelity-Refinement Routing and Hypergraph State Regulation
papers.abstract: Diffusion models have become a strong prior for low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) restoration. However, existing samplers apply one structure-detail trade-off to the whole image, set the restoration emphasis of each step by the timestep, and derive each next state recursively from the current one, carrying its errors forward. We propose RouteDiff, a state-aware dual-route diffusion framework that routes detail to where it can be trusted, regulates each reverse step by the state it has reached, and re-enters the trajectory from an anchored estimate. Fidelity-Refinement Routing (FRR) equips one shared U-Net with a conservative fidelity route and a detail-oriented refinement route, fuses them pixel-wise with a confidence map, and exposes their disagreement as route evidence. Hypergraph State Regulation (HSR) organizes the current features and this evidence into a state hypergraph, whose soft hyperedges group scattered regions in the same state. Its readout yields an ordered stage judgment that modulates the bottleneck, and its incidence guides feature interaction in the skip connections. Estimate-Anchored Re-entry (EAR) re-projects a route-aware anchor onto the trajectory at a fixed step and hands the new state back to HSR to be judged again. With the ten network evaluations of its baseline, RouteDiff achieves the best peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index (SSIM) on four datasets with inserted, real and simulated noise (40.95 dB and 95.13% on Mayo 2020; 45.18 dB and 97.23% on Mayo 2016). It also generalizes to unseen doses of real scans and yields the highest Dice (80.92%) in downstream segmentation.

authors.name: Xinyuan Wang
authors.institution: Tianjin University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

authors.name: Ruili Li
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Tianyang Li
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Yan Li
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: LEDGER: LLM-Evidence-Driven Graph-Encoded Clustering-Friendly Representations for Short Texts
papers.abstract: Short-text clustering is important for analyzing user-generated content in social networks and online services, supporting applications such as topic discovery and user intent analysis. However, the desired grouping depends on an application-specific clustering criterion that general-purpose text embeddings may not capture. Large language models (LLMs) can apply such a criterion to a pair of texts without human annotation, and existing methods use their responses as generated descriptions, binary decisions or selected neighbours. These discrete outputs discard how strongly the LLM supports a pair and how many judgments stand behind it. Each judgment is also used alone or within the neighbourhood of a single text, so the relations that link judgments across the corpus remain unused. In this paper, we propose LEDGER, an LLM-guided graph representation learning framework for short-text clustering. LEDGER aggregates the repeated numerical scores of each text pair into an accumulated score and an observation count, which define an evidence target for every queried pair. The pairs whose scores reach a threshold form a relation graph, over which a graph encoder propagates text features with a propagation range learned jointly with the encoder. A pairwise predictor trained to match the evidence targets shapes the learned representation, and a distilled student encoder extends it to unqueried texts without further LLM requests. Extensive experiments on seven datasets with four frozen text embeddings show that LEDGER achieves the highest mean clustering accuracy and NMI against five comparison methods, and ablations show that the graph, the learned propagation range and the evidence target each improve performance.

papers.title: Veech dichotomy for specific covering surface over Veech surface
papers.abstract: It is known that Veech dichotomy, which states that minimal directions are uniquely ergodic, holds for Veech surface and covering surface branched at a single non-periodic connection point of Veech surface. We give a sufficient condition for Veech dichotomy holds for a finite translation cover of a Veech surface, and applies it on branched cover of square-tiled surfaces to construct examples that satisfy Veech dichotomy but aren't Veech surfaces.

papers.title: Learning Graph-Conditioned Predictors in Weight Space
papers.abstract: The same node attributes can imply different labels in different structural contexts. Yet fast graphless models typically treat topology as additional evidence supplied to a globally shared predictor. This assumes that structure augments the available information, rather than determining how node attributes should be interpreted. We introduce SCOPE (Structure-COnditioned PrEdictor), in which a small generator maps each node's cached structural fingerprint to coefficients over a shared low-rank basis, producing a context-specific update to a global weight matrix. The base predictor, basis, and generator remain shared across all nodes, while the resulting transformation adapts how attributes are processed in each relational environment. Once fingerprints are cached, inference requires only a forward pass and no online message passing. This design combines context-specific specialization with global parameter sharing, compact low-rank adaptation, and message-passing-free inference. On two large OGB node-classification graphs, conditioning the weights with raw positional signals yields clear gains over supplying the same signals through input concatenation. Further results under a structure-transductive held-out-node protocol and in teacher-free graph classification show that the mechanism extends beyond a particular distillation setting. These findings establish graph structure not only as predictive evidence, but as context that determines the predictor used to interpret that evidence.

authors.name: Hao Zhu
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Porosification of the dielectric layer in alternating-current electroluminescence devices enables high-resolution tactile imaging
papers.abstract: Vision-based tactile sensing enables high-resolution contact perception, yet bulky optical architectures consume valuable space and constrain the functional design of dexterous robotic hands. Here we introduce a self-emissive tactile imaging strategy based on alternating-current electroluminescence (ACEL) devices, in which a compressible porous dielectric encodes contact pressure into spatial emission patterns without external illumination or discrete sensing pixels. We identify a nonlinear capacitance-dependent emission window that provides a basis for tunable pressure-to-light conversion. Pore-size engineering further suppresses local emission deficiencies, reducing spatial intensity variation by nearly ninefold and enabling faithful imaging of contact features down to 100 {\mu}m. The continuous electroluminescent interface also reproduces complex contact patterns without computational reconstruction of electrical fields. Direct lamination of the ACEL device onto a complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) image sensor is expected to enable compact contact imaging in an assembly less than 5 mm thick, substantially thinner than conventional vision-based tactile sensors. This approach could reduce the space required for high-resolution tactile imaging, offering greater design freedom for dexterous robotic hands.

authors.name: Jia-Sen Xie
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Optoelectronic Materials and Technology

papers.title: Sustaining In-Network Computation in Satellite Networks: An Architecture for Semantic Continuity
papers.abstract: Satellite computations often outlast the paths and providers initially serving them. We argue that in-network computing should organize changing execution opportunities around one continuing logical computation: workers execute ready operations, while consumers recognize which results already contribute. We present an architecture separating logical computation, stream context, and physical binding, and show in wildfire assessment how retained observations support recomputation while reachable association history stays in place. A 300-node Linux prototype examines placement, dependency assembly, and continuation. Across 120 images, stage-wise placement delivers 82.08% of positions within deadlines versus 76.06% for single-node placement, while traces separate blocked output delivery from dependencies split across providers. Across 50 observations with 20-node isolation, Confirmation-Coordinated Rebinding (CCR) coordinates replanning, source replay, cross-attempt acceptance, and in-band confirmation to complete all 50 observations with verified outputs using seven replays and 13 ignored duplicate outputs.

papers.title: $\ell^p$-Busemann space and the coarse Novikov conjecture
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of an \(\ell^p\)-Busemann space, which is a complete Busemann convex geodesic metric space whose tangent cones admit uniformly controlled homogeneous bi-Lipschitz embeddings into \(\ell^p\)-spaces. An \(\ell^p\)-Busemann space is called admissible if it contains dense sequences of closed convex subsets isometric to certain Finsler manifolds. We then prove that the rational coarse Novikov conjecture holds for proper metric spaces with bounded geometry that admit coarse embeddings into admissible \(\ell^p\)-Busemann spaces.

authors.name: Xianjin Wang
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Spectroscopic evidence for unconventional surface magnetism in the Kondo insulator FeSb$_2$
papers.abstract: Kondo insulators have a non-magnetic bulk due to many-body screening of local moment by conduction electrons. However, the surface of these systems has reduced density of itinerant electrons and may experience a Kondo breakdown, leading to recovery of non-zero local moments and possible magnetic order. Here we use angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy to investigate the (010) surface of a $d$-$p$ electron Kondo insulator FeSb$_2$, which is predicted to host a bulk $d$-wave altermagnetic state in the absence of Kondo screening. We find anisotropic splitting on the surface states with a maximum in the $k_z$ direction and a minimum in the $k_x$ direction. The splitting is apparently suppressed with increasing temperature or with Te doping, suggesting that the splitting arises from a magnetic order rather than Rashba effects. Considering the proximity of the bulk to a $d$-wave altermagnetic state and considering the symmetry of the crystal on the surface, we postulate that our observations may be consistent with an emergent surface altermagnetic order. Such an unconventional 2-dimensional magnetic order naturally hosted on an insulating, non-magnet bulk substrate may offer a promising platform for versatile applications.

authors.name: Erin E. Fleck Jonathan A. Sobota

papers.title: Counterexamples to Ecker's Conjecture
papers.abstract: Analogous to Perelman's W-entropy defined for Ricci flow, K. Ecker defined a functional W for the mean curvature flow in R^{n+1} and the region it encloses, and made the conjecture that this functional is monotonically increasing in time. In this paper, we give a negative answer to Ecker's conjecture.

authors.name: Jiarui Chen
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Mock Observations: Morphological Analysis of Galactic Bars in IllustrisTNG Simulations
papers.abstract: Galactic bars are important tracers of disk-galaxy evolution, yet reported bar fractions vary among observational studies and between observations and cosmological simulations. We compare bar statistics and properties in the IllustrisTNG simulations(TNG100 and TNG50 at z~0.1) with Sloan Digital Sky Survey(SDSS) galaxies at0.1<=z<=0.1264. We generate synthetic r-band TNG images,match SDSS observational conditions,and analyze mock TNG and real SDSS images using a common image-based framework of source segmentation,morphological classification, and isophotal ellipse fitting. For face-on late-type galaxies with log(M*/Msun)>10,the global bar fractions are 26.68+/-0.23%,24.96(-.76/+.78)%, and 13.42(-1.07/+1.15)% for SDSS,TNG100,and TNG50,respectively. TNG100 broadly agrees with SDSS over 10^10<~M*<~10^11.2Msun but shows a higher fbar at higher masses, whereas TNG50 remains lower than SDSS over most of10^10<~M*<~10^11.7Msun. Bulge-disk decompositions show fewer high-n bulges in TNG100 than in SDSS,particularly at high masses,but more in TNG50. These differences in bulge concentration may contribute to the different bar fractions. Bar length generally increases with stellar mass,and this trend depends little on the adopted bar-length definition. However, the outer ellipticity-decline estimator(R0.85max) yields systematically larger bar lengths than the ellipticity-peak estimator (R(eps,max)^bar). Massive TNG100 galaxies have more extended stellar disks than SDSS,which may contribute to their smaller relative bar lengths(Rbar/Re). Our results indicate that observational conditions,sample selection,and bar-identification methodology can affect the inferred bar fraction,emphasizing comparable observational conditions and analysis procedures in simulation-observation comparisons. Our SDSS measurements may underestimate the bar fraction relative to observations with higher spatial resolution.

authors.name: Jun-Yu Gong
authors.institution: The University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center

papers.title: LoopSkim: Lossless Multi-Depth Speculative Decoding for Looped Language Models
papers.abstract: Looped language models such as Ouro and Raven apply one weight-shared block several times per token, so autoregressive decoding (AR) runs every loop of every token in sequence. Pipelined self-speculative decoders overlap these loops by drafting tokens from shallow readouts and verifying them at full depth. Yet every loop of a looped LM ends in a readout of the next token, and draft tokens pass through every depth anyway, so each depth can check them without an extra pass. We introduce LoopSkim, in which the depth of the pipeline is the verifier. Draft tokens copied from the context, as in prompt lookup decoding, enter after the first loops, any later readout that contradicts one replaces it at that depth, and only full-depth readouts commit tokens. LoopSkim fixes the random draws of every position in advance, so each check compares two tokens and decoding stays lossless in exact arithmetic under sampling for any number of checks and draft chains. Without training, its speedup over AR averages 1.73x that of LoopSpec across greedy decoding and sampling, and its checks between the first loops and full depth speed it up on every model. An optional draft head adds a second chain and raises this average to 1.99x.

authors.name: Muhan Xiao
authors.institution: PLA Rocket Force University of Engineering

papers.title: Strong Standard Completeness of a Hypersequent Calculus for Cyclic Involutive Residuated Lattices
papers.abstract: We present a hypersequent calculus $H_R$ for cyclic involutive residuated lattices and prove strong standard completeness for arbitrary theories in a fixed countable propositional language. Standard models are chains on $[0,1]$; neither commutativity nor equality of the monoid unit and the dualizing constant is assumed. The chain semantics is the class $K_R$ defined by unit cyclicity and all ordered finite-history conditions. Every countable member of $K_R$ embeds into a standard chain preserving the entire signature. The construction combines central-support reconstruction, gap insertion and relative contraction. A relative comparison construction supplies the required chain countermodels. We also prove admissibility of the unrestricted density rule for theoremhood and effective elimination from finite proofs without additional assumption leaves. Elimination uses terminating enumeration of density-free proofs; ordinary Cut is retained, and no complexity bound is claimed. Further constructions give bounded standard embeddings for nontrivial countable chains of involutive uninorm logic and pseudo-uninorm logic with weak commutativity. Using ordinary chain completeness for arbitrary theories, these yield strong standard completeness for both logics. A companion Lean~4 development formalizes the main results, with its scope and external inputs stated explicitly.

papers.title: Learning From the Best: What Makes Popular Hugging Face Models?
papers.abstract: Hugging Face has become a central platform for sharing and reusing pre-trained models, yet it remains unclear which practices are associated with higher visibility and adoption. Prior studies describe model reuse and model-card quality but do not systematically compare popular and unpopular models across documentation, repository structure, platform metadata, and technical metadata. We studied 66,909 Hugging Face models collected on 2026-02-28 and extracted 31 features across four dimensions: Documentation, Models, Platforms, and Techniques. For downloads and likes, we compared the top 10% popular models with the bottom 80% using statistical tests and effect sizes, trained five classifiers to predict popularity, ranked feature importance with the best-performing model, and tested whether predictions held across model domains and contributor affiliations. Popular models consistently had longer model cards, more code examples, and more GitHub and arXiv links, while quantized models showed contrasting patterns under downloads and likes. A Random Forest reached AUC 0.861 for downloads and 0.848 for likes, with root-level file counts and model size also among the most important features. Cross-group transfer stayed mostly above random but dropped by 0.12-0.17 AUC on average, showing that prediction performance was partly group-specific. The findings remained stable after removing download outliers and under alternative popularity thresholds, and a manual review of popular model cards linked the key documentation features to concrete content. We derive recommendations for model practitioners and directions for future research on model-sharing platforms.

authors.name: Bach Le
authors.institution: Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City

papers.title: Words Speak Louder? Exploring the Language Shortcut of LLM-Driven Incomplete Multimodal Learning
papers.abstract: Is a face or a voice still heard once the words are known? Incomplete multimodal learning increasingly uses large language models (LLMs) as fusion engines: modality features enter as token blocks and missing modalities become placeholders. We find that LLM-driven fusion can override non-verbal evidence it can read. Contrasting its full-input prediction with counterfactual views, the same model shown one modality or no content, we identify language shortcuts. We build MR-Bench: MR-Bench-A types every test sample of four sentiment benchmarks; MR-Bench-H contains 900 human-validated clips (620 language-shortcut, LS; 280 non-verbal-shortcut, NS) from seven sources, and every model is scored on all of them. Zero-shot MLLMs solve at most 32.7% of the LS clips; adding the transcript to the muted video lowers vision-language accuracy by 46.1-53.1 points. Yet inverting a text-only model's answers solves 94.4%, so LS accuracy alone cannot establish use of non-verbal evidence. Inside the fusion LLM, fused states align increasingly with the text view late in the decoder. Counterfactual-View Reliability learning (CoVeR) trains views as unimodal judges and withholds fused supervision where they disagree. It achieves state-of-the-art results on five benchmarks without extra inference cost in accuracy mode. On MR-Bench-H, it reaches 61.7% LS and 93.6% NS accuracy; robust mode raises LS accuracy to 63.0% while lowering NS accuracy to 84.8%. Among LS clips solved without text, adding text causes errors on 30.1% with CoVeR versus 32.2% with LLM-Fusion. Project page: https://peacelwh.github.io/CoVeR/.

authors.name: Chong Xiao
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Zhuang Qi
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Organic-Inorganic Composite Materials

papers.title: AdaModalX: Synchronization-Free MFM Inference for Distributed Multimodal Mobile Sensing via Progressive Data Orchestration
papers.abstract: Multimodal foundation models (MFMs) support generalizable inference in distributed mobile sensing applications by integrating heterogeneous data streams. However, existing MFM inference pipelines typically require complete and synchronized multimodal inputs, whereas mobile sensing streams arrive asynchronously due to network variability and heterogeneous data volumes across modalities. Waiting for all modalities increases end-to-end latency, while inference with incomplete inputs can reduce accuracy. We argue that multimodal inference should depend on the utility of available information rather than modality completeness. Based on this principle, we propose AdaModalX, a progressive multimodal inference framework that decouples inference execution from modality synchronization through runtime utility-aware orchestration. At each device, importance-aware data uploading uses a lightweight probe distilled from the edge-side MFM to allow reliable samples to exit locally while uncertain samples continue uploading. At the edge, on-demand MFM activation constructs candidates from fully received samples and, when needed, imputed features derived from partially received delayed inputs. A lightweight contribution assessor built on frozen MFM encoders estimates candidate utility and activates the MFM once the candidate meets its corresponding utility threshold. Experiments on four mobile sensing applications show that AdaModalX improves the accuracy-latency trade-off, achieving up to 26.97% accuracy improvement and up to 64.75% end-to-end latency reduction.

authors.name: Zimu Zhou
authors.institution: City University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen Research Institute

papers.title: Decomposition Bounds for MCMC with Mixture Targets: Multimodality and Heavy-Tailedness
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative mixing-time bounds for Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms targeting multimodal and heavy-tailed mixtures. The dynamics of a Markov chain are decomposed into local and global levels, and possibly weak Poincar\'{e} inequalities at both levels are combined to form convergence bounds. We apply this framework to location and scale mixtures of strongly log-concave distributions, obtaining explicit convergence bounds for random-walk Metropolis, proximal, and random-scan Gibbs samplers. For location mixtures connected along a finite path, the bounds depend polynomially on the number of components and exponentially on neighboring separation, remaining informative as the overall diameter grows. For scale mixtures, we relate the global dynamics of the chain to the isoperimetry of the log-scale mixing distribution, and illustrate the effect of heavy-tailed targets by examining inverse-gamma mixing distributions.

papers.title: Injectra: Retrofitting Extensibility into Web-Based Desktop Applications
papers.abstract: Large language models can generate code based on natural language prompts, opening up new possibilities for users to customize software and extend its functionality. This paper proposes and implements Injectra, a general-purpose code injection and feature enhancement system for existing desktop clients, suitable for applications whose user interfaces are built using embedded browser engines (such as Electron) or system WebViews (such as Tauri). Injectra decouples the host integration logic from the upper-layer enhancement code. Combining both runtime integration and pre-launch bootstrap mechanisms, it injects JavaScript, HTML, and CSS into the application's internal Web runtime environment through a unified execution channel, thereby enabling modifications to interface rendering, adjustments to interactive behaviors, and client-side functionality extensions. The system uses a command-line interface (CLI) as a unified entry point, allowing external tools, AI agents, and MCP integration layers to reuse its injection and enhancement capabilities. We tested 38 desktop applications already installed on our macOS machine; code injection was successfully completed for all of them. We demonstrated the system's capability to extend functionality through various enhanced use cases and also successfully validated the Windows version. Based on Injectra, we further developed an LLM-powered enhancement tool driven by selection and annotation: users select interface objects within the original application and describe their modification requirements; the large language model then generates the enhancement code, which is injected, executed, and rendered by Injectra. The system's source code has now been released as open source: https://github.com/sqmw/injectra.

papers.title: Post-fusion Event-aware Time-Frequency Refinement for Audio Moment Retrieval
papers.abstract: Audio Moment Retrieval (AMR) aims to locate the temporal segment within a long audio recording that semantically corresponds to a natural-language query. This task is particularly challenging because query-related audio events are often sparsely distributed and embedded in complex acoustic environments, where background sounds and acoustically similar events can easily obscure the target moments. Existing methods mainly strengthen audio-text semantic interaction to enhance the query-related information in audio frames, but seldom refine the resulting audio representations before temporal localization, limiting their ability to accurately distinguish target events from irrelevant acoustic interference. To address this issue, we propose ETR-AMR, a post-fusion event-aware time-frequency refinement framework for AMR. Specifically, an event-aware time-frequency refinement (ETR) strategy is proposed after audio-text interaction to refine fused audio frame features before temporal moment localization. ETR consists of two complementary mechanisms: time frame gating and frequency refinement. The time frame gating mechanism estimates frame-wise event relevance to emphasize query-related audio frames and suppress redundant temporal responses, while frequency refinement applies learnable time-frequency reweighting to enhance discriminative event-related frequency patterns and reduce background-dominant interference. By jointly refining fused audio frame features in the temporal and frequency domains, ETR produces more discriminative event-aware features for accurate temporal boundary prediction. Experiments on four AMR datasets demonstrate that ETR-AMR achieves superior performance compared with existing methods, especially on the high-quality CASTELLA benchmark. Duration-wise analysis further confirms the effectiveness of ETR for medium and long audio moments.

papers.title: EEGProbe: Do Vision-Language Models Really Understand EEG? A Benchmark for Signal-Grounded EEG Signals Evaluation
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) have shown strong multimodal capabilities across scientific and biomedical domains, yet their ability to understand electroencephalography (EEG) signals remains unclear. We introduce EEGProbe, a signal-grounded benchmark for evaluating whether general-purpose VLMs can extract and reason from minimally processed, channel-wise EEG without task-specific feature engineering or EEG-specific adaptation. EEGProbe contains 620 EEG-centered questions across 13 subtasks and three capability categories: EEG Signal Classification, EEG Cross-modal Alignment, and EEG Neurophysiological Reasoning. To reduce shortcut-based answering, EEGProbe preserves the temporal structure of the recordings where possible, minimizes benchmark-induced processing, and applies signal-necessity testing followed by expert verification. We evaluate 11 representative open- and closed-source VLMs under a unified zero-shot protocol. The strongest model, GPT-5.6 Sol, achieves an overall score of only 41.63\%, with cross-modal EEG alignment emerging as a major bottleneck. We further examine model behavior from a neurophysiological perspective and analyze how temporal, spectral, spatial, and physiological EEG structure relates to model successes and failures. Inference-time neurophysiological guidance can reshape model predictions by helping models recognize the neurophysiological patterns present in the input and connect them with relevant neurological knowledge, narrowing the gap between general multimodal competence and EEG understanding. EEGProbe provides a testbed for current VLMs and a basis for developing future multimodal models that can interpret EEG evidence more reliably. The EEGProbe benchmark will be publicly available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/2122ZHU/EEGProbe.

authors.name: Haozhe Zhu
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Delay-induced anomalous density-polarization relation in chiral active matter
papers.abstract: Aligning active matter can spontaneously exhibit diverse forms of ordered collective motion, and higher local density is generally expected to enhance local polarization. Meanwhile, delays in agents' responses are widespread in real active systems, raising the question of how delayed alignment affects collective motion and, in particular, whether higher local density still strengthens polar order. Here, using a chiral active particle (CAP) model with delayed alignment, we uncover a counterintuitive anomalous density-polarization relation (DPR) within droplets: the local polarization first increases and then decreases with increasing local density. Analysis of the deviation-angle dynamics reveals a delay-induced supercritical discrete Hopf bifurcation. Noise-sustained oscillations before the bifurcation and self-sustained oscillations afterward broaden the deviation-angle distribution and reduce polarization. Increasing the delay shifts the bifurcation to lower densities, enhancing the anomalous DPR in agreement with simulations. Using the nonequilibrium landscape-flux theory, we further identify the nonequilibrium flux as the dynamical origin of the anomalous DPR. Our findings not only establish time delay as a control knob for collective behavior in chiral active matter, but also offer a useful analytical perspective on anomalous density-order relations in other nonequilibrium systems exhibiting collective order.

authors.name: Jun Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: State-Message Interaction Adapter for Cross-Domain Few-Shot Segmentation
papers.abstract: Cross-domain few-shot segmentation adapts natural-image pretrained encoders to medical or industrial domains from a few pixel-annotated support masks. Within frozen DINOv3, intermediate per-head attention messages already carry target-background distinctions that baseline final-layer similarities and predictions do not consistently reflect. We propose the State-Message Interaction Adapter (SMIA) to learn how per-head messages should update each receiving token representation while keeping pretrained attention and FFN parameters frozen. Inserted right after per-head aggregation, SMIA conditions the transformation of each head's aggregated output (message) on each patch's pre-attention feature (state), allowing similar contextual messages to produce distinct or opposing updates depending on the receiving position. Because scarce support masks cover only limited state-message combinations, a shared low-rank bilinear map confines the learned interactions to low-dimensional state, message, and output subspaces. Added before each adapted block's frozen FFN, these updates yield adapted features that are refined by frozen FFNs and deeper blocks for linear readout. With only 0.51M trainable parameters and single-pass, support-free inference, SMIA achieves six-dataset mean mIoUs of 77.40% at 5 shots and 80.99% at 10 shots across 20 medical and industrial tasks, surpassing the strongest prior methods by +3.61 and +3.93 percentage points. In controlled 10-shot comparisons across three benchmarks on the same DINOv3 backbone, SMIA also outperforms parameter-matched AdaptFormer, LoRA, and ParaX with a better precision-recall balance.

authors.name: Siqi Zhang
authors.institution: PLA Rocket Force University of Engineering

papers.title: The Price of Not Planning: Parallel Sampling Depth Peaks at the Reconstruction Threshold
papers.abstract: Masked diffusion models sample the tokens of one round independently. Planned decoders first generate a coarse plan, then fill in the tokens in parallel. We ask when a plan saves rounds, how many it saves, and how fine it must be. We study this on broadcast trees: the leaves are the tokens, the internal nodes are the plan, and the edge correlation $\theta$ sets how strongly tokens depend on the plan. Errors are measured by the forward Kullback-Leibler divergence $\varepsilon$, and the lower bounds hold for every deterministic value-adaptive rule, also with learned conditionals. We show that a decoder without the plan needs of order $\min\{n,(n/\varepsilon)^{\alpha}\}$ rounds below the reconstruction threshold, where $\alpha=\log b/(4\log(1/\theta))$ rises to $1/2$ at the threshold, and that the exponent stays below $1/2$ above it (binary channel: $0.02\le\theta\le0.98$). With the plan, $\log_b n+1$ rounds suffice. In the binary model below the threshold, a plan with units of $m$ tokens needs of order $\log_b(n/m)+\min\{m,(n/\varepsilon)^{\alpha}\}$ rounds, so it gives logarithmic depth exactly when $m$ is logarithmic. A plan therefore helps most near the threshold, and only if its units are small. Exact divergence computations in the Gaussian model with up to $2^{20}$ leaves confirm these exponents below the threshold.

authors.name: Jian Lu
authors.institution: Shenyang National Laboratory for Materials Science

papers.title: Learning What Pairs Miss for Higher-Order Multimodal Alignment
papers.abstract: Contrastive learning beyond two modalities now scores the whole tuple with multilinear products, volumes, and fusion heads, critics that can represent the joint distribution. In practice these critics still behave like bags of pairs. Their negatives break at least two of the three pairs, a single pairwise check rejects them, and when most samples can be solved by pairs the higher-order term receives almost no gradient. To solve this problem, we propose CHORD (Contrastive Higher-Order Residuals with Decoys), which trains a residual against decoys drawn from a calibrated pairwise model, negatives that the pairwise model finds plausible, so that rejecting them often needs all three modalities. Drawing decoys costs one inner-product query over a memory bank, and the optimal residual is the log-ratio between the data and the pairwise model, so the decoy loss also bounds what that model misses. On M3-Mix, where one in ten training samples needs all three modalities, our CHORD improves accuracy on those samples by 21.2 percentage points over the strongest of eight baselines. CHORD also gives the best two-to-one results on every real dataset, and its residual improves other retrievers without retraining.

authors.name: Yingxu Wang
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Science and Technology

papers.title: On strongly pseudoconvex K\"ahler--Berwald manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish the equivalence between the K\"ahler--Finsler and K\"ahler--Berwald conditions for complex Finsler metrics. That is, a K\"ahler--Finsler metric always satisfies the complex Berwald condition: its Chern--Finsler nonlinear connection reduces to the Chern connection of a K\"ahler metric. We also provide, for the first time, smooth weakly K\"ahler--Finsler examples which are not K\"ahler--Berwald; and propose a condition that is formally stronger than weakly K\"ahler--Finsler, with equivalence holding in complex dimension two. Then we prove the de Rham decomposition and uniformization theorems for K\"ahler--Berwald manifolds, and show that every strongly pseudoconvex locally symmetric complex Finsler metric is both K\"ahler--Berwald and complex Einstein--Finsler. Additionally, we establish several rigidity theorems for the Kobayashi and Carath\'eodory metrics: $F_K$ is K\"ahler--Berwald if and only if it is K\"ahler; if the manifold is simply connected, then $F_C$ is K\"ahler--Berwald if and only if it is K\"ahler.

authors.name: Xiangyu Zhou
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Decompositions of the diagonal of complete intersections in products of projective spaces
papers.abstract: We study rationality of very general complete intersections in products of projective spaces. By constructing specific reference varieties and apply specialization method in the form of relative torsion orders, we extend the quintic constructions by Hotchkiss and the quartic constructions by B\"ohning, Graf von Bothmer, Pirutka and Zhang to very general complete intersections in products in every characteristic. In particular, we prove that very general quartic hypersurfaces of positive dimension admit no decomposition of the diagonal in every characteristic.

papers.title: Enhancing Exploration in Ensemble Kalman Inversion via Covariance Inflation and Projected Dropout
papers.abstract: Ensemble Kalman inversion (EKI) is a derivative-free and parallelizable method for parameter estimation in Bayesian inverse problems involving expensive forward models. It adapts Kalman filtering by repeatedly assimilating the observation data through an artificial dynamical system with identity state evolution and the parameter-to-observation map as its observation operator. However, its performance can be limited by ensemble collapse and confinement to the affine span of the initial ensemble. We propose an exploration-enhanced EKI framework that combines multiplicative covariance inflation with a projected-dropout correction of the ensemble mean. Inflation helps maintain ensemble spread, while projected dropout enables the mean to explore directions beyond the initial affine span. For linear inverse problems, we provide a discrete-time, finite-ensemble analysis of the resulting method and prove the least-squares objective converges exponentially to its minimum in expectation. Within the initial ensemble subspace, the contraction factor is independent of the conditioning of the inverse problem, and the limiting ensemble covariance provides a low-rank representation of the posterior covariance. Experiments on ill-conditioned linear systems, 100-dimensional nonlinear benchmarks, and a PDE-constrained barotropic flow inverse problem demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers.title: MagBerry: A Julia package for modeling magnon and phonon topology and transport
papers.abstract: We present MagBerry, a Julia package for studying the topology and transport of magnons, phonons, and their hybrid excitations. It combines magnetic models and linear spin-wave Hamiltonians from Sunny.jl with native modules for harmonic phonons and magnon--phonon coupling. These excitations are treated within a common bosonic Bogoliubov--de Gennes formulation. The package calculates bulk and boundary spectra, Berry curvature, and Chern numbers, and resolves the spin and phonon angular momentum carried by each mode. Transport calculations include thermal Hall, spin and orbital Nernst, and phonon angular momentum Hall responses. The package also evaluates the extended Berry curvature dipole contribution to nonlinear magnon thermal Hall transport. Relaxation-time Boltzmann theory gives heat and angular momentum currents. Examples based on published models reproduce topological magnon boundary spectra and illustrate phonon geometry and nonlinear transport. For an altermagnetic hybrid model, we extend a published study of the d-wave phonon angular momentum texture by calculating its Boltzmann transport coefficients. The resulting tensor describes how the longitudinal and transverse angular momentum currents vary with temperature and the direction of the temperature gradient.

papers.title: LoopSkill: Evidence-Bound Lifecycle Control and the Safety-Liveness Tradeoff in Coding Agents
papers.abstract: Coding agents can edit repositories and announce completion, but conversational claims do not prove that artifacts, dispatches, state versions, and authority still agree. LoopSkill is an evidence-bound lifecycle control plane with a schema-validated sole writer, durable outbox routing, artifact-bound reports, recovery, independent review, and heartbeat-gated finalization. We evaluate a locally frozen v3.3.12 integration under a common 1,800-second budget on a selected subset of SWE-bench Lite. The original 140-cell plan was administratively truncated after interim outcomes were visible, so the 60-cell analysis is exploratory and nonconfirmatory. Of 58 scored cells, blind artifact success was 7/19 for LoopSkill, 11/19 for implementation plus independent review, and 14/20 for an ordinary coding agent; two cells were apparatus null. Across 18 complete LoopSkill-versus-review pairs, the descriptive risk difference was -0.222 with exact McNemar p=0.125. No scored LoopSkill workflow finalized. The results expose a safety-liveness and fixed-budget cost tradeoff. They do not establish comparative superiority, long-horizon efficacy, or a false-accept rate.

papers.title: An improved weighted broad $L^2$ estimate in $\mathbb{R}^2$
papers.abstract: For a compact smooth plane curve $S$ with nonzero curvature and a union $X\subseteq B_R$ of unit balls satisfying a one-dimensional Katz--Tao condition, we prove $\|\mathrm{Br}_A E_S f\|_{L^2(X)} \leq C_{\varepsilon,\varepsilon'} R^{\varepsilon}|X|^{13/62}\|f\|_2$. The proof relies on a refined local broad estimate that uses density decomposition and the short frequency intervals associated with coarse tubes.

papers.title: High-quality intrinsic circular dichroism in silicon-based bound states in the continuum metasurfaces via strong coupling
papers.abstract: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) can significantly enhance spin-selective light-matter interactions. However, current BIC metasurfaces generally rely on single or multiple chiral BIC modes to enhance circular dichroism (CD), limiting their application in functional integrated devices. This paper proposes a method that utilizes the strong coupling effect in BIC metasurfaces to achieve intrinsic CD with both a high quality factor (Q-factor) and high efficiency. The metasurface is designed as a silicon-based cross-shaped nanohole array, which can simultaneously support a TM-like BIC mode and a TE-like guided-mode resonance (GMR) mode. By introducing under-etching to break the out-of-plane symmetry and tuning the in-plane asymmetry parameter, strong coupling between the quasi-BIC (QBIC) mode and the GMR mode can be induced, thereby achieving near-perfect intrinsic CD with a high Q-factor. In the strong-coupling region, the resonant wavelengths of the QBIC and GMR modes exhibit anti-crossing behavior, while the imaginary parts of the eigenfrequency cross; the corresponding Rabi splitting energy reaches a minimum of 3.16 meV, and the induced intrinsic CD achieves a maximum of 0.995 at a wavelength of 1653.9 nm, with a high Q-factor of 1083. The evolution of far-field polarization singularities shows that, under strong coupling, the {\Gamma} point corresponds to a left-handed circular polarization singularity (C-point). Furthermore, the strong-coupling-induced CD exhibits good robustness. Even under considerable variations in structural parameters, the high-Q and high-efficiency CD response is maintained. This method offers a novel design strategy for integrated chiral photonic devices and holds promise for applications in areas such as chiral sensing, chiral lasers, and nonlinear chiral optics.

authors.name: Guanhua Yang
authors.institution: Beijing Urban Construction Design & Development Group (China)

papers.title: Unit-Level Conformal Inference for Panel Counterfactuals
papers.abstract: We develop conformal inference for panel counterfactual estimators using the exchangeability of prediction errors across units rather than over time. Existing conformal methods for panels with few treated units rely on temporal properties of treated-unit residuals, which are vulnerable to strong temporal heterogeneity such as nonstationarity. We instead hold out each control unit, hide its relevant outcomes, and predict them using the same rule applied to the treated unit. Target-date estimators, including difference-in-differences and synthetic control, use controls' pre-treatment and target-date outcomes to construct the counterfactual, allowing both full conformal confidence sets and Jackknife+ intervals. Full-path estimators, including factor-model imputation and matrix completion, also use controls' outcomes at other post-treatment dates; for these, we use the Jackknife+. Both procedures yield finite-sample, period-wise confidence sets under this across-unit exchangeability, without requiring stationarity or random assignment. We characterize when the coverage holds and show why a common prediction rule alone does not ensure it. For multiple treated units, a block Jackknife+ covers their average effect, while a relabeling test is exact for sharp nulls over all treated cells. We show that the synthetic control placebo test is a full conformal test of no effect that extends to full-path estimators. We also relate our procedures to a parametric bootstrap and classify common estimators by the inference they allow. We illustrate our procedures in three empirical applications.

papers.title: A Gaussian Primitive Data Management Framework for Efficient 3DGS Trajectory Rendering
papers.abstract: Trajectory rendering, which renders novel views of a reconstructed 3D scene along a camera path, is a core operation in digital twins and autonomous inspection. Structured 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) renders a single view in real time by decoding sparse anchors into Gaussians on demand, but it renders a trajectory view by view: every view projects all anchors to select them, re-decodes anchors already requested by neighboring views, and runs all steps on the GPU while the CPU idles. We treat this as a spatial data management problem, where anchors are spatial objects, views are range queries, and decoded Gaussians are shared derived data, and propose GDM-GS, which removes redundancy at three levels. Within a view, an anchor index and an occluder index answer each view as a holed-frustum range query, so out-of-view and provably hidden anchors are never decoded. Across views, shared materialization decodes each requested anchor once per group of consecutive views while preserving each view's selection. Across processors, a hybrid pipeline balances selections between the CPU and the GPU before grouped decoding under bounded memory. Experiments on large-scale public scenes show that GDM-GS substantially reduces trajectory rendering latency while preserving image quality.

authors.name: Haolun Ma
authors.institution: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

authors.name: Lei Li
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: MetricHand: Geometry-Aware Flow Matching for 4D Hand Reconstruction in Metric World Space
papers.abstract: Egocentric hand motion provides physical motion supervision for dexterous manipulation and vision-language-action pretraining. Reliable use of this supervision requires accurate and temporally coherent 4D hand reconstruction in metric world space. Existing methods typically lift framewise estimates produced under weak perspective into world coordinates. By ignoring joint-dependent depth variation at close range, this approximation couples errors in translation, orientation, and articulation that persist after world lifting and worsen under occlusion. We present MetricHand, a geometry-aware flow matching framework for 4D hand reconstruction in metric world space. MetricHand encodes depth priors from hand-object interaction regions into joint-associated representations that preserve local spatial structure and metric scale. Fused with visual features, this geometry guides coarse metric estimation and conditions every step of temporal generation. The model jointly recovers world-space translation, global orientation, MANO articulation, and shape, while structural priors and temporal context support estimation under partial occlusion. MetricHand reduces camera-space MPJPE by 49.3% and 52.9%, absolute world-space MPJPE by 28.7% and 21.7%, and wrist localization error by 48.5% and 37.9% relative to HaWoR, respectively. World-space acceleration error decreases by 44.2% and 64.3%, demonstrating improved temporal fidelity alongside more accurate absolute localization.

authors.name: Likui Zhang
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Xiaoqing Yin
authors.institution: Anhui University of Finance and Economics

papers.title: Physics-informed and event-aware forecasting of ammonia emissions in aerobic chicken manure composting bioreactors: A PINN-PatchTST-GPR framework with symbolic dynamic extraction
papers.abstract: Predicting ammonia (NH3) concentrations during aerobic chicken manure composting provides critical feedforward signals for intelligent aeration. However, the concurrence of long-term biochemical evolution and intermittent forced-aeration pulses poses significant modeling hurdles across steady baselines, transient surges, and risk quantification. Existing data-driven models lack physical consistency, while mechanistic kinetic models struggle with environmental disturbances. To bridge this gap, we propose PINN-PatchTST-GPR, a physics-informed neuro-symbolic forecasting framework. Validated on a 28-day composting campaign across six vertical bioreactors, the framework couples a channel-independent PatchTST backbone with macroscopic kinetic constraints, dynamic physical bounds, and a Gaussian process regression (GPR) event specialist. Multi-channel sensor streams drive discrete differential equation residuals and non-negativity bounds, strictly ensuring physical plausibility. A block-split conformal prediction module yields nominal 90% distribution-free prediction intervals, while PySINDy and PySR extract low-complexity symbolic equations for quiescent and surge regimes. The model achieves an overall RMSE of 0.8256 +/- 0.0132 ppm, R2 of 0.9817 +/- 0.0006, Epeak of 1.6793 +/- 0.0725 ppm, and Etime of 0.7 +/- 0.2 min. For uncertainty quantification, it attains PICP90 of 99.792 +/- 0.047%, MPIW of 6.951 +/- 0.128 ppm, and IS0.1 of 6.968 +/- 0.128 ppm. Symbolically, PySINDy yields an RMSE of 0.4624 +/- 0.0758 ppm (R2 = 0.9896), while PySR yields 2.4084 +/- 0.0864 ppm (R2 = 0.9523). Biologically, the 20-min aeration strategy minimizes cumulative NH3 emissions. Overall, PINN-PatchTST-GPR harmonizes global forecasting, localized transient responsiveness, and risk quantification for precision composting.

papers.title: Rethinking the Verification of Machine Unlearning
papers.abstract: Machine unlearning claims require evidence that a model has removed the influence of specified training data. Yet widely deployable post hoc verifiers. infer unlearning largely from predictive behavior, the final model response that remains under the provider's control. We make this limitation concrete through Output-Level Deceptive Response (ODR), an attack that produces responses accepted by output based verifiers while preserving the original representation state. By separating output conformity from internal unlearning, ODR motivates a rethinking of machine unlearning verification, shifting the audit target from what the model returns to what changes inside it. We operationalize this shift through Representation Unlearning Verification (RUV), a gray box verifier that compares intermediate forward representations in the original and unlearned models. RUV traces a four-stage response through activation reorganization, representation displacement, neighborhood disruption, and loss of manifold support. Matched retained controls distinguish target specific responses from global model drift, while joint permutation calibration combines the four evidence views into an adaptive decision. Experiments spanning exact and approximate unlearning, class and sample level requests, multiple datasets, and diverse architectures show mean ODR deception success rates of $97.0\%$ and $97.7\%$, respectively. RUV achieves mean verification accuracies of $98.9\%$ and $94.9\%$, while rejecting $99.5\%$ and $99.8\%$ of the corresponding ODR submissions.

authors.name: Youwen zhu
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics

papers.title: UMM-JEPA: Generative Pretraining via Masked Next-Scale Representation Prediction for Unified Multimodal Models
papers.abstract: Unified multimodal models can support both visual understanding and generation, yet generative training does not necessarily improve understanding. We argue that this limitation may arise from a mismatch between the representation targeted by generation and the perceptual representation used for understanding. Conventional generation objectives primarily optimize synthesis-oriented spaces such as discrete visual codes or generative latents. We therefore introduce UMM-JEPA, which reformulates generation as progressive prediction of continuous visual-understanding representations. The model constructs a multi-scale representation hierarchy from coarse to fine, while pixel rendering is decoupled from representation pretraining and attached only afterward. Controlled comparisons show that the representation-prediction objective accounts for most of the understanding improvement, while a data-matched control leaves the group means nearly unchanged. UMM-JEPA reaches a 16-benchmark visual mean of 51.71, against 46.36 for the understanding-only Qwen-VL baseline, and the text mean also rises. Compared with discrete-code and latent-flow generation objectives, perceptual representation prediction yields stronger and more consistent transfer to understanding. Linear probes and visual-evidence interventions further reveal richer object and spatial structure and stronger use of image-specific information. These results suggest that generation can benefit understanding when it directly supervises the perceptual representations that understanding consumes.

papers.title: Selection-Aware Certification of Client-Constrained Fraud Rule Portfolios Under Synthetic Distribution Shift
papers.abstract: Selecting fraud-rule portfolios to satisfy a precision or recall floor can overfit the data used for selection. We study finite-family certification for bounded OR portfolios, comparing point-estimate selection, a fixed safety margin, and one-sided Clopper-Pearson lower bounds with Bonferroni adjustment. In a factorial follow-up with 6,400 datasets from two author-designed synthetic generators, full-validation certification reduced the held-out floor-violation rate by 29.1 percentage points on average versus full-validation point selection, while reducing deployment by 31.7 points. Compared with a fixed 0.05 margin, certification reduced violations by 22.2 points and deployment by 29.4 points; results varied across conditions. Using the full rather than half validation sample increased deployment by 17.1 points on average, without a uniform reduction in shifted-test violations. In a separate 400-dataset no-shift sweep, certification deployment rose from 61.3% to 90.2% as validation size increased from 1,500 to 15,000; no violations occurred among 2,887 deployed portfolios tested on 100,000-row holdouts. A temporal case study on the public synthetic Bank Account Fraud Base dataset used recall at a 5% false-positive-rate cap; the selected candidate pool captured less than 1% of test fraud, showing limited coverage in this setup. Together, these experiments characterize how finite-family certification changes the reliability-deployment tradeoff for bounded OR portfolios under specified synthetic conditions. The evidence covers the evaluated generators and one public synthetic BAF case study; it does not estimate performance on real transaction populations or robustness to arbitrary distribution shift. The authors revised and rewrote this abstract after receiving a draft from OpenAI Codex.

papers.title: From Retouched Images to Paired Videos: A Synthetic Benchmark for Face Video Retouching
papers.abstract: Paired unretouched/retouched face videos are costly to produce because professional editing must remain consistent over time, while releasing identifiable face footage raises privacy, consent, and governance concerns. We present DeepVFR, an initial controlled synthetic benchmark-not a new retouching architecture-for paired face video retouching. Starting from paired synthetic DeepFRR images, Wan2.2 generates mild-motion source clips, and backend-specific face transfer constructs synchronized proxy retouching targets, followed by automatic validity screening and manual visual inspection. DeepVFR contains 1,024 pairs of 150-frame clips at 30 fps, evaluated under an identity-disjoint protocol with explicit frame correspondence; release metadata will record the construction route. Within-benchmark baselines, external checkpoints applied to DeepVFR, qualitative analysis, and a 17-participant ranking study establish reference behavior in the controlled domain. The constructed targets exhibit a substantial low-preference tail in the human study. Because both streams inherit synthetic content and the targets additionally inherit commercial-API or face-transfer artifacts, the benchmark neither replaces artist-retouched captured video nor establishes synthetic-to-real generalization. DeepVFR provides a starting point for paired supervision and controlled evaluation. Data, individual study rankings, and training logs will be made publicly available upon acceptance. Broader motion coverage and real-video validation remain future work.

authors.name: Hongwei Yue
authors.institution: North China University of Water Resources and Electric Power

papers.title: An LLM-assisted theoretical model for aeroengine installation noise scattering
papers.abstract: A theoretical model is developed for the canonical problem of aeroengine fan noise impinging on, and scattering from, a nearby semi-infinite rigid plate. The model chains two Wiener--Hopf problems in different coordinate systems. The first stage solves the duct-radiation problem analytically in axisymmetric cylindrical coordinates. The second stage expands the field incident on the plate into a double angular spectrum of plane waves: the axial spectrum is inherited from the first stage, while the spanwise spectrum is generated by a Weyl--Sommerfeld expansion of the cylindrical harmonics. Each spectral component is then scattered by the plate. The mathematical crux is the coordinate transformation between the axisymmetric duct frame and the Cartesian plate frame. The core physical insight--that the Weyl--Sommerfeld identity provides an exact spectral bridge between these systems--originates entirely with the authors. The heavy algebra of translating between the two spectral representations, together with the associated numerical verification, was carried out with the assistance of a large language model (LLM), under strict human oversight and independent numerical cross-checking. This division of labour enables the LLM to handle tedious symbolic manipulation without compromising rigour. Results are presented for spinning modes radiating from a cylindrical duct with a subsonic jet into a quiescent ambient. The case study demonstrates that, under systematic verification, LLMs can accelerate tedious algebra in theoretical fluid mechanics, contributing a concrete empirical example to the broader discussion on AI's role in theoretical research.

papers.title: CARET: Clinical Assertion-Aware Residual Calibration for Medical Image-Text Alignment
papers.abstract: Medical vision--language models align radiographs with free-text reports, but radiology language distinguishes explicit findings, negation, uncertainty, and omission. Treating these report states as interchangeable during feature adaptation can change image predictions without supporting visual evidence. We introduce CARET, a parameter-efficient image-side adaptation method that retains pretrained image and text encoders and uses paired positive and negative clinical statements to define a low-dimensional semantic correction space. A bounded residual adjusts image features along these directions, while assertion-aware supervision distinguishes explicitly present and absent findings from uncertain or unmentioned ones. At inference, the adapter requires only an image; textual references remain fixed. In zero-shot classification, CARET achieves 67.80\% accuracy on CheXpert 5$\times$200 and 65.20\% on RSNA. These scores exceed the published CLEFT-LoRA results by 1.06 and 0.27 percentage points, respectively. Comparisons to literature baselines are informative but not controlled for differences in pretraining and evaluation protocols. Ablations across eight components identify the four-state distinction and assertion objective as major contributors, with task-dependent effects for nonmention preservation and pair alignment.

papers.title: Leafwise thermalization near vacuum for the inhomogeneous Landau equation with very soft and Coulomb potentials
papers.abstract:
We study the inhomogeneous Landau equation with very soft and Coulomb potentials, $\gamma\in[-3,-2]$, for data near vacuum. Unlike for $\gamma>-2$, the collisions along a free trajectory have a divergent time integral, so the dynamics is not a perturbation of free transport. It is instead organized along \emph{leaves}, the velocity distributions in the variable $z=x-tv$: on each leaf the solution follows a homogeneous Landau flow with a leaf-dependent collision rate, first far from equilibrium and then near a Maxwellian whose parameters approximately solve a compressible Euler system with the free-expansion prefactor $t^{-2}$.
  For data of size $\epsilon$, analytic in velocity and Gaussian in space, we prove global existence of classical solutions, relaxation of every leaf (not uniform in $x/t$), and convergence of the leaf parameters at rate $t^{-1}$. The solution scatters in $L^1$ to the free transport of a thermalized profile that generally remains at a fixed relative distance from the data. The $L^1$ distance to the scattering state decays like $(1+\epsilon\log t)^{-(p-3)/p}$ at $\gamma=-2$ and $(1+\epsilon t^{|\gamma|-2})^{-(p-3)/p}$ for $\gamma<-2$, where $\langle v\rangle^{-p}$ is the velocity decay of the data; these rates are sharp when the spatial profiles stay away from Maxwellians. Each leaf relaxes on its own clock: as a power of $t$ proportional to its collision rate at $\gamma=-2$, and as a stretched exponential of its clock for $\gamma<-2$. We also prove the near-Maxwellian and homogeneous results we need beyond the literature, including at $\gamma=-2$.

papers.title: Role-Separated Diffusion Transformers: Global Rule Isolation and Deterministic Sampling Manifold Compression
papers.abstract: We present Role-Separated Diffusion Transformers (RoSeDiT), a new diffusion transformer architecture that isolates the global rule from the image tokens. RoSeViT showed in visual reasoning that a vanilla ViT spreads a shared rule over all $L$ tokens at an entropy of order $Ld$, whereas an enforced controller route reduces it to order $d$. In class-conditional DiT and SiT, the class and the noise level are explicitly conditioned by adaLN, so a RoSeViT-style controller channel on the ViT side is insufficient to establish the full role separation. By introducing the adaLN listening mechanism, which makes adaLN compute under the controller's command, RoSeDiT brings the entropy theorem and role separation into the latent diffusion domain. Under the same SiT training and evaluation protocol at the same level of parameter count, RoSeDiT surpasses SiT at all four model scales at 400K steps, and RoSeDiT-L/2 even surpasses SiT-XL/2's 17.2 FID with 15.34 and 32% fewer parameters. RoSeDiT-XL/2 surpasses SiT-XL/2's 7M-step FID of 8.3 at 1.4M steps with 7.98, using one-fifth as many training steps.
