We further observe that models with the same denoising loss can have a large FID gap, which indicates a misalignment between the denoising objective and the image manifold. We formalize this phenomenon into Deterministic Sampling Manifold Compression (DSMC), a two-stage training schedule with which RoSeDiT-XL/2 surpasses SiT + REPA's 4M-step FID of 5.9 at 2.4M steps with 5.84.

papers.title: Spherical functions of the quantum symmetric pair of type FII
papers.abstract: We prove Schl\"osser's conjecture relating quantum FII spherical functions to Askey--Wilson polynomials for equal left and right coideal parameters and determine the corresponding radial operator. An explicit transport formula gives the shifted restrictions for arbitrary nonzero parameters.

papers.title: Hard or Mislabeled? Failure Screens Enrich Vision Benchmarks for Label Errors
papers.abstract: Hard vision benchmarks often keep images that strong classifiers get wrong. Since a classifier is also marked wrong when the label is wrong, such failure screens may collect label errors. We measure this on ImageNet's twice-relabeled validation set with 103 classifiers. Among the 1,892 images that all 66 supervised classifiers get wrong, 61% have a wrong label, versus 11.1% overall. The fewer images a screen lets through, the more of them are mislabeled, along approximately one curve. Fit on one model family, this curve predicts the screens of two held-out model families with a mean error of 2.4 percentage points, and replays of ImageNet-D's and ImageNet-Hard's screens within 0.1 and 6.3 points. On new pools, ImageNet-V2 and CIFAR-10, enrichment at the strictest screens is stronger than the curve predicts: on ImageNet-V2, by human relabeling, 67% of the images that all 66 classifiers get wrong are mislabeled, against 46% predicted. Screens that let models choose among only some of the classes, as ImageNet-A's does (200 of 1,000), fall below the curve. By ReImageNet, 32% of ImageNet-Hard's ImageNet images have no correct label. ScreenAudit, which comprises an audit tool, a script that rebuilds corrected answer sets for the 5,464 decided ImageNet-Hard images (of 5,646) from ReImageNet's gated release, and per-image audits of 1,198 benchmark images, will be released later.

papers.title: EEGHyena2: Fixation-Inspired Joint Lexical-Grammatical Conditional Random Field for Interpretable EEG-to-Text Decoding
papers.abstract: A sentence is built from words that carry lexical meaning and grammatical roles, and brain activity during reading reflects both. Current EEG-to-text decoders, however, let a large language model (LLM) propose and order the words, so fluent output can reflect the LLM's prior more than the recorded EEG. In this study, we asked whether fixation-linked EEG carries lexical and grammatical evidence during natural reading and how a decoder can use such evidence. Fixation-related potential analyses showed that content and function words differ reliably in group-averaged EEG but only weakly in single words. We therefore propose EEGHyena2, a structured decoder in which a bidirectional encoder inspired by StripedHyena 2 feeds a semantic head that ranks a fixed lexicon and a part-of-speech (POS) head that predicts grammatical categories; a joint word-POS conditional random field (CRF) scores a restricted candidate lattice, and a frozen Llama-2 scores the candidates in context. On two natural-reading corpora, ZuCo and ROAMM, it matched the state-of-the-art method on BLEU-1 (21.4 vs 21.3), exceeded it on ROUGE-1 F1 (23.3 vs 20.3), lowered the character error rate on ROAMM (75.3% vs 84.7%) and decoded each recording about 3-10 times faster than LLM candidate search. The CRF learned transitions that mirror English syntax, and the encoder drew local context from its convolutions and distant context from attention. Decoders can thus pool weak word-level EEG evidence across the sentence through explicit lexical and grammatical structure, with the language model adjudicating among candidates rather than generating them, which lowers decoding cost and keeps decisions inspectable.

authors.name: Chenlan Liu
authors.institution: University of International Business and Economics

papers.title: Puzzle: One Pass Is Not Enough for Open-Vocabulary Remote Sensing Segmentation
papers.abstract: Open-vocabulary remote sensing image segmentation (OVRSIS) enables the segmentation of unseen classes without additional annotation or retraining. By analyzing the predictions of existing OVRSIS methods, we find that many misclassified patches coexist with visually similar, correctly classified patches of the same class within the same image. Unfortunately, most of these methods stop after a single inference rather than using their predictions to guide further inference. Motivated by this observation, we propose \textbf{Puzzle}, a plug-and-play iterative re-inference framework that combines prediction history with a visual-similarity prior to progressively refine patch-level attention. Puzzle employs a lightweight history-conditioned controller to regulate each patch's contribution as an information source and its reliance on visually similar patches, while an adaptive stopping rule determines when to stop. It keeps the segmentation model frozen and reuses the same controller across different models and datasets without retraining. Extensive experiments demonstrate consistent performance improvements across diverse OVRSIS models and datasets, highlighting the strong transferability of Puzzle. Moreover, Puzzle can further improve the performance of SOTA methods.

papers.title: Classification of ${\rm GL}_1(D)\times {\rm GL}_{n-1}(D)$-distinguished representations
papers.abstract:
Let $D$ be a quaternion division algebra over a non-Archimedean
  local field $F$ of characteristic zero.
  We prove the conjecture of Dagar, Sharma, and Verma classifying irreducible smooth
  representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n(D)$ distinguished by
  $\mathrm{GL}_1(D)\times\mathrm{GL}_{n-1}(D)$ for $n>2$.
  These are precisely the trivial representation and the
  irreducible normalized parabolic inductions
  $\one_{n-2}\times\tau$, where $\tau$ is an infinite-dimensional
  irreducible representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(D)$ distinguished
  by $\mathrm{GL}_1(D)\times\mathrm{GL}_1(D)$.
  The proof combines a choice of cuspidal inducing factor
  with orbit conditions and multisegment methods.

papers.title: Normalized ground states of Kirchhoff equation on waveguide manifolds
EviRef: Evidence-Specific Memories for Logical Anomaly Detection across Capture Conditions
papers.abstract: Logical anomalies arise when every component looks normal but their combination violates the scene rules. In practical inspection, these rules must hold under varying backgrounds, illumination, and imaging quality, with only a few dozen normal images per scene, whereas existing methods couple normality with appearance and merge different constraints into one reference. We model logical normality as decomposable constraints and propose EviRef, a training-free method that builds a separate reference memory for each family of evidence. Component prototypes built once per scene parse images under any capture condition into one label space, on which occupancy and relation constraints are verified. Semantic constraints are verified with whole-image embeddings independent of parsing, and additional evidence such as text is admitted through a task-level gate without modifying existing memories. On VID-AD, EviRef attains a mean image-level area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 92.1% (88.9% with visual evidence alone), the highest among the compared methods under each of five capture conditions, with a standard deviation of 0.5. Even with memories built from only 20 normal images per task, it surpasses all compared methods that use 50 normal images per task.

authors.name: Wenqi Cai
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Chao Zhang
authors.institution: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs

papers.title: The Dirichlet problem for sum Hessian equations on uniformly $(k-1)$-convex domains
papers.abstract: In this paper, we mainly study the sum Hessian equation with general boundary values in the case $2\leq k\leq n$. Under the conditions that the boundary is uniformly $(k-1)$-convex, the right-hand side is monotone non-decreasing in $u$, convex in the gradient, and has a suitably small linear gradient growth, we prove the existence of a unique smooth admissible solution. The proof constructs the global subsolution and gradient barriers by using strictly $k$-convex function, and derives the boundary second-order estimates from the tangential linearizations and a duality inequality for the boundary curvature.

papers.title: Chiral-phonon-mediated spin current injection into an Ising superconductor
papers.abstract: We theoretically propose chiral-phonon-mediated spin current injection into an Ising superconductor in a chiral-insulator/Ising-superconductor heterostructure, where nonequilibrium phonons driven by a temperature gradient transfer their angular momentum to electron spins via interfacial phonon-spin conversion. Using the nonequilibrium Green's function formalism, we derive an expression for the injected spin current and show that it depends on the difference between the contributions from the two phonon branches with opposite circular polarizations. We further investigate the temperature dependence of the injected spin current density at different in-plane magnetic field strengths. In the superconducting state, the spin current density increases with temperature or in-plane magnetic field strength. In addition to the kink at the superconducting transition, a second kink appears below the transition temperature. The position of this kink is consistent with the onset of phonon-induced two-quasiparticle excitations as the superconducting gap decreases with increasing temperature. We further investigate the magnetic-field dependence of the kink temperature in a temperature--magnetic-field phase diagram.

papers.title: A Note on the Cosupport of Balmer-Favi Idempotents
papers.abstract: Let $g_x$ be the Balmer-Favi idempotent at a point $x$ of the spectrum of a rigidly-compactly generated tensor triangulated category. We study the equality $\operatorname{Cosupp}(g_x)=\operatorname{gen}(x)$ by expressing $g_x$ as a local dual. We prove the equality for the derived category of a Noetherian scheme and for the stable module category of a finite group scheme over a field of positive characteristic. For $E(n)$-local spectra we express the maps between distinct monochromatic layers of the sphere in terms of the chromatic fracture square. The height-two splitting gives the equality through height two at every prime. For a Noetherian local ring we characterize the Gorenstein property by the form of its closed-point idempotent.

papers.title: Strong Well-Posedness for One-Dimensional Quantile-Dependent SDEs with H\"older-Continuous Diffusion
papers.abstract:
We establish strong well-posedness for one-dimensional stochastic differential equations whose drift and diffusion coefficients depend on a prescribed quantile of the solution's marginal law. The diffusion coefficient is uniformly non-degenerate and H\"older continuous in space. The drift is the sum of a non-increasing H\"older-continuous component and a globally Lipschitz component of at most linear growth. Both components are Lipschitz continuous in the quantile variable. The main obstacles are the limited spatial regularity of the diffusion and the quantitative control of quantiles in terms of the $L^1$-distance between densities.
  We freeze the quantile path and combine uniform H\"older estimates for the resulting densities with a cancellation argument for the second-order diffusion perturbation. This yields an $L^1$-stability estimate for the frozen density flows and, together with uniform tail bounds and positive lower density bounds, a Volterra-type estimate for the frozen quantile map. An exponentially weighted supremum norm makes this map a strict contraction on $[0,T]$, giving a unique self-consistent quantile path and hence a unique strong solution. When the diffusion coefficient is independent of the quantile variable, the Yamada--Watanabe approximation also yields stability with respect to the initial condition.

papers.title: ProSing: Zero-Shot Fine-Grained Singing Technique Conversion
papers.abstract: We study zero-shot fine-grained singing technique conversion (STC), which applies specified techniques to selected regions of an existing singing recording while preserving lyrics, melody, timing, and singer identity. Existing singing conversion and synthesis methods offer complementary strengths in source preservation and explicit technique control, but combining both in an audio-to-audio setting remains underexplored, especially with limited technique-annotated data. We propose ProSing, a zero-shot fine-grained STC framework that adapts a pretrained flow-matching acoustic model with frame-level technique conditioning. To mitigate conditioning shortcuts during adaptation, we introduce a paired training strategy to learn generalizable technique representations. We further incorporate continuous pitch trajectories for explicit and expressive control of pitch-related techniques. Subjective and objective evaluations on unseen singers and source recordings show that ProSing achieves accurate technique control while preserving singing naturalness and singer similarity.

papers.title: Fundamental group and $Q$-curvature on open four-manifolds
papers.abstract: Let $(M,g)$ be a complete, connected, and non-compact four-manifold with nonnegative scalar curvature and nonnegative $Q$-curvature. If $g$ is not Ricci-flat, we show that both the fundamental group $\pi_1(M)$ and the integral of $Q$-curvature are finite, satisfying $$|\pi_1(M)|\int_MQ_g d\mu_g\leq 8\pi^2$$ with the equality holding if and only if $(M,g)$ is isometric to $(\mathbb{R}^4, e^{2u}|\mathrm{d}x|^2)$ with vanishing isoperimetric ratio.

papers.title: Spectral Gaps and Low-Energy Modes in Anisotropic High-Contrast PDEs
papers.abstract: We study the low-energy spectrum of high-contrast partial differential equations with strongly anisotropic inclusions. The inclusion stiffness and mass are scaled by a contrast parameter \(\eta\), while a small material eigenvalue \(\epsilon\) controls anisotropy. Stable extensions of local kernel fields give eigenvalue upper bounds proportional to the inverse contrast, uniformly in anisotropy. Additional low-energy modes arise from fields whose nonzero differential images lie in weak material directions. Each fixed family of compatible weak fields yields additional eigenvalue upper bounds of order $\epsilon+ \eta^{-1}$, provided a stable extension exists. Under discrete stability assumptions, we obtain corresponding finite element bounds for the weak modes represented by the mesh. For separable scalar diffusion, we prove norm-resolvent convergence to independent background Dirichlet and inclusion Neumann operators as contrast tends to infinity with anisotropy fixed. Numerical experiments for four PDE models illustrate weak modes and mesh-dependent spectral transitions, and scalar diffusion experiments also test spectral decoupling and eigenvalue counting.

authors.name: Lijian Jiang
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Beijing

papers.title: A unified cross-scale framework for the dynamic Waddington landscape
papers.abstract: The Waddington epigenetic landscape is a foundational concept in developmental biology, yet its quantitative formulations remain largely disconnected from the population dynamics that originally motivated the metaphor. Existing approaches typically describe either intracellular gene-regulatory dynamics or population-level cell kinetics, but rarely both within a unified framework. Here, we develop a unified PDE-integral framework that couples stochastic gene-regulatory dynamics with probability-conserving population renewal, yielding a dynamic Waddington landscape $U(\vec{x}, t) = -\log f(\vec{x}, t)$ defined directly from the evolving epigenetic probability density $f(\vec{x}, t)$. Rigorous mathematical analysis of this framework establishes its well-posedness and provides conditions for the existence and uniqueness of stationary solutions. Application to canonical gene regulatory circuits shows that proliferation is not merely a determinant of population size, but an active regulator of landscape topology. Population renewal reshapes attractor stability and transition barriers in a circuit-dependent manner, generating transient plasticity in some regulatory architectures while stabilizing progenitor states in others. Under highly proliferative conditions, these interactions further produce oscillatory ``breathing'' landscapes. Together, these results establish population renewal as an integral component of cell-fate regulation and extend the Waddington landscape from a static description of intracellular dynamics to a predictive multiscale framework linking gene regulation, cell-state dynamics, and tissue homeostasis.

papers.title: dit.xpu : Taming DiT Sparse Inference on Mobile SoCs
papers.abstract: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) enable on-device image generation and editing but incur high attention costs at high resolutions. Existing sparse attention reduces computation, yet dynamic sparsity introduces preprocessing and irregular data accesses that poorly fit mobile NPUs. We present DiT.XPU, a sparse DiT inference framework for heterogeneous mobile SoCs. DiT.XPU combines tile-aligned sparse attention with anchor-based error compensation by exploiting slowly varying dense-sparse output residuals across denoising steps. Heterogeneous XPU collaboration overlaps NPU dense attention with GPU sparse calibration, while mask-guided dataflow reduces data transfers and layout conversion by overlapping data movement with computation. Across five DiT models on two Snapdragon smartphones, DiT.XPU achieves up to 1.56x end-to-end denoising speedup over the Hexagon-NPU backend and 11.5x attention-kernel speedup over the fastest alternative, while preserving generation quality close to dense attention. Code is available at https://github.com/IF-LAB-PKU/dit.xpu.

authors.name: Jiayu Chen
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Beyond Clumsy Agentic Tool Calling: How Cueing and Spotting Make the Difference
papers.abstract: LLM-based task-oriented agents depend on tools to interact with their environments, but may overlook execution feedback, repeat ineffective calls, or persist with unproductive strategies. These behaviors can hinder agents' ability to use tools autonomously and sustain task progress. We characterize tool-use symptoms at two temporal granularities: local clumsy tool-use behaviors and tool-use detours spanning multiple interactions. Towards greater autonomy in tool use, we present ToolPulse, an online middleware supporting autonomous tool use through cueing and spotting. ToolPulse tracks execution state and temporal interaction patterns, monitoring proposed calls before dispatch and inspecting execution feedback prior to the agent resumes reasoning. It combines state-based rules, semantic sequence analysis, and interaction-feature similarity to identify intervention opportunities and provide verbal reminders, structured feedback, or context-specific advice from auxiliary models. Our process-oriented evaluation distinguishes trigger validity, behavioral cessation, and substantive correction alongside task outcomes and resource costs. Using SWE-agent with three backbone models, we evaluate 1,350 trajectories on 90 Python, C++, and Java bug-fix tasks, comparing unassisted execution with four assistance strategies. Substantive responses follow 61.6-90.9% of valid triggers for tool-use detours. Concise reminders achieve the highest observed aggregate substantive-response rate; more elaborate assistance offers symptom-dependent benefits and can be less effective. Aggregate repair outcomes remain close to baseline, with token savings in selected settings. These findings support proactive runtime assistance for autonomous tool use. The gap between behavioral adjustment and aggregate repair gains calls for careful decisions on intervention timing and assistance strategy in autonomous agents.

authors.name: Yan Liu
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Generate, Align, and Restore: MLLM-Empowered Diffusion for Generalizable Low-light Image Enhancement
papers.abstract: Low-light image enhancement (LLIE) is essential to numerous vision applications operating under adverse illumination. Despite substantial advances, real-world nighttime enhancement remains challenging due to the scarcity of strictly aligned day-night pairs and complex degradations involving extreme darkness and heterogeneous artificial light sources, leading to fragile generalization. To overcome these challenges, we propose MrLIE (MLLM-empowered reference Low-light Image Enhancement), a novel reference-based unsupervised LLIE framework that synergizes the generative and reasoning capabilities of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) with conditional diffusion. MrLIE employs the MLLM as a high-fidelity reference synthesizer and diagnostic critic, iteratively generating, diagnosing, and correcting normal-light references directly from degraded nighttime observations. Based on this, our method governs the enhancement process through two complementary mechanisms, in which a confidence offset module rectifies spatial-geometric inconsistencies for reference reliability and a structure-anchored injection scheme harmonizes aligned reference cues, low-light structural constraints, and ControlNet additive anchoring during the denoising process. Extensive experiments on diverse benchmarks demonstrate that MrLIE achieves superior perceptual quality, natural appearance, and robust generalization.

authors.name: Haoang Li
authors.institution: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

papers.title: Absence of binding for the helium anion
papers.abstract: We study the helium anion in the nonrelativistic Coulomb model with an infinitely massive nucleus and spin-$\frac12$ electrons. We prove the absence of binding, with $E^{\mathrm{F}}(3,2)=E^{\mathrm{F}}(2,2)$ and no three-electron ground state. A decomposition relative to the helium ground state and completion of the square reduce the problem to a one-dimensional variational inequality.

papers.title: Long-Horizon Causal Inertial Odometry in Multistory Buildings
papers.abstract: In indoor 3D localization inside multistory buildings, an elevator or an escalator accelerates for a few seconds and then cruises at constant velocity for tens of seconds. Gait excitation disappears, the specific force degenerates into a constant gravity reaction, and instantaneous velocity becomes unobservable within a 1-2 s window. The output of short-window learned inertial odometry consequently degrades toward the conditional mean of the training set, and vertical displacement is systematically underestimated. We propose Local-Token Causal Attention (LTCA), a long-horizon architecture that compresses each 1 s inertial window into a 1 Hz motion token and sustains, over a bounded 60 s causal cache, the motion state established at the onset event. We further introduce a pluggable barometer branch that, when online, supplies a direct elevation constraint to the vertical channel through local differential height observations, and we train it with paired online/fallback conditional training so that the barometer also regularizes the representation shared by the two modes during training. On MSIO, our benchmark of nine buildings, the RoNIN and TLIO instances reach 3D trajectory errors (ATE-3D) of 2.83/4.18 m and 2.44/5.12 m on the Seen and Unseen splits, respectively, with the barometer online. With the barometer disabled at inference, the same weights fall back to pure inertial inference and reach 3.24/4.28 m and 2.64/5.23 m, still below every native short-window baseline. We further validate the framework on the public RoNIN and TLIO benchmarks.

papers.title: Security Authentication as Protective Friction: Understanding the Dual Effects of Authentication Measures in e-Government Platform
papers.abstract: E-Government platforms, such as government credit platforms, handle highly sensitive personal data, requiring stringent security authentication (e.g., facial recognition, multi-factor verification) that protects users but impedes their experience. Drawing on Tomalin's (2023) e-friction typology and the emerging literature on beneficial design friction, we reconceptualize these authentication measures as protective friction, a theoretically distinct form of non-elective, overt, impeding e-friction that serves a security-enhancing function. We propose a dual-pathway model in which protective friction simultaneously reduces privacy-security risk perception (protection pathway) and increases effort cost (cost pathway), with self-efficacy moderating only the risk pathway. This differential pattern suggests that what matters is not users' ability to overcome friction, but their comprehension of its protective purpose, a construct we term protective mechanism comprehension. We outline a mixed-methods research design combining a survey of platform users and semi-structured interviews with platform staff at a Chinese municipal credit center to test this model. This research-in-progress contributes to IS theory by extending e-friction research from conceptual typology to empirical investigation, identifying when security friction becomes beneficial rather than burdensome.

papers.title: Program Distillation: Transferring LLM Capability from System 2 to System 0
papers.abstract: Recent studies leverage large language models (LLMs) to construct executable programs through environment interaction, feedback analysis, and code revision. However, prior work has mainly treated LLMs as optimizers, overlooking their ability to transfer knowledge across system levels. We propose Program Distillation (PD), a framework that formalizes the transfer of abilities from System 2 to System 0. During learning, the LLM provides task knowledge and draft strategies; at deployment, a student program executes the resulting policy. We show that this approach can improve performance while reducing inference time. We introduce PDBench, a benchmark comprising 27 discrete- and continuous-control tasks with fixed initial policies, and PDMetaHarness, a model-harness-independent meta-system for monitoring and guiding the learning process. The strongest model achieves a normalized mean score of 0.728, surpassing PPO (0.656) and Jev-like decision models (0.239), while running exclusively on CPUs and reducing inference costs. Our analysis shows that performance is largely driven by the first breakthrough during learning, and structural modifications have a slightly lower success rate than parameter modifications but typically yield larger gains. We further introduce style distillation, which enables interpretable stylistic control over the learning process. Overall, we present an analytical framework for PD and demonstrate its practical viability.

authors.name: Wanying Ren
authors.institution: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs

papers.title: Rigidity of complete self-shrinkers
papers.abstract: Let $X:M^n\to\R^{n+1}$ be an $n$-dimensional complete self-shrinker with constant squared norm $S$ of the second fundamental form. For $n=4$, we prove that if $f_3=\sum_i\lambda_i^3$ is constant, where $\lambda_i$ denotes principal curvatures, then $S=0$, or $S=1$ and the image $X(M^n)$ in the rigid cases is one of the hyperplane, the sphere or the standard generalized cylinders. In every dimension, under assumption of sub-exponential growth we prove the same conclusion. Without assumption of sub-exponential growth, we prove if $S\leq 3+1/\sqrt n$, then the same conclusion holds.

papers.title: VAST: Compiling Grounded Vulnerability Scenarios into Verifiable, Multi-Step Environments for Evaluating LLM Red-Team Agents
papers.abstract:
Evaluating Large Language Model (LLM) security agents requires reproducible environments whose workflow difficulty can be varied and whose failures can be diagnosed. We present VAST (Verifiable Adversarial Scenario Training & Evaluation), a declarative range compiler separating vulnerability scenarios from a compiler-introduced workflow-hardening layer. Following a post-hoc code and AST audit across all topics, the main benchmark retains 109 seed edges (45 with strict upstream CVE annotations), 72 family identifiers (62 under shared-HMAC relay grouping), 81 topic configurations (76 core plus 5 bounded execution models), and 1,387 instances (359 canonical four-gate-revalidated specs plus 1,028 seed variants) in a 42:39 partition.
  On the TopicServer compiler stratum, a budget-matched 270-episode prompt contrast across 10 compiled mechanism-family clusters (30 P2/P3/P4 instances, 40 turns, temperature 0.0) shows that glm-5.3, grok-4.7, and deepseek-v4-pro solve 12/90 instances under contract_only and 14/90 under generic_hint (cluster sign p=1.00), whereas supplying the shared workflow protocol in full_guide lifts completion to 76/90 (28/30, 23/30, 25/30; cluster sign p<=0.00391). On the separate ranges_v2 ledger, a 126-episode evaluation across 6 non-TopicServer workflows and multi-container Docker/Linux stacks solves 88/126 (69.8%) (28/42, 31/42, 29/42), while an 18-episode intervention on asynchronous Redis worker chaining (v2_02) lifts solves from 0/18 to 18/18 (100%) in 4-6 turns when installed worker modules are disclosed in GET /sched/directory. Finally, a three-seed (s in {42, 1024, 2025}) LoRA recipe comparison on Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct across 37 lineage-disjoint families (231 episodes on 33 held-out instances) yields 0/33 for Base, 1.67 +/- 2.89 / 33 for Golden SFT, and 4.67 +/- 2.31 / 33 for Header-Recovery SFT, with all solves on v2_03.

papers.title: Local asymptotic normality for Cox-Ingersoll-Ross drift parameters under high-frequency sampling and the strict Feller condition
papers.abstract: For the ergodic Cox--Ingersoll--Ross (CIR) diffusion with known diffusion scale and a fixed initial value, we prove local asymptotic normality (LAN) of the exactly sampled experiment for the drift parameters whenever the Feller index exceeds $1$, assuming only a vanishing mesh and a diverging observation horizon. This improves the previously known condition that the index exceed $(11+\sqrt{89})/2$. The proof cuts off the continuous score near $0$, recovers the remainder by exact conditional centering on each sampling interval, and transfers LAN by a conditional-likelihood argument.

papers.title: UACS: Uncertainty-Aware Clustering and Sparse Parameter Estimation for Multi-Condition Wheel Center Force
papers.abstract: Accurate wheel center force (WCF) estimation is important for vehicle durability analysis and condition monitoring, whereas direct measurement requires dedicated transducers and increases instrumentation cost and complexity. As a result, soft sensors have attracted considerable attention as a practical alternative. However, developing reliable soft sensors remains challenging due to varying working conditions, unknown condition relationships, and high-dimensional model representations. This paper proposes an uncertainty-aware clustering and sparse parameter estimation framework (UACS) for WCF signal estimation under diverse and unlabeled working conditions. A MISO-FIR model is first constructed using easily accessible sensor signals to estimate the unmeasurable force signal. The uncertainty of estimated parameters is quantified through confidence ellipsoids, and pairwise hypothesis testing is developed to identify statistically similar working conditions. Based on these uncertainty-aware comparisons, working conditions are grouped in an unsupervised manner, and sparse parameter estimation is performed within each cluster. The UACS framework simultaneously reduces the number of required models and active parameters while maintaining estimation accuracy. Experiments using real-world vehicle data demonstrate that the UACS framework achieves estimation accuracy comparable to condition-specific models while substantially reducing the number of required models and outperforming conventional distance-based clustering approaches.

authors.name: Mian Li
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: Tight Bounds for Differentially Private Cut Release
papers.abstract: We give a polynomial-time algorithm for releasing a nonnegative weighted synthetic graph under $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-edge differential privacy. Given an $n$-vertex nonnegative weighted graph $G=(V,w_G)$, the output $H=(V,w_H)$ satisfies, with probability at least $1-\beta$, simultaneously for every $S\subseteq V$, $|w_G(S,V\setminus S)-w_H(S,V\setminus S)| \le\gamma w_G(S,V\setminus S)+O\bigl((n\log n)/(\varepsilon\gamma)\bigr)$, provided that $\gamma,\varepsilon,\delta,\beta$ are at least inverse polynomial in $n$. For constant $\gamma,\varepsilon$ and $\delta=\beta=n^{-10}$, this improves the recently obtained additive error bound of $O(n\log^7 n)$ to $O(n\log n)$. We also prove a matching $\Omega(n\log n)$ lower bound. Our algorithm combines degree decomposition with private multiplicative weights, using a degree-sensitive semidefinite oracle to generate update proposals from single Gaussian samples. Each proposal is validated by a noisy check of its exact entropy decrease, and a joint R\'enyi analysis of sampling and validation avoids additional logarithmic losses.

papers.title: Are Average Estimates in Line Graphs Biased Toward Areas of Higher Variability?
papers.abstract: When estimating the average value of a data series in line graphs, do viewers systematically overweight regions of higher variability? This is the question that Moritz et al. [14] set out to answer, and across two preregistered experiments they reported evidence for a bias they termed variability overweighting. Using their released data and code, I first reproduce their reported analysis, then ask whether their inference survives an equally valid analytic choice: measuring estimation error against the average of the displayed marks of each stimulus, rather than against a reference series that, for one mark type, is never shown. Under this alternative operationalization, the effect is substantially reduced and, for one mark type, reverses. Splitting the analysis by whether variability appears in the upper or lower region of the graph further reveals an asymmetry that the original direction-corrected analysis collapses away. I argue that the deeper issue is what verbal theories leave unspecified. When a theory is silent about which operationalization it requires, the metric ends up doing the theory's arguing for it. I close with a discussion of what reproduction and reanalysis are for: not verdicts on truth, but instruments for making analytic contingency visible and for forcing theories to say more.

papers.title: Impact of Wind-Solar-Battery Growth on Electricity Prices: Reserve Scarcity and Transmission Congestion
papers.abstract: This paper asks whether sequential wind, solar, and battery storage additions that eliminate unserved energy also remove modeled reserve scarcity and transmission congestion. Thirty-one cumulative portfolio states are evaluated on a modified IEEE 24-bus system for a constructed stressed day using a 24-hour day-ahead unit commitment model with network constraints, co-optimized energy and upward reserve, chronological battery storage, and an approximation of the Electric Reliability Council of Texas operating reserve demand curve. The thermal baseline has 106 MWh of unserved energy, whereas 450 MW of wind is sufficient to serve all demand. However, with 1,500 MW of wind, the hourly modeled reserve scarcity price still reaches \$5,000/MWh because wind output declines after the system peak. Adding 1,800 MW of solar reduces the load weighted daily average modeled reserve scarcity price from \$1,136.2/MWh to \$101.2/MWh and confines modeled reserve scarcity to three evening hours. Adding 250 MW/1,000 MWh of battery storage further lowers the average to \$4.3/MWh and reduces wind curtailment from 631 MWh to 306 MWh. Transmission congestion nevertheless remains: all residual wind curtailment occurs at bus 21, wind capture prices at buses 21 and 23 differ by \$31.8/MWh, and identical battery storage plants yield normalized net energy market revenues of \$201/(MW$\cdot$day) and \$121/(MW$\cdot$day) at buses 19 and 21, respectively. These results show that unserved energy, modeled reserve scarcity, and locational congestion effects measure distinct operating conditions and should be evaluated separately but interpreted together.

authors.name: Xingpeng Li
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Real zeros of Durfee polynomials: Proof of the Canfield--Corteel--Savage conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the conjecture of Canfield, Corteel, and Savage that for every positive integer $n$, the Durfee polynomial $D_n(x)=\sum_{d=1}^{\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor}p(n,d)x^d$ counting partitions of $n$ by the side length of their Durfee square has only real zeros. More precisely, $D_n$ has a simple zero at the origin and exactly $\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor-1$ simple negative zeros. Consequently, for every $n\ge1$, the sequence $p(n,1),\ldots,p(n,\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor)$ is strictly log-concave and unimodal. As a further consequence, the Durfee square side length of a uniformly chosen partition of $n$ has the same distribution as $1$ plus a sum of independent Bernoulli random variables.

papers.title: Thouless's bandwidth conjecture: a proof by elliptic periods
papers.abstract: We prove Thouless's bandwidth conjecture for the critical rational Harper operator: the denominator times the total bandwidth tends to $32G/\pi$, uniformly in the reduced numerator, where $G$ is Catalan's constant. We identify a universal limit of the normalized even coarea density. Positive real part and evenness give an integrable endpoint bound, so the local law determines the bandwidth. An exact finite-matrix formula reduces the local law to one normalized period for each fixed odd numerator. Explicit boundary polynomials, point blowups, and intersections determine a compact genus-one family. Nodal-annulus calculations fix its period equation and hence the universal density. An exact rational Fourier identity and uniform closed-path bounds extend the result to all reduced numerators and both denominator parities. The singular matrix limit, including its subtraction and normalization, is proved separately in detail.

authors.name: Yongqiang Zhao
authors.institution: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs

papers.title: Coalgebra for True Concurrency
papers.abstract: We give the coalgebra for true concurrency along the way paved by traditional coalgebra based on bisimulation. This coalgebra is based on truly concurrent bisimulation, and we give its definition and a simple truly concurrent process algebra.

papers.title: Relax-and-Sparsify Approximation Algorithms for Sparse Ridge Regression
papers.abstract: This paper studies sparse ridge regression in the low-rank, high-dimensional setting that often arises when data collection is expensive. By exploiting the low-rank structure, we develop approximation algorithms within a relax-and-sparsify framework: solve a convex relaxation and then sparsify its solution to satisfy the original sparsity constraint. Specifically, we establish a tight rank-dependent sparsity bound for the convex relaxation by decomposing its support into two parts. This decomposition in turn motivates two approximation strategies, parameter reduction and binary redistribution, each exploiting a different part. Experiments on synthetic and real datasets show that the binary redistribution algorithms outperform the benchmarks in most instances.

authors.name: Yongchun Li
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Who May Release, Who Must Repair: Separating Authorization from Report Accountability in Personalized Services
papers.abstract: Personalized services often rely on different parties to compute results and decide whether data permissions and service policies allow delivery. The computing party's report may omit permitted inputs, leaving the delivery party to decide whether to wait for correction. Requiring correction first can delay service despite valid input permissions. Delivering first instead requires preserving responsibility for the incomplete report. We design an interface that checks input permissions separately from reporting requirements and records who must correct omissions and who may verify corrections. We evaluate three implementations on scripted histories and generated cases against a design treating omissions as authorization failures. When policy permits delivery before correction, our interface releases results that the alternative withholds while preserving repair assignments. These assignments remain in force through policy changes, so changing delivery rules does not erase earlier obligations. The interface makes the basis for release and outstanding repair responsibilities traceable across cooperating parties.

papers.title: The Sense Paradigm for World Models
papers.abstract: Latent world models predict the future in an embedding space rather than in pixels. An encoder trained only to predict collapses and maps every observation to the same point, so existing models add a mechanism against collapse, such as a target network, a variance penalty or a distribution penalty. These mechanisms keep the embedding from collapsing, but they leave its distances without meaning, and the model cannot tell a reversible transition from an irreversible one. We propose Sense, a single cross-entropy loss over the directed distance $d(x\to y)=\sum_i \mathrm{ReLU}(y_i-x_i)$ that replaces these mechanisms. The loss avoids collapse on its own, and since the encoder no longer needs the predictor, the predictor is fitted afterwards to fixed embeddings by plain regression. On four pixel environments, the return distance learned by Sense detects irreversible transitions with an AUC between 0.95 and 1.00, where LeWorldModel stays between 0.39 and 0.59. On TwoRoom, the navigation benchmark of LeWorldModel, planning with Sense reaches the goal in 100% of episodes against 91% for LeWorldModel. As the goal moves farther away, the planning failure rate of every baseline grows, while that of Sense stays near zero in Cup, Cliff and Sokoban and is the lowest of all methods in Pendulum.

papers.title: Saturation and Semi-Saturation Numbers of Joins with Complete Graphs
papers.abstract: For a nonempty family $\mathcal F$ of graphs, a graph is $\mathcal F$-semi-saturated if adding any missing edge creates a copy of some member of $\mathcal F$ containing the added edge, and is $\mathcal F$-saturated if it is also $\mathcal F$-free. The minimum numbers of edges in such graphs of order $n$ are denoted by $\operatorname{ssat}(n,\mathcal F)$ and $\operatorname{sat}(n,\mathcal F)$, respectively. We study these parameters for families of graphs obtained by taking the join of a fixed complete graph with each member of a given graph family. Assume that every member of $\mathcal F$ has at least $8$ vertices, minimum degree at least two, and no triangle containing two vertices of degree two. We give explicit sufficient conditions under which $\operatorname{sat}(n,K_t\vee\mathcal F) =\binom{t}{2}+t(n-t)+\operatorname{sat}(n-t,\mathcal F),$ and characterize all extremal graphs. For the family $\mathcal C_{\ge r}=\{C_\ell:\ell\ge r\}$ of subdivisions of $C_r$, this identity holds for fixed $t\ge1$ and $r\ge4t^2+8t+29$ and all sufficiently large $n$. For $K_t\vee C_k$ with $k\ge2t^2+3t+4$, we establish the corresponding identity for saturation when $n\ge2(k+t-2)^3$ and for semi-saturation when $n\ge56k^3+t-1$.

authors.name: Junxue Zhang
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Stripped White Dwarfs as Spectroscopic Clocks: Abundance Transitions in Partial Tidal Disruptions
papers.abstract: We investigate partial tidal disruptions of He and CO white dwarfs (WDs) by a $10^{4}\,M_{\odot}$ intermediate-mass black hole (IMBH) using three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations. We construct realistic WD structures and abundance profiles with MESA and map them into FLASH to follow the remnant response and the time-dependent composition of the fallback debris in single pericentre passages on tightly bound orbits ($e=0.9$). The element-specific fallback rates exhibit pre-peak compositional transitions that trace the WD's stratified layers. In the grazing encounter ($\beta=0.55$), hydrogen dominates the earliest returning debris, followed by helium, showing a H$\rightarrow$He transition. Deeper encounters ($\beta=0.7$ and $0.8$) penetrate the CO core and produce a He$\rightarrow$C transition, that occurs earlier relative to peak fallback and is stronger in the deeper encounter. These signatures provide a potential spectroscopic diagnostic for identifying CO-WD tidal disruption events (TDEs). We then develop a semi-analytic model for repeated tidal stripping and predict passage-to-passage compositional evolution, in which the stripped material becomes progressively enriched in heavier elements as deeper layers are exposed, leading to stronger and earlier abundance transitions in later flares. We find that WDs can survive several dozen ($\sim 30$-$80$) passages, depending on their initial mass and compactness. Our results link time-dependent abundance signatures to repeating WD disruptions and provide testable observable predictions for identifying IMBH-powered transients.

papers.title: Interactive Structured Environment Scaling for Large Language Model Agentic Reasoning
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning via environmental interaction is a cornerstone post-training paradigm for evolving large language models into autonomous agents capable of multi-turn tool use and exploration. Because the environment defines what the policy observes and how actions are verified, its structure directly bounds the capabilities an agent can acquire. Yet existing structured and retrieval environments rely on upstream pre-filtering---extracting a compact subgraph around the gold answer or retrieving fixed passages before the policy acts. We show that such pre-filtering introduces a fundamental measurement confound: because per-question subgraphs enclose ground-truth paths, they compress the candidate space by orders of magnitude and leak answer locations via local topology, allowing a question-blind degree heuristic to surface gold answers far above chance. To restore path selection, candidate pruning, and optimal stopping as genuine policy decisions, we propose RISE (Interactive Structured Environment), which transitions structured reinforcement learning from static subgraphs to full-scale interactive databases along two coupled axes. First, Decision-Space Scaling exposes the unpruned knowledge graph via a five-stage graph-agnostic typed intent adapter under a bounded call budget and a multiplicative grounding reward gate. Second, Learning-Frontier Scaling overcomes within-group variance collapse under group-normalized objectives by uniting model-independent structural tier progression with a self-evolving competence-frontier bandit. Across nineteen benchmarks and three model backbones, RISE substantially advances in-domain and unseen-schema knowledge-graph reasoning, transfers zero-shot to open-domain passage retrieval, and significantly enhances out-of-domain mathematical and logical deduction.

authors.name: Peng Yu
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Exact multiplicity for a Minkowski-curvature Neumann problem with a step weight
papers.abstract: The DEG1 challenge asks whether positive solutions of a super-exponential Minkowski-curvature equation are unique for step weights with a single sign change and negative mean. In this paper, we give a Neumann counterexample by studying $\left(\frac{u'}{\sqrt{1-(u')^2}}\right)' + \lambda a_{\mu,h}(t)(e^{u^2}-1)=0$ with $u'(0)=u'(2h)=0$, where $a_{\mu,h}=1$ on $(0,h)$ and $a_{\mu,h}=-\mu$ on $(h,2h)$, with $\mu>1$. Using the shooting method, we prove that the positive solution curve has exactly two nondegenerate folds for $(\lambda,h)$ in a nonempty open region. As $\mu$ increases through the corresponding critical values, the number of positive solutions is successively $1$, $2$, $3$, $2$, and $1$.

papers.title: Learning When to Continue and When to Stop: Termination-Aware OPSD
papers.abstract: On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) improves language model reasoning by distilling from a frozen teacher initialized identically to the student and conditioned on privileged information. However, we identify an underexplored termination mismatch in OPSD: the student fails to reliably learn when to continue and when to stop. This mismatch manifests in two opposing failure modes-premature termination, where reasoning stops before sufficient progress is made, and repetition-driven over-generation, where the model continues generating after reasoning has stalled. Our analysis shows that the teacher-student discrepancy on EOS grows during OPSD training, while length-capped trajectories are frequently dominated by unproductive repetition. To address this issue, we propose TA-OPSD (Termination-Aware On-Policy Self-Distillation), which augments the original OPSD objective with two targeted objectives. Stop/Continue Distillation addresses premature termination by explicitly aligning the teacher and student on whether reasoning should continue, while Repetition-Aware Unlikelihood Training addresses repetition-driven over-generation by discouraging repetitive continuations in the student's failed trajectories. The resulting objective improves termination behavior from complementary directions: continuing when further reasoning is needed and stopping when reasoning becomes unproductive. Experiments on mathematical reasoning tasks with Qwen3 (1.7B/4B/8B) show that TA-OPSD consistently outperforms OPSD and other baselines across all three model scales. Beyond the performance gains, ablation and behavioral analyses show that the two proposed objectives effectively mitigate their corresponding termination failures, reducing both premature termination and repetition-driven over-generation.

papers.title: A new formula for Moore-Penrose inverses of rank-deficient Toeplitz matrices
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new formula for the Moore-Penrose inverses of the rank-deficient Toeplitz matrices, based on the quasi-direct decompositions of Toeplitz matrices. Numerical examples are presented to verify the validity and the efficiency of our method.

papers.title: Finite sums of weighted composition operators on the Fock space
papers.abstract: We study finite sums of weighted composition operators on the classical Fock space. We show that no cancellation phenomenon occurs when the composition symbols are pairwise distinct: such a sum is bounded, compact, or belongs to the Schatten class S_p, 0<p<\infty, if and only if each summand has the corresponding property. We also obtain two-sided essential norm estimates and quantitative Schatten norm comparisons for fixed distinct nonconstant symbols. As an application, we obtain corresponding boundedness, compactness, and Schatten-class results for finite sums of generalized Volterra-type integral operators.

papers.title: Sparse Rotatable Arrays (SRAs) for Cell-Free MIMO: Network-Wide Design of Antenna Activation and Panel Orientation
papers.abstract: This paper investigates a sparse rotatable array (SRA)-enabled cell-free multiuser multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) system. Under a network-wide antenna activation budget, distributed access points (APs) select active antenna elements from their installed arrays and adjust panel orientations, enabling joint control of sparse array apertures and antenna directivity. To avoid frequent hardware reconfiguration in response to instantaneous channel variations, we formulate a two-timescale stochastic optimization problem to maximize the expected minimum-user rate. Long-term antenna activation and panel orientations are optimized based on user spatial distributions and statistical channel state information (CSI), while short-term precoders adapt to instantaneous CSI. Under line-of-sight (LoS) propagation, we derive the optimal single-user antenna allocation, characterize the two-user max-min signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) and establish conditions for discrete activation and panel rotation to attain the continuous-position benchmark, and obtain a closed-form multi-AP zero-forcing (ZF) allocation benchmark under a continuous antenna-count relaxation. For the general mixed-integer nonconvex stochastic problem, we develop an alternating algorithm based on sample-average approximation (SAA), integrating uplink-downlink (UL-DL) duality for short-term precoding, weighted minimum mean-square error (WMMSE) surrogates for panel-orientation optimization, and multi-start greedy search for antenna activation. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed design outperforms the fixed-array benchmark, improves all-user service reliability with fewer active antennas, and adapts effectively to nonuniform user spatial distributions.

authors.name: Ailing Zheng
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

authors.name: Qingqing Wu
authors.institution: Affiliated Hospital of Guizhou Medical University

authors.name: Xiyuan Liu
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Organic-Inorganic Composite Materials

papers.title: Diagnosis and Recovery in AI Workflows with Scarce Expert Capacity
papers.abstract: We study sequential decisions in AI workflows and other automated execution systems where failures of uncertain origin require recovery under limited shared expert capacity. Recovery choices affect future diagnostic demand, while expert availability changes which recovery actions are worthwhile. We coordinate diagnostic requests, expert dispatch, and checkpoint-based recovery to maximize expected net operating value. A finite-horizon model tracks uncertain error locations, remaining time, and shared expert capacity. Structural analysis shows how competition for diagnosis changes unaided recovery. When a full rebuild from checkpoint 0 is the best unaided fallback after failure, a larger expert pool can justify retaining more work despite a lower chance of immediate success. Capacity can also raise net operating value before fixed staffing costs while reducing diagnostic hours when advice is requested only after a failed trial. Our Diagnosis-Resource-Recovery Control (DRRC) policy coordinates these decisions through local recovery lookahead and estimates of service requirements and remaining time; its learning-augmented variant uses task-specific quality and duration estimates. In controlled simulations, larger pools draw more requests before repair, and selective diagnosis raises net value chiefly by reducing recovery costs. In a digital twin based on 177 software defects, DRRC with reference-assisted diagnosis increases mean timely completion by 3.27 percentage points and mean net value by 1.85% relative to automated recovery, although the net-value advantage remains uncertain across repositories. Expert capacity changes when workflows seek advice and how much work they preserve. Expansion may raise or lower diagnostic hours, so capacity and recovery design should be assessed jointly by their contribution to net operating value.

authors.name: Jiheng Zhang
authors.institution: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

papers.title: Weighted unit equations in cyclic cubic orders
papers.abstract: We study nonrational integral units $u,v$ satisfying $au+sv=1$, with integers $1<a<s$, in varying cyclic cubic fields. The ratio $u/v$ generates the joint order $R=\mathbb{Z}[u,v]$ and gives effective finiteness for each fixed first weight and each fixed gap. Consecutive weights yield exactly seven simultaneous-isomorphism classes, at $a=2,4,13$; in every proper order among them, $\{-1,u,v\}$ generates $R^\times$.

papers.title: Fractional integration with singularity on the light-cone
papers.abstract: In this paper, we solve a classical problem investigated by Gelfand and Shilov on a family of fractional integral operators whose kernels have singularity appeared on the light-cone in R^n+1. As an implication, we obtain a desired sharp estimate for the L^p to L^q-boundedness of cone multiplier operators having a negative order.

papers.title: A Graph Theory Assisted Method for Determining Limiting Probability Distributions of Higher Order Markov Chains
papers.abstract: This paper presents a graph theory assisted method that checks a sufficient condition for the existence of the limiting probability distribution of a higher order Markov chain and identifies this distribution when the condition is satisfied. This method is more effective as compared to the direct verification of the condition since the latter hinges wholly on computations of the full spectrum on a large-size transition matrix. Even though the graph theoretic tools employed here are well known, their utilization in the context of a higher order Markov chain is new. This method is also implemented as an easy-to-use MATLAB function {\tt gtam}. Several illustrative examples are provided too.

papers.title: Approximate $K$-Conjugacy of Minimal Cantor--Circle Extensions I: The Rigid Case
papers.abstract: We study approximate $K$-conjugacy for minimal Cantor--circle extensions with arbitrary circle homeomorphism cocycles, allowing orientation reversal. Under the assumption of classical rigidity, we show that two such systems are approximately $K$-conjugate if and only if there exists an ordered unital graded $K$-theory isomorphism satisfying the finite coefficient $K$-condition. Our approach combines dynamical corrections along Kakutani--Rokhlin towers with the classification and uniqueness theory of $C^*$-algebras. Moreover, the crossed-product isomorphisms implementing approximate $K$-conjugacy can be chosen as inner perturbations of a fixed isomorphism and its inverse.

authors.name: Huaxin Lin
authors.institution: Shanghai Institute for Mathematics and Interdisciplinary Sciences

authors.name: Sihan Wei
authors.institution: Shanghai University of International Business and Economics

papers.title: Contraction Analysis and Control of Polynomial Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: Contraction analysis has found broad applications in synchronization, tracking, observer design, and nonlinear feedback control. However, establishing contraction conditions for polynomial dynamical systems remains challenging due to their state-dependent Jacobians. In this article, we develop a tensor-based framework for contraction analysis of polynomial dynamical systems by exploiting the structure of orthogonally decomposable (odeco) coefficient tensors. By transforming the dynamics into modal coordinates, we derive necessary and sufficient semicontraction conditions and characterize state-dependent semimetrics. We establish fundamental limitations on exponential contraction and prove polynomial decay of differential displacements on forward-invariant regions. To accommodate more general polynomial dynamical systems, we extend the framework to include linear dynamics and non-odeco tensor perturbations, deriving computationally tractable contraction certificates with explicit robustness guarantees. We further develop convex feedback synthesis conditions based on linear matrix inequalities for general input matrices. We demonstrate the effectiveness and computational scalability of the proposed framework through numerical experiments on both synthetic systems and nonlinear elastic relaxation models.

authors.name: Anqi Dong
authors.institution: China Automotive Technology and Research Center

papers.title: Flow Matching for Sampled-Data Control of Angular Distributions
papers.abstract: Synchronization and clustering in oscillator networks depend on the joint distribution of the phases. Flow Matching can steer this distribution by learning an angular velocity field from shortest arcs between paired configurations. Each arc is traversed at constant speed, yet the resulting field can vary along its own trajectories. In this article, we study how to control angular transport on the circle and product torus when each controller evaluation selects a rate to hold until the next update. Using the same local velocity samples, Flow Matching learns the instantaneous angular rate and MeanFlow learns its average along the reference trajectory over the control interval. Under direct angular actuation, holding the exact average gives the reference displacement. We relate the displacement error of holding the instantaneous rate and the training residual of MeanFlow to the conditional covariance of the teacher velocities. Experiments with 100 phases show that endpoint pairing affects the comparison. MeanFlow gives smaller one-step errors under minibatch pairing, while permutation alignment reverses the ranking for exchangeable phase clusters.

authors.name: Anqi Dong
authors.institution: China Automotive Technology and Research Center

papers.title: Uniqueness and nondegeneracy of positive solutions for a class of fractional Schr\"odinger equations in $\mathbb R$
papers.abstract: We study positive solutions $u\in H^s(\mathbb R)$ of the fractional Schr\"odinger equation $(-\Delta)^su+\lambda u=f(u)$ in $\mathbb R$, where $0<s<1$, $\lambda>0$, and $f$ is a general nonlinearity such that $f(t)/t$ is increasing. We prove that, under a single concavity condition on an auxiliary function, positive solutions are unique up to translations. The result applies to all positive solutions rather than only to ground states, and it allows $f'$ to be unbounded below at zero. It covers pure powers, sums of powers, logarithmic and saturable nonlinearities, for suitable ranges of the parameters. We further prove that every positive solution is nondegenerate, with the kernel of the linearized operator spanned by $u'$, and that it has Morse index one. If moreover $f(\sqrt h)/\sqrt h$ is concave, then for $1/2\le s<1$ a positive solution with prescribed $L^2$ norm is unique together with its Lagrange multiplier. The proofs are purely variational, using neither a continuation argument in $s$ nor the nondegeneracy of the linearized operator. Our method rests on the convexity of the action along an interpolation between symmetric decreasing functions that preserves a suitable integral quantity, and this convexity allows us to identify every positive solution as a constrained minimizer. For $1/2\le s<1$ we use the height interpolation of Delgadino, Yan and Yao, while for $0<s<1/2$ we introduce a new two-level interpolation.

papers.title: Efficient scheduling of particle annihilation for long-time Wigner simulations
papers.abstract: Particle annihilation (PA) plays an indispensable role in alleviating the numerical sign problem in long-time simulations with the Wigner branching random walk (WBRW) method. However, the effect of PA frequency on long-time accuracy remains poorly understood, leaving its choice largely empirical. To provide systematic guidance for PA scheduling, we establish an overall error estimate for PA through a uniform mesh, separating WBRW variance, resampling variance and squared bias. The analysis shows that, beyond merely controlling particle growth, PA replaces the exponential-in-time variance bound with a linear-in-time bound, thereby alleviating the numerical sign problem. It also reveals bias-variance trade-off induced by PA frequency: frequent PA limits variance but can increase accumulated bias. More importantly, building on the newfound error structure, we propose a variance-constrained cost optimization strategy for adaptive PA scheduling across several PA methods. An intrinsic-time reparameterization provides a common clock for variance control, PA scheduling, and branching dynamics under time-dependent potentials. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical variance behavior and bias-variance trade-off, and results of our schedule populate the low-cost regime of the empirical Pareto frontier objecting to balance accuracy and efficiency.

papers.title: A Testing Method for Detector Error Models in Quantum Error Correction Compilers
papers.abstract: A quantum error correction (QEC) compiler produces, from a code and a noise model, both the physical circuit to execute and a detector error model (DEM). The DEM lists the probability of each error mechanism and the measurements it flips. Decoders consume the DEM without verification, so a defect that describes the noise incorrectly calibrates the decoder against wrong rates and silently degrades the logical error rate. Existing techniques for testing quantum software judge correctness by crashes or by statistics of sampled outputs. DEM defects that only distort rates lie below what sampling can resolve at the error rates where QEC operates. We present DEMVal, a testing method that validates each model the compiler emits against a reconstructed reference, with rates obtained from outside the compiler under test. It compares the two models exactly, so its sensitivity is independent of the physical error rate. The reference can be built in three ways that jointly cover the pipeline from source program to emitted model. Applied to NVIDIA's CUDA-Q QEC, Riverlane's Deltakit, and the deq component of Microsoft's QDK-EC, DEMVal found six defects, all confirmed by the developers and fixed. Sampling could have exposed only the four defects that drop, merge, or misplace mechanisms, and exposing all four requires millions of samples per experiment. Even analytically optimal moment tests miss the two rate-level defects, while exact model comparison detects all six with no samples. To our knowledge, DEMVal is the first systematic testing method for the error-model semantics of QEC compilers.

papers.title: What the Averages Hide: Monocular Metric Depth Models Still Fail in Everyday Scenes, Mostly on Scale
papers.abstract: Zero-shot monocular metric depth models are evaluated by averaging metric and scale-aligned scores across datasets. Averages cannot show how many images still have severely wrong metric depth, whether depth is under- or overestimated, or whether different models fail on the same images. We propose an evaluation built on per-image results: the failure rate (metric $\delta_1$ < 0.5); scale-aligned metrics for structure, and the bias, dispersion and absolute error of the alignment scale for scale; and a cross-model comparison that separates shared from model-specific failures. We apply it to 11 recent architectures with and without ground-truth intrinsics (18 model evaluations) on the 7 everyday-scene benchmarks (4,406 images) used by MoGe-2. Metric depth estimation is not solved in everyday scenes, and the remaining difficulty is mainly scale: the best of the 18 evaluations still has a failure rate of 7.7% (datasets weighted equally); pooled over all failures, 78.8% have intact structure, and after scale correction 98.3% no longer fail. Images failed by at least 6 architectures make up 7.3% of the data, concentrated on HAMMER and DIODE; even when selected only by architectures of other families, they hold 34% to 40% of the error of the top 6 models, against 14% to 18% for as many random images from the same datasets. Adding objects reduces the scale error of most models; ground-truth intrinsics and, in most families, larger models reduce the failures but do not remove them. We recommend reporting failure rates, structure and scale separately, and results stratified by how many models fail. We will release the code, the per-image results with shared-failure labels, and two diagnostic sets built from TUM RGB-D.
