These results show that GRAFT provides a simple and effective mechanism for reusing learned capabilities across language and multimodal models in continual learning.

papers.title: Earth World Model: Physics-constrained latent dynamics for forecasting and environmental scenario analysis
papers.abstract: World models have been widely applied to multi-agent planning and forecasting, but exogenous environmental changes are rarely incorporated as replaceable drivers in a unified state-evolution process. This limits assessment of whether environmental perturbations propagate through physical systems with faithful dynamics. We propose the Earth World Model (EWM), an Earth-centred forecasting framework that compresses heterogeneous multi-source observations into a reusable low-dimensional latent state representing the system's history and current condition. Given explicit exogenous drivers, a shared transition operator recursively updates the latent state, and physics-constrained decoding produces multi-step forecasts. Replacing the drivers enables environmental scenario analysis and evaluation of dynamic-response fidelity. We evaluated EWM for power forecasting and environmental-perturbation response at six photovoltaic sites and one wind-power site. Across four photovoltaic sites and three forecast horizons, three independent training runs yielded mean $R^2$ values of 0.8578-0.9095. In a separate six-site decoder ablation, the mean net per-unit response $\rho$ under the prescribed irradiance intervention increased from 0.180 with a multilayer perceptron decoder to 0.922 with an analytic physical decoder, close to site- and horizon-specific analytic references. The wind model achieved an injection elasticity of $0.9990 \pm 0.0006$, while pre-intervention outputs remained unchanged. These results show that forecast fit and intervention response should be evaluated separately and that the tested EWM configurations preserved response amplitude and temporal boundaries under the prescribed interventions.

authors.name: Jinnong Liao
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Robotics and Systems

papers.title: ECOD: Experience-Calibrated On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Turn Agents
papers.abstract: Sparse and delayed rewards make reinforcement learning challenging for long-horizon language agents. On-policy distillation (OPD) complements environmental rewards with dense teacher feedback on student-generated contexts. Standard OPD can misalign supervision with relative teacher competence, student trajectory outcomes, and the temporal structure of task execution. Recent variants adjust guidance through divergence-based weighting and temporal schedules, while joint calibration from task-completion experience remains underexplored. We introduce Experience-Calibrated On-Policy Distillation (ECOD), which allocates teacher supervision at the task, trajectory, and turn levels. ECOD compares teacher and student success-rate posteriors under matched task conditions, restricts direct supervision to failed student trajectories, and derives a temporal prior from successful teacher lengths. The resulting weight applies to teacher losses or teacher-derived advantages. We evaluate ECOD on ALFWorld and WebShop with Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. Under matched teacher settings, ECOD improves standard OPD by up to 4.06% in relative ALFWorld unseen success. Across both model scales, ECOD-assisted SOD, TCOD-F2B, and ATOD configurations yield average paired relative gains of 6.20% on ALFWorld unseen and 7.05% on WebShop, with WebShop gains ranging from 2.29% to 21.60%. These results support experience-calibrated supervision allocation as a reusable mechanism across distinct distillation objectives.

authors.name: Yan Gao
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: The governing equation for probability density of transition path time
papers.abstract: Transition path time is the time it takes a system to move from the initial state (State A) to a final state (State B) without recrossing back to State A in between. The transition path time is probabilistic in nature, and considerable research has been devoted to studying its distribution. In this paper, we derive a governing integral equation that expresses the density of the transition path time in terms of the probability density of the first passage time, which is well understood. An efficient numerical method is provided to solve this governing equation. Several numerical examples are presented to validate the governing equation and to compare the densities of the transition path time and the first passage time.

authors.name: Yan Liu
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Xu Sun
authors.institution: Jiangsu Key Laboratory for Chemistry of Low-Dimensional Materials

papers.title: WL-Headset Law: Projecting Future Headset Evolution from a Decade of Display and Mass Data
papers.abstract: Tracking a decade of headset display and mass changes can inform forecasts. However, comparing headset resolution requires pixels per degree (PPD), which is often unreported and estimated using unclear assumptions. Therefore, we compile the open-source, evidence-linked HMD Resolution and Mass Database (HRMD) with 241 configurations from 2016--2026 and introduce structure- and axis-aware robust calibration (SARC) to estimate missing central PPD. Compared with official PPD, SARC reduces PPD estimation error from 14.8% for traditional geometric estimation to 3.2%. Based on HRMD, we introduce the Weight-Linked Headset Law (WL-Headset Law), which models PPD by year, mass, and category. The law reveals 7.4% annual PPD growth at fixed mass and category. Meanwhile, head-worn mass fell by 6.5% annually after category adjustment. At an eyeglass-like mass of 30g, the law projects average central PPD of 60 (normal visual acuity) around 2035 and 120 (higher acuity) around 2044 if trends persist.

authors.name: Jialin Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Hai-Ning Liang
authors.institution: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

papers.title: Separating learning from search and feedback in budgeted inverse design of periodic unit cells
papers.abstract: To design a periodic material, engineers choose the shape and dimensions of a repeating cell to meet target properties. With few simulations, the benefit of a learned predictor can be hard to separate from the effect of which designs the search tries and how it uses simulator feedback. We compare two ways to predict properties in a library of 80 cell architectures, with up to 30 simulator calls per target. For each architecture, both searches use a table of predicted properties at different dimensions. One fills the table with predictions from neural networks. The other fits a simple model to the existing simulations for that architecture. Both searches use the difference between the predicted and simulated properties to adjust the next design. We generated 200 targets from simulated designs after fixing the analysis plan. The two searches showed no detectable difference in how often they matched all three properties within 2% or in the mean error of their returned designs. The upper limit of the 95% confidence interval for the gain in overall success rate was 4.5 percentage points. Follow-up controls on these targets changed success from 83.5% to 36.0% with a degraded table and 96.5% with an oracle table. In separate tests, using the simulation result to adjust the next design increased success for both types of table. Results cover one library and a coarse 32^3 voxel simulator. Designers can use this comparison to judge what a learned predictor adds when the search, feedback and budget are the same.

authors.name: Shaoliang Yang
authors.institution: Obstetrics and Gynecology Hospital of Fudan University

authors.name: Jun Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Convergence rate of periodic homogenization for convex Hamilton--Jacobi equations with super critical viscosity
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to studying the convergence rate in periodic homogenization of the viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation (with supercritical viscosity index $\sigma>1$) \[ \partial_t u_\varepsilon+H(x/\varepsilon,\partial_xu_\varepsilon)=\varepsilon^\sigma\Delta u_\varepsilon,\quad (x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}_+,\ \] subject to a given initial datum. For Tonelli Hamiltonians $H$, the solution $u_\varepsilon$ is proved to converge to a certain $u:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ (solving the effective problem) in the optimal rate $O(\varepsilon^{\min\{\sigma-1,1\}})$. We also obtain a rate for the case of non-convex Hamiltonians and discussed its optimality therein.

authors.name: Jianlu Zhang
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: From Vision to Interaction: Evaluating Dynamic Social Intelligence of VLM Agents in ALIVE-World
papers.abstract: As AI agents are increasingly deployed in real-world applications and take on social roles, dynamic social intelligence, the ability to continuously perceive multimodal cues, infer latent cognitive states, intervene through embodied actions, and ultimately achieve social goals, has become essential. However, existing evaluations largely fragment social intelligence into text-based abstractions, static reasoning tasks, or embodied simulators that lack social dynamics. These approaches fail to capture the multimodal, continuous, and interpersonal complexity of authentic human interactions. To bridge this gap, we introduce ALIVE-World, an embodied simulation environment supporting dynamic multimodal interactions encompassing egocentric vision, language, and non-verbal action. To provide socially grounded interactive feedback, we populate this environment with counterpart agents driven by a profile-conditioned, dual-system (intuitive-affective and logical-cognitive) architecture. Building upon this platform, we propose ALIVE-Bench to transform the assessment of social intelligence into a trackable quantitative framework. By deeply leveraging underlying environmental states and agents' internal variables, ALIVE-Bench systematically evaluates Vision-Language Model (VLM) agents across four critical dimensions: perception, understanding, influence, and outcome. Extensive evaluations reveal that dynamic social intelligence is fundamentally multi-dimensional and scenario-dependent. We identify a critical bottleneck between upstream perception and downstream social intervention, exposing VLM vulnerabilities in fine-grained proxemic awareness, adaptive intervention, and multi-party coordination. By uncovering these limitations and the diverse interaction strategies they produce, this benchmark provides actionable insights for the future behavioral alignment of multimodal agents.

papers.title: Precise Analytic Boundaries and Positive Symplectic Paths in the Stability Diagrams of Elliptic Relative Equilibria
papers.abstract: We investigate the dependence of the linear stability of elliptic relative equilibria on the mass parameter and eccentricity. Using a periodic matrix Riccati decomposition, we derive explicit analytic curves separating hyperbolic--hyperbolic and complex--saddle spectra. The construction applies to the Lagrangian, Euler--Robe, and $(2+2)$-body families. A Hermitian Riccati factorization also yields an eccentricity-independent sufficient condition for positivity of the associated operators under every unit-circle boundary condition, and hence for hyperbolicity of the monodromy matrix. Finally, we construct an explicit lower bound for the second antiperiodic degeneracy curve by a finite trigonometric test function. This bound agrees with the value and tangent of the degeneracy curve at the circular limit. Together, these results provide analytic descriptions and estimates for distinct spectral boundaries in the stability diagrams.

authors.name: Jian Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: tsspiral: An R Package to Create Circular Versions of Time Series Plots
papers.abstract: `tsspiral` is an open-source R package that introduces a circular approach to time series visualisation using polar coordinates. We refer to this circular representation of time series data as a spiral. `tsspiral` provides a collection of `ggplot2` geometries for creating a spiral representation of time series data. In our approach, we arrange observations around a circle. Each year is represented by a circle, with the angular position corresponding to the day of the year, and successive years appear as concentric rings. This arrangement facilitates the exploration of periodicity, seasonality, and recurring temporal patterns, particularly in long time series. The package also supports temporal hierarchical visualisations to compare patterns across time scales. By bringing polar-coordinate-based visualisation into routine time series analysis, `tsspiral` offers a practical tool for exploring temporal patterns and communicating complex time-dependent structures. Rather than treating spiral plots as standalone graphics, our approach brings them into the grammar of graphics framework, enabling users to explore temporal patterns through a broader range of visual encodings.

papers.title: Midsagittal Corpus Callosum Parameterization: A Framework for Spatially Detailed Diffusion MR Imaging Analysis
papers.abstract: The corpus callosum (CC) is the largest white matter structure in the human brain and plays a central role in interhemispheric communication. Diffusion MR imaging is widely used to investigate microstructural organization, but commonly used analysis approaches have important limitations. Voxel-based methods rely heavily on accurate inter-subject registration and smoothing choices, tract-based spatial statistics (TBSS) restricts the analysis to a narrow white matter skeleton, and parcellation approaches reduce spatial detail by averaging diffusion measures over relatively large regions. In this work, we introduce a parameterization framework for the analysis of the midsagittal CC that resamples the structure using a standardized grid of points, establishing a geometric correspondence across individuals without explicit inter-subject registration. In a test-retest dataset, the method provided stable measurements while covering most of the midsagittal CC, and sensitivity analyses showed that results in the central CC changed little under perturbations of the input CC mask, whereas peripheral regions were more sensitive. The framework was further evaluated in group analyses of aging and Alzheimer's disease in datasets that differ in acquisition protocol and spatial resolution. Effect-size maps and quantitative comparisons showed that its results were largely consistent with TBSS and parcellation-based analyses in the overall spatial pattern of effects, while also revealing additional spatially localized differences. These findings suggest that the parameterization provides a simple, computationally efficient, and spatially detailed approach for investigating midsagittal CC microstructure, offering a structure-specific complement to whole-brain and region-based methods.

papers.title: Whole-Slice Misses Escape Round-Trip Filtering and Volumetric Dice in a Source-Free Flow-Matching Segmenter
papers.abstract: SymmAdapt, a source-free flow-matching segmentation pipeline, relies on two quality gates: a round-trip filter on pseudo-labels and volumetric Dice in evaluation. We audit both on 120 AMOS CT patients unseen in training and adaptation. The model often misses the spleen on whole slices, severely so in 30.0% of patients. The round-trip filter passes 83.31% of these lost slices, because its round trip reproduces the miss and the filter scores only organs present in the pseudo-label. Volumetric Dice depends on how much volume is missed, not where, and self-training leaves 96.5% of lost slices lost (96.6% on a second noise stream). A model-free repair, Chain-and-Fill, met all pre-registered endpoints on 119 further patients and could not be distinguished from SAM 2 propagation in severe-group gain, with 1/357 rather than 63/357 harmed patient-seed pairs. Reporting lost slices next to volumetric Dice makes the error visible at no cost.

papers.title: TyphoonWorld: A Residual Token World Model for Probabilistic Forecasting of Typhoon Imagery
papers.abstract: A satellite forecast of a typhoon should give a low-error picture of the next two days, together with an ensemble whose members are coherent fields and whose spread responds to the storm at hand. A small direct regression network already gives the lowest squared error on held-out storms, so a generative model has to earn its cost through the part of the future that the regression smooths away. We present TyphoonWorld, a discrete-token world model that generates only that part. Conditioned on tokens of the regression forecast, the latest frames and the best-track state at forecast time, it samples residual fields lead by lead, and members add these residuals to the regression center. We compare it under one protocol with per-pixel Gaussian networks, a diffusion model of the same residuals, residuals from other storms and an unconditional token world model, on 276 forecast windows from 46 held-out storms of Digital Typhoon. TyphoonWorld matches the squared error of the regression, lowers the CRPS of the area colder than 220 K, a direct measure of deep convection, by 14 to 39% against every other ensemble, and ties its spread to forecast error as closely as the Gaussian network, with a correlation of 0.78 across windows. It uses 56% of the parameters of the unconditional world model.

authors.name: Tianyi Li
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Estimation of Heterogeneous and Functional Cox Model
papers.abstract: Cox or proportional hazards model is the most commonly used regression model for failure time data and has been extended in various ways. In this paper, we consider inference for a heterogeneous and functional Cox model with the focus on estimation of the latent heterogeneous or subgroup structure based on interval-censored failure time data. For the problem, we propose a novel sieve maximum likelihood estimation procedure with the uses of B-splines and Bernstein polynomials. For the implementation of the proposed method, an EM algorithm is developed and the number of subgroups can be determined in a data-driven manner. Also the resulting estimators are shown to be consistent and asymptotically normal, and an extensive simulation study shows that the proposed method works well in practice. Finally, we apply it to an Alzheimer's Disease study that motivated this investigation and provide some new insights about the roles of imaging and clinical factors in the progression of Alzheimer's disease.

authors.name: Jianguo Sun
authors.institution: Tianjin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: SemMask: Semantic-Prioritized Progressive Masking for Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract: Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) are designed to enable globally parallel generation. However, in practice, they often exhibit pseudo-autoregressive behavior and a function-word-first bias, which undermines their performance on tasks such as text writing and code generation that benefit from global planning and parallel decoding. To address this, we propose SemMask, a novel fine-tuning paradigm that leverages a semantic-prioritized progressive masking strategy to encourage the model to decode high-information semantic tokens early and globally, thereby enhancing its global planning and parallel generation capabilities. Specifically, we first use the gradients of the original DLM with respect to each token to identify semantic tokens. During masking, these semantic tokens are preserved with priority, establishing a progressive generation order in which semantic tokens are decoded prior to function tokens. Meanwhile, we adjust the loss weight for semantic tokens to further reinforce their early prediction. Experimental results show that SemMask achieves quality comparable to strong autoregressive baselines on both text writing and code generation tasks, while providing superior semantic coherence. Notably, SemMask achieves higher accuracy with substantially fewer decoding steps, indicating that the early establishment of semantic structure improves the efficiency--accuracy trade-off.

papers.title: Scaling laws in machine learning on non-ideal experimental data enable inverse design of radiative-cooling coatings
papers.abstract: Materials informatics increasingly targets multicomponent materials, yet experimental datasets inevitably contain non-ideal variations arising from imperfect uniformity and reproducibility in composition, coating formation, and measurement. Whether machine-learning prediction accuracy scales with amount of data under these conditions remains unclear. Here, we develop an automated platform that produced and optically characterized 11,520 radiative-cooling coatings spanning nine material and processing parameters. Forward and inverse neural networks, and a spectrum-conditioned diffusion model were trained on subsets of 10 to 10,000 samples. All models exhibited power-law scaling, with prediction errors decreasing with dataset size. Experimental inverse-design validation showed that larger datasets produced spectra closer to a broadband-emitter target. The diffusion model generated multiple candidate parameter sets, allowing selection among alternative solutions based on ease of fabrication, cost, and scalability. These results demonstrate predictable learning-curve scaling in non-ideal experimental data and provide a quantitative basis for estimating the benefit of additional experimental data, and thus the cost-effectiveness of materials-informatics.

papers.title: WTR-Drive: World-Task Decomposition with Structured Risk Supervision for End-to-End Driving
papers.abstract: Proposal-conditioned scene predictions can lack a common object-level reference across candidate trajectories. Aggregate planning scores also leave the objects and times associated with violations implicit. We present WTR-Drive (World-Task-Risk Driving), a Drive-JEPA-based planner that separates shared scene estimation from proposal-conditioned reasoning. A proposal-independent World Memory estimates object states, map structure, and future motion by re-reading the original visual features at each refinement round. Proposal feedback updates a residual Task branch without writing back to World Memory. This branch guides refinement through candidate-specific retrieval and gated visual feedback. A final Task readout supplies candidate-conditioned features for scoring. We derive structured risk targets from existing candidate-scoring rollouts without additional simulator calls. For at-fault collision and time-to-collision violations, the targets encode event existence, association with shared object slots, and the first violation time bin. On the NAVSIM navtest split, WTR-Drive achieves 94.66 PDMS on v1 and 88.24 EPDMS on v2 (expert-frame sequential evaluation). These scores are 0.96 and 0.44 points above the published Drive-JEPA values, respectively. Candidate-level analysis shows that higher best-candidate scores can coexist with lower selected-trajectory scores, revealing a gap between candidate quality and selection effectiveness.

papers.title: Newton-PINet: A fast physics-informed neural network with Newton linearization for meta-learning nonlinear PDEs
papers.abstract: Scientific machine learning has opened new avenues for solving parameterized partial differential equations (PDEs), enabling models to learn a family of PDEs and generalize to unseen instances. In this context, data-driven operator learning methods typically require large training datasets, while physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) suffer from difficult optimization and limited generalization, especially for nonlinear PDEs. We propose Newton-PINet, a physics-informed network enhanced by Newton linearization, offering an effective meta-learning framework for nonlinear PDEs. Newton-PINet (i) employs a physics-informed multilayer network with skip connections, where the output-layer weights are solved by least squares; (ii) adopts a two-stage learning strategy that first leverages gradient-based training to learn robust representations from the available training tasks, and then performs gradient-free fine-tuning on the output layer for fast task-specific generalization; and (iii) incorporates a Newton linearization method to speed up the least-squares iteration for nonlinear PDE problems. On a challenging nonlinear reaction-diffusion benchmark, Newton-PINet achieves up to three orders of magnitude lower relative error than recent neural solvers, while using 16x fewer training tasks and over an order of magnitude less training time (about 5 minutes versus several hours). This work advances the meta-learning of PINNs toward data-efficient, fast, and generalizable physics solvers. The code and datasets are publicly available at: https://github.com/fycAIwj/Newton-PINet.

authors.name: Chang Wei
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Chin Chun Ooi
authors.institution: Institute of Materials Research and Engineering

papers.title: Generative Data Augmentation Without External Data: An Empirical and Theoretical Study on Deep Networks
papers.abstract: Generative data augmentation adds samples from generative models to a classifier's training set. Many influential studies use generators pre-trained on large external datasets, and so mix the value of synthetic data with knowledge transferred through pretraining. We study the case without external data, where each generator learns only from the classifier's own training set, and ask when and why adding generated samples to that training set raises or lowers the classifier's test accuracy. We train classifiers with four backbones on six datasets, two of them medical, adding samples from four generators. We bound the excess risk of a classifier trained with synthetic data, that is, how far its population risk can lie above the minimum risk within its hypothesis class. The bound charges synthetic data for the total variation distance between the real and generated distributions and credits synthetic data for a larger training set. The gain from adding synthetic data, the fall in population risk, is at most the excess risk of the real-only classifier, which trains on the real images alone. Read through the bound, the experiments suggest that synthetic data help most when our classifiers detect only a small discrepancy between the generated and real data and the real-only classifier has room to improve, and that synthetic data help little or hurt when the detected discrepancy is large. Generators with a larger lower bound on the total variation distance, a bound that we estimate from our own classifiers, tend to help less on five of the six datasets, and on the CIFAR datasets the most accurate backbone gains the least. The bound gives these directions but not the size of the largest gains, most of which traditional augmentation also reaches at the same number of optimizer steps.

papers.title: Zero area of quartic Fibonacci Julia sets
papers.abstract: We give a computer-assisted proof that the Julia set of the degree-four Fibonacci renormalization 2-periodic point has zero planar Lebesgue measure. As a corollary, the degree four Fibonacci polynomial $z^4+c_{\mathrm{Fib}}$ has zero measure Julia set.

authors.name: Runze Zhang
authors.institution: Tianjin University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: Some Considerations on Measuring and Comparing Things
papers.abstract: Measurements and relationships between measurements are basic aspects underlying science and technology. In the present text, we present and discuss some of the approaches for measuring, normalizing, and comparing entities represented in terms of a set of measurements. Three main categories of measured values (constant, direct, or inverse) are proposed, underlaid by the relationship between data variation or intervals of interest and magnitude of the quantifications. For example, in certain cases the variation of measurements can be expected to be proportional to the relative magnitude (e.g.~when the magnitudes extend over long ranges). The considered approaches to comparing measurements include the Euclidean distance, three types of proximity based on the latter, as well as the Jaccard and coincidence indices. The presentation is complemented by graphical illustrations.

authors.name: Gonzalo Travieso
authors.institution: Instituto de Física de São Carlos

papers.title: Statistical and Optimization Models for Generating Electricity in Energy Markets
papers.abstract: Electricity generation has become a remunerative avenue for new investments, particularly in the area of renewable energy resources. This paper introduces a framework for integrating statistical methods with optimization modeling to improve decision support in electricity generation. The analysis begins by evaluating the success of mini-grid projects installed across the globe using both a probit and a Bayesian hierarchical model to estimate the probability of project success. Furthermore, we provide a multi-resource optimization framework for determining the optimal profit in electricity generation while reducing carbon emissions in production facilities. We also analyze the impact of a battery energy storage system and bidding behavior in the Alberta electricity market by constructing a mixed-integer self-scheduling model that determines optimal charging and discharging strategies. Numerical experiments show how storage systems can enhance energy arbitrage profitability and influence market clearing prices. Finally, we propose a Stochastic Dynamic Programming (SDP) model to maximize profit in electricity generation while accounting for price volatility. Integrating statistical methods with optimization-based modeling reveals great value in achieving more effective, profitable, and clean energy systems.

papers.title: Understanding Users' Security, Privacy, and Trust Concerns in Healthcare AI Systems
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly integrated into healthcare systems, from clinical information retrieval to workflow automation and decision support, which introduces new security, privacy, and trust risks with direct implications for patient care. While prior work has examined these risks from technical and regulatory perspectives, less is known about how these risks are naturally discussed in online communities. To address this gap, we conduct a large-scale analysis of 14 medical communities on Reddit and extract 6,514 relevant posts. Through systematic qualitative coding and LLM-assisted classification, we investigate concerns expressed in healthcare AI discussions, their prevalence, and how they evolve over time. Our analysis reveals that users perceive healthcare AI as expanding traditional healthcare trust boundaries and attack surfaces through integrations with electronic health records, third-party services, cloud platforms, and automated clinical workflows. Posts express concerns about over-privileged access to sensitive records, opaque data flows, unauthorized secondary use, and unsafe automation can amplify the consequences of errors and misuse. We identify four attitudes toward these risks: exploring questions of accountability and harm, cautiously accepting AI with stronger safeguards, skepticism about system trustworthiness, and resignation to growing data exposure and automation. Longitudinal analysis shows that SP&T discussions have increased significantly, with shifts coinciding with major healthcare AI deployments, privacy incidents, and regulatory developments. These findings illuminate changing trust relationships and data-governance challenges, informing the design and governance of safer, more transparent, and accountable healthcare AI systems.

papers.title: Real-time dynamics with bead-Fourier path integrals. III. Atomistic condensed-phase simulations
papers.abstract: Accurately accounting for nuclear quantum effects (NQEs), including zero-point energy and nuclear tunneling, is essential for a reliable prediction of the structural, thermodynamic, and dynamical properties of chemical systems, particularly those involving light atoms. However, incorporating NQEs could render simulations of large-scale chemical systems computationally prohibitive, particularly when combined with expensive electronic-structure calculations. One potential avenue for reducing cost is to use bead-Fourier path integrals (BF-PIs). In Paper I, we introduced the BF centroid molecular dynamics (BF-CMD) method, in which BF-PIs were used to compute an effective potential for CMD, and in Paper II, we introduced BF ring polymer MD (BF-RPMD), taking the BF-PI and using it for approximate real-time dynamics. Both papers featured a series of model systems and were able to reduce the number of beads needed to converge dynamical properties by a factor of 2 to 4, depending on the system. In this work, we report the first implementation and application of the BF-PI framework to atomistic simulations using liquid bulk water and hexagonal ice as test cases. As in our previous papers, we find that adding just a single Fourier component to the path yields a 4- and 8-fold reduction in the number of beads while achieving results that agree with reference PI simulations for liquid water and ice, respectively. We also demonstrate that we can reduce simulation costs by up to 5.5x compared to standard PIs by reducing the number of force calculations and normal-mode transformations.

papers.title: Barron Approximation and locally optimal weight densities for shallow neural networks
papers.abstract:
Mean field theories provide optimization results for shallow neural networks by analyzing the weight distribution in infinite width limits. Corresponding results for finite sized networks are obtained by particle approximations, for which sharp quantitative bounds are still an open problem.
  In this paper, we consider a modified mean field loss, which allows a more fine grained control over finite sized networks. We prove convexity and equidistribution properties, which directly lead to Barron type approximation results for networks sampled from local loss minimizers. We demonstrate that particle approximations of the new loss function naturally lead to gradient descent methods with dropout type regularization.

papers.title: MeltKV: Memory-Aligned KV Cache Compression via Variable-Bit Packed Vector Quantization for Long-Context LLMs
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly rely on long contexts, making Key-Value (KV) caches dominate memory usage and inference latency. Existing vector quantization (VQ) methods effectively compress KV caches to sub-4-bit levels but often overlook inefficiencies in memory alignment and decoding speed. This work introduces MeltKV, a memory-latency co-optimized KV cache quantization framework for long-context LLM serving. MeltKV employs a memory-aligned variable-bit index packing scheme that adaptively assigns bit-widths to grouped key channels and compactly stores indices within standard data-types, eliminating redundant bits. Additionally, head-wise codebook sharing reduces the total codebook size while maintaining accuracy. Experiments demonstrate that MeltKV effectively compresses KV representations to sub-4-bit levels down to 1 bit and, at comparable perplexity, achieves 48.1% lower memory usage and 52.9% lower latency than state-of-the-art VQ methods.

authors.name: Jiyun Han
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Inorganic Synthesis and Preparative Chemistry

papers.title: Conditional Stochastic User Equilibrium as a Gibbs Distribution: Tractable Flow Laws and Exact Path-Free Sampling
papers.abstract: Treating traffic counts as data calls for the joint distribution of link flows. Stochastic user equilibrium (SUE) gives a single flow vector, and independent route choice at fixed probabilities ignores congestion feedback between travelers. Conditional stochastic user equilibrium (CSUE), in which each traveler of a finite population chooses a route by logit conditional on the routes of all others, contains this feedback but has been hard to compute with at scale. Under separable link costs and a common route-choice precision, the CSUE conditionals are those of a unique Gibbs distribution whose energy is a left-endpoint discrete congestion potential, and for continuous nondecreasing costs the law concentrates on deterministic logit SUE in the large-population limit. When the routes of each origin are the paths of an acyclic bush, retaining origin- or OD-level labels gives an unnormalized layered link-flow law with an explicit product-form multiplicity. On this representation we build a block Metropolis-Hastings sampler whose proposal is an integer version of Dial's loading under frozen costs. It leaves the CSUE law on the bush route sets invariant without enumerating paths or storing individual routes, and at stationarity the mean rejection rate of a block lies between one and two times the total variation distance between its proposal and exact conditional. In experiments, the sampler reproduces reference laws from exact enumeration and traveler-level Gibbs sampling, whereas independent route choice at frozen costs reproduces mean flows but overstates link-flow standard deviations by up to 48% and distorts correlations. On Sioux Falls, the block sampler attains 76.1 times the minimum effective sample size per CPU second of traveler-level Gibbs sampling, and on Chicago Sketch, with over one million travelers, its sampled covariance is used to assess traffic-count locations.

papers.title: A DGLA approach to global extensions and deformations of Lie algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the global extension problem of Lie algebras from the perspective of dgLas and the Maurer--Cartan formulism. We propose a new equivalence relation of global extensions, generalizing the early work of Agore and Militaru. This new concept can be better adopted in the study of classical contraction and deformation problems for Lie algebras. Meanwhile, we construct dgLas that control based formal deformations of global extension structures under these equivalences. As byproducts, we obtain the classification of infinitesimal deformations in terms of the cohomology of the controlling dgLas and the corresponding obstruction theory. We relate the dgLa controlling deformation of global extensions under framed equivalence to that of non-abelian extensions constructed by Fr\'egier, obtaining a geometric interpretation of the decomposition of global cohomology into as a disjoint union of non-abelian cohomology. As an application, we study a particular family of an In\"on\"u--Wigner contraction from $\g\rtimes_{\mathrm{ad}}\g$ to $V_{\mathrm{ab}}\rtimes_{\mathrm{ad}}\g$ in the framework of global extension, deformation, and the dgLa approach.

papers.title: Continuous Lower-Limb Joint-Angle Estimation from sEMG and IMU: The Conditional Value of Cross-Activity and Cross-Subject Data under Update-Matched Controls
papers.abstract: Intent-driven exoskeleton control needs a continuous, causal estimate of the wearer's joint kinematics and an answer to a second question: whose data should train the estimator for a new user? Borrowing the user's recordings of other activities, or other users' recordings of the same activity, is usually evaluated as "more data" versus "less data," which confounds the information a source carries with the optimizer updates it adds and hides negative transfer behind averages. We separate these effects for hip, knee, and ankle angle estimation from high-density sEMG and an IMU across six locomotion activities on all ten participants of a public dataset. A compact residual causal TCN-GRU decoder is frozen, and an update-matched replay control prices every added source against the same number of updates on the user's own data. A user's own other activities raise $R^2$ from 0.722 to 0.788, of which +0.048 is information beyond replay; stair descent is a reliably harmful donor and sit-stand-walk a reliably beneficial one. Other users' same-activity data help while the user has only the target activity ($G_\mathrm{T} = +0.053$) and half as much once own other-activity data exist ($G_\mathrm{W} = +0.028$); at full calibration, donor value collapses after one to two target records. Per-target gains from the two sources correlate, and leave-one-participant-out gates recover most of the cross-subject value only at low calibration. Data value is hierarchical, state-dependent, and directional; the bottleneck is deciding, without test labels, when to transfer.

authors.name: Jiaying Xu
authors.institution: Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University

authors.name: Zhen Dong
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Large Language Models for AI Infrastructure
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to design, optimize, and operate the infrastructure behind AI training and serving, yet the literature remains fragmented across hardware design, machine learning systems, electronic design automation, and high-performance computing. We present a comprehensive survey of LLM-assisted AI infrastructure across its lifecycle, from accelerator design and kernel engineering to compilation, deployment, operations, data management, and energy optimization. We organize the literature by the primary resource the LLM manages: artifact-centric methods for computational artifacts, operational-centric methods for deployment context and system state, and resource-centric methods for data and energy. These categories span the lifecycle and cover AI-specific concerns such as distributed-training configuration, inference serving, GPU-cluster scheduling, and data loading. Building on this taxonomy, we conduct a cross-study quantitative synthesis of reported results. Because studies adopt heterogeneous benchmarks, baselines, hardware, and metrics, we compare methods only where evaluation conditions permit and align results along common dimensions: functional correctness, execution performance, throughput, resource and energy consumption, operational outcomes, and optimization cost, keeping each result's native metric, baseline, and setting rather than collapsing them into a single score. This comparison reveals where LLM-driven methods yield consistent gains, how reported gains in workload orchestration depend on the evaluation environment, from simulators to real clusters and production, and where evidence is still lacking. Together, the taxonomy, lifecycle perspective, and quantitative evaluation provide an evidence-grounded reference for LLM-driven engineering of AI infrastructure.

papers.title: Resolvent-based modeling of turbulent flow over multilayer compliant surfaces
papers.abstract: Compliant coatings offer a passive approach to modifying near-wall turbulence and potentially reducing skin-friction drag, but high-fidelity exploration of the coupled parameter space is costly. We develop a two-way coupled resolvent-Galerkin framework for turbulent channel flow over finite-thickness, layered viscoelastic coatings. The fluid is modeled using the Navier-Stokes equations linearized about a turbulent mean state, while the solid is represented by a through-thickness Galerkin discretization of the elastodynamic equations. The solid response is condensed into a spectral surface-impedance operator at the fluid-solid interface. At $Re_\tau = 180$, stiff panels approach the rigid-wall response, whereas more compliant panels modify the low-rank response associated with the near-wall cycle. A Reynolds-number study shows that panels with fixed nondimensional material stiffness can produce different responses depending on whether their thickness scales with inner or outer flow length scales. The influence of viscoelastic damping is examined across low- and high-frequency regimes, where stiffness-proportional damping alters the high-frequency fractional-energy distribution, while the low-frequency distribution remains relatively insensitive to damping. For multilayer panels, the fluid-facing material determines the interfacial wave speed, while the subsurface stiffness distribution modifies the panel's effective thickness. Temporal stability analysis identifies regions of parameter space where a steady harmonic response is relevant and regions where instabilities grow. Finally, a leading-order, covariance-based drag-estimation framework relates the coupled response to changes in the mean flow and to the estimated skin-friction drag. Together, these tools provide a basis for screening coating designs and selecting candidates for high-fidelity simulations and experiments.

papers.title: An Optimal Online Algorithm for Single-machine Scheduling with Two Agents
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the online two-agent scheduling problem on a single machine, where jobs arrive over time. The objective is to minimize the weighted sum of the agents' makespans, denoted as $C_{\max}^A + \theta C_{\max}^B$, for a given priority weight $\theta \ge 1$. A significant gap has persisted between the established theoretical lower bound on the competitive ratio and the performance of the best-known online algorithms. For the parameter range $1 \leq \theta \leq \tfrac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2}$, we propose novel online algorithm which achieves a competitive ratio of $1+\tfrac{\theta}{1+\theta}$. This result matches the theoretical lower bound.

authors.name: Peihai Liu
authors.institution: East China University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Xiwen Lu
authors.institution: East China University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Hermitian Positive Definite Neural Networks for Matrix-CFAR Geometric Signal Detection in Nonhomogeneous Clutter
papers.abstract: Matrix information geometry (MIG) detectors exploit the Riemannian geometry of Hermitian positive definite (HPD) matrices to achieve robust object detection in nonhomogeneous clutter. The matrix constant false alarm rate (matrix-CFAR) method is a representative MIG detector that relies on the geometric structures with respect to specific metrics. In most cases, computing representative HPD covariance matrices requires numerical methods, typically involving computationally intensive iterative optimization algorithms. Although explicit formulas are available for certain cases, such as the log-Euclidean (LE) mean, they are generally unavailable for many other matrix means and medians. To address this challenge, we propose integrating the Hermitian positive definite neural network (HPDNet) into the matrix-CFAR framework, replacing conventional numerical optimization procedures with a learned, geometry-preserving mapping that directly estimates representative HPD covariance matrices from data. In the simulations, the framework is evaluated for MIG detectors using both means and medians associated with the affine-invariant Riemannian metric, the LE metric, and the Bures--Wasserstein metric, on both simulated compound-Gaussian clutter and real IPIX sea clutter. In both cases, the HPDNet is trained solely on simulated data to assess its applicability to the study of real data. The results show a significant reduction of computational cost in testing, while maintaining detection performance and robustness.

authors.name: Takumi Sato
authors.institution: Tohoku Medical and Pharmaceutical University Hospital

authors.name: Linyu Peng
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Inverse Problem for Super-linearization with Single Observable and Diagonalizable Principal Submatrix
papers.abstract: Super-linearization is, roughly speaking, embedding an $n$-dimensional nonlinear dynamical system into an $(n + m)$-dimensional linear system. We introduce and address, in this paper, the inverse problem: given a linear system $\dot x= M x$, what type of dynamical systems can be super-linearized to it? We focus on the special case where the dimension reduction is one (i.e., $m = 1$) and the leading $n$-by-$n$ principal submatrix of $M$ is diagonalizable, and provide a solution to the problem.

papers.title: Polarization of Fast Radio Bursts due to Propagation in Magnetized Plasma
papers.abstract: Polarization measurements of radio transients, particularly their frequency dependence, shed light on the magnetic environments of these sources. We extend the analytical solution of radiative transfer of the polarization properties of such transients to both a cold magnetized plasmas beyond the high-frequency approximation and a relativistic plasma with synchrotron emission. The Faraday mixing coefficients are enhanced makes Stokes parameters $Q$, $U$, and $V$ to exhibit a more rapid and complex frequency-dependent evolution. A relativistic plasma medium can also generate both Faraday roataion and conversion with a smaller magnetic field. The relativistic plasma is investigated as a persistent radio source (PRS) associated with FRB, and it is found that, although the observed PRS luminosity can be accounted for, an FRB can propagate out only under certain special parameter conditions. We apply the model to fit the polarization profile of GPM J1839$-$10 and revisit some FRBs. All sources with Faraday conversion require that the environment's magnetic field not exceed 100~G. The magnetic field of FRB 20180301A and GPM J1839$-$10 are almost perpendicular to the light of sight for at least some times.

authors.name: Nan Xu
authors.institution: Suzhou University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Borel $(2n+1)$-coloring for bounded degree function graphs
papers.abstract: Let $G=(X,E)$ be a Borel graph generated by $n$-many bounded-to-one Borel functions. We show that $G$ admits a Borel proper $(2n+1)$-coloring, which answers a problem of Kechris, Solecki and Todor\v{c}evi\'{c}.

authors.name: Junhao Chen
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: A proof of a conjecture on bipartite correspondence packing
papers.abstract:
A correspondence cover assigns a set of possible colors to each vertex of a graph. For each edge, a matching between the two endpoint color sets specifies the forbidden color pairs. A correspondence coloring selects one color at each vertex so that no forbidden pair is selected. A full correspondence packing is a collection of such colorings that uses every color at each vertex exactly once.
  We prove a conjecture of Cambie, Cames van Batenburg, Davies, and Kang [Random Structures & Algorithms 64 (2024), 62--93]. For every sufficiently large $D$, there is a positive integer $k(D)=(1+o(1))D/\log D$ such that every correspondence cover of any finite bipartite graph has a full correspondence packing if each color has at most $D$ forbidden partners and each vertex has $k(D)$ colors. More precisely, we prove this conclusion with \[
  k(D)=\left\lceil\frac{D}{\log D-2\log\log D-6}\right\rceil \] for every integer $D\ge\lceil e^{20}\rceil$.

papers.title: LINK: Lightweight and Inductive Node-to-Node Propagation Rule Learning for Traffic Kriging
papers.abstract: Spatio-temporal traffic kriging aims to reconstruct traffic time series at unobserved locations with no historical traffic observations by leveraging spatial and temporal dependencies across the road network. Existing Graph Neural Network (GNN)-based approaches primarily rely on neighborhood aggregation to capture spatial dependencies, thereby modeling traffic interactions implicitly and making it difficult to accurately recover traffic magnitudes at locations without historical observations. To address this limitation, we propose LINK, a Lightweight and Inductive Node-to-node propagation rule learning paradigm for traffic Kriging. LINK introduces three key designs: 1) a propagation-centric traffic kriging paradigm that explicitly learns a shared node-to-node transition rule; 2) a context-aware Spectral Propagation Network that performs traffic-state propagation in both the spectral and time domains; and 3) TraffiKrig, a realistic traffic kriging benchmark that preserves heterogeneous road-segment characteristics and road-specific metadata while enabling systematic comparison of representative kriging methods under a unified metadata-enhanced setting. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LINK achieves strong reconstruction accuracy and computational efficiency. Compared with the strongest baseline on each subset, LINK achieves an average MAE reduction of 54.7% over original baselines. LINK also achieves substantial efficiency improvements, reducing training time by 66.5% and inference time by 86.6% compared with the fastest competing methods. Zero-shot experiments further demonstrate the transferability of the learned propagation rule across regions.

papers.title: Distribution-Free Probabilistic Environmental Control Barrier Functions with Application to Adaptive Cruise Control
papers.abstract: Safety control under environmental uncertainty is challenging when the uncertainty distribution is unknown and reliable support bounds are unavailable. This paper introduces CPP-ECBF, a distribution-free approach that combines conformal predictive programming with probabilistic environmental control barrier functions. For separable environmental safety functions and i.i.d. uncertainty, CPP-ECBF converts the probabilistic safety condition into a sample-based deterministic control constraint that provides finite-horizon safety with prescribed probability $1-\epsilon$ and calibration confidence $1-\tilde{\beta}$. For adaptive cruise control, an offline conformal uncertainty bound yields an explicit linear upper bound on the ego-vehicle acceleration, which is enforced by a quadratic-programming safety filter. In 10,000 Monte Carlo trials, 99.97% of trials satisfied the finite-horizon safety criterion, exceeding the prescribed confidence of 85%. Moreover, CPP-ECBF reduced the conservatism of worst-case robust enforcement, increasing the admissible acceleration upper limit by $5.90\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$ on average.

papers.title: ScoutCache: Efficient Few-Step Autoregressive Video Diffusion via Conditional Readout and Selective Caching
papers.abstract: Few-step autoregressive video diffusion enables efficient long video generation, but inference still incurs substantial computational costs from repeated denoising and KV cache operations. Existing acceleration methods reduce parts of this overhead, while historical KV reading and cache construction remain costly across video chunks. To address these challenges, we propose ScoutCache, a training-free framework that jointly optimizes denoising, historical KV reading, and cache construction. We observe that shallow feature changes provide useful information for estimating clean latent updates, while historical KV dependence varies across Transformer layers and attention heads but remains relatively stable across video chunks. Based on these observations, we develop Conditional Denoising Readout (CDR) to estimate intermediate denoising updates from shallow feature changes and known noise variations. We further introduce Output Risk Guided Historical KV Reading (ORHR) to allocate historical reading budgets based on attention output perturbations, and Content and Coverage Guided Sparse Cache Construction (CCSC) to reduce cache construction costs by selecting informative spatial tokens while maintaining spatial coverage. Extensive experiments on Self-Forcing and LongLive using VBench and MovieGen demonstrate that ScoutCache achieves up to 2.28$\times$ and 1.86$\times$ speedups, respectively, while consistently improving generation quality without modifying pretrained model parameters.

papers.title: Linglong Agent Service: A Runtime for Centralized Agent Reasoning and Distributed Execution
papers.abstract: LLM agents can use remote tools and cloud sandboxes, but integrating reasoning, session state, and heterogeneous execution sites remains a runtime design problem. We present Linglong Agent Service (agentsvc), a self-hosted HTTP service and embeddable Python runtime that treats execution site as a configurable dimension alongside model, tools, and context. A parent service retains inference orchestration, tool descriptions, and conversation history; each inference request selects one child environment for file, shell, terminal, and MCP operations. Direct HTTP and child-initiated WebSocket tunnels carry the same application interfaces, including portable request context and centrally managed updates. The normal core path requires no third-party Python packages, with an optional Windows pseudo-terminal dependency. We further present online_debugger as the process-scale special case of execution-site separation: an instrumented program submits exception evidence, executes session-scoped inspection tools inside the incident process, and resumes the same diagnostic session. Its default prompt requires failing-then-passing reproduction evidence for source changes, while runtime patch activation and failed-call recovery remain unimplemented. We explain the design through constrained expected-utility reasoning, compare concrete mechanisms with Hermes Agent, Pi, Codex, and Claude Code, and report implementation and regression-test evidence. The current evidence establishes executable contracts, not performance advantages, repair accuracy, or production recovery. The source code is open source under the MIT license at https://github.com/mz24cn/agents.

papers.title: What Makes a Good Move? Learning to Act from Experience in Visual Worlds
papers.abstract: Learning visual policies requires turning interaction experience into guidance for individual decisions. Trajectory outcomes obscure action quality, while unguided exploration can revisit familiar situations. We present \textsc{LightAct}, an experience-learning framework that connects skill-guided exploration with policy internalization. Interaction segments are summarized into experience entries and consolidated into a game-specific skill that guides root collection toward broader state coverage. At each root, candidate actions are compared through short rollouts under a shared frozen policy. Environment-reported score gains are averaged across continuations and normalized into relative action rewards, producing reusable supervision for reinforcement learning. Policy training uses a compact dataset of just 1,024 decision roots collected in a single source game and paired with their action rewards. Across 170 GameWorld tasks spanning 34 games, \textsc{LightAct} improves overall progress by 23.6, 29.2, and 13.0 percentage points at the 2B, 4B, and 9B scales, respectively, with our strongest model competitive with reported proprietary-model results. Ablations show broader root-state coverage with skill guidance and consistent gains across three policy optimizers. Case studies show how rollouts distinguish actions with identical immediate gains.

papers.title: One Run Is Not Enough: Reminding a small Gemma 4 coding agent of its last finding made no measurable difference in a paired test
papers.abstract: When a coding agent runs out of room, its earlier findings are cut and it forgets them. We tested a simple fix: automatically putting the agent's last finding back in front of it. We fixed the rules in advance and ran 98 paired coding tasks with and without this reminder, using Gemma 4 31B (QAT, 4-bit) in the Gemma 4 Developer Agent harness. The reminder made no measurable difference: across all 98 tasks, 47 were solved with it and 48 without (-1.0 points, 95% interval [-8.3, +6.3], exact McNemar p=1.0). The primary outcome (a documented deviation from our preregistration), the first 48 pairs, was 29/48 with memory against 25/48 without (+8.3 points, [-2.1, +18.3], p=0.22); the extension of 50 tasks, decided after that result, pointed the other way (18/50 against 23/50, -10.0 points, p=0.125), so the sign did not replicate. With 19% of tasks flipping between two identical no-memory runs, the combined interval excludes harms larger than about 8 points and gains larger than about 6, and the design had 80% power only for effects of about +-12 points or more. The model almost never wrote notes (2 of 16 and 4 of 32 runs), and memory cost context: the first request is larger and something was injected at only 47% to 65% of compactions. The registered secondary, repeated actions per compaction, was also null. Two directional hypotheses found on Modal did not replicate on Kaggle. We also report an A/A calibration and a validity funnel (129 tasks, 105 valid). Together these results show that single-run memory claims on task sets of this size sit inside run-to-run noise. The treatment is a harness mechanism and does not test agent-written memory.

authors.name: Patrick Passos
authors.institution: Instituto Federal de Educação, Ciência e Tecnologia do Pará

papers.title: Graph Intersections and Hypergraph Discrepancy
papers.abstract:
Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs on $n$ vertices with $e(G)=p\binom{n}{2}$ and $e(H)=q\binom{n}{2}$, where $p,q\in(0,1)$ are fixed. Bollob\'as and Scott studied intersections of two graphs under random relabelling and asked for the minimum $L^2$ norm of the deviation of their intersection size from its expected value. We answer this question by proving that, for graphs of order $n$ with fixed edge densities $p,q\in(0,1)$, the minimum is \begin{equation*} \left(\sqrt{\frac{p(1-p)q(1-q)}{2}\cdot\frac{1-\sqrt R}{1+\sqrt R}}\right)n+o(n), \end{equation*} where $R=\max\{p,1-p,q,1-q\}$. The coefficient of the linear term is best possible.
  Bollob\'as and Scott defined the positive and negative discrepancies of two hypergraphs as the largest deviations of their intersection size above and below its expected value under relabelling, respectively. They asked for the minimum product of the positive and negative discrepancies of two $(n/2)$-uniform hypergraphs on $n$ vertices with $\frac{1}{2}\binom{n}{n/2}$ edges. We answer this question by proving that the minimum product of these discrepancies is $0$ if $4\mid\binom{n}{n/2}$ and $1/4$ otherwise.

papers.title: Splitting and Mixed Deformations of Toric Generalized K\"ahler Potentials
papers.abstract: We study splitting phenomena for extremal toric generalized K\"ahler structures on products of compact toric manifolds. We prove that every extremal symplectic potential splits when the skew-symmetric parameter $B$ is block diagonal, without any restriction on $A$. We also construct two types of non-splitting examples on $\mathbb{CP}^1\times\mathbb{CP}^1$: an explicit constant-generalized-scalar-curvature structure with a splitting potential but a non-product generalized K\"ahler structure, and a deformation family of constant-generalized-scalar-curvature structures with genuinely non-splitting potentials.

authors.name: Li Sheng
authors.institution: Central Hospital Affiliated to Shenyang Medical College

papers.title: On the nodal set of the second eigenfunction of the Laplacian in convex domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$
papers.abstract: Let $\Omega$ be a bounded convex domain in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $n\ge2$. We prove that the closure of the interior nodal set of any second Dirichlet eigenfunction of $\Omega$ intersects $\partial\Omega$. The proof combines the ground-state derivative and the quantitative log-concavity estimate of Andrews and Clutterbuck with a variational argument.

papers.title: Tightness of bulk crossing heights for the planar discrete Gaussian free field
papers.abstract:
Let $\phi_N$ be the planar discrete Gaussian free field in $[-2N,2N]^2\cap\mathbb Z^2$, with zero boundary condition imposed by killing the associated simple random walk on exit. We consider the least height $H_N$ at which the two-sided level set $\{|\phi_N|\leq a\}$ contains a nearest-neighbor left--right crossing of $[-N,N]^2\cap\mathbb Z^2$. We prove that $(H_N)_{N\geq1}$ is tight, uniformly over all box sizes. More precisely, for every $a\geq0$ and $N\geq1$, \[
  \Phi\!\left(-a\sqrt{\frac{2}{\log2}}\right)
  \leq\mathbb{P}(H_N>a)
  \leq4\exp\!\left\{-2^{-29}\frac{a^2}{\log(2+a)}\right\}, \] where $\Phi$ is the standard normal distribution function. The upper bound yields uniform polynomial moments and a uniform exponential moment of $H_N^2/\log(2+H_N)$. For the upper bound, we compare a marked loop-soup exploration with a graph in which independent site variables open incoming edges. We then estimate connections in a massive field using two auxiliary vertices and bound the Gaussian remainder when the mass is removed. The lower bound uses a Gaussian translation inequality and a square-shell estimate for the Dirichlet energy, without using the massive-field argument. In particular, a height independent of $N$ gives any prescribed crossing probability below one, whereas every fixed finite height has a uniformly positive failure probability.

authors.name: Xiang Fang
authors.institution: Wuhan University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Two-Stage Staffing with Random Arrival Rate: A Simulation Optimization Approach
papers.abstract: In service systems, the arrival rate in the same time period and day of the week exhibits randomness, yet can be more accurately estimated or forecast right before that period, which motivates a two-stage staffing scheme with advance base staffing and pre-shift surge staffing. Existing approaches usually impose strong assumptions on the arrival process and service systems' operational logic and other further approximations (i.e., stylized models) to derive explicit staffing policies. This paper proposes a simulation optimization approach (SOA) for more general arrival processes and service systems by effectively addressing some intertwined challenges. By recasting the original formulation into computationally tractable structures and designing an efficient coordinate-search algorithm, it constructs a two-stage staffing lookup table offline, which allows managers to make real-time surge staffing decisions without any further simulation. Comprehensive numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed SOA has significantly better staffing performance and substantially broader applicability compared to existing approaches. Even under the stylized models, the cost savings delivered by our SOA compared with existing approaches range from the low tens to several tens of percent, depending on different problem parameters; the advantage further amplifies when the actual problem deviates from the stylized models. In a nurse-staffing case study grounded in real-world data, the proposed SOA delivers approximately 8% to 13% cost savings over a state-of-the-art benchmark.

papers.title: Speaking-Clock Mamba: Phoneme-Conditioned State-Space Modeling for Visual Forced Alignment
papers.abstract: Visual forced alignment (VFA) locates phoneme and word boundaries in a silent talking-face video given its transcript. Existing methods mainly enforce transcript order at the decoding stage, leaving the encoder without an explicit mechanism to anchor its temporally evolving representation to transcript progress. As a result, phoneme-specific evidence is blurred and alignment drift accumulates over long sequences. In this paper, we propose Speaking-Clock Mamba, which makes transcript progress part of the temporal recurrence. A selective state-space (Mamba) backbone is inserted between the visual frontend and the Conformer cross-attention encoder, and a Phoneme-Conditioned Selective Scan (PCSS) conditions its input-dependent step size on a supervised, structurally monotone speaking clock that estimates progress through the transcript. Since causal and bidirectional variants of this backbone make complementary errors, a training-free selector picks the more confident alignment per utterance. Experiments on LRS2 and LRS3 show consistent gains over protocol-matched baselines, and the supervised clock provides an explicit estimate of alignment progress.

papers.title: Weighted composition operators between Qp spaces: Boundedness and compactness
papers.abstract: We characterize boundedness and compactness of weighted composition operators $W_{u,\varphi}:Q_{p_1}\to Q_{p_2}$, where $W_{u,\varphi}f=u(f\circ\varphi)$, $p_1>0$, and $0<p_2<1$. A separation theorem for the two terms in $(W_{u,\varphi}f)'$, together with value and derivative embedding theorems, gives two capacity conditions on $u$ and $\varphi$. For $p_1=1$ and $p_1>1$, the derivative condition has a maximal-integral and an area-integral form respectively.

papers.title: The Walsh spectrum of the Dobbertin APN function
papers.abstract: APN functions yield the best resistance to differential attacks when used as a building block of a block cipher. APN functions induced by monomials over finite fields have received particular interest both for their simplicity and their unique properties. A key property of APN functions is their linearity, which has been determined for all known APN monomials outside of the Dobbertin APN monomials. In this paper, we close this gap and determine the complete Walsh spectrum and in particular the linearity of the Dobbertin APN monomial, answering a problem that has been open for more than 20 years. Using known connections, our result also yields the asymptotically largest Sidon sets in elementary abelian $2$-groups constructed so far as well as binary linear codes of minimum distance $5$ that are almost optimal.

papers.title: Universal Analytical Description of Magnetoexcitons in Two-Dimensional Semiconducting Materials
papers.abstract: Matching the Coulomb and logarithmic limits of the Rytova--Keldysh model gives a universal zero-field spectrum for monolayer exciton $s$ states, $E_n\simeq-\mathrm{Ry}^*/[n-1/2+f_n(\xi)]^2$, where $\xi$ is the screening parameter. Analytical radii determine diamagnetic coefficients and the magnetic crossover scale. Zero-field deviations peak near $1\%$ across the full screening range $0\leq\xi\leq100$. For the sampled hBN-encapsulated monolayers, magnetoexciton energies agree with numerical spectra to sub-meV rms up to $100\T$ and capture the measured orbital shifts. Shared parameters link optical and magneto-optical spectra.
