papers.title: Equal Dose, Different Coverage:Tracing Rate and Duration in Image Editing
papers.abstract: Benchmarks for scientific image editing test whether a model draws the outcome of a described process, leaving open which representations carry its errors and whether correcting them yields the right quantity. We study this question with an airbrush of fixed deposition profile, under which exchanging rate and duration preserves the dose and should preserve the endpoint, yet changes the edited coverage. Matched-norm activation patches across text positions and denoising stages show that, in distilled FLUX with Chinese prompts, representations at unchanged text positions (context) carry this discrepancy: early context transfers 3.51 of the 3.98 percentage-point (pp) signed route difference, against 0.09 pp for equal-norm updates at the two changed digits. Early image latents transmit native (unpatched) route differences across two FLUX configurations and OmniGen, while text-position effects depend on configuration. The trace predicts an intervention: share early context between routes while each retains its own digits. On independent English layouts, this reduces the distilled-FLUX absolute route gap from 1.13 to 0.60 pp, outperforms early digit sharing, and improves agreement more than in base FLUX under directly paired tests. Calibrated evaluation, which prescribes an area for each dose, separates this gain from accuracy: sharing the full prompt encoding produces identical route images with target errors of 8-16 pp, and stating the target percentage directly retains a compressed area response. Localization predicts a consistency gain on new layouts, and calibration measures the quantity error that agreement leaves unresolved.

authors.name: Yi Liu
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Liaoning

papers.title: Orbital graph structure of alternating full groups and simple torsion amenable groups of exponential growth
papers.abstract:
We develop a framework for constructing simple alternating full groups A(G, X), associated with finite fragmentations of minimal expansive dihedral Cantor actions, with controlled orbital-graph codings and purely non-Hausdorff singularities. We also prove that positive entropy of a naturally labeled admissible orbital line forces exponential word growth of the acting group.
  As an application, we construct continuum many pairwise abstractly nonisomorphic, finitely generated, infinite, simple, torsion, amenable groups of exponential word growth. They arise as alternating full groups of fragmented minimal expansive dihedral Cantor actions with linearly repetitive generic regular orbital graphs and purely non-Hausdorff singularities.
  Under the same minimality, expansivity, linear repetitivity and singularity assumptions, if every finite clopen coding is determined by a bounded fragmentation window, the alternating full group has intermediate word growth.

authors.name: Yitong Zhang
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Parameter Recovery for the Modified Leray-alpha Model via Continuous Data Assimilation
papers.abstract: In this study, we extend the recursive length-scale recovery method for the simplified Bardina model to the three-dimensional modified Leray-alpha model. The main difficulty is that the unknown parameter also occurs in the nonlinear convection term, so estimating the error in the parameter update requires control of second spatial derivatives of the velocity error. We combine continuous data assimilation with a recursive update of the squared length scale, using observed low Fourier modes and computed high Fourier modes. Under uniform regularity bounds on the reference solution and suitable conditions on the observations and the recovery procedure, we prove geometric convergence of both the parameter and velocity errors at the update times. When the update-window lengths are uniformly bounded, this convergence is exponential in time at the update times.

authors.name: Jing Tian
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: When Does Confidence Reveal Problem Difficulty?
papers.abstract: While confidence signals are commonly evaluated for their ability to predict a model's own correctness, their relationship with problem difficulty remains less understood. In this work, we investigate a wide range of confidence-related signals and whether they can serve as indicators of problem difficulty across various task domains. We find that perturbation inconsistency, semantic entropy, and solution length exhibit strong associations with population difficulty than token-level uncertainty. Notably, these relationships persist even when restricting the analysis to problems correctly answered by the focal model, suggesting that such signals capture information about difficulty beyond their ability to predict the model's own correctness. We further explore applications of these signals, illustrating the potential and limitations of using confidence-related signals to guide inference-time decisions. Our findings highlight the utility of model-specific signals as imperfect but informative proxies for population-level problem difficulty.

papers.title: Two-Sided large oscillations of the argument of the Riemann zeta function and its iterates
papers.abstract:
Assuming the Riemann hypothesis, we establish lower bounds for large oscillations of the iterated argument functions \(S_n(t)\) of the Riemann zeta function. As a corollary, we prove that, for every fixed integer \(n \geq 0\),
  \[S_n(t)=\Omega_{\pm}\Big(\frac{(\log t)^{1/2}(\log_3 t)^{1/2}}{(\log_2 t)^{n+1/2}} \Big).\] For even \(n\), this recovers two results of Chirre and Mahatab in 2021. For odd \(n\), our result strengthens theirs by establishing the missing direction of oscillation with the same order of magnitude.

papers.title: Social Welfare and Equilibrium in Distributed Microgrid Prosumer Coordination Under a Mixed Competitive-Cooperative Setting
papers.abstract: Price-based distributed prosumer coordination in distribution networks is fundamentally challenging when the aggregator pursues grid-level goals that couple prosumers' decisions, because the Lagrangian fails to separate and nodal prices are undefined under conventional dual decomposition. This paper develops a novel method that embeds mixed competitive-cooperative objectives exactly into prices, which are split into energy, congestion, and grid-objective components, closing the gap between the social welfare optimum and the competitive equilibrium. To compute the equilibrium, a distributed optimization algorithm is developed based on the projected Arrow-Hurwicz-Uzawa scheme. Explicit step-size rules are developed for the algorithm to guarantee $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{L})$ and $\mathcal{O}(1/L)$ ergodic convergence rates. Simulations on an IEEE 33-bus feeder that is connected to prosumers and electric vehicle fleets validate the accuracy and efficacy of the proposed methods.

papers.title: Kadison's open problem and $R^*$-algebras
papers.abstract: We study $R^*$-subalgebras of von Neumann algebras. In finite homogeneous type $\mathrm I_n$, every $R^*$-subalgebra is locally finite-dimensional. We also give a trace criterion for local finite dimensionality in the semifinite setting under a finite-trace hypothesis, and prove an approximate halving property for projections in strongly dense $R^*$-subalgebras of type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors. For three projections in an $R^*$-subalgebra of a type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor, the reduced word-length filtration gives bounds on layer growth, criteria for stabilization, and uniform bounds on minimal-polynomial degrees at each fixed word length. Finally, we give a negative answer to Kadison's fifteenth problem by constructing an infinite-dimensional unital $*$-algebra generated algebraically by three projections in which every selfadjoint element has finite spectrum. The resulting $R^*$-algebra embeds unitally into every type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor.

papers.title: Minimum cores in lattice graphs: zonotope structure and quartic growth
papers.abstract: A core of a graph is a nonempty vertex set in which every member has at least as many neighbours inside the set as outside. We study the minimum size $c_{m,n}$ of a finite core in the graph on $\Z^m$ joining points at sup-norm distance at most $n$. The local majority condition imposes a global geometric constraint: the convex hull of every core has an explicit lattice zonotope $H_n^{(m)}$ as a Minkowski summand. In the plane, this zonotope has width asymptotic to $6\zeta(3)n^3/\pi^2$. We prove that all its lattice points form a core and construct a shell with $O(n^4)$ points. Together with a packing argument, this gives $c_{2,n}=\Theta(n^4)$ and coordinate widths $\Theta(n^3)$ for every minimum core. We determine $c_{2,1}=12$ and $c_{2,2}=96$ by analytic arguments and prove uniqueness up to translation in both cases. Explicit forced-set and deficit certificates determine further minima within the prescribed zonotope hull. We distinguish these restricted results from global optimality and state the remaining geometric conjectures. We also give a direct reduction from \textsc{Clique} showing that the core problem is NP-complete on general finite graphs, which settles a conjecture of Hassanpour in the terms in which it was posed.

papers.title: ThermoSight: From Appearance to Internal Thermofluid Fields via Physics-Guided Neural Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Most neural reconstruction methods focus on reproducing scene appearance, yet inferring physical states from visual observations is essential for machine understanding of the physical world. Reconstructing the internal temperature and soot fields of radiating thermofluids such as flames is challenging yet essential for improving energy efficiency and assessing heat exposure and fire spread. In flames, temperature and soot concentration jointly govern visible emission, and soot self-absorption alters the light that reaches each camera. With limited views, changes in the two fields can offset one another in the recorded RGB images, making temperature and soot difficult to disentangle. ThermoSight, a physics-guided neural framework for scientific imaging, jointly reconstructs continuous three-dimensional temperature and soot volume fraction fields from limited calibrated flame images without field-level ground truth during optimization. A differentiable spectral model links these fields to measured RGB through thermal emission, self-absorption, and calibrated camera responses. Temperature-dependent emission spectra and wavelength-dependent attenuation constrain shared fields across RGB channels, reducing temperature-soot ambiguity. Chromaticity consistency, observation-derived spatial constraints, and soot regularization complement intensity fitting. In a synthetic ablation, wavelength-resolved attenuation reduces temperature RMSE in the hot, sooty region from 234 to 112 K relative to a three-channel approximation, with nearly identical RGB PSNR (65.23 vs. 65.24 dB). Measured data yield coherent fields and competitive RGB reconstructions. These results demonstrate that physics-guided neural fields recover interpretable internal physical quantities beyond visually consistent appearance.

authors.name: Hefei Ling
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Chun Lou
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Coal Combustion

papers.title: From Companion to Guardian: Designing an Emergency Support System Using a Quadruped Robot for Older Adults
papers.abstract: As older adults increasingly live alone, emergency support becomes an important function for home companion robots. In Australia, demand for the care and support workforce is projected to nearly double between 2020-21 and 2049-50. Service robots such as robot dogs may support older adults by combining everyday companionship with assistance when human support is not immediately available. We present the design and implementation of a domestic companion-robot system on a Unitree Go1 quadruped platform that combines companionship with emergency awareness and response. The system uses a three-stage interaction model consisting of companion, danger-awareness, and emergency modes. A rule-based escalation policy combines signs detected from visual and speech input to determine the current risk level and adjust how long the robot waits for the user to confirm safety before entering emergency mode. Additional detected signs can shorten this waiting time. Users can confirm safety, request immediate help, stop robot motion, or reset the system. We verified the implemented decision rules and escalation timing through 105 automated trials and 25 staged physical trials. Additional visual evidence shortened the waiting time, and the system entered emergency mode when the waiting time ended without confirmation.

authors.name: Chunyang Meng
authors.institution: Affiliated Hospital of Jining Medical University

papers.title: A Convergence Analysis of the Random Feature Method for Linear PDEs
papers.abstract: The Random Feature Method (RFM) distinguishes itself among machine learning approaches to partial differential equations (PDEs) through its superior accuracy and computational efficiency. Nevertheless, the theoretical underpinnings of RFM remain incompletely elucidated. This paper provides a comprehensive analysis of RFM within the framework of kernel methods, focusing on two principal aspects: (i) approximation by finitely many random features in Sobolev norms and the PDE residual seminorm, and (ii) estimation over the induced reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) from finitely many noiseless collocation observations. We relate both problems to kernel ridge regression (KRR) and establish upper and lower bounds in terms of the eigenvalues of the associated integral operators under the respective assumptions. Combining the approximation and estimation lower bounds, we establish a lower bound under simultaneous restrictions on the numbers of random features and collocation observations. We further quantify how activation regularity affects these eigenvalues, obtaining algebraic upper bounds for finitely smooth activations and stretched-exponential upper bounds for analytic activations.

authors.name: Jingrun Chen
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Liquid-liquid criticality in a fluid whose two structures favor mixing
papers.abstract: The generic two-state description of liquid polyamorphism requires a non-ideality opposing mixing for liquid-liquid separation. This condition assumes that the free energy of the underlying fluid is independent of the structural order, an assumption that fails when the local structures differ in size or attraction. We derive a closed-form stability condition after density relaxation for a van der Waals closure based on the second virial coefficient of a pair potential whose internal state determines both the contact distance and the well depth. The condition recovers the familiar result for structures identical in size and attraction but can change sign within the liquid when they differ. In ten of the thirty-four parameter sets examined, a critical state preferred by the liquid requires a non-ideality favoring mixing. For one such fluid, we construct the coexistence curve, which terminates at the predicted critical point at positive pressure. Attraction and excluded volume provide distinct contributions to the density-order coupling; only the former survives on a fixed lattice with single occupancy. Removing the excluded-volume contribution restores the familiar condition in 58 of the 82 such critical states found. Thus, within this closure, liquid-liquid separation can occur with a non-ideality favoring mixing.

authors.name: Marcio Pazetti
authors.institution: Universidade Federal do Vale do São Francisco

papers.title: Property A and the identification of the maximal and reduced uniform Roe algebras
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a discrete metric space of bounded geometry. We prove that $X$ has property A if and only if the canonical map $$\lambda:C^*_{u,max}(X)\to C^*_u(X)$$ is an isomorphism.

authors.name: Jintao Deng
authors.institution: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics

papers.title: Analytic Model for Transient Plateau Filling in Vibrational Distributions of Periodically Driven Plasmas
papers.abstract: In periodically driven molecular plasmas, the vibrational distribution function is governed by the competition between vibration--vibration (V-V) up-pumping along the anharmonic ladder and vibration--translation (V-T) relaxation, producing the Treanor--Gordiets distribution. When vibrational energy accumulates across cycles faster than V-V exchange can populate the upper levels, the Gordiets plateau remains transiently depleted. Existing algebraic models assume a quasi-steady plateau, whereas exact transient solutions of the nonlinear V-V diffusion equation require the elapsed time since excitation and the source strength, which are unavailable in multidimensional simulations that track only local macroscopic variables. Here, elapsed time is replaced by a local vibrational energy timescale formed from the vibrational energy per molecule and its period-averaged rate of change. This reduces the diffusion equation in level space to an ordinary differential equation solved in closed form without linearization, yielding a level-dependent correction to the steady plateau governed by a single dimensionless group: the number of V-V collisions per energy timescale weighted by the plateau amplitude at the Treanor minimum. The distribution front advances as the square root of this group, and the steady distribution is recovered as the group grows large. Compared with state-to-state master-equation calculations for N$_2$ under nanosecond pulse trains spanning 300-1500 K, 0.041-1 atm, and 1-100 kHz (1440 sampled states), the model reduces the 90th-percentile error in level populations from 1.88 decades for the steady model and 1.32 decades for an adapted self-similar solution to 0.53 decades, at essentially the evaluation cost of the steady model.

papers.title: Evidence-Calibrated Selective Decoding for Reliable Visual Question Answering
papers.abstract: Visual question answering systems can produce confident responses that are weakly supported by their input images. Contrastive decoding can reduce this dependence on language priors, but a fixed correction may also overturn a correct answer, while selective answering can conceal errors by reducing coverage. We develop evidence-calibrated selective decoding, a framework that separates three decisions: whether local visual evidence supports a candidate, how strongly to correct the original distribution, and whether the resulting answer should be released under a verification budget. Evidence Verification across Crops (EVC) measures visual support and disagreement; Adaptive Contrast Correction (ACC) applies a bounded modification within the backbone's plausible candidate set; Budgeted Selective Answering (BSA) calibrates an answer-admission threshold on held-out images. We provide a complete mathematical specification, bounded-perturbation analysis, and an evaluation protocol that distinguishes forced answering from selective risk. Our quantitative analysis re-examines published baselines on POPE instantiated over MSCOCO, A-OKVQA, and GQA, together with four MME subtasks. These public measurements reveal variation across backbones, tasks, and correction settings that motivates adaptive control. The proposed framework has not yet undergone model-level evaluation; its effectiveness remains a falsifiable hypothesis rather than an established empirical result.

authors.name: Shiyu Gu
authors.institution: Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

authors.name: Luis Miguel Santana

papers.title: Sharp Gaussian Approximation for Q-Learning
papers.abstract: Gaussian approximation provides a foundation for online statistical inference in reinforcement learning. We establish sharp non-asymptotic Gaussian approximation rates in Wasserstein distance for asynchronous Q-learning with Polyak-Ruppert averaging. We prove an upper bound of $\widetilde{O}(n^{-1/4})$, where $n$ is the number of iterations, together with a matching lower bound up to logarithmic factors. Q-learning is more challenging to analyze than linear stochastic approximation due to the nonlinearity of the Bellman operator. Asynchronous updates introduce further challenges due to Markovian noise. Our analysis separates the errors from Bellman nonlinearity, Markovian noise, and the finite-sample covariance discrepancy. In particular, we show that Markovian noise induces an unavoidable bias even when the Bellman operator is linear. The trade-off between this bias and the covariance discrepancy determines the convergence rate. We further extend our analysis to the synchronous setting and establish a sharp rate of $\widetilde{O}(n^{-1/2})$.

papers.title: Rank Functions of Flag Matroids with Applications to Order-Neutral Submodular Valuations
papers.abstract: We provide a rank function axiomatization for flag matroids and show that it is cryptomorphic to the definition of flag matroids as a sequence of matroid quotients. Afterwards, we present some applications of flag matroid rank functions by providing solutions to selected problems. In particular, we discuss connections between flag matroids and submodular valuations in computational economics by showing that rank functions of flag matroids of length $k$ are precisely the same as $\{0, 1, \dots, k\}$-order-neutral submodular valuations. We then prove that $v:2^E\to \mathbb{R}$ is an order-neutral submodular valuation if and only if $v$ can be written as $v(X) = b|X| + \sum_{i=1}^l c_ir_{N_i}(X), \quad b \in \mathbb{R}, c_i > 0$, where $N_{i+1}$ is a quotient of $N_i$. Doing so allows us to prove that every order-neutral submodular valuation is a gross-substitute valuation and that not every order-neutral submodular valuation is a Rado valuation. Furthermore, we prove that if $|E|\geq 3$, then a set $A$ is a Sidon set if and only if all $A$-submodular valuations are order-neutral, if and only if all $A$-submodular valuations are gross-substitute valuations.

papers.title: Is Gravity a Real Force or Merely a Geometrical Effect?
papers.abstract: Whether gravitation should be regarded as a fundamental force or as a manifestation of spacetime geometry remains an interesting conceptual question in physics. In Newtonian mechanics, gravitation is described as a force acting between massive objects, whereas General Relativity describes gravitational phenomena in terms of spacetime curvature, with freely falling bodies following geodesics. With this fundamental difference, it is legitimate to ask whether gravity is a real force or not, and it is very common to receive from experts a somewhat condescending answer such as "Drop a rock on your foot and you will feel that the force is real". This paper does not attempt to determine whether gravity is fundamentally a force or a geometrical phenomenon. Rather, it questions whether commonly invoked everyday experiences provide valid grounds for deciding between these interpretations.

papers.title: Adiabatic Electronic Momentum and the Continuity Equation with Nonlocal Effective Core Potentials in an Electronic Phase-Space Hamiltonian
papers.abstract: Adiabatic electronic momentum and current density provide fundamental information about electronic motion induced by nuclear motion under the Born-Oppenheimer separation. In practical electronic structure calculations, core electrons in heavy atoms are commonly replaced by effective core potentials (ECPs), whose nonlocal components introduce additional contributions to electronic momentum and the continuity equation. Here, using a phase-space electronic Hamiltonian approach, we investigate these nonlocal components on adiabatic electronic momentum and the continuity equation in small molecules with moving nuclei. We demonstrate that this approach efficiently describes adiabatic electronic momentum and the divergence of electronic current density when the nonlocal contributions to the corresponding electronic operators are properly accounted for. We find that the nonlocal correction to electronic momentum is important when the ECP-centered atoms move but is small otherwise, reflecting the spatial locality of the electronic response and ECP. We further examine the implications of moving ECPs, which account for the motion of nonlocal pseudopotentials with the nuclei to restore Galilean covariance, for adiabatic electronic transport. We show that, for nondegenerate systems with time-reversal symmetry, moving ECPs do not modify the coordinate space adiabatic evolution of time-reversal even observables through second order in nuclear velocity, although they can alter the electronic momentum operator and its feedback on nuclear dynamics.

authors.name: Zhen Tao
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Reliable Conditioned Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability via Subsolution Learning on Exact Local Windows
papers.abstract: Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability computes the maximal safe set and a safety filter for a given obstacle configuration, but it must be re-solved whenever the obstacles change, which a deployed robot cannot afford. Learning a single value function conditioned on the obstacle set removes the re-solve, yet it sharpens the central weakness of learned reachability: one network must now cover a whole family of safety problems, and its approximation error carries no preferred sign, so rare obstacle configurations silently produce false-safe states. To address these challenges, we present a conditioned reachability model designed so that the remaining error falls on the conservative side. Specifically, our method caps the obstacle margin, which makes the value function provably local, in the sense that obstacles farther than a known threshold cannot affect it, so the model reads only a body-frame window, trains on small scenes, and transfers to scenes of any size with millisecond per-scene preparation. Moreover, the output structure builds the value bound into the model. By training with counterexample mining over the finite-dimensional window configuration space, we maximize the claimed safe volume subject to the HJ inequality, so the learned set grows toward the true safe set from the conservative side. Across all tested obstacle settings, ours is the only method that combines recovery comparable to per-scene DeepReach training with near-zero rollout collisions. We also extend the method to a 10D quadrotor, again with markedly lower collision rates than the baselines.

papers.title: First-order convergence of finite-difference approximations to the minimum action for diffusions with multiplicative noise
papers.abstract: We prove first-order convergence of finite-difference approximations to the Freidlin--Wentzell minimum action for diffusions with multiplicative noise, which answers the question of the sharp rate left open in [Hong, Jin, Sheng, \emph{IMA J. Numer. Anal.} 45 (2025), 1501--1536]. As shown in that work, a bound on the action controls only the $L^2$ norm of the velocity, which leads to a half-order estimate for the difference between the discrete and continuous actions. To improve it, we use the discrete Euler--Lagrange equation to derive mesh-independent $L^\infty$ bounds on the velocity of piecewise affine interpolants of stationary discrete paths with bounded action. For the case of a unique continuous minimizer, we identify the leading coefficient of the error between the discrete and continuous minimum actions on uniform grids, and a scalar example shows that the first-order error bound is sharp. We also prove strong $H^1(0,T;\mathbb R^d)$ subsequential convergence of interpolated discrete minimizers. Numerical experiments for a two-protein genetic toggle switch confirm first-order convergence of the discrete action for transitions in both directions.

authors.name: Diancong Jin
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: FinVision: Multimodal AI for Visualizing Financial Narratives
papers.abstract: Financial narratives contain rich information about firms' performance and business conditions. Conventional text analysis often summarizes this information into numerical representations, which may not fully preserve the dynamic structure described in the narrative. In this study, we develop FinVision, a domain-specific multimodal generative model that translates financial narratives into visual representations of contemporaneous market dynamics. Using 87,940 paired observations of Management Discussion and Analysis (MD&A) disclosures and stock price charts, FinVision learns the average relationship between a firm's narrative account of a fiscal year and its stock-price dynamics over the same period. Given an MD&A alone, the trained model generates a text-implied stock chart, extending financial text analysis beyond numerical representations toward text-to-visual generation. We validate FinVision in two ways. First, held-out tests show that the model generates stock-chart representations that closely resemble observed charts and outperform direct LLM prompting, general-purpose text-to-image models, and the same architecture without financial-domain adaptation. Second, we examine the economic validity of the generated representations by comparing text-implied and observed stock charts. The resulting discrepancy is systematically associated with weaker investor responses around subsequent 10-K filings and with worse subsequent market and operating outcomes. Overall, our findings show how domain-adapted multimodal generative AI can create a new visual representation of financial text and provide an additional modality for studying business communication.

authors.name: Yixuan Tang
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Allen H. Huang
authors.institution: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: AdaptType: Accessible and Customizable Multimodal Text Entry in Virtual Reality for People with Upper-Body Motor Impairments
papers.abstract: Text entry in virtual reality (VR) is cumbersome, especially for people with upper-body motor impairments. Existing techniques often demand both fine and gross motor control, yet users' motor abilities vary widely. To address this range of needs, we present AdaptType, a multimodal VR text entry system that enables users to configure input techniques that best suit their abilities, and scaffolds customization through ability-based recommendations. Through a study with 10 participants, we found that customized multimodal techniques improved text entry speed compared to gaze- or hand-only techniques, and complemented voice for error correction, decreasing failure rate from 15.1% to 2.0%. We found that AdaptType yielded high text entry speed (36.26 WPM) and accuracy (0.36% error rate), with low task load and high usability ratings. We also found ability-based recommendations effectively scaffolded customization. Our work contributes more accessible and personalized VR text entry solutions for people with upper-body motor impairments.

papers.title: A Speech-LLM Framework for Enrollment-Free Wake-Word-Guided Target-Speaker Recognition in Complex Noisy Scenarios for Seamless Human-Machine Interaction
papers.abstract: Target-speaker automatic speech recognition (TS-ASR) is essential for reliable human-machine interaction in complex acoustic environments, where overlapping speech and background noise make it difficult to identify and recognize the intended speaker. Existing approaches typically rely on speaker enrollment or cascaded processing pipelines, limiting their flexibility in practical applications. To address these limitations, we propose an enrollment-free Speech-LLM framework that leverages wake-word text as a lexical cue to guide target-speaker recognition. Specifically, a text-cue encoder extracts lexical representations from the wake word, which are integrated into a pretrained speech encoder through cross-attention to establish an implicit association between the wake-word occurrence and the target speaker. This enables the model to selectively recognize subsequent commands from the target speaker without requiring enrollment speech or explicit wake-word boundaries. Furthermore, a large language model (LLM) unifies command transcription and non-target speaker rejection within a single autoregressive framework. To improve robustness against complex acoustic interference, we develop a large-scale speech synthesis and simulation pipeline with a progressive four-stage training strategy. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves a command character error rate of 16.15% and a non-target speaker rejection rate of 91.56%, yielding a unified score of 87.70%, compared with 71.70% for the strongest enrollment-free baseline. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of wake-word-guided speaker selection and highlight the potential of integrating target-speaker recognition and rejection within a unified Speech-LLM framework for robust human-machine interaction.

papers.title: Role of crystal-field degrees of freedom in square and rectangular skyrmion lattices in noncentrosymmetric tetragonal magnets
papers.abstract: We investigate the role of crystal-field degrees of freedom in stabilizing square and rectangular skyrmion lattices in a noncentrosymmetric localized-moment model on a square lattice. The magnetic phases are determined using self-consistent mean-field calculations. We first consider a single crystal-field doublet with exchange and polar-type Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interactions. We find square skyrmion lattices with distinct magnetic periods, as well as a rectangular skyrmion lattice that spontaneously breaks the in-plane fourfold rotational symmetry. Their stability and field-induced phase sequences are strongly controlled by the crystal-field wave function, including reentrant behavior of the rectangular phase. Second-neighbor exchange further modifies the competition among these states. When a second crystal-field doublet is retained, additional rectangular skyrmion lattices with distinct modulation patterns emerge, together with axial single-$Q$ states and various double-$Q$ states. These results demonstrate that crystal-field degrees of freedom provide a microscopic mechanism for tuning the stability, spatial symmetry, and topology of multiple-$Q$ magnetic states.

papers.title: Stagewise Adaptive Boosting
papers.abstract: Stagewise algorithms and sparsity-inducing regularization are two influential approaches to high-dimensional modeling. Existing stagewise theory, however, largely centers on convex regularization, whereas stronger sparsity and other structural preferences are often pursued through fixed-level nonconvex optimization rather than generating an entire adaptive solution path. We develop stagewise adaptive boosting, a general framework that builds a monotone path by selecting the update consistent with structural preference. The framework can encourage sparsity along the path itself and also admits extensions that promote other properties of the solution, including group selection, similarity across models for multiple outcomes, and known priorities or prerequisite relations among predictors. We study its theoretical property as well as finite sample performance using simulations and real-data analyses. Across these studies, the proposed pathwise approach often achieves predictive performance comparable to commonly used baselines while selecting substantially smaller models. These results suggest that adaptive stagewise learning provides a practical route to stronger sparsity and richer structural control without repeatedly solving separate weighted or nonconvex optimization problems.

papers.title: History independence and base-dominant rigidity for polynomial skew products
papers.abstract: We study history independence of fast directions and its relation to the Binder--DeMarco dimension formula for regular polynomial skew products of degree $d\ge2$. Assuming uniform expansion on the support of the measure of maximal entropy and a base Lyapunov exponent larger than the vertical exponent, we prove that history independence is equivalent to conjugacy to a polynomial product by an affine shear map. Under history independence, the measure of maximal entropy satisfies the Binder--DeMarco dimension formula. If, in addition, the splitting is dominated, the dimension formula also implies history independence. The proof first upgrades the measurable fast direction to a holomorphic line field and then uses its invariance on periodic fibers to force the affine product structure. The converse dimension implication combines an entropy comparison argument with rigidity of local symmetries of periodic fiber Julia sets.

papers.title: A Las Vegas algorithm for satisfiable SAT formulas, with an application to timetabling
papers.abstract: Many scheduling problems need many different feasible timetables, and a view of how much freedom each event has. We study a Las Vegas algorithm that samples satisfying assignments of a Boolean formula one variable at a time: it draws each value from an estimate of its conditional probability, propagates, and restarts on a contradiction. Every output is a checked solution and comes with the exact probability of producing it. We prove that a run succeeds with probability at least $2^{-K}$, where $K$ is the expected Kullback--Leibler divergence between the true and estimated conditional probabilities along the run of a uniform solution. We also bound the distance of the outputs from uniform from the samples alone; it is a divergence in the opposite direction to $K$, so a sampler can succeed more often while being farther from uniform. On generated timetabling instances counted exactly, belief propagation on the timetabling problem brings $K$ to at most about one bit, and the estimated counts are within 2% of the exact ones. On a real university instance of the International Timetabling Competition 2019, rerunning only the failed runs delivered all 72 requested timetables with each of two estimators. Belief propagation succeeds in 31% of runs. Steered by a Markov chain that carries a nearly feasible timetable, it succeeds in 65% of runs, with outputs at least 300 bits from uniform. There the importance weights are too uneven to estimate the number of timetables, and we certify a lower bound instead. For random 3-SAT, an estimator whose $K$ grows logarithmically would give a polynomial-time Las Vegas algorithm beyond the densities at which any algorithm is proved to succeed; we conjecture that one exists below the satisfiability threshold.

papers.title: HEmIF-Bench: Benchmarking H&E-to-mIF Models BeyondVirtual-StainFidelity
papers.abstract: Hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-to-multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF) generators predict spatial protein expression from routine histology, yet pixel-level marker reconstruction does not establish downstream utility. We present HEmIF-Bench, evaluating five frozen generators across eight datasets spanning molecular, cellular, tissue, and patient scales. HEmIF-Bench decouples internal encoder features from generated outputs, benchmarking both against the pathology foundation reference UNI2. Mirroring the clinical workflow where pathologists rely on mIF to define cell phenotypes, delineate tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) and germinal centers (GCs), and stratify patient risk, we evaluate external CD3 recovery, single-cell classification, dense nuclear segmentation, TLS/GC segmentation, and patient survival prediction. Across the benchmark, foundation-model-based MIPHEI-ViT leads among the generators, while non-foundation models show task-specific strengths. Comparing the two routes reveals that internal encoder features generally outperform generated outputs, and larger output marker panels do not guarantee stronger downstream utility across datasets. Moreover, neither internal encoder features nor generated outputs consistently surpass frozen UNI2. These findings show that pixel-level stain fidelity does not equate to downstream utility, and that generators trained at current paired-data scales have yet to surpass large-scale pure-H&E foundation models. With the expansion of paired translation cohorts and the advancement of foundation-based generative architectures, HEmIF-Bench establishes a definitive benchmark for tracking when H&E-to-mIF generation crosses the threshold to deliver genuine value beyond routine histology for tumor microenvironment analysis and precision oncology.

authors.name: Fuxian Zhao
authors.institution: Affiliated Hospital of Youjiang Medical University for Nationalities

authors.name: Hyokeun Park
authors.institution: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: AGI: Agility Index for Power Systems Dynamic Performance, Inspired by Reynolds Number
papers.abstract: Multiple established metrics and indices exist to quantify the dynamic performance of power systems. With the growth of inverter based resources, these mostly conventional metrics and indices may not encompass all important elements and variables that hold information about the grid performance, especially the damping properties. This paper proposes the Agility Index (AGI), which is a Reynolds number-inspired metric for power system dynamics relating the ratio of inertia to damping. With the current trends towards high-power inverter assets and reduced-inertia grids, explicit attention is necessary in monitoring inertia and damping together. This paper shares insights the AGI presents about the dynamic performance of power systems.

papers.title: Extensions of $q$-supercongruences arising from a quadratic summation of Gasper and Rahman
papers.abstract: In this paper, inspired by recent work of Guo and Zhao, and of Guo and Zudilin, we establish two parametric extensions of their $q$-supercongruences using Gasper and Rahman's quadratic summation, the Chinese remainder theorem, and the creative microscoping method. These extensions yield two one-parameter generalizations of the $q$-supercongruences considered by Guo and Zhao and by Guo and Zudilin.

papers.title: Centered Ablation: Why Last-Layer Directional Ablation Under-Fires or Collapses, and a Closed-Form Fix
papers.abstract: Directional ablation removes a hidden state's component along a "behaviour direction" while a language model runs. It is the standard way to switch a behaviour such as refusal off, but it is erratic: on some models it barely fires, on others the text collapses into repetition. We show why, and fix it. At the last residual stream, ablation is exactly a logit bias: a fixed vocabulary footprint scaled by a gate, the cosine between the hidden state and the direction. The gate is measured from the origin, but last-layer states share a large common mode far from it, so a direction that overlaps the common mode fires on benign text and under-fires on its targets. Centered Ablation (CA) projects the common mode out of the direction, in closed form. Across 8 models, CA raises attack success by 29 and 46 points where the standard recipe under-fires, cuts collapse on Gemma-2-9B from 50\% to 1\%, and preserves 12 to 40 points more benign answers on high-overlap models, 39 to 46 more than the affine offset of prior work. Two numbers computed before generation predict, on models the analysis had not seen, which gain faithfulness and which gain attack success, and a collapse index marks when text degenerates. We also show that two standard safety judges score collapsed text in opposite directions, which can fabricate a 46-point effect.

papers.title: Sensing with OFDM Signals: How Do the Constellations Affect the Sensing Accuracy?
papers.abstract: This paper investigates how communication constellations affect joint range-velocity estimation with data-bearing orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) signals. To this end, starting from the continuous-time sensing process, we derive a discrete observation model and specify its validity conditions. For multiple targets with unknown delays, Doppler shifts, and complex gains, the complete Fisher information matrix (FIM) admits a structural factorization separating deterministic channel derivatives from random symbol-energy weights. This structure yields a Jensen-type lower bound on the average conditional Cramer-Rao bound (CRB), which is attained exactly by constant-modulus constellations. Single-target closed-form expressions further reveal the dependence of the bounds on the transmitted energy distribution and physical OFDM parameters. We also formulate two-dimensional fast Fourier transform (FFT), concentrated maximum-likelihood (ML), and sliding-subarray multiple signal classification (MUSIC) processing under the derived observation model. Numerical results support the theoretical optimality of constant-modulus constellations but also show that the CRB gap between phase-shift keying (PSK) and quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) becomes negligible when the numbers of subcarriers and OFDM symbols are considerably large. The performance of ML estimation closely approaches the derived bounds, which confirms the effectiveness of the theoretical analysis. FFT processing exhibits grid-induced error floors. In the considered scenarios, MUSIC provides lower estimation errors than FFT and exhibits a more pronounced constellation dependence.

authors.name: Junjie Chen
authors.institution: Anhui University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: Exact Redundancy under Average and Almost-Sure Distortion Constraints
papers.abstract: We characterize the exact redundancy of lossy source coding under average and almost-sure distortion constraints. For general source and output alphabets, we establish the asymptotic redundancy coefficients under suitable regularity conditions. Under the average distortion constraint, the coefficient is half of the minimum probability that an output reveals information about the source, among all rate-distortion optimal channels. Under the almost-sure distortion constraint, the coefficient is either $1/2$ or $1$, depending on whether the $D$-tilted information is constant or not. Both converse results follow from a common change-of-measure inequality. Finally, we verify the required conditions under both distortion requirements always hold for finite alphabets.

papers.title: Distance-Certified Polyak-type Stepsizes for Subgradient Methods under H\"older Growth
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider nonsmooth convex optimization under a H{\"o}lder growth condition, with quadratic growth and weak sharp minima as two important special cases. Existing subgradient methods often employ predetermined decaying stepsize schedules, whereas the classical Polyak stepsize selects its stepsize adaptively but requires knowledge of the optimal value. We introduce a new distance-certified subgradient method (\DCSG) that follows a one-step optimization principle analogous to that underlying the Polyak stepsize, without requiring the optimal value. Specifically, \DCSG{} maintains a valid upper certificate for the current squared distance to the solution set. The method selects each stepsize by minimizing the worst-case upper bound on the next squared distance over all distances consistent with this certificate. We show that the resulting minimax problem admits a closed-form solution, yielding an explicit adaptive stepsize update. Under uniformly bounded subgradients, \DCSG{} improves upon the convergence rate of the classical subgradient method and matches the state-of-the-art rates for Lipschitz convex optimization under H{\"o}lder growth. In particular, it achieves linear convergence under sharp growth. Numerical experiments illustrate the performance of \DCSG.

authors.name: Yang Zheng
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: EgoSwarm: Learning Decentralized Robot Swarm Intelligence from Human Swarm Demonstrations
papers.abstract: Advancing from individual embodied intelligence to swarm embodied intelligence is a key step toward scalable, general-purpose embodied intelligence. Complex tasks often require multiple agents to divide responsibilities, coordinate handovers, and manipulate shared objects collaboratively. However, existing robot learning methods rely primarily on individual demonstrations, which provide limited supervision for modeling dependencies among agent actions, while collecting multi-robot demonstrations at scale remains difficult. Human egocentric demonstrations offer a scalable alternative, yet distributed observations from multiple participants cannot directly supervise decentralized policies. We introduce EgoSwarm, the first robot learning framework for learning decentralized multi-robot collaboration from human swarm demonstrations. EgoSwarm collects more than 50 hours of collaborative experience using a robot-free multi-person egocentric system. We introduce the Swarm Interaction Packet (SIP) and Swarm Interaction Token (SIT) to recover cross-agent interaction relations from distributed observations and transform this experience into local supervision consistent with deployment-time information constraints. We further propose SwarmVLA, which transfers knowledge of swarm behavior to decentralized policies conditioned on local observations, local history, and limited neighbor messages. SwarmVLA achieves a mean success rate of 72.2% across three categories of multi-robot collaborative tasks. Project page:https://xitong-c.github.io/EgoSwarm_Page/.

authors.name: Ziqiang Liu
authors.institution: Central South University of Forestry and Technology

papers.title: Variance-adaptive confidence regions for fixed-benchmark binomial mixtures, with application to LLM evaluation
papers.abstract: We construct confidence intervals for linear functionals $\theta(F_m)=\int h\,dF_m$ of the empirical law $F_m$ of success probabilities $p_1,\dots,p_m$, from independent counts $c_i\sim\mathrm{Bin}(n,p_i)$, as for a language model run $n$ times per problem. Coverage is at least $1-\alpha$ for every $n$, $m$ and fixed $(p_i)$, simultaneously for all bounded $h$. The variance-adaptive (VA) region tests each candidate mixing law with the conditional variance of the tail counts it implies. This variance is linear in the law, so the region is a linear program, and cell envelopes keep it valid off-grid. Regions calibrated for iid sampling target a super-population law and are conservative for $\theta(F_m)$. With all $n$ tail counts, fixed $n$, continuous $h$ and a grid refined as $m\to\infty$, the identification part of VA's width is first-order worst-case optimal, as for any localization with the same index set. Under a rule fixed before the main comparator runs, VA was narrower than a two-stage plug-in band at every $n$ (median width ratio 0.60 at $n=128$), but not than the asymptotic, pointwise AMARI interval at $n=128$; on real rollout pools it was wider than both pointwise and Bonferroni-adjusted AMARI at $n\le128$. For $P(p>0)$ and pass@$k$ with $k\gg n$ the data support only lower bounds.

authors.name: Kuancheng Ye
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Multi-bubble blowup for the energy supercritical Schr\"{o}dinger equation
papers.abstract:
This article establishes the existence of finite time multi-bubble Type II blowup solutions for the focusing energy supercritical nonlinear Schr"{o}dinger equation. Given integers $K\geq 2$ and $L\geq 2$, a positive integer exponent $p$, and a dimension $d>d_\ast(p,K,L)$, we construct solutions concentrating at any prescribed $K$ distinct points $\{x_j\}_{j=1}^K\subset\mathbb R^d$, with the asymptotic form  egin{equation*} \psi(t,x)=\lambda^{ rac1p}(t)\sum_{j=1}^K Q ig(\lambda(t)(x-x_j) ig)+\zeta^\ast(x)+o_{\dot H^\sigma}(1),\qquad t	o0, \end{equation*} where $\lambda(t)=t^{- rac12-
u}$, $
u=- rac12- rac{L}{\lambda_+}$, $s_c= rac d2- rac1p$, and $s_c<\sigma<s_c+ rac{4
u}{1+2
u}$. Here $Q$ is the positive radial stationary profile, $\lambda_+$ is the slow characteristic exponent in its asymptotic expansion at infinity and $\zeta^\ast$ is the limiting radiation determined by the outer profile. The proof combines a matched asymptotic construction of a finite order approximate solution with high order energy estimates and a compactness argument. The key ingredients are the elimination of the self-similar oscillatory branch through a quantized choice of blowup rate and the quantitative control of the combined algebraic tails of the translated ground state potentials.

authors.name: Xuanying Li
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Developing a Sky-End Fibre Aperture for the AMASE Fibre Bundle
papers.abstract: The Affordable Multiple-Aperture Spectroscopy Explorer (AMASE) project aims to enable high-resolution spectroscopy of ionised gas in galaxies. However, fabricating ultra- dense fibre bundles with micrometre-level precision presents significant challenges. We detail a fabrication process that combines precision machining, stress-reducing handling, and iterative polishing. Although the final prototype did not meet the optical performance targets, our methods reduced manual labour, improved reproducibility, and identified critical failure modes, providing essential information for future astrophotonic instrument designs.

papers.title: Testing General Relativity by Reconstructing Dark Energy and the Growth Index with Physics-Informed Neural Networks
papers.abstract: We extend the Cosmo-PINN, a physics-informed neural network for model-independent cosmological reconstruction, to reconstruct the dark energy equation of state parameter $w_{\mathrm{DE}}(z)$ and the growth index $\gamma (z)$ of matter perturbations. The reconstruction is performed through three modules: the background module, the matter growth module, and the growth index module. The background module learns the dark energy density $\rho _{\mathrm{DE}}(z)$ from cosmological observations, and $w_{\mathrm{DE}}(z)$ is reconstructed through the residual of the conservation equation. The reconstructed background is then passed to the other two modules, which reconstruct the observables $f(z)$ and $f\sigma _{8}(z)$ either directly from the linear perturbation equation of General Relativity or through an independently reconstructed growth index $\gamma (z)$. Comparing the two reconstructions on the same background provides a consistency test of the underlying physical framework. The network is trained on the DESI DR2 Baryon Acoustic Oscillations, Cosmic Chronometers, Type Ia Supernovae, and redshift-space distortion data. Posterior uncertainties for the reconstructed cosmological parameters and functions are obtained through Hamiltonian Monte Carlo sampling. For the different data combinations, the posterior median of the present-day dark energy equation of state lies within the range $w_{\mathrm{DE,0}}\in \lbrack -0.930,-0.867]$, while the phantom divide crossing takes place at $z\simeq 0.41$--$0.53$. The posterior median of the present-day growth index reconstructed from the data lies within $\gamma _{0}\simeq 0.60$--$0.62$, indicating suppression of the growth of cosmic structure.

papers.title: Switching Structure and Finite-Event Optima for One-Orbit Minimum-Fuel In-Plane HCW Maneuvers
papers.abstract: Under in-plane Hill$\unicode{x2013}$Clohessy$\unicode{x2013}$Wiltshire dynamics with independently bounded radial and along-track thrust, we prove that every target reachable within one orbit has a fixed-time minimum-fuel control with at most ten switches. We first show that regular optima have at most four radial and six along-track switches, coupled through a shared costate. Of the 35 candidate count pairs, 11 require minimum durations, one cannot be optimal, and 23 are attainable at arbitrarily short durations. We then convert singular-arc optima into bang/off optima with at most five switches by preserving terminal moments. We demonstrate terminal accuracy and whole-arc Pontryagin consistency through 55,296 numerical transfers.

papers.title: Read, Then Shade? How Visual Evidence Changes Incentive-Driven Misreporting in Vision-Language Advisors
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) increasingly read a scene and report it to someone who acts on the report, sometimes under objectives that differ from that person's. We ask whether a stated incentive moves what a VLM reports, and whether this changes when the value must be read from pixels rather than given as text. In seeded synthetic scenes, a model reads the position of a target on a labelled axis and reports one integer to a fixed receiver; it is paid, in simulation, for accuracy or for a report a few units to one side, and every scene is also presented with the true value as text. Across a pilot and three follow-up studies with hash-frozen protocols, four small open VLMs from three families, and 15,170 held-out trials, a stated payoff moved reports in both modalities, and exact compliance at three units was significantly lower with the image than with text for three of four models; Qwen2.5-VL 7B showed no reliable difference. Adding the true value as text to the image prompt removed the gap in every model. For InternVL3 the gap vanished on scenes it read correctly when it wrote its reading first; for Gemma 3 it persisted. For Qwen2.5-VL 3B, which read every scene correctly, the gap held in four of five payoff paraphrases, nearly vanished when the model wrote its reading before its report or when the prompt stated that the client wants the truth, vanished with an unpaid goal, and persisted when the model reported before stating its reading; how often it shaded at all, even with text, depended strongly on the wording. When told that the client wants the true value, three of four models still shaded every text report. Visual input did not make these advisors reliably more truthful; it made compliance with a stated incentive depend on whether the read value is made explicit and on output order, a dependence that text-only evaluations and mean-shift metrics do not reveal.

papers.title: Sharp First-Hit Identification from Finite Depth Samples
papers.abstract: Which depths in a new camera view are determined by finitely many source-depth measurements? Pointwise uncertainty bounds do not answer this question: unobserved geometry between samples can change which surface is encountered first. We study a bounded Lipschitz class of continuous source inverse-depth fields with interval observations and known camera pose. Building on classical Lipschitz envelopes, we characterize the exact set of attainable first-hit depths and construct a globally admissible scene for every value in that set. The set can be disconnected. We also give a necessary and sufficient test for several proposed depths to be first hits of one shared scene. An epipolar reduction uses scalar cone inequalities without enumerating surfaces. In a rectified model with source spacing $h$, interval half-width $\varepsilon$, baseline $b$, and slope bound $L$, we prove a sharp worst-case inverse-depth diameter of $\max\{Lh+2\varepsilon,2\varepsilon/(1-bL)\}$ when $bL<1$, subject to sufficient depth and domain range for attainment. Exact samples still give the sharp bound $Lh$ at $bL=1$, while above this threshold ambiguity need not vanish as sampling becomes arbitrarily dense. Any positive measurement uncertainty can destroy uniform stability at the critical threshold. We provide constructive examples, an exact rational validation oracle, and a frozen ten-scene evaluation using reference, stereo, and learned-depth observations. The experiments separate solver correctness under the scene assumptions from failure of those assumptions: fixed learned-depth bands often yield narrow but incorrect sets. The results identify what a specified scene class permits; they do not infer a continuum regularity or physical-scene guarantee from sampled predictions.

papers.title: Toward Planning Representations That Separate Task Structure from Visual Content
papers.abstract: Effective planning requires representations that preserve task-relevant geometry and object identity while ignoring visual variation that does not alter the task. Existing evaluations of visual generalization often change several factors simultaneously, making the source of a failure difficult to identify. We introduce a controlled evaluation of object-goal navigation (ObjectNav), the task of reaching an instance of a named object category, in procedurally generated ProcTHOR houses. Training and evaluation houses share floor plans, object locations, goals, and start states, while visual factors are changed individually or in combination. Across model-free reinforcement learning (RL), model-based RL, and agents using frozen pretrained visual representations, our results show that appearance changes impair navigation, but their effects differ sharply by factor. Surface material changes account for most of the average change in success, whereas clutter and lighting have little effect. The magnitude of a global image statistics shift does not reliably predict performance: changing only the goal object's appearance can substantially impair an end-to-end agent despite a small image-level change. We found that a model based agent that plans over frozen features from the pretrained DINOv2 image encoder achieves the highest success (0.83) under the full shift, but remains sensitive to surface appearance. Our experiments reveal an important requirement for planning representations: they must separate invariant spatial task structure from appearance.

papers.title: When Does an AUROC Comparison Survive a Change in Population Mix?
papers.abstract: Does an AUROC comparison survive a change in the proportions of tasks, populations, or image corruptions? A pooled-AUROC ranking of failure detectors or uncertainty scores describes one particular mix of groups. We study two fixed scores for a common binary target under mixtures of fixed group-conditional laws. Using the cross-group AUC decomposition, we prove that every rational symmetric quadratic comparison geometry is realizable by finite scalar-score distributions. Universal dominance is thus coNP-hard, and even exhaustive checks of every mixture on fewer than $K$ groups can miss a $K$-group reversal. A grid bound gives a dimension-uniform approximation certificate with sharp $1/m$ order. Common score marginals across groups make the comparison numerator linear, with an error envelope for imperfect alignment. These results yield exact finite-bank audits, explicit reversal mixtures and distances, and simultaneous population statements. For failure detection with a frozen ResNet-50 on ImageNet-C, 15 of 18 confidence-score comparisons win in every corruption family on a discovery split, and all 15 are finite-bank certified over all family mixtures on a held-out split; over all 15 corruption types, of 14 discovery winners the corrected grid certifies 10, leaves 3 unresolved, and finds one confirmation reversal of at least 0.05 AUROC. An audit of all 11,019 released Stable LM 2 12B outputs and 35 uncertainty methods finds 66 confirmation-set comparisons that win within all four tasks yet reverse under mixing. Discovery-fitted marginal rank alignment removes all 66; an alignment-error envelope certifies 83 comparisons. Label checks also change several selected reversals. The findings distinguish robustness of frozen scores from robustness after calibration; they do not establish human-error detection, robustness to unseen corruptions, or generalization beyond the evaluated banks.

papers.title: Exact Sparse Assignment with Costly Target Embeddings: Fixed-Realization Certificates and an Empirical Audit
papers.abstract: Embedding-based one-to-one association is common in vision and data integration: detections are associated with tracks and records are linked across databases. Such pipelines often solve a sparse optional assignment whose edge scores add a cheap term to an inner product of neural embeddings. When target embeddings are costly, one can acquire them selectively and stop once a certificate proves that the current assignment is optimal. We give such a certificate for unit-norm embeddings. It bounds the unknown part of every reassignment by a support function and maximizes the resulting robust gains with a second sparse assignment; a shared owner-centred bound dominates any fixed-centre triangle bound. We make precise what is certified when network features are not batch-invariant: the realized values of the acquired rows and every unit-ball completion of the rest, not a second forward pass in a different batch. Auditing against a separately batched cache tests a different property; on our first pilot it produced a spurious $2.49\times10^{-6}$ objective failure. We audit the corrected protocol on four public text entity-matching benchmarks with two frozen encoders; no image data is used. All 96 certificate simulations and 120 online selective timings were exact on their own realization (largest objective gap $6.82\times10^{-13}$). At group size 8 the shared certificate acquires on average 60% of candidate-active targets, against 74% (mean centre), 69% (MEB) and 60% (zero centre): it beats the mean and MEB centres but not the zero centre, and savings concentrate in one benchmark (7% acquired). The prespecified runtime claim is contradicted: selective execution is +0.510 s slower per run (dataset-cluster 95% interval [+0.248, +0.772]). Uniform-microbatch re-encodings preserved the optimum in only 5 of 8 encoder-dataset cells, and 45 of 120 online runs disagreed with an eager cache at near-ties.

papers.title: Learning Advantage Function Surrogates via Convex Conjugate Matching
papers.abstract: A policy trained to make per-unit decisions, such as how much of a product to order, tells us the best action but not the cost of deviating from it. That cost, the advantage function, is what downstream systems need when they have to depart from the per-unit optimum: to estimate the impact of ordering more or fewer units, to respond to a one-off vendor discount, or to satisfy a shared capacity constraint. The advantage function is what makes such trade-offs computable, yet pure policy-learning algorithms often produce the policy alone, without a critic that would yield it. We propose a method to train an advantage function surrogate through price perturbations motivated by a Fenchel-Young loss. We describe a two-stage recipe (fit the policy, then the cost model) and illustrate it on a multi-period inventory management problem.

papers.title: State-Machine Governance of Adaptive Enforcement: Evidence from a Paired-Scenario Evaluation
papers.abstract: AI-assisted security systems can recommend rapid policy changes, but governing their execution requires explicit authorization, evidence, and recovery rules. This study evaluated a machine-verifiable, state-machine-governed transition procedure implemented in ZTGuard using 36 matched scripted scenarios and deterministic vendor-connector simulations. Each pair held the starting state, telemetry, AI recommendation, and scheduled vendor condition constant. The sole dependent variable, Control, was the equal-weight mean of traceability, accountability, audit-chain completeness, and reliable rollback capability. Mean Control was 0.720 (SD = 0.218) for the scripted operator-driven baseline and 0.972 (SD = 0.131) for the governed procedure. A two-tailed paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test yielded V = 359, p < .001, with a matched-pairs rank-biserial correlation of .899. Twenty-six pairs favored treatment, nine were tied, and one favored baseline. The findings support controlled artifact utility, not production readiness. Interpretation is limited by purposive sampling, scripted operators, simulated connectors, overlapping components, and arm-specific scoring rules.

papers.title: Goldman's Ergodicity Conjecture and Branched Developing Maps
papers.abstract: We prove that every representation $\rho:\pi_1(\Sigma_g)\rightarrow\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathrm{R})$ which sends every simple closed curve to a hyperbolic element admits a branched developing map. As a corollary, the mapping class group action on the Euler class zero component of the $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathrm{R})$-character variety of a genus $g$ surface is ergodic if $g\geq3$. (The action is not ergodic if $g=2$.) Moreover, almost every representation of nonzero Euler class admits a branched developing map.

papers.title: Seen but Unsaid: Locating and Repairing Cross-Image Comparison in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) often fail to match a point or an object across two images, even when the answer can be decoded from their own hidden states. We trace this failure from the visual tokens to the answer letter, in Qwen3-VL (2B-32B), InternVL3.5-8B, and Gemma-3-12B, on synthetic shape matching, same-instance point correspondence (HPatches), and semantic correspondence (SPair-71k), and find two distinct failure points, a small set of attention heads that carries the comparison, and a repair that touches 0.02% of the parameters. Two failure points: exact copies are compared but not read out. An answer-position probe exceeds the calibrated output by 15 to 25 points in every family, for nameable and unnameable shapes alike, and steering along the probe's direction moves no more answers than random directions. Semantic correspondences are present in the visual tokens but never reach the answer. One pathway: redistributing the cross-image attention of 16-32 heads, with its mass preserved, removes 17-22 points of synthetic and 15-32 points of HPatches accuracy, against at most 7 for random or attention-matched heads. A lever that training finds on its own: training only these heads' query and key projections raises SPair-71k accuracy by 28.3 points (Qwen3-VL-8B) and 25.1 points (InternVL3.5-8B), beats both layer-matched and attention-matched heads, and transfers to HPatches and BLINK. An unconstrained all-layer adapter routes 21-51% of its gain through the attention of the same heads, against at most 7% for random heads, and does so by changing what they read (83-86% of the effect) rather than their weights. Every decision rule was frozen before its run, and every reported number is recomputed by independent verification scripts.

papers.title: Characterization of Cubic Graphs with Exactly Two Lonely Edges
papers.abstract: Perfect matchings are fundamental to understanding structural connectivity in cubic graphs, with "lonely edges" (edges in exactly one perfect matching) forming a critical underexplored class. Goedgebeur et al. (J. Graph Theory, 112 (2026) 276-289) established an upper bound of 6 on the number of lonely edges in 3-connected non-double covered cubic graphs and completely characterized the classes $\mathcal{U}_k$ for $3 \le k \le 6$. Narayana et al. subsequently gave a recursive characterization of the subclass in which the two lonely edges lie in the same perfect matching. This paper completes the classification by presenting a full structural characterization of $\mathcal{U}_2$, the family of 3-connected cubic graphs with exactly two lonely edges. We identify the minimally non-contractible "primitive kernels" of $\mathcal{U}_2$ and develop constructive operations to generate any graph in $\mathcal{U}_2$ from these kernels.

papers.title: Delayed Heuristic-Behavior-Target Coupling for Off-Policy Reinforcement Learning in Inventory Control
papers.abstract: Many reinforcement learning methods tie data collection to the task policy, while coordinating independently optimized behavior and target policies remains challenging. Policies learned by these methods can perform unreliably in long-horizon tasks under uncertainty, such as inventory control, where failures can incur extreme costs. We introduce Heuristic Behavior Policy Optimization (HBPO), an off-policy framework that routes heuristic guidance through persistent behavior learning, coupled with target-policy, updating separately with residual-based advantage estimation and emphatic weighting. Under matched environment interaction budgets on DSIS and its risk-augmented variant DSIS-RB, HBPO recovers many high-cost initial policies and improves most non-collapse comparison groups. Cold starts achieve competitive costs without final cost collapse across all tested seeds. We identify a transmission chain in the delayed heuristic-behavior-target coupling as a key driver of recovery and improvement. Generation-level diagnostics trace heuristic uptake and subsequent selective target responses, while component ablations support the contribution of this transmission mechanism to policy recovery and improvement.

papers.title: A new class of Manin triples of compatible Lie algebras
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a new class of Manin triples of compatible Lie algebras and investigates the corresponding bialgebra structures. To this end, we first study an invariant-c$2$c form on a compatible Lie algebra, namely a nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form that is invariant with respect to one Lie bracket and is a commutative $2$-cocycle with respect to the other, which naturally arises from a quadratic differential Novikov algebra. Then we introduce the notion of compatible Lie-anti-pre-Lie algebras (compatible LAPL algebras in short), which serve as the underlying algebra structures of compatible Lie algebras endowed with invariant-c$2$c forms. Furthermore, we introduce the notion of a compatible LAPL bialgebra, which is shown to be equivalent to a Manin triple of compatible Lie algebras with respect to the invariant-c$2$c form. We investigate triangular compatible LAPL bialgebras, which are obtained from antisymmetric solutions of the compatible LAPL Yang-Baxter equation. We also use $\mathcal{O}$-operators of compatible LAPL algebras to construct such solutions. Finally, we show that every differential Novikov bialgebra gives rise to a compatible LAPL bialgebra and that this construction preserves triangularity.

papers.title: Vanishing geodesic distance phenomenon and boundedness of curvatures
papers.abstract: This article concerns a conjecture proposed by Michor and Mumford in their 2005 paper, in which the vanishing of the geodesic distance is associated to the local unboundedness of the sectional curvature. In this article, we consider a Riemannian Banach manifold with all of its curvature tensors locally bounded. We derive several properties regarding the local boundedness of curvature tensors, and give a sufficient condition for a non-degenerate geodesic distance, which partially verifies the conjecture in its converse form.

authors.name: Yuxiu Lu
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Dual-Stage Channel-Posterior Integration for MLM-Aided Token Communications
papers.abstract: Token transmission over conventional digital modulation is vulnerable to channel impairments, leading to bit errors that cause received tokens to become contextually inconsistent. This paper proposes a receiver-side dual-stage channel-posterior integration framework for masked language model (MLM)-aided token reconstruction. In the proposed framework, the receiver detects unreliable token positions from channel reliability and constructs a vocabulary-level channel-posterior. In particular, within the receiver, Posterior-Weighted Input Embedding (PWE) injects this posterior into the MLM input, while Adaptive Output Logit Fusion (AOF) reuses it at the output with a channel-adaptive weight. Consequently, multiple unreliable tokens can be reconstructed in a single bidirectional MLM inference without retransmission, transmitter-side encoding, or additional MLM training. Experiments over noisy channels show up to a $67.2$\% improvement in cosine similarity over context-only MLM reconstruction, with consistent gains across different MLM architectures and existing language-model-aided methods.

papers.title: EVIDENT: Evaluating Evidence Grounding in GUI Agents
papers.abstract: GUI agents are increasingly evaluated by whether they complete web tasks, but surface success can hide a critical failure: the final answer may not be supported by evidence observed during navigation. We introduce EVIDENT, an evidence-driven benchmark for evaluating whether GUI agents ground their decisions in observable web evidence. EVIDENT contains 220 real-world English and Korean tasks spanning semantic grounding, contextual inference, and visual grounding, each paired with human-curated evidence metadata specifying what must be verified. We further separate surface task completion from evidence-grounded success using three metrics: TSR, ESR, and GSR, which respectively measure outcome success, required evidence observation, and claim-level evidence support. Experiments on commercial and open-source GUI agents reveal substantial gaps between surface success and evidence-grounded success, especially in contextual and visual tasks. These results show that current evaluations can overestimate agent reliability and highlight the need to assess not only whether agents answer, but whether they verify.
